title: Force garbage collection at end of each slot
idea: Trigger an explicit garbage collection or memory release at the end of each slot, when the node is idle, to bound memory growth between slots. Check whether Lighthouse runs any per-slot memory release (for example malloc_trim or a jemalloc purge) from its slot timer.
evidence: common/malloc_utils/Cargo.toml:36-38 Linux builds enable tikv-jemallocator feature background_threads

~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/tikv-jemalloc-sys-0.6.1+5.3.0-1-ge13ca993e8ccb9ba9847cc330696e02839f328f7/build.rs:221-228 and :457 that feature compiles background_thread:true into malloc_conf

~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/tikv-jemalloc-sys-0.6.1+5.3.0-1-ge13ca993e8ccb9ba9847cc330696e02839f328f7/jemalloc/include/jemalloc/internal/arena_types.h:7-8 dirty_decay_ms 10s, muzzy_decay_ms 0
common/malloc_utils/src/glibc.rs:14-20 fixed 128KB mmap threshold to keep glibc heap small
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7471 per_slot_task has no explicit release
gap: No explicit slot-aligned release. Jemalloc background threads already purge dirty pages on a ~10s decay (about one slot), so memory is returned between slots asynchronously. Only an explicit arena purge (arena.<MALLCTL_ARENAS_ALL>.purge) or malloc_trim(0) for sysmalloc builds from per_slot_task is missing.
impact: Small for default jemalloc builds, because the background purge already does time-based release; could help sysmalloc/glibc builds and reproducible builds that link Debian libjemalloc without the compiled conf.
refute_note: The earlier review missed that Linux builds turn on jemalloc background purge threads via the tikv-jemallocator background_threads feature, which is a time-based equivalent of per-slot release. I confirmed no malloc_trim, mallctl purge or prof call anywhere in the workspace sources.

title: Flag to tune GC growth percent
idea: Expose a runtime flag that sets how much the heap may grow before the next collection, so operators can trade memory for fewer collection runs. In Lighthouse the analogue is exposing allocator purge/decay knobs on the CLI.
evidence: common/malloc_utils/src/jemalloc.rs:3 jemalloc configured only via .cargo/config.toml
common/malloc_utils/src/glibc.rs:126 only sets M_MMAP_THRESHOLD, env override
beacon_node/src/cli.rs: no allocator flag
gap: Add optional CLI/env flags for jemalloc decay/glibc trim in malloc_utils::configure_memory_allocator.
impact: Operator memory-vs-CPU tuning only; no default gain.

title: Use SHA-NI accelerated sha256 implementation
idea: Use a sha256 implementation that dispatches to CPU SHA extensions (SHA-NI/ARMv8 crypto) for tree hashing and pool its buffers. Check that the sha256 crate used by Lighthouse's tree hashing detects and uses SHA instructions at runtime.
measured_best: gave a nice boost on Celeron, not benchmarked (pr:caplin#7060)
evidence: ~/.cargo/registry/src/*/ethereum_hashing-0.8.0/src/lib.rs:107-140 cpufeatures x86_sha_extensions latch; DynamicImpl::best() picks Sha2 (SHA-NI) when present, else ring
ethereum_hashing-0.8.0/Cargo.toml:31-36 default features zero_hash_cache+ring (ring does its own ARMv8 crypto detection)
lh-perf-research-base/Cargo.toml:153 ethereum_hashing = "0.8.0" with default features
tree_hash merkleize_padded.rs:2 and milhouse tree.rs:4 import ethereum_hashing::hash32_concat/hash_fixed
impact: Already in place: tree hashing in tree_hash and milhouse goes through ethereum_hashing, which dispatches to SHA-NI at runtime.

title: Benchmark mimalloc or tcmalloc as global allocator
idea: Allow selecting an alternative global allocator (mimalloc, tcmalloc) and benchmark it against jemalloc on state transition runtime and RSS. Check whether Lighthouse has a build feature for mimalloc and what the benchmarks showed.
measured_best: mimalloc 13,120 ms vs jemalloc 22,559 ms vs glibc 17,471 ms, but RSS 45.4 MiB vs 23.0 MiB (pr:lighthouse#10046)
evidence: common/malloc_utils/Cargo.toml:14-26 only jemalloc and sysmalloc features
Cargo.lock has no mimalloc crate; grep for mimalloc/tcmalloc across the tree finds nothing
lighthouse/Cargo.toml:80 malloc_utils with jemalloc
gap: Add a mimalloc feature to malloc_utils (GlobalAlloc in lib.rs) and benchmark. The measured result (state transition 13.1 s vs 22.6 s jemalloc) is attractive but RSS doubles (45 vs 23 MiB), and the PRs were not adopted.
impact: Possibly ~40% faster state-transition-heavy workloads but about 2x RSS; unclear net win on a mainnet node, and jemalloc stats/profiling metrics would be lost.

title: Async random bytes in peer discovery
idea: Generate random bytes for peer discovery with a non-blocking API so waiting for entropy cannot block the event loop or async executor. Check whether Lighthouse's discovery code calls a blocking OS random source on an async worker thread.
evidence: discv5-0.12.0/src/rpc.rs:33 rand::random uses non-blocking thread RNG
discovery/mod.rs:850 NodeId::random()
impact: None.

title: Avoid big-integer construction from literal zero
idea: In hot paths, construct zero big integers with the zero-value constructor instead of parsing or converting a literal, avoiding a needless allocation and initialization. Check Lighthouse hot paths that build U256/BigUint zeros through conversions.
evidence: grep U256::from(0)/BigUint::from(0): no hits
impact: None.

title: Zero-copy byte views instead of buffer copies
idea: In gossip encoding, req/resp, pubkey cache, shuffling, randao xor and database keys, use views over the existing bytes instead of copying into new buffers, and do byte operations in place. Check Lighthouse for to_vec/clone of byte buffers in these paths where a slice would do.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1338-1435 key.as_slice().to_vec() for DB keys
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:179-198 to_vec of state lists
gap: Most paths use slices; DB key construction and hdiff buffers still allocate Vec copies; could take &[u8] keys or reuse buffers in store ops.
impact: Small allocation savings on store writes; likely under 1% of CPU.

title: Low-allocation hex encoding of roots and pubkeys
idea: Convert 32-byte roots and 48-byte pubkeys to hex with a specialised helper that writes into a reusable buffer or lookup table instead of string concatenation or per-call allocation, and use it everywhere roots are stringified (gossip, fork choice, cache keys). Check whether Lighthouse formats roots to hex strings on hot paths, for example as map keys or in logs that are always evaluated.
measured_best: toRootHex 156 ns to 105 ns; GC time ~2.9% to <2.3% (pr:lodestar#7060, pr:lodestar#7036)
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/topics.rs:374 hex::encode only for fork digest topic names
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1313 hex only in a log path
Hot-path maps key on Hash256 (fixed bytes), not strings
gap: Lighthouse keys caches and fork choice on Hash256/PublicKeyBytes byte arrays and formats hex only at logging/API edges (tracing fields are lazy), so there is no hot-path stringification to optimise.
impact: Little to gain; hex formatting is off the hot path.

title: Move large beacon values instead of deep copying
idea: Avoid generic deep-copy assignment of large beacon types (states, blocks) and pass them by move or reference, including inside the async runtime. Check Lighthouse for clone() of BeaconState or large containers where ownership could be moved.
measured_best: genericAssign 40.65% of CPU during sync, gone after (pr:nimbus#1166)
evidence: Rust moves by default; hdiff.rs:185 uses take_validators/mem::take
impact: None beyond audits.

title: Remove event listeners when their task ends
idea: Unregister per-slot event listeners and signal handlers when the task that added them finishes, so closures and captured data are not retained and do not accumulate. Check Lighthouse for event subscriptions or broadcast receivers that are added per slot or per request and never dropped.
measured_best: heap graph before/after, no numbers (pr:lodestar#1560)
evidence: beacon_chain/src/events.rs:222-290 broadcast subscribe
http_api/src/lib.rs:3511 receiver owned by SSE stream
impact: None.

title: Avoid per-call closure allocation on hot paths
idea: Do not allocate a closure per timer or per response chunk; pass arguments directly or reuse one pre-bound handler, which also avoids capturing large objects that delay freeing. Check Lighthouse network handlers for boxed closures or futures created per chunk.
evidence: No per-chunk boxed closure pattern found in lighthouse_network rpc
impact: None.

title: Iterate large structs by reference, precompile regexes
idea: Iterate collections of large structs by index or reference instead of copying each element by value, and compile static regexes once at module scope. Check Lighthouse hot loops for by-value iteration with clones and for Regex::new inside functions.
evidence: consensus/types/src/core/graffiti.rs:19 Regex::new per as_utf8_lossy call
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/methods.rs:60 Regex::new per ErrorType Display
common/account_utils/src/validator_definitions.rs:522,531 Regex::new per file name
gap: Static regexes are compiled inside functions on each call; move to LazyLock/OnceLock statics in Graffiti::as_utf8_lossy, ErrorType::fmt, and the keystore name check (or replace with char filtering).
impact: Saves microseconds per call; only matters on API/log paths with graffiti and RPC errors.

title: Keep small hash buffers on the stack
idea: Write hot helpers so small buffers (32-byte hashes, cache keys) do not escape to the heap: slice the addressable value directly and use real inlinable functions instead of function-pointer variables. Check Lighthouse for Vec allocations of fixed small size where a stack array would do.
measured_best: isCode 33.7 -> 24.8 ns/op, 1 alloc -> 0 (pr:caplin#22741)
evidence: Cargo.lock:3810 ethereum_hashing 0.8.0 hash_fixed returns [u8;32] by value (lib.rs:31)
impact: Rust has no escape-analysis heap/stack issue; hash helpers already return arrays by value. Nothing to gain.

title: Zeroed buffer for wasm snappy decompression output
idea: When decompressing snappy into an output buffer, allocate a fresh zeroed buffer instead of an uninitialised pooled one that caused heavy mark-sweep GC. Check how Lighthouse allocates snappy decompression output buffers.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:115-124 decompress_len bound then decompress_vec into a fresh exact-size Vec
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/codec.rs:187-190,283-285,319-320 RPC path: FrameDecoder read_exact into fresh vec![0; length]
impact: None left: both gossip and RPC decode into fresh, bounded, zeroed buffers; there is no GC so the original problem (pooled uninitialised wasm buffer causing mark-sweep) cannot arise.

title: Enlarge young generation for network worker heap
idea: Size the young generation of the network thread's heap so short-lived message objects die there without repeated scavenge copying. For Lighthouse the analogue is per-thread allocator caches (tcache) sized for the network threads.
measured_best: scavenge >200 MB and 3% of worker time before (pr:lodestar#5829)
evidence: .cargo/config.toml:2 JEMALLOC malloc conf narenas:16
common/malloc_utils/src/jemalloc.rs:1-10 conf overridable via _RJEM_MALLOC_CONF
gap: jemalloc tcache is on by default with default sizing; Lighthouse only sets narenas:16 and does not tune tcache max/size for network threads. A tcache or dirty_decay_ms setting could be added to the malloc conf string in .cargo/config.toml, only after profiling.
impact: Possibly slightly fewer arena lock hits for network threads; no measured gain, marginal.

title: Bound chunks per native hashing call
idea: Split very large hashing layers into bounded batches per call into the native SHA256 routine so one call does not run long without a yield point. Check whether Lighthouse hashes whole large layers in one blocking call on an async worker thread.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1657-1719 work runs via spawn_blocking
~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/tree_hash-0.12.1/src/merkle_hasher.rs:200 MerkleHasher streams leaves
impact: Hashing runs on blocking threads, not async workers, so no yield point is needed; native sha256 is in-process Rust, not a cgo-like call.

title: Cheap overflow-checked u64 multiplication
idea: Implement checked u64 multiplication with a cheap overflow test instead of widening to big integers. Check Lighthouse safe_arith and reward calculations for u128 or bigint multiplication where checked_mul would do.
measured_best: 30% faster with 32-bit operands, 8x faster when one is longer than 32 bits (pr:teku#3376)
evidence: Cargo.lock:8807 safe_arith 0.1.0
~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/safe_arith-0.1.0/src/lib.rs:150-151 safe_mul uses checked_mul
impact: Already uses native checked_mul; no bigint widening.

title: Clear references before returning objects to pool
idea: Before putting an object back into an object pool, clear every field that holds pointers or buffers so idle pooled objects do not pin block-sized memory. Check any Lighthouse object or buffer pools for retained large capacity after reuse.
evidence: milhouse 0.9.0 (Cargo.lock:6570) has no node pool; grep for object pools in beacon_node found none for blocks/buffers
impact: Lighthouse allocates per message via jemalloc and frees on drop; no object pools that could pin memory.

title: Complete futures on publisher thread
idea: Complete returned futures on a thread owned by the publisher, not the subscriber thread, so chained continuations do not block the subscriber from its next event. Check Lighthouse channels where a receiver runs heavy continuation work inline on the event loop.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1657-1719 heavy work offloaded to blocking tasks
impact: No future-completion-on-subscriber-thread pattern; Tokio wakers schedule continuations on the executor and heavy work goes to the beacon processor.

title: Configurable size of native state node pool
idea: Let operators size the preallocated tree-node pool used for state representation, so small nodes (bootnodes) do not reserve hundreds of MB. Check whether Lighthouse preallocates any fixed-size pool or arena for tree-states and whether it is configurable.
measured_best: 454 MiB vs 837 MiB for a bootnode (pr:lodestar#10226)
evidence: Cargo.lock:6570 milhouse 0.9.0; .cargo/config.toml:2 jemalloc
impact: Tree-states use Arc nodes allocated on demand from jemalloc; there is no preallocated node pool to size.

title: Hold hot constants in native integer type
idea: Store hot spec constants (min deposit, max effective balance, ejection balance) in the native integer type used by arithmetic, so each use does not convert or allocate. Check Lighthouse state processing for repeated conversions of ChainSpec values inside loops.

title: Size runtime threads from container CPU quota
idea: Set worker thread counts from the container cgroup CPU quota instead of host core count, avoiding throttling and oversubscription in containers. Check whether Lighthouse sizes tokio and rayon pools from num_cpus or from available_parallelism with cgroup awareness.

title: Serialize arena-backed proving on one thread
idea: When a prover uses a per-thread arena whose slabs are never released, run all proofs on one long-lived thread or behind a one-at-a-time permit, so only one proof-peak slab is pinned. Check whether Lighthouse runs any arena-allocating crypto job on arbitrary pool threads.
measured_best: OOM about every 40 min (~29 GB RSS) fixed; slab count stays 10 vs 10 to 14 before (pr:ethlambda#641)

Cargo.lock kzg stack: c-kzg, rust_eth_kzg, blst; no proving arena is used
gap: Lighthouse does not run a prover with a per-thread arena that never releases slabs; KZG/blob verification and cell recovery allocate through the global jemalloc.
impact: None.

title: Bump native state-transition library
idea: Upgrade the native state-transition dependency to a release that includes performance work. Check Lighthouse dependency versions for performance-relevant crates (tree hashing, BLS, ssz) behind upstream.
evidence: Cargo.toml:295-303 [patch.crates-io] milhouse, ethereum_ssz, tree_hash, ssz_types pinned to recent sigp git revs
Cargo.lock: milhouse 0.9.0, tree_hash 0.12.1, ethereum_ssz 0.10.4 (git), ethereum_hashing 0.8.0, blst 0.3.17, c-kzg 2.1.8, rust_eth_kzg 0.9.1
impact: Generic dependency-bump idea; the perf crates track sigp heads via git patches, no specific stale release found offline.

title: Use jemalloc as default global allocator
idea: Make jemalloc the default allocator of the node (with in-process arena configuration and an opt-out), since the system allocator fragments and inflates RSS with large long-lived state allocations. Check Lighthouse's global allocator selection and its platform defaults.

common/malloc_utils/Cargo.toml:37-38 background_threads on Linux
impact: Already default with arena tuning, background threads, metrics and opt-out.

title: Jemalloc heap profiling over HTTP endpoint
idea: Expose jemalloc heap profiling through an HTTP debug endpoint so memory growth can be diagnosed on running nodes. Check whether Lighthouse can dump jemalloc heap profiles at runtime.

~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/tikv-jemalloc-sys-0.6.1+5.3.0-1-ge13ca993e8ccb9ba9847cc330696e02839f328f7/jemalloc/src/ctl.c:140-145,194 prof options exist in the bundled jemalloc

idea: Configure jemalloc with background purge threads and shorter dirty/muzzy decay times so freed pages return to the OS and RSS stays lower. Check Lighthouse's jemalloc config string for background_thread and decay settings.

~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/tikv-jemalloc-sys-0.6.1+5.3.0-1-ge13ca993e8ccb9ba9847cc330696e02839f328f7/build.rs:457 always_enabled = CARGO_FEATURE_BACKGROUND_THREADS; :221-228 adds background_thread:true; :236-244 appends JEMALLOC_SYS_WITH_MALLOC_CONF

~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/tikv-jemalloc-sys-0.6.1+5.3.0-1-ge13ca993e8ccb9ba9847cc330696e02839f328f7/jemalloc/include/jemalloc/internal/arena_types.h:7-8 defaults dirty_decay_ms 10000, muzzy_decay_ms 0

refute_note: The earlier review misread build.rs: always_enabled comes from CARGO_FEATURE_BACKGROUND_THREADS, which malloc_utils turns on for Linux, so background_thread:true is compiled in. I also checked the jemalloc 5.3 decay defaults and the reproducible override path.

title: Drop memory wiping and copies in hash path
idea: Remove secure memory wiping and extra copies around digest computation in hashing of public data. Check whether Lighthouse's sha256 wrapper zeroizes contexts or copies inputs for non-secret hashing.
evidence: ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/ethereum_hashing-0.8.0/src/lib.rs:24-40 hash/hash_fixed/hash32_concat thin wrappers

title: Expose native memory as external GC buffers
idea: Hand native memory to the managed runtime as external buffers with a size-reporting finalizer, so the garbage collector does not scan backing memory. Not directly applicable to Lighthouse; check only if Lighthouse exposes memory to a GC'd embedder.

impact: Lighthouse is native Rust with no garbage-collected embedder, so external-buffer handoff does not exist.

title: Faster HTTP stream implementation for beacon API
idea: Use a faster stream implementation in the HTTP server stack to raise beacon API throughput. Check Lighthouse's HTTP API server (warp/axum/hyper) for throughput limits versus a newer stack.
measured_best: almost 2x http performance (pr:nimbus#8394)
evidence: Cargo.toml:114 axum 0.8, :172 hyper 1, :276 warp 0.4 (migration to axum in progress, :304)
impact: The idea is replacing Nim chronos' stream type; Lighthouse already runs on hyper/axum, and the beacon API is not a throughput bottleneck.

title: Fewer allocations per async future
idea: Reduce allocations per async future or task, make waiting on already-finished futures cheap, and cancel many futures in one call. Check Lighthouse hot paths that box futures or spawn a task per small item.
evidence: Cargo.toml:250 tokio multi-thread runtime; beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs uses queued work events, not a task per item
impact: The idea targets Nim async future overhead; Rust futures are stack-state machines with no per-future heap allocation unless boxed, and the beacon processor batches work into queues.

title: Fine-grained locking around beacon state
idea: Replace a coarse lock around beacon state with fine-grained locks so readers and writers in different services contend less. Check Lighthouse for a single RwLock guarding head state or caches that many services take.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:455-468 separate RwLocks for fork_choice and cached_head plus recompute_head_lock

idea: Update the backtrace/stack collection library to fix a memory leak. Check whether Lighthouse captures backtraces on hot paths (errors, panics hooks) and whether that leaks.

lighthouse/src/main.rs:96-102 - RUST_BACKTRACE=1 set at startup
impact: Backtraces are captured only on panic, never on hot paths; the leak was in a Nim library.

title: Destroy thread-pool task objects after run
idea: Make sure task objects in the thread pool used for signature verification are freed after running, to avoid a per-task leak. Check Lighthouse's signature verification job dispatch for retained task state.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1657-1676 - signature work runs as spawn_blocking closures, owned and dropped after run
impact: Rust closures are dropped after execution; no manual task-object destruction exists to forget.

title: Avoid nested thread pool oversubscription
idea: Avoid running several parallel runtimes at once (for example rayon inside state transition plus a solver's own threads), which oversubscribes CPUs; use one pool or plain threads. Check Lighthouse for rayon work nested inside tokio blocking tasks or other pools.
evidence: common/task_executor/src/rayon_pool_provider.rs:24-41 - two extra rayon pools (25% and 80% of CPUs) plus the global rayon pool
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/kzg_utils.rs:344-477 - par_iter on global pool from blocking tasks
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1657 - spawn_blocking worker threads
gap: Pools are sized separately (80%+25% of CPUs, plus the global pool and tokio blocking threads), so total runnable threads can exceed core count when several are busy. A single shared budget or sizing the pools to sum to num_cpus would remove it.
impact: Small reduction in context switching during KZG/column work bursts; measured effect unknown, likely marginal.

title: Release large init-time temporaries after startup
idea: Drop large temporaries created during node initialization so they are not referenced for the process lifetime, and reuse a single validator pool instance. Check Lighthouse startup (genesis/checkpoint load, builder) for large values kept in long-lived structs.
evidence: lh-perf-research-base/beacon_node/client/src/builder.rs:343,386 genesis_state is local and moved into the chain builder
beacon_node/client/src/builder.rs:388-420 the WeakSubjSszBytes anchor bytes are decoded into locals and dropped after the builder call
beacon_node/client/src/lib.rs:21-28 Client keeps only the chain Arc, network globals and listen addresses, not the config
common/eth2_network_config/src/lib.rs:50-53,86 genesis_state_bytes is a &'static slice for hardcoded nets
beacon_node/src/lib.rs:52,125 client_config.genesis is cloned twice during startup (a temporary startup peak, dropped when building finishes)
impact: No large init-time temporaries are kept for the process lifetime. Only a temporary startup peak remains, from cloning the checkpoint bytes.

title: Pool gossip decompression buffers per topic
idea: Keep a per-topic pool of reusable output buffers for decompressing inbound gossip on the network thread, instead of allocating a new buffer per message. Check Lighthouse's gossipsub snappy transform for per-message Vec allocation.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:122-123 - new Decoder and decompress_vec allocate a fresh Vec per inbound message
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:129 - the Vec becomes Message.data and is owned downstream
gap: In SnappyTransform::inbound_transform, the decompressed Vec is moved into the Message and kept by gossipsub and the beacon processor, so a pool would need buffer return on drop. Gain is limited to malloc cost for blocks/blobs/attestations; a thread-local reusable Decoder would save only the small decoder setup.
impact: Saves one allocation per gossip message (the exact-size Vec); glibc/jemalloc handles this well, so gain is small.

title: Reuse SHA-256 hasher without per-call allocation
idea: Hash with one-shot functions on stack buffers or a pooled reusable hasher instead of allocating a hasher object per call in tree hashing. Check whether Lighthouse's hash32_concat and tree-hash paths allocate a Vec or hasher per hash.
measured_best: Sha256(32B,32B) 78.2 -> 52.1 ns, 2 allocs -> 0 (pr:caplin#22489); pooled 77.30 -> 47.65 ns/op (pr:prysm#15427)
evidence: ~/.cargo/registry/src/*/ethereum_hashing-0.8.0/src/lib.rs:36-41 hash32_concat uses a stack DynamicContext and returns [u8;32]
ethereum_hashing-0.8.0/src/lib.rs:31-33 hash_fixed returns an array
~/.cargo/git/checkouts/milhouse-*/d67aabd/src/tree.rs:544 milhouse internal nodes use hash32_concat
~/.cargo/git/checkouts/tree_hash-*/e5ea187/tree_hash/src/merkle_hasher.rs:141-151,200-203 MerkleHasher uses SmallVec buffers, one per merkleization, not per hash
tree_hash merkleize_padded.rs:82-139 uses hash_fixed and hash32_concat
impact: Already allocation-free per hash on the milhouse and tree_hash hot paths.

title: Lazy split iterators instead of split slices
idea: Use lazy split iterators instead of functions that build an intermediate slice of substrings in loops. Check Lighthouse parsing paths that collect split() results into Vec only to iterate.
evidence: beacon_node, common, lighthouse, boot_node - grep for split(...).collect::<Vec found no non-test hits
impact: Rust split is already lazy and no hot-path code collects split results only to iterate.

title: Cap network library direct buffer memory
idea: Set an explicit cap on the network library's off-heap buffer memory because the default bound is effectively far larger than needed. Check Lighthouse libp2p/yamux buffer and window limits for oversized defaults.
measured_best: default effectively allocates 256MB; capped at 32MB (pr:teku#2424)
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/utils.rs:44 - yamux::Config::default() with no limits set
yamux-0.14.1/src/lib.rs:89-90 - defaults: connection receive window 1 GiB, 512 streams
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/utils.rs:50-51 - mplex does get max streams 32 and ResetStream
gap: Yamux is left at defaults (1 GiB per-connection receive window, 512 streams) while mplex has explicit caps. Buffers only grow if the peer sends data without being read, but a malicious peer could hold up to 1 GiB per connection. Call set_max_connection_receive_window(Some(..)) and set_max_num_streams in the yamux config.
impact: Bounds worst-case per-connection memory; no change for honest peers, so a robustness gain rather than a speed gain.

title: Linked-list or deque FIFO job queues
idea: Back FIFO job queues with a structure that pops from the front in O(1) instead of an array whose shift is O(n). Check Lighthouse beacon processor queues for Vec::remove(0) style front removal.
measured_best: array shift 3.6us/op vs list 14ns/op at 16000 items; shift up to 17% CPU (pr:lodestar#3738)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_queue.rs:31-60 FifoQueue on VecDeque push_back/pop_front
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_queue.rs:77-88,237-246 PeerWork and LifoQueue also VecDeque
impact: Beacon processor queues are O(1) at the front.

title: Bounded queue with internal locking for throttling
idea: Implement the throttling task queue as one bounded channel that carries the limit itself, instead of an unbounded queue guarded by external locks, to cut contention between producers and workers. Check Lighthouse's beacon processor work queues for external Mutex around queue plus counter.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:148-149 bounded mpsc::channel(max_work_event_queue_len)
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_queue.rs:31-60 per-type bounded FifoQueue owned by the single manager task, no lock
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:170-182 only Mutex is the DuplicateCache HashSet
impact: Producer/worker handoff is a bounded channel with the limit inside; queues are single-owner so no external lock contention.

title: Set heap limit near real usage to fail fast
idea: Set the runtime heap limit close to real usage so a memory bug crashes with OOM instead of causing long GC stalls. For Lighthouse the analogue is a memory limit or watchdog that fails fast instead of swapping.
measured_best: old space 1.5-2GB; limit 6000 to 4096 MB (pr:lodestar#3516)
evidence: common/malloc_utils/src/lib.rs:1-20 allocator is jemalloc/glibc, no managed heap
impact: No GC heap in Rust; a leak is bounded by the OS/cgroup OOM killer already.

title: Raise runtime heap limit for memory spikes
idea: Raise the default runtime heap ceiling so non-finality or DoS memory spikes do not crash the node or thrash the GC. Not directly applicable to Lighthouse, which has no managed heap limit.
evidence: common/malloc_utils/src/lib.rs:1-20 native allocator, no heap ceiling
impact: No V8-style heap ceiling exists in Lighthouse.

title: Reduce stack usage of light-client data store
idea: Change how large objects are passed or held in the light-client data store so they do not sit on the stack. Check Lighthouse light-client server code for large values passed by value through deep call chains.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_finality_update_verification.rs light client path; Rust stack-use concern is Nim-specific
impact: Nim stack/GC-specific; light client server objects are small and Arc/moved in Rust.

title: Allocate startup block summaries outside GC heap
idea: Allocate the large startup table of block summaries with manual allocation outside the managed heap to lower memory. Check how Lighthouse holds block summary tables built at startup (fork choice, block roots).
evidence: common/malloc_utils/src/lib.rs:1-20 no managed GC heap; tables live in native allocator already
impact: Nothing to move out of a GC heap; Rust has none.

title: Upgrade network library adaptive buffer allocator
idea: Upgrade the networking library to a version whose adaptive byte buffer allocator has much lower memory overhead. Check Lighthouse libp2p buffer allocation strategy and version.
measured_best: decrease memory overhead dramatically, upstream claim (pr:teku#9669)
evidence: Cargo.lock:5779-5780 libp2p 0.57.0 (Rust, no Netty-style adaptive pooled allocator)
impact: Netty-specific; rust-libp2p uses per-read buffers, no adaptive allocator to upgrade.

title: Newer runtime GC with soft heap target
idea: Run on a newer VM with a better garbage collector and a soft max heap target that can be exceeded when necessary. Not directly applicable to Lighthouse; the analogue is a soft memory target in the allocator.
measured_best: lower memory usage without risk of high GC costs (pr:teku#2382)
evidence: common/malloc_utils/src/lib.rs:1-20 jemalloc feature or glibc, selectable
common/malloc_utils/src/glibc.rs glibc arena/trim tuning
gap: Lighthouse tunes jemalloc/glibc (arena count, trim) but has no soft memory target that scales decay with usage; would need a periodic task in malloc_utils reading RSS and adjusting purge/trim.
impact: Marginal RSS reduction on some nodes; no GC cost to avoid.

title: Park idle worker threads instead of spinning
idea: Park idle worker threads until a wake signal or short timeout instead of busy-spinning when no work is queued. Check Lighthouse worker loops and any custom pools for spin or tight polling.
evidence: beacon_node/timer/src/lib.rs:24 sleep-based loop
grep spin_loop/park_timeout/thread::spawn in beacon_node, common: none
work_reprocessing_queue.rs yield_now only in tests
impact: No busy-spin loops exist; tokio and rayon park idle workers. Nothing to gain.

title: Pin runtime version after regressions
idea: Benchmark runtime or toolchain upgrades before rollout and pin the version when a new release regresses performance. Check whether Lighthouse pins its Rust toolchain and benchmarks compiler upgrades.
measured_best: poor performance on Node 1.24.0-rc.0, no numbers (pr:lodestar#7291)
evidence: lighthouse/Cargo.toml:7 rust-version = 1.91.0 (MSRV only)
no rust-toolchain file; CI uses channel: stable (.github/workflows/test-suite.yml:121)
Makefile/Dockerfile: no pinned compiler version found
gap: Release builds follow the latest stable compiler with only an MSRV floor. Add a rust-toolchain.toml pin for release builds and a benchmark gate (e.g. state-transition bench) before bumping.
impact: Avoids silent compiler regressions; not a measurable speedup by itself.

title: Pool snappy stream readers and writers
idea: Reuse snappy stream reader/writer objects (each with ~142 KB scratch buffers) from a pool instead of creating one per response chunk or message. Check whether Lighthouse rpc codec creates a new snappy FrameEncoder/Decoder per chunk.
measured_best: 64-block BeaconBlocksByRange response burned ~8.7 MB of garbage (pr:caplin#23423)
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/codec.rs:127 and 389 FrameEncoder::new(Vec::new()) per message
codec.rs:187,281,318 FrameDecoder::new(limit_reader) per decode
codec.rs:184 decoded_buffer = vec![0; length] per message
~/.cargo/registry/src/*/snap-1.1.2/src/write.rs:83 each FrameEncoder allocates a MAX_BLOCK_SIZE (64 KiB) src Vec
gap: Replace per-message FrameEncoder/FrameDecoder in SSZSnappyInboundCodec/OutboundCodec encode/decode with a reused encoder (reset the inner Vec) or snap::raw::Encoder with a persistent buffer, as raw frames are single-chunk.
impact: Saves roughly 130-200 KiB of allocation churn per RPC chunk (e.g. 64-block ByRange response ~8 MB of garbage); small CPU gain with jemalloc, helps RSS fragmentation.

title: Preallocate collections with known capacity
idea: Give vectors and maps their known capacity up front instead of growing them by repeated reallocation. Check Lighthouse hot paths for Vec::new followed by push in loops of known length.

consensus/state_processing/src/upgrade/gloas.rs:250 Vec::new in loop

title: Precompute shuffled committees off the hot path

title: Prover on system allocator instead of bump arena
idea: Run the prover on the system allocator rather than a bump arena so resident memory does not ratchet up over the node's lifetime. Check whether Lighthouse uses bump or arena allocators whose memory is never returned.
evidence: common/malloc_utils/src/lib.rs:1 only jemalloc or glibc
grep bump/bumpalo in repo: no hits
impact: Lighthouse has no prover and no arena allocator, so memory is returned normally.

title: Scoped bump arena only for proving threads
idea: Use a bump-arena allocator only on proving threads, reset per phase, while all other threads use the system allocator. Check whether Lighthouse could use scoped arenas for short-lived heavy jobs such as epoch processing.

evidence: grep bumpalo/arena: no hits
common/malloc_utils/src/lib.rs:1 global allocator only
impact: No proving threads; epoch processing relies on milhouse sharing and the global allocator, and arenas there are not a known win.

title: Reclaim receive buffers, slab allocator for packets
idea: Clear receive buffers before trying to reclaim them so reuse succeeds instead of allocating per packet batch, use a slab-style allocator for many small allocations, and poll the socket before the p2p state machine. Check Lighthouse discv5/QUIC receive paths for per-batch buffer allocation.
evidence: ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/discv5-0.12.0/src/socket/recv.rs:124-137 two stack buffers [0; MAX_PACKET_SIZE] allocated once and reused by recv_from in the loop

impact: No per-packet buffer allocation on the discv5 receive path; discovery traffic is light, so remaining small copies do not matter.

title: Release allocator instead of debug allocator
idea: Use the production allocator for long-lived state views in release builds instead of a debug allocator with tracking overhead. Check Lighthouse release profiles for debug or tracking allocators enabled.

common/malloc_utils/src/lib.rs:1 jemalloc on unix, glibc otherwise
impact: Rust release builds have no tracking debug allocator; jemalloc-profiling is opt-in only.

title: Avoid reference cycles that leak memory
idea: Remove annotations or patterns that make cyclic references uncollectable, which leaked memory. Check Lighthouse for Arc cycles in caches or service handles that are never broken.

Services hold Arc<BeaconChain>; no cycle seen but none guarded
gap: No leak found; an audit of chain-owned tasks holding Arc<BeaconChain> (spawn_timer, graffiti_calculator) would be needed, using Weak where a cycle exists.

title: Remove needless iterator-to-vector collections
idea: Do not convert iterators or views into owned vectors in hot paths and REST/sync code when they are only iterated. Check Lighthouse for collect::<Vec<_>>() followed by a single iteration.
measured_best: every one is an unnecessary copy/allocation (pr:nimbus#8551)

beacon_node/http_api/src/validators.rs:72,120,168 collect into response Vec (needed, serialized)
gap: Most of the ~210 collect::<Vec> sites are required (borrow release, response bodies, ownership). A few only inspect first/len/is_empty, e.g. naive_aggregation_pool set_bits (use iter().next() plus a count) and builder_deposits_cache::seed_from_state. Needs a per-site audit; no systematic hot-path offender found.
impact: Negligible on a mainnet node; these are small, non-hot allocations (aggregation pool insert is per-attestation but the Vec is tiny).

title: Shared constant zero hash instead of temporaries
idea: Pass a shared constant zero hash to calls instead of constructing and zero-filling a 32-byte temporary at each call site in hot paths. Check Lighthouse tree hashing for Hash256::zero() built in loops instead of a static.
measured_best: saves a 32-byte zero fill per call, no timing (pr:nimbus#3770)
evidence: ~/.cargo/git/checkouts/tree_hash-*/e5ea187/tree_hash/src/merkleize_padded.rs:125,284 get_zero_hash returns a reference into static ZERO_HASHES

ethereum_hashing-0.8.0/src/lib.rs zero_hash_cache LazyLock ZERO_HASHES
impact: Zero hashes are shared statics or consts; in Rust, a const Hash256::ZERO costs nothing extra.

title: Reuse and stop timers in loops
idea: In loops and debounce helpers, keep one reusable timer or ticker and stop or reset it, instead of creating a new timer per iteration or event that lives until it fires. Check Lighthouse loops for tokio::time::sleep created per iteration inside select! where an Interval would do.
measured_best: time.After channel is not freed until the event fires (pr:prysm#7175)
evidence: beacon_node/timer/src/lib.rs:24 one sleep per slot, awaited and dropped
beacon_node/network/src/service.rs:935 next_unsubscribe Sleep stored and reset, not recreated per select iteration
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:1441 backfill event Sleep stored in a field
impact: tokio Sleep is freed on drop, so the Go time.After leak cannot happen; the remaining per-slot sleeps run once per slot.

title: Async runtime tracing of task scheduling
idea: Integrate a tracing facility for the async runtime that captures scheduling and task-poll events, so executor stalls and hot tasks can be found. Check whether Lighthouse can record tokio task poll times in production.
evidence: lighthouse/Cargo.toml:37 optional console-subscriber feature

impact: Lets operators find executor stalls and hot tasks on live nodes; diagnostic only, no direct speedup.
refute_note: Grepped the workspace for RuntimeMetrics, tokio-metrics, task poll hooks, thread park hooks and tokio_unstable; only console-subscriber exists. OTLP tracing and beacon_processor worker-time histograms give per-work timing, not per-poll scheduling data.

title: Shared memory messaging between worker threads
idea: Pass messages between worker and main thread through shared memory with atomics instead of copying them. Check Lighthouse cross-thread channels that clone or serialize large payloads instead of sharing an Arc.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:143 tokio mpsc channels in one address space
impact: None: Rust threads share memory; payloads move by ownership or Arc, no structured clone.

title: Skip expensive direct buffer cleaning
idea: Configure the pooled network buffer runtime to skip its costly buffer cleaner path for stability after OOMs. Relevant to Lighthouse only if it uses a comparable pooled-buffer runtime.
evidence: Cargo.toml:177 libp2p with tokio TCP/QUIC, no pooled direct-buffer runtime
impact: None: no Netty-style buffer cleaner exists.

title: Schedule job runs only below max concurrency
idea: When pushing to a job queue, schedule a run only if running jobs are below max concurrency, since running jobs pull the next item themselves. Check Lighthouse beacon processor for redundant wakeups or spawns per enqueued item.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:890 can_spawn = current_workers < max_workers
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1193 spawn_worker only on a dequeued event or when a queue pop yields work
impact: Already done: a single manager loop owns the queues and spawns a worker only when under max_workers; no per-item wakeup.

title: Native slice-to-array conversion for byte copies
idea: Convert byte slices to fixed 32-byte arrays with the native slice-to-array conversion instead of allocate-plus-copy loops in hot helpers. Check Lighthouse for Hash256::from_slice patterns that go through intermediate Vec.
measured_best: BenchmarkToBytes32 0.4843 -> 0.2438 ns/op (pr:prysm#11838)
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/config.rs:479 extend_from_slice used for message id, not a Vec to array path
impact: None: Rust Hash256::from_slice is a direct copy; the Go allocate-plus-copy loop does not exist.

title: Configurable executor thread counts and queue sizes
idea: Make async worker thread counts and queue sizes configurable so large hosts can tune parallelism. Check whether Lighthouse exposes tokio worker count and beacon processor queue lengths as flags.
evidence: beacon_node/src/cli.rs:1618 --beacon-processor-max-workers
beacon_node/src/cli.rs:1630 --beacon-processor-work-queue-len
lighthouse/environment/src/lib.rs:172 RuntimeBuilder::new_multi_thread() with defaults, no worker or blocking thread flag
gap: Processor workers and queue lengths are flags, but tokio worker_threads and max_blocking_threads are not; only tokio's TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS env var works. Add flags in EnvironmentBuilder::multi_threaded_tokio_runtime.
impact: Lets hosts with many cores or containers cap or raise tokio threads; benefit is tuning, not a default speed-up.

title: Allocate buffers uninitialized when immediately overwritten
idea: Allocate sequences without zero-initialization when they are overwritten right away, such as network and era file read buffers and fork choice tracker arrays. Check Lighthouse for vec![0u8; n] buffers that are fully overwritten by a read.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/codec.rs:188 vec![0; length] then read_exact (also 283, 319)
gap: Snappy decode buffers are zero-filled then fully overwritten. Could use Vec::with_capacity plus take().read_to_end, avoiding the memset in rpc/codec.rs decode paths.
impact: Saves one memset per RPC message decode (up to a few MB for blocks/columns); marginal next to snappy decode cost.

title: Green threads for event-channel consumers
idea: Run each event-channel consumer on a lightweight task instead of a dedicated OS thread, so many subscriber channels do not each hold a thread stack. Check Lighthouse for std::thread::spawn per service or channel consumer that could be an async task.
measured_best: ~70 fewer platform threads x ~1MB stack = ~70MB less committed memory (pr:teku#10426)
evidence: validator_client/builder_store/src/lib.rs:365 only std::thread::spawn outside tests
grep of std::thread::spawn/Builder across repo: no per-channel consumer threads in beacon node
impact: Lighthouse consumers are tokio tasks already; no thread-per-subscriber.

title: Write small messages directly when queue empty
idea: Write small outgoing messages such as attestations directly to the socket when the write queue is empty, bypassing the queue. Check Lighthouse's libp2p send path for queueing overhead on small gossip messages.
evidence: ~/.cargo/git/checkouts/rust-libp2p-b7fa834aec8fc27c/accba72/protocols/gossipsub/src/queue.rs:63 try_push always enqueues to priority/non_priority queues
gossipsub handler.rs polls queue then Sink::start_send
gap: Gossipsub in the sigp libp2p fork always goes through the per-peer queue, then the handler; a bypass would need to be in the fork's behaviour send path. The queue is a cheap in-memory push.
impact: Would save at most one task wakeup per small message; the socket write still goes via yamux and the handler, so gain is tiny.

title: Do not yield while holding state references
idea: Avoid suspending (await/yield) inside state transition while holding references to states, because the suspended scope keeps them alive; yield in the caller after they are dropped. Check Lighthouse async functions that hold BeaconState values across await points.
measured_best: memory 4GB after 1h down to 1.1-1.8GB (pr:lodestar#2011)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:121 awaits are sleeps, no state held
impact: Rust drops values deterministically; no GC-style retention of suspended scopes, so no memory gain.

idea: Resolve attesting indices in gossip verification, the op pool, fork choice vote updates and duties from a per-epoch committee/shuffling cache instead of recomputing the shuffling from a BeaconState per attestation. The shuffling is fixed for the epoch, so one computation serves every attestation.
measured_best: 95% reduction in attestation processing time (best case) (pr:lighthouse#841)
evidence: lh-perf-research-base/beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:1547-1560 obtain_indexed_attestation_and_committees_per_slot

title: Shuffling cache keyed by epoch and dependent root

Compute each shuffling once (at epoch transition or slot tick, deduplicating concurrent computations) so attestation committees come from the cache without recomputing the shuffling or needing a full state.

title: Same-message signature check for equal-data attestations
idea: Group unaggregated gossip attestations by (slot, attestation data root), aggregate the pubkeys and signatures of each group and do one signature check per group, falling back to per-attestation verification on failure. Verification cost scales with distinct data, not message count.
measured_best: 128 sigs: 130.5 ms vs 8.97 ms; CPU 140-160% vs >=300% (pr:lodestar#5729)

title: Serve duty queries from epoch caches, not loaded states

title: Compute duties for all validators in one committee pass
idea: When a duties request names many validators, iterate the target epoch's committees once while looking up members in a validator-index set or map, instead of searching the committees separately for each validator. This turns O(validators x committees) work into a single pass.

title: Bounded per-subscriber SSE queues, drop slow clients

title: Bound state regeneration for far-out API requests
idea: Reject API requests that would force regenerating or advancing a state through arbitrarily many slots: future slots beyond the clock, sync duties beyond the next period, or replays of empty slots beyond a cap, returning 404/400/503. This stops a single request from starving block import.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:964-998 state_root_at_slot returns None for slot > clock and the head state root for slots past head (no forward replay)

beacon_node/http_api/src/lib.rs:474-511 not_while_syncing_filter
impact: No API state path replays empty slots forward without bound; the Lodestar wedge (regen from head to a near-clock slot) cannot happen because Lighthouse serves the head state for slots past head.
refute_note: Earlier review missed not_while_syncing_filter: the validator endpoints that would call state_at_slot with a lagging head return 503 once the head is more than 2 epochs behind the clock while syncing, which is the empty-slot replay cap the idea asks for, enforced at the API layer.

title: Separate small committee cache for HTTP committees route

title: Promise cache deduplicating concurrent state requests
idea: Put a promise cache in front of HTTP state loading so concurrent requests for the same state root share one computation, with a concurrency cap, instead of each request loading or replaying the state.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/state_id.rs:196-197 StateId::state calls chain.get_state directly, no in-flight sharing
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1817-1826 get_hot_state checks state_cache then releases the lock and loads from disk, so concurrent misses each load
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2310-2322 load_cold_state_by_slot drops historic_state_cache lock before hdiff load/replay, no promise
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:106,287-301 Promise + MAX_CONCURRENT_PROMISES only for attester shufflings
beacon_node/http_api/src/task_spawner.rs:22-23 HTTP work goes through beacon_processor ApiRequestP0/P1 queues, which caps concurrency by worker count but does not dedup

impact: Bursts of parallel requests for the same non-cached state (indexers, explorers) do one reconstruction instead of N; no effect on pure validator nodes.
refute_note: Checked the store layer (hot state_cache and historic_state_cache lock scopes) for implicit dedup through lock holding: locks are dropped before the expensive load. The beacon processor worker pool is the only concurrency cap; there is no PromiseCache or equivalent anywhere.

idea: When blobs or columns for a block are missing, query the local EL first and send RPC requests to peers only for the ones still missing. Share one received-sidecar set between the EL and the p2p fetch paths so no sidecar is fetched twice.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:970-991 custody_lookup_request filters sampling columns by cached_data_column_indexes (gossip and EL-imported columns are skipped)
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:209-222 lookup block with MissingComponents triggers fetch_engine_blobs_and_publish_full
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:398-433 data request starts as soon as the block is downloaded, not after the EL fetch settles
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1370 partial-column cell requests wait for local_fetch_settled
gap: The subtraction the earlier review asked for already exists: lookups skip columns already in the DA cache, and RPC lookup blocks trigger getBlobs. What is missing is ordering and in-flight sharing: the lookup custody request starts on block download, in parallel with (and before) the EL fetch that runs only after block processing, and ActiveCustodyRequest does not re-check the DA cache to drop columns the EL fills while requests are in flight. Fix: for recent blocks, run getBlobs first (or gate custody_lookup_request on it), and re-filter pending column indices against cached_data_column_indexes before each continue_requests.
impact: Fewer redundant column RPC bytes and KZG verifications during unknown-block lookups when the EL holds the blobs; small on mainnet where gossip usually wins.
refute_note: Found that custody_lookup_request already dedupes against the DA cache and that sync_methods triggers getBlobs for lookup blocks, so the earlier fix is already there; the remaining gap is that the RPC request is not gated on, or refreshed after, the EL result.

title: Trigger getBlobs on first gossip column sidecar
idea: Start the EL getBlobs fetch when the first valid data column sidecar arrives on gossip, also before its block arrives. The missing columns are then built from EL blobs sooner than with a trigger on block arrival only.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1119-1135 getBlobs triggered on first uncached partial header

beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:926-1024 process_gossip_verified_data_column: republishes as partial and processes, MissingComponents only calls check_reconstruction_trigger, no getBlobs
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1242 BlockRootUnknown for full columns is Gloas-only (needs the bid); Fulu full columns verify without the block
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1936 trigger on gossip-verified block
gap: A full Fulu data column sidecar arriving before the block passes gossip verification (it carries the signed header and commitments) but does not trigger getBlobs; only partial headers and blocks do. Fix: in process_gossip_verified_data_column, on the first column for a block root, build a PartialHeaderOrBid::PartialHeader from the column header/commitments and call fetch_engine_blobs_and_publish_full (lighthouse#7329 did this and was closed unmerged).
impact: Saves tens to hundreds of ms when a full column beats the block; only matters for nodes or peers not using partial columns.
refute_note: Checked that the BlockRootUnknown branch the earlier review cited only fires for Gloas, and that the Fulu full-column success path has no EL trigger; lighthouse#7329 is closed unmerged.

title: Call getBlobs before block verification completes
idea: Start the EL getBlobs fetch as soon as a gossip block header is seen, before consensus and execution verification of the block. The local blobs then win the race against gossip and can be published.
measured_best: 116 hits and 156 blobs published in 30 min on mainnet, up from a few hits per hour (pr:lighthouse#6600)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1936 spawn_fetch_block_columns before chain.process_block
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:960 detached executor.spawn task
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1127 also triggered by a partial-column header
impact: The EL fetch runs at the same time as consensus and execution verification, so columns are published early.

title: Fetch blobs from EL during block lookup sync
idea: In unknown-block / lookup sync for a block by root, also try engine_getBlobs before requesting blobs or columns from peers. Availability can then resolve locally without RPC.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:208 EL fetch only after lookup process_block returns MissingComponents

beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:398 DataRequest moves to Request and custody_lookup_request is sent as soon as the block is downloaded, in parallel with block processing
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:971 cached_data_column_indexes is checked once, when the request is made, before the EL result exists
gap: SingleBlockLookup::continue_requests issues custody_lookup_request to peers as soon as the block is downloaded. The getBlobs call (fetch_engine_blobs_and_publish_full in process_rpc_block) runs only after process_block completes. The peer column RPC is therefore never skipped when the EL has the blobs. Lodestar calls getBlobs before each peer by-root request. The missing step is to gate the custody request on an EL attempt, or to re-check the DA cache before the request is sent.
impact: Saves column RPC bandwidth on lookups when the EL holds the blobs. Availability already resolves locally, so latency barely changes.

title: Fetch EL blobs for blocks published via API
idea: When a block is published through the HTTP API without blob data, still trigger the EL getBlobs fetch and the column requests for it, because later gossip duplicates of the block are ignored.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:172 fetch_columns when request has no blobs and no locally cached payload blobs
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:221 NetworkMessage::FetchBlockColumns after gossip publish
beacon_node/network/src/service.rs:692 spawn_fetch_block_columns with EnvelopeSource::Http
impact: Blocks published through the API without blobs still get EL blobs and partial-column requests.

title: Use existence-only EL blob query
idea: Use an existence-only Engine API call (HasBlobs) to learn which blobs the EL holds, so held cells can be advertised to peers at once without the slower full getBlobs round trip.
evidence: beacon_node/execution_layer/src/engine_api/http.rs:71-73 only engine_getBlobsV2/V3/V4 constants
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:398-460 V4 path fetches cells and proofs
gap: No existence-only Engine API call (HasBlobs or similar bitmap query) and no early advertisement of held cells before the full getBlobs response. Fix: add the method in execution_layer and use its bitmap to set present cells in the partial assembler early. Needs EL support.
impact: Lets partial-column peers learn held cells one EL round trip earlier; tens of ms on propagation.
refute_note: Searched execution_layer and fetch_blobs for has_blobs, blobs_exist, bitmap and availability queries; only the getBlobs family exists.

title: Fill partial column cells from EL blobs
idea: On a partial data column header, fetch the matching blobs from the EL (getBlobsV3) and fill the cell assembly locally. Fewer cells must come from peers.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1123 first-seen partial header triggers fetch_engine_blobs_and_publish_full
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:161 getBlobsV4 (custody cells only) with V2/V3 fallback at :190

title: Run blob tracker only for gossip blocks
idea: Start post-import fetch of missing blobs/columns (EL or peers) only for blocks that arrived via gossip, not for blocks imported by sync or other paths.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1936 gossip block triggers spawn_fetch_block_columns
beacon_node/network/src/service.rs:697 HTTP-published block triggers it
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:214 RPC lookup block with MissingComponents also triggers EL fetch
range sync/chain segment path does not call it
gap: Range-sync and backfill paths already do not fetch from the EL, so waste is limited. Lighthouse also fetches for RPC lookup blocks (publish_blobs=false), which is deliberate. Dropping that would only avoid one EL call per lookup block.
impact: Little to gain: only lookup-sourced blocks differ and the extra EL call there can save a peer download.

title: Skip EL reconstruction when nothing is missing
idea: Skip the EL getBlobs/sidecar build routine when the block has no KZG commitments or all its blobs or columns were already seen on gossip. This avoids needless engine calls and sidecar building.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:144 returns early when versioned_hashes is empty
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:1020 no check of already-seen columns before calling the EL
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:531 dedupe against gossip/DA cache only after the EL response
gap: Add a guard in fetch_and_process_engine_blobs_inner (or fetch_engine_blobs_and_publish_full) that returns early when the DA checker/partial assembler already holds all custody columns for block_root, before calling get_blobs_v4/v3/v2.
impact: Saves an engine call, and cell/proof processing, only when all columns arrived before the EL fetch. This is rare since the fetch starts at block arrival.

title: Build only custodied columns from EL blobs
idea: When data column sidecars are built from EL blobs, compute only the columns that the node custodies (column bitmap), not all 128 columns that are then filtered.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:158 V4 path requests only custody columns from the EL
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:686-705 V2/V3 path calls blobs_to_partial_data_columns for all columns, then filters by custody_columns_indices
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/kzg_utils.rs:425-472 blobs_to_partial_data_columns computes all cells and builds every column, no index parameter
gap: Only the V4 path is custody-scoped. The V2/V3 fallback builds all 128 partial columns, then filters to custody and then dedupes against observed and cached columns. Fix: pass the custody indices minus already-known columns into blobs_to_partial_data_columns and build only those columns (cell computation via compute_cells still covers the whole blob).
impact: Saves column assembly work and allocations per block on V2/V3 ELs for non-supernodes; cell FFT cost stays, so modest.
refute_note: Re-read the builder and the V2/V3 path; the custody filter and the observed/cached dedupe both run after all columns are built.

title: Publish recovered columns off the availability path
idea: Publish columns recovered from EL blobs or reconstruction in a detached task after storing them, so block import and DA completion do not wait on network sends. Coalesce repeated partial publishes per (block, column).
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:357 publish_fn called before process_engine_blobs_fulu, but it only spawns
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:1263 publish_data_columns_gradually runs in a detached executor.spawn task

gap: Recovered full columns are published in a detached task, so this half is done. Partial-column republishes are not coalesced: each merged partial update in process_gossip_partial_data_column (gossip_methods.rs:1404/1421) calls PublishPartialColumns -> Network::publish_partial at once. Prysm batches these over a 250 ms window per (block, column).
impact: Import and DA do not wait on network sends. Coalescing would reduce partial-column protocol chatter when partial columns are enabled.

title: Publish only needed recovered columns
idea: When recovered columns are redistributed to gossip, publish only the columns that the network still needs instead of all of them.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:697 EL columns filtered to custody columns before import and publish
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:720 columns already observed on gossip or known to DA are dropped
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:1298 each gradual batch re-filtered with observe_gossip_data_column, PriorKnown dropped
impact: Only custody columns not yet seen are published, in shuffled delayed batches, which cuts outbound bandwidth.

title: Mark data available at 50% columns
idea: On nodes that custody all columns, treat a block as data-available once at least 50% of columns are verified (enough to reconstruct), and import it before reconstruction of the rest completes.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:212-234 make_available requires received == num_of_data_columns_to_sample (Ordering::Equal), Less => None
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:620 total/2 only gates reconstruction start
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/pending_components.rs:218-220 Gloas is_blob_data_available also needs >= full sampling count
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/mod.rs:643 Gloas 50% only gates reconstruction
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3785-3870 import after 50% happens only via reconstruct_data_columns -> process_availability, i.e. after reconstruction completes

PR #7598 was closed unmerged.
impact: Supernodes import without waiting for reconstruction (and its scheduled delay) when only about half the columns have arrived; saves hundreds of ms on such blocks, only on nodes custodying >= 64 columns.
refute_note: Also checked the Gloas pending_payload_cache path and the reconstruction-to-import flow in beacon_chain.rs; both require the full sampling count before import, so the 50% threshold is never an availability shortcut.

title: Reconstruct remaining columns from half
idea: Once at least 50% of data columns for a block are held, recover the missing columns by erasure-coding reconstruction (cell recovery), store and publish them, instead of downloading every column.
measured_best: <800ms to recover with 20 blobs (pr:lodestar#7940)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:611-639 check_and_set_reconstruction_started requires received >= total/2 and < sampling count
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:537-620 reconstruct_data_columns imports only sampled, not-yet-held columns
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3785-3870 reconstruct then process_availability
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:1213-1217 attempt_data_column_reconstruction publishes recovered columns (publish_data_columns_gradually)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/custody_context.rs:492-497 should_attempt_reconstruction only when sampling > 50%
impact: Supernodes recover all columns from half, import and republish them.

title: Delay column reconstruction to wait for gossip
idea: Wait a short configurable time before starting column reconstruction (longer while syncing), because the missing columns often arrive via gossip or getBlobs and reconstruction is CPU-heavy.
measured_best: reduces the unnecessary amount of reconstructions during fast block import (commit:grandine@9e43a4aea5ad)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:73 QUEUED_RECONSTRUCTION_DELAY 150ms
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:1139-1166 delay reset on every new column for the root, zero after 1/4-slot deadline
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1488-1520 check_reconstruction_trigger schedules instead of running
impact: Debounced reconstruction avoids redundant KZG recovery when gossip or getBlobs completes the set.

title: Cap reconstruction debounce delay
idea: Put a hard maximum (for example 1 s from first enqueue) on the debounced delay before column reconstruction, so repeated column arrivals cannot postpone reconstruction and publication indefinitely.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:1139 DelayColumnReconstruction handler
work_reprocessing_queue.rs:1157 delay_queue.reset(delay_key, reconstruction_delay) on every arrival with no cap on total delay
work_reprocessing_queue.rs:1148 delay set to 0 only after the 1/4-slot deadline
lighthouse#7702 was closed, not merged
gap: Track first-enqueue time per block_root in queued_column_reconstructions and skip reset (or cap the delay at about 1s from first enqueue) in the DelayColumnReconstruction arm.
impact: Only affects supernodes. It bounds reconstruction postponement under a steady stream of columns, but the 150ms window and the 1/4-slot deadline already limit it.

title: Dynamic reconstruction timeout, none on non-supernodes
idea: Compute the reconstruction timeout dynamically, and do not run column reconstruction on nodes that do not custody enough columns.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/custody_context.rs:492 should_attempt_reconstruction requires sampling count > NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS/2
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1488 check_reconstruction_trigger gated by it; it is the only caller of attempt_data_column_reconstruction
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:1139 delay 150ms, or 0 after the 1/4-slot deadline, derived from slot duration
impact: Non-supernodes never reconstruct, and the delay adapts to the slot position.

title: Run column reconstruction once per block
idea: Record the block roots for which column reconstruction was dispatched, is in flight or is complete, and skip new reconstruction requests for them. Share one reconstruction result across concurrent requesters.
measured_best: duplicate rate 4-6% to 0 in test (pr:lighthouse#8985)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:592-639 reconstruction_started flag set under write lock (gossip path dedup)
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:1153-1166,1357-1361 per-root queue entry, None marks dispatched (pruned on the next dispatch)
beacon_node/http_api/src/block_id.rs:433-447 get_blobs_by_versioned_hashes calls reconstruct_blobs on every request
beacon_node/http_api/src/block_id.rs:501-534 get_data_columns_for_blob_reconstruction reads columns from DB per request
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/kzg_utils.rs:767-822 reconstruct_blobs_with_indices runs recover_cells_and_compute_kzg_proofs per blob when fewer than 128 columns held
gap: Only the gossip column-reconstruction path is deduplicated. The API blob paths (BlockId::get_blobs_by_versioned_hashes and the PeerDAS branch of get_blinded_block_and_blob_list_filtered) rerun reconstruct_blobs -> recover_cells_and_compute_kzg_proofs for every request on a semi-supernode/partial-custody node, with no in-flight sharing and no result cache; concurrent requests for the same block (e.g. several rollups/L2 indexers) each pay the full recovery.
impact: On semi-supernodes serving /eth/v1/beacon/blobs, N concurrent requests for a recent block cost N full cell recoveries (~hundreds of ms of CPU each with many blobs); a shared per-root future/short-lived cache would make it one.

title: Dedicated thread pool for column reconstruction
idea: Run data column computation and cell recovery on a dedicated (high-priority) thread pool, separate from the general pool and the fork choice/block import threads, so heavy KZG work does not starve other tasks.
measured_best: reduces p99 latency during high load (commit:grandine@9af9e4de859b)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3811,3845 reconstruction on RayonPoolType::HighPriority
common/task_executor/src/rayon_pool_provider.rs:4-56 high pool = 80% of CPUs, 'critical tasks use the global pool'
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:656-690 compute_custody_columns_to_import: spawn_blocking_handle + into_par_iter compute_cells on the global rayon pool
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:440-470 build_data_sidecars via spawn_blocking on global pool
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/kzg_utils.rs:400-420 compute_cells into_par_iter (global pool)
beacon_node/http_api/src/block_id.rs:437 API reconstruct_blobs runs on a beacon-processor blocking thread
gap: Only DataAvailabilityChecker::reconstruct_data_columns (and the Gloas equivalent) run in the scoped HighPriority pool. Column computation (compute_cells in blobs_to_data_column_sidecars / blobs_to_partial_data_columns from fetch_blobs::compute_custody_columns_to_import and publish_blocks::build_data_columns) runs on the global rayon pool shared with other parallel work, and API-driven recovery in kzg_utils::reconstruct_blobs runs on a generic blocking thread. The high-priority pool is also not isolated (80% of CPUs, overlapping the global pool).
impact: Under load, getBlobs column computation and API recovery compete with other global-pool rayon work; grandine reports lower p99 from moving both compute_cells and recovery to a dedicated executor.

title: Run KZG reconstruction off async and fork-choice threads
idea: Call PeerDAS KZG and reconstruction functions in blocking tasks or async jobs off the caller, async runtime and single-threaded fork choice mutator. Do not spawn a new validation task per column for the same delayed block.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2451-2475 gossip column verification in spawn_blocking_handle
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2514-2541 partial column verification in spawn_blocking_handle
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:619-633 send_rpc_custody_columns wraps work as async Work::RpcCustodyColumn
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1701-1703 RpcCustodyColumn -> task_spawner.spawn_async
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4264-4304 check_rpc_custody_columns_availability_and_import calls put_rpc_custody_columns inline in async fn
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:350-360 put_rpc_custody_columns runs KzgVerifiedDataColumn::from_batch_with_scoring (batch cell-proof KZG) synchronously
gap: RPC custody columns (single-block lookups and custody requests) are KZG batch-verified inside an async task on the tokio runtime: NetworkBeaconProcessor::process_rpc_custody_columns -> BeaconChain::process_rpc_custody_columns -> check_rpc_custody_columns_availability_and_import -> DataAvailabilityChecker::put_rpc_custody_columns -> KzgVerifiedDataColumn::from_batch_with_scoring (and PendingPayloadCache::put_rpc_custody_columns for Gloas), with no spawn_blocking. Gossip, partial and reconstruction paths are correctly offloaded.
impact: A by-root response of many columns x many blobs (tens of ms of KZG) blocks a tokio worker, delaying networking and other async tasks during lookup sync bursts.

title: Bound parallelism of per-blob cell recovery
idea: Run per-blob cell recovery on worker tasks with a bounded number in flight, zero-copy views of inputs and reused buffers, instead of spawning one task per blob. This limits peak memory and scheduling overhead.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/kzg_utils.rs:889 reconstruct_data_columns uses into_par_iter over blobs (rayon, bounded by pool threads)
beacon_node/crypto/kzg/src/lib.rs:307 recover_cells_and_compute_kzg_proofs takes cell refs but to_vec()s inputs
gap: Parallelism is rayon-bounded by pool size, not one task per blob, so peak in-flight is limited. Missing: reused buffers and fully zero-copy inputs (cell_ids.to_vec(), cells.to_vec() per blob).
impact: Small allocation savings during supernode reconstruction; negligible for non-supernodes.

title: Semi-supernode: custody half the columns
idea: Offer a mode that custodies and subscribes to 64 of 128 column subnets, enough to reconstruct all blobs, to serve blobs with about half the bandwidth and storage of a supernode.
measured_best: Storage ~50% vs supernode (64 vs 128 columns) (pr:prysm#16029)

beacon_node/src/config.rs:130-134 semi-supernode sets custody override
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/custody_context.rs:43-44 cgc override (number_of_custody_groups/2)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/custody_context.rs:492-497 no reconstruction at exactly 50%
beacon_node/http_api/src/block_id.rs:501-534 blobs served by reconstruction from >=64 columns
impact: Half the column bandwidth/storage of a supernode while still serving blobs.

title: Custody first half of columns to skip reconstruction
idea: Custody the first 64 columns, which hold the original blob data, so blobs can be served directly without reconstruction CPU cost.
measured_best: avoids reconstruction CPU load (pr:nimbus#7752)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/custody_context.rs:507 sampling_columns_for_epoch slices ordered_custody_column_indices

title: Background reconstruction of historical custody columns
idea: Run a background service that reconstructs missing custody columns from stored half-sets for recent history, walking from head back to the retention floor, so full columns can be served without download.
evidence: searched beacon_node/beacon_chain, store, network for background column reconstruction; only block-time reconstruct_data_columns (data_availability_checker.rs:537) and historic state reconstruction (store/src/reconstruct.rs) exist
beacon_node/http_api/src/block_id.rs:501 stores only keys present; no backfill of missing custody columns
gap: Add a background task that walks from head to the data column retention floor, finds blocks with at least 64 but fewer than custody columns stored, calls kzg_utils::reconstruct_data_columns and stores the results.
impact: Only helps nodes with half-sets on disk (semi-supernode/supernode after custody changes). It saves peer downloads for serving historic columns. Niche.

title: Reconstruct API blobs from stored columns
idea: Serve blob sidecars in the blobs API by reconstructing them from stored data column sidecars once at least half are held, and hold sidecars as Arc to avoid copies.

title: Share blobs and cells by Arc, not copy
idea: Hold blobs, sidecars and partial-column cells behind Arc/shared references on the heap and pass them by reference to KZG and caches, so each clone does not copy 128 KiB.
evidence: consensus/types/src/data/data_column_sidecar.rs:47 DataColumnSidecarList = Vec<Arc<DataColumnSidecar>>
consensus/types/src/data/blob_sidecar.rs:296 BlobSidecarList = RuntimeVariableList<Arc<BlobSidecar>>

title: Store a blob as one flat byte array
idea: Represent a blob as one flat byte array instead of a 2D slice of 32-byte field elements, removing a slice header per element.
measured_best: 24-byte slice header overhead per 32-byte element avoided (pr:prysm#11614)
