evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:680 signature_verify_chain_segment does one load_parent for the segment
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:731 only the first block gets the loaded parent; others have parent: None (line 711)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1360-1364 blocks without parent call load_parent -> get_advanced_hot_state
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1130 state_cache hit on the previous block's post-state (cheap milhouse clone)
gap: The first block reuses the segment pre-state. Every later block gets its pre-state again through load_parent and the state cache, instead of carrying the post-state forward. It is cheap when the cache hits. Fix: pass the post-state of block N into block N+1's PreProcessingSnapshot in process_chain_segment.
impact: Saves one state cache lookup and clone plus one parent block read per block in range sync; under 1 ms per block when the cache hits.
refute_note: Found that the first block of the segment already reuses the signature-verification parent (line 731). This was not in the earlier review, but it confirms that the other blocks are not carried forward.

title: Evaluate cheap flags before 32-byte hash comparisons
idea: In short-circuit conditions on the import path, evaluate cheap boolean flags first and the 32-byte root comparison last.
evidence: consensus/proto_array and beacon_chain import path use plain Hash256 equality; no hot short-circuit with a 32-byte compare ahead of a flag found
gap: A 32-byte memcmp in Rust costs nanoseconds and the compiler/LLVM choices make the reorder immaterial; no hot site identified.
impact: Negligible.

title: Structural checks before pubkey collection and signature verification
idea: Run cheap structural checks (for example attestation bits equal proof participants, bitfield lengths) before collecting public keys and verifying signatures, so malformed blocks are rejected without crypto work.
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/block_signature_verifier.rs:168-184,284-306,429-435
consensus/state_processing/src/common/get_attesting_indices.rs:25-31,113-147
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:721,911-955
impact: Malformed bitfields, bad committee indices and oversized operation lists are rejected while signature sets are collected, before the single batch verify. Pubkeys come from the decompressed pubkey cache.

title: Return early from post-block fcU when no payload attributes
idea: In the post-block forkchoiceUpdated path, return early when there are no payload attributes (no local proposer next slot) before fetching or copying the head block.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:6737 early exit only when no proposer data is registered at all

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:6750 spawn_blocking head read: overridden_forkchoice_update_params (fork choice read lock, get_preliminary_proposer_head), get_pre_payload_attributes, proposer_shuffling_decision_root_at_epoch, and for gloas a second fork choice read lock plus should_build_on_full
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:6895 has_proposer_preparation_data(proposer) is checked only after all of that
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5531 overridden_forkchoice_update_params_or_failure_reason takes fork choice read lock
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1931 prepare_beacon_proposer runs after every head change
gap: prepare_beacon_proposer exits early only when the EL holds no preparation data at all. On any node with an attached VC, each head change spawns a blocking task and runs overridden_forkchoice_update_params, which takes the fork choice lock. It also runs proposer_shuffling_decision_root_at_epoch and, post-gloas, a second fork choice read lock plus should_build_on_full. All of this runs before has_proposer_preparation_data(proposer) finds the next-slot proposer is not local. The fix: compute the proposer index from the proposer cache first and return before the head and fork choice work.
impact: Saves one or two fork choice read locks and a blocking task per head change on non-proposing slots; the absolute time is small (microseconds), and there is no block copy because the head is an Arc.

title: Run state defragmentation after block import
idea: Run the state tree defragmentation/compaction walk in a background task after block import completes, not synchronously before taking the fork choice write lock.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5881 apply_pending_mutations before state root (milhouse persistent tree)

title: Delay attestation production while head block imports
idea: When a block that will become head is being imported, make attestation production wait (bounded, e.g. 1.5s) on a condvar until it is imported, so attestations vote for it instead of its parent.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2010-2039
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4572
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1561-1571,1720-1745
beacon_node/http_api/src/validator/mod.rs:295
gap: produce_unaggregated_attestation never waits. The early attester cache gets the block only after the state transition, the EL newPayload and fork choice (beacon_chain.rs:4572), so it covers only the DB-write window. A current-slot block that passed gossip verification but is still in state transition, notify_new_payload or data availability when the VC asks at 1/3 slot gets an attestation for its parent. Nothing in produce_unaggregated_attestation or the http_api attestation_data handler does a bounded wait on an in-flight import of a request_slot block.
impact: Fewer wrong head votes for late blocks that arrive near the attestation deadline. Only blocks that arrive in the ~100-500ms before 1/3 slot are affected.

title: Apply EL payload status after block accepted in fork choice

evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1555 notify_new_payload awaited during verification
Lighthouse starts newPayload as a future in parallel with state transition and passes the status into fork choice on_block; Grandine's change is about its actor message ordering.
gap: n/a
impact: None; no equivalent interleaving problem.

title: Reject known, finalized or non-descendant blocks before state load

idea: Recompute and set the head right after the block's state transition/import succeeds, before post-processing steps (attestation handling, caches, pruning), so head and downstream consumers see the block sooner and head-lock contention drops.
measured_best: Said to have a big impact on block processing time; no numbers (pr:prysm#9224)

title: Import block once half of columns are available
idea: Treat a PeerDAS block as available, and import it, as soon as about 50% of data columns are accepted, since the rest can be reconstructed; complete the remaining columns in the background instead of waiting for all custody columns. This cuts import latency on supernodes.

gap: Reconstruction starts at 50%, but import waits for it to finish. To match, make_available would accept >= 50% verified columns, import the block with the received set, and fill and persist the custody columns in the background.
impact: On supernodes this removes the wait for KZG cell recovery (hundreds of ms) before import once half the columns arrive. No effect on non-supernodes.
refute_note: Read make_available and check_and_set_reconstruction_started directly; there is no availability shortcut under another name. The only early step is that reconstruction is triggered at half.

title: Use in-memory head state when parent is head

title: Reject blocks with huge parent skip distance
idea: Reject blocks whose parent is more than a configurable number of slots behind, so minority forks cannot force long state advances and storage of their states.

refute_note: Searched git history (read-only) and found that Lighthouse once had this exact check and removed it on purpose in #4403. Today only the attestation path and a skip-slot metric remain.

title: Move parent state into import, no clone

title: Narrow deposit signature pre-verification set

title: Advance next-slot state immediately after head update
idea: Right after a block becomes head (including late blocks), advance and cache the head state to the next slot at once, so proposals and attestations do not wait for a later state advance.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:125-131 single advance at 3/4 slot; skipped for the slot if past it
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:258-290 advance_head advances head one slot into state cache

gap: When a head changes after the 3/4-slot timer has fired (a late block), nothing advances the new head state to the next slot. Spawn advance_head after recompute_head when the timer has already run for this slot.
impact: Removes a per-slot or epoch transition from the proposal path after late blocks. This is tens of ms, or hundreds at epoch boundaries.
refute_note: I also checked after_new_head, the FCR head-state advance (not cached), the shuffling and proposer caches (partial advances only) and block production state loading. None of them eagerly caches a next-slot head state after a late block.

title: Send proposer FCU before next-slot cache update
idea: On late-block tasks, send fork choice updates with payload attributes only when a local validator proposes next, and do it before updating the next-slot cache, giving the EL more time to build.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:6893-6902 prepare_beacon_proposer returns early unless the EL has preparation data for the specific next-slot proposer (local-proposer gate exists)
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/lib.rs:1578-1581 every FCU attaches cached payload attributes for (next_slot, head_root) when present
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1907-1935 head update sends FCU first, then prepare_beacon_proposer (second FCU with attributes; comment accepts the double call)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5396-5460 withdrawals for new attributes are computed via partial_state_advance before the attribute FCU is sent
gap: The local-proposer gate exists, so the earlier evidence that it was 'gated on any registered proposer' was wrong. The missing part: on a new head, the first FCU has no attributes because none are cached yet for the new root. The attribute FCU then waits for withdrawals to be computed (a state advance). Computing the attributes before or in the first FCU would give the EL one FCU and more build time.
impact: Gives the EL a little more build time on proposer slots after late blocks and saves one FCU. The effect is small.
refute_note: Corrected the evidence: the per-proposer gate is at beacon_chain.rs:6896, and the any-proposer check at 6738 is only an early exit. Lighthouse has no separate next-slot cache, so the 'before cache update' ordering becomes 'before the withdrawals state advance', which is not done.

title: Notify reprocess queue on every import path
idea: When a block or payload is imported through any path (gossip, RPC columns), notify the reprocessing queue so attestations waiting on it are released at once instead of on a fallback timer.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:4104 notify_import_after_column helper
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1009,1450,1957,4087 gossip column, partial column, block and envelope paths notify
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:191,290,363 RPC block, custody column and envelope paths notify
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:1037 EL-blobs path notifies
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:1213-1226 attempt_data_column_reconstruction: Imported -> recompute_head_at_current_slot only, no notify
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:589-610 HTTP-API block import: recompute_head only, no reprocess notification
beacon_node/http_api/src/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes.rs:334-346 HTTP-API envelope import: no PayloadEnvelopeImported notification
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:53 QUEUED_ATTESTATION_DELAY 12s fallback
gap: Not every import path notifies. attempt_data_column_reconstruction (network_beacon_processor/mod.rs) completes the import through reconstruct_data_columns and only calls recompute_head_at_current_slot, so attestations queued on that root (or, post-Gloas, on its payload) wait for the 12s QUEUED_ATTESTATION_DELAY fallback. The HTTP API paths (publish_blocks.rs publish_block_p2p result handling and execution_payload_envelopes.rs process_execution_payload_envelope) also do not send BlockImported/PayloadEnvelopeImported; http_api has no beacon_processor_send handle for this. Fix: call notify_import_after_column after reconstruction import, and plumb a reprocess sender (or an import event the network processor listens to) for the HTTP paths.
impact: Attestations waiting on a block or payload that became available through column reconstruction, or was published via the HTTP API, are released at once instead of after up to 12s.

title: Query optimistic status once per batch tail
idea: When importing a batch of blocks, query execution validity/optimistic status for the last block only, since a valid tail implies valid ancestors.
evidence: beacon_chain.rs:3208 process_chain_segment imports blocks sequentially
block_verification.rs newPayload response recorded per block into fork choice
impact: Lighthouse learns validity from each newPayload response, not by querying optimistic status per block, so there is no per-block query to skip.

title: Run state transition concurrently with newPayload
idea: During block import, send engine_newPayload and run the consensus state transition concurrently instead of sequentially, so import costs the max of the two, not the sum.
measured_best: shed about 200ms on a normal slot (pr:prysm#12590)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1531-1571 PayloadNotifier future spawned with spawn_handle before state advance
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1573-1710 catch-up per_slot_processing and per_block_processing run while newPayload is in flight
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4092-4112 into_executed_block awaits payload_verification_handle afterwards
impact: Import already costs max(newPayload, state transition).

title: Persist block concurrently with verification
idea: Start writing the block and blobs to the database in parallel with signature, state transition and payload verification, and delete them if verification fails, so DB I/O is off the critical path to head.
measured_best: Persisting a block took 1-2s, up to 3s under I/O lag (pr:lodestar#5473)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4733-4756 PutBlock/PutState/blobs ops pushed and written only after fork choice on_block, inside import_block
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4759-4761 fork choice write lock held until DB write completes
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1488-1534 do_atomically_with_block_and_blobs_cache is one synchronous write, no early/speculative path
gap: Start the block (and blobs/columns) DB write concurrently with signature/state/payload verification and roll back with StoreOp::DeleteBlock on failure; must keep fork choice and DB consistent (issue #2028 comment at import_block).

refute_note: Checked the full import_block tail and the store atomic write for any speculative or early persist of blocks or columns; none exists, data columns stay in the DA checker until import.

title: Write blobs in parallel with fork choice write
idea: During block import, write blobs/columns to the database in parallel with the fork choice and block write instead of sequentially.
measured_best: small gain, no numbers (pr:lighthouse#8404)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1519-1534 blobs_db.do_atomically runs, then hot_db.do_atomically, strictly sequential
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1536 rollback of blob ops on hot_db failure already exists
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4740-4756 blobs op added to the same ops batch as PutBlock
gap: Run the blobs_db write concurrently with the hot_db write (e.g. std::thread::scope / rayon::join) inside do_atomically_with_block_and_blobs_cache, joining before the block cache guard and fork choice lock are released; rollback logic is reusable.
impact: Overlaps the blob/column write with the hot DB write on import of blocks with data; saves up to the blob write duration (few to tens of ms).
refute_note: Grepped hot_cold_store.rs for spawn/thread::scope/rayon::join and found no parallel write; upstream PR #8404 that did this is not in the tree.

title: Parallel attestation signature verification per block
idea: Verify the signatures of all attestations in a block in parallel across threads during block import, since BLS verification dominates import time.
measured_best: Block import 0.351->0.226 s/op (1024 validators), 0.529->0.352 s/op (3072); ~50% faster (pr:teku#1106)
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/block_signature_verifier.rs:459-461 ParallelSignatureSets::verify calls verify_signature_sets once
crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:36-110 single-threaded randomized batch verify, one multi-pairing
consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/block_signature_verifier.rs:283-308 attestation sets collected sequentially
gap: Lighthouse already batch-verifies all block signatures with random-scalar multi-pairing (cheaper than Teku's per-attestation verify) but on one thread despite the struct name. Change ParallelSignatureSets::verify to split sets into N chunks and run verify_signature_sets per chunk with rayon (or the blocking pool), AND-ing results; also parallelize pubkey aggregation/set construction in include_attestations.

title: Reuse in-hand state instead of DB refetch
idea: Load the beacon state once per block and pass the reference (pre- and post-state) to later steps such as fork choice vote processing, instead of re-reading state from the database.
measured_best: 3 DB fetches reduced (pr:prysm#1257)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4454-4462 import_block takes the post-state by value
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4532-4540 fork_choice.on_block receives &state
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4720-4734 shuffling cache, attestation observation, validator monitor and slasher reuse the same &state
impact: No extra DB reads on import.

title: Pause gossip intake while processing current block
idea: While the current-slot block is being processed, stop pulling new gossip jobs from the network processor so the block gets full CPU, instead of capping concurrency for the whole slot.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:890 can_spawn only checks current_workers < max_workers
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:801-810 worker completion only decrements worker count and per-peer block queue state

beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1290 any other work spawns immediately whenever a worker slot is free, even while a block is processing
gap: Track a current-slot block-in-flight flag in the BeaconProcessor manager loop (set when spawning GossipBlock, cleared on WorkerFinished) and hold attestation/aggregate/low-priority work in their queues while it is set.
impact: More CPU for block signature verification and state transition in the hot window; modest because queue priority already favours blocks and workers are capped at num_cpus.
refute_note: Checked the scheduler work_queue per-peer block gating and the reprocess queue; both are unrelated to pausing other work while a block runs.

title: Pipelined block processing stream
idea: Process blocks as a pipeline of validate/process/post-process stages, with parent-missing blocks held in a pool and requeued when the parent arrives.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1500-1530 ParentUnknown returned and handled by sync lookups
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs reprocess queue for early/unknown-parent work
impact: Lighthouse's design is a beacon processor work queue plus sync lookups with its own staged verification (gossip -> signature -> import); a Lodestar-style stream pipeline would be a redesign with no clear gain.

title: Plain struct for signature-only indexed attestation
idea: For indexed (payload) attestations used only for signature verification in block processing, use a plain struct instead of an SSZ tree-backed container, avoiding tree node allocation.
evidence: consensus/types/src/attestation/indexed_payload_attestation.rs:15 plain struct (VariableList + PayloadAttestationData + AggregateSignature), no milhouse tree
consensus/state_processing/src/consensus_context.rs:32,197-210 cached in a HashMap and built once per payload attestation
impact: No tree-node allocation for indexed payload attestations; already in place.

title: Point pubkey lookups for sync aggregate
idea: When processing a SyncAggregate, look up the 512 committee pubkeys individually in the state pubkey index instead of building a map of all validator pubkeys.
measured_best: 190k-entry map and 190k lookups reduced to 512 lookups (pr:prysm#9177)
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1753-1767 get_sync_committee_indices does 512 pubkey_cache().get() lookups
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:2979-2993 update_pubkey_cache only inserts validators past the cached length

impact: No per-block full validator map build.

title: Cheap pre-checks before EL validation

title: Validate block outside the fork choice lock

title: Checkpoint sync from unfinalized state
idea: Allow checkpoint sync from a recent unfinalized state by treating it as the fork choice anchor, so a node can start and attest during long non-finality.
measured_best: node catches up and attests immediately from a 6-epoch-old unfinalized checkpoint (pr:prysm#17559)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_fork_choice_store.rs:169-174 anchor epoch/root used as both justified and finalized regardless of the state's real finality

gap: The fake-finalized anchor exists (manual --checkpoint-state), but under long non-finality descendants of the anchor carry a real justified checkpoint older than the anchor epoch, so node_is_viable_for_head rejects them and the head sticks at the anchor until the chain justifies again. Prysm's PR clamps descendant justified/finalized checkpoints to the anchor; Lighthouse has no clamp. Also missing: a non-finalized StateId option on checkpoint-sync-url, status/range-sync handling when our fake finalized epoch is ahead of peers, and custody/backfill origin handling.
impact: Lets a node resync and attest within minutes during long non-finality instead of failing to find a finalized checkpoint; no gain in normal mainnet operation.
refute_note: Beyond the earlier review, checked the fork choice store init (anchor forced as justified+finalized), the proto_array viability filter, and searched fork_choice/proto_array for any checkpoint clamp (none). The viability check means the manual-file path likely does not work under real non-finality, which strengthens the gap; the store-test WSS tests only cover anchors near finality.

title: Compute block root after broadcasting proposal
idea: Defer hash_tree_root of the proposed block until after it is broadcast, using only the slot for pre-broadcast logging, to take the HTR off the proposal critical path.

idea: Advance the head state to the proposal slot (slot and epoch processing, including any epoch transition) before the slot starts, cache it, and have block production clone that state and run only process_block on it, passing the known state root. evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/verify_deposit.rs:23 deposit sig via deserialized PublicKey
crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:113 batch takes deserialized points
gap: Verification goes through deserialized PublicKey/Signature wrappers; blst has no compressed-byte verify path used. Gain only for rare signatures (deposits, bids); wrappers already deserialize once and pubkeys come from a decompressed cache.
impact: Negligible; the hot attestation/block paths use the decompressed pubkey cache, which is faster than passing compressed bytes.

title: Cap batch size at the native verifier limit
idea: Cap the number of signature sets in one verification package at the native verifier's limit, so packages do not overshoot and fall back to slower individual verification.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:110 gossip batches capped at 64
blst-0.3.17/src/lib.rs:1337 blst imposes no cap on set count (chunks internally)

title: Avoid stream overhead in batch verify code
idea: In batch BLS verification glue code, avoid the slower IntStream-style collection handling in favour of plain collections, as measured in production.
evidence: crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:95-120 plain Vec collections in batch glue
impact: Rust iterators have no stream overhead; Java-specific.

title: Use library EIP-2333 key derivation
idea: Derive keys per EIP-2333 with the BLS library's built-in implementation instead of a slower generic one.

gap: Replace BigUint mod_r and Lamport derivation with blst's keygen/derive_child (blst::min_pk::SecretKey::derive_child_eip2333) in derived_key.rs.
impact: Only wallet/keystore tooling (account manager); no effect on a running node.

title: Subgroup-check each pubkey once and reuse it
idea: Validate each public key (infinity and subgroup check) once when first seen, record or cache the validated object, and reuse it for sync committee and other verification, aggregating trusted keys with plain point addition. Expensive group checks and re-deserialization are not repeated.

idea: Marshal secret keys without padding and use a dedicated zero-key check instead of a generic comparison.

evidence: Cargo.toml:238 snap only; no aggregated-proof type in consensus/types

title: Verify deposit signatures only when the outcome depends on it
idea: When processing deposit requests or pending deposits (including Gloas builder onboarding), skip BLS signature verification for deposits whose result does not depend on it (pubkey already known or already pending, non-builder credentials), using a pubkey-to-index map. Only deposits that can create a new validator or builder pay for a pairing.

title: Larger gossip signature batch size limit
idea: Raise the maximum number of signature sets per batch verification for gossip attestations (e.g. 50 to 1000, or up to the native verifier bound) so more sets share one multi-pairing and final exponentiation.
measured_best: -16% CPU no-validator, -6% validator mode (pr:prysm#15467)
evidence: beacon_node/src/cli.rs:1654-1664 hidden flag --beacon-processor-attestation-batch-size (default 64)

gap: The configurable limit (what Prysm #15467 added) already exists as hidden CLI flags; only the default is still 64. Remaining work: benchmark larger defaults (e.g. 256-1000) and raise them. idea: Store decompressed validated pubkeys in a plain map behind a mutex instead of an LRU cache, since the working set (all validators) is never usefully evicted. This drops the LRU bookkeeping heap.

title: Skip re-verifying already verified sidecars
idea: Track in the DA cache or quarantine which blob/column sidecars were already KZG-verified (gossip or EL) and at fork choice import or RPC processing verify only sidecars from unverified sources; accept identical known columns without re-verifying.

The fix is to filter out exact matches against the cached KZG-verified columns before from_batch_with_scoring. Open PR sigp/lighthouse#10363 does this but is not merged.

refute_note: Beyond the earlier review, I found that the gossip path does skip identical cached columns and verifies only missing cells (data_column_verification.rs:431, data_availability_checker.rs:187). Lookups also exclude columns cached at request time, so the remaining gap is only RPC responses that race with gossip. Gloas pending_payload_cache has the same gap.

title: Drop sidecars and fetches for imported blocks
idea: Ignore received blob/column sidecars and skip pending RPC fetches for blocks already imported with DA satisfied or whose tracker was removed, and do not register historical sync data in the gossip blob pool. No redundant verification, requests or pool growth occur.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1152 verify_is_unknown_sidecar drops columns already observed
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:187 missing_cells_for_column_sidecar returns None when column already cached (skips KZG)

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1139 no check that the block is already imported with DA satisfied before inclusion proof and KZG

Add an early check in validate_data_column_sidecar_for_gossip_fulu against fork choice / DA checker for block_root already imported and return an ignore error. Gossip blob pool does not exist so that part is n/a.

title: Bound or fail fast on DA wait
idea: During sync, payload envelope import and block import, bound the data availability or sampling wait (for example one slot) or check availability synchronously and return an error so the batch or block is retried, instead of waiting indefinitely on a gossip subscription.

impact: Lighthouse DA is a non-blocking pending-components cache; import returns MissingComponents and completes when data arrives, so there is no wait on a gossip subscription to bound.

title: Bounded cache of in-flight sampled blocks
idea: Keep blocks awaiting column sampling in a bounded cache with eviction, serve them to peers from it, and skip refetching blocks already held.

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/mod.rs:118 Gloas cache is also a bounded LruCache(32)
impact: Bounded LRU holds in-flight blocks, serves them over req/resp and lets sync skip refetching.

title: Run DA check concurrently with block verification
idea: Persist gossip blobs from the gossip handler and run the data availability check concurrently with consensus verification and EL newPayload (one cancel-on-failure group), joining only at the end instead of running sequentially.

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/import.rs:106-118 envelope: EL newPayload handle awaited, then availability is only a cache join (put_executed_payload_envelope)

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1409-1418 into_execution_pending_block_slashable runs verify_kzg_for_available_block serially before consensus/EL verification for RPC blocks with data
gap: On the gossip and envelope paths, the DA check is a cache join at the end. Range sync and RPC blocks that carry columns work differently: signature_verify_chain_segment (verify_columns_against_block) and SignatureVerifiedBlock::into_execution_pending_block_slashable (verify_kzg_for_available_block) run column KZG verification in sequence before signature verification, state transition and newPayload. KZG is not run in parallel with them and joined at import.
impact: Gossip path: nothing to gain. Range sync: KZG for the whole segment (128 columns per block on supernodes) is serial with signature and execution work. Overlapping it would improve sync throughput.

title: Merge pre-import block cache into DA cache
idea: Serve recent and pre-executed blocks to req/resp from the one bounded data availability cache instead of a separate, unbounded pre-import cache.

title: Skip duplicate blob arrival notifications

title: Retry pending block only when all columns arrive
idea: Retry a block waiting for columns only once every sampled column is accepted (after reconstruction finishes), not on each sidecar or at half, so the work queue is not flooded with redundant retries.

impact: Lighthouse does not retry a pending block per sidecar; the DA cache imports when components are complete and reconstruction runs once, so no redundant retry flood exists.

title: Delay RPC fetch of missing sidecars
idea: Delay RPC fetches of missing blobs/columns by a slot-time-based interval (about 0.5 to 1 s, capped by the attestation deadline), so gossip can deliver them first and redundant requests are avoided.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1972 gossip block with MissingComponents starts no RPC fetch
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:2874-2886 the lookup is started only by attestations for a block not in fork choice (about 1/3 slot)

The Gloas column BlockRootUnknown path (gossip_methods.rs:790) and unknown-parent lookups fetch at once, with no wait capped at the attestation deadline.

refute_note: The earlier review missed that Lighthouse does not fetch at block arrival at all. Its lookup starts from attestations at about 4s and needs 3 corroborating peers, and it filters columns already received on gossip. This gives the 'let gossip deliver first' effect without a timer.

title: Request missing blobs immediately on block seen
idea: When a gossip block arrives, enqueue a peer request for missing blobs at once instead of waiting for the availability wait to expire.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1972 MissingComponents only traces a log, no request
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:921 lookups start only from attestation/unknown-parent messages

Lighthouse relies on EL getBlobs and gossip columns first, so a delayed trigger would be needed to avoid wasted requests.

title: Pull late block when blobs arrive first
idea: If blobs arrive on gossip but the block does not arrive by a cutoff, fetch the block and remaining blobs from peers instead of waiting.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1241-1246 a Gloas gossip column for an unknown block root returns BlockRootUnknown
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1386-1392 the same for partial columns ('Block not known, trigger lookup')
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:778-793 BlockRootUnknown sends UnknownBlockHashFromAttestation to start a block lookup
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1173-1185 the partial column path does the same
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:921-925,1036-1056 the lookup starts after peer corroboration
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1016-1023 a Fulu column with a known parent goes to the DA checker as MissingComponents and starts no block lookup
gap: Gloas already does this: a column for an unknown block root starts a block lookup at once, with no cutoff. Fulu, the live fork, does not. A Fulu column carries a signed header, so with a known parent it verifies without the block, sits as MissingComponents, and the block is fetched only when attestations arrive. Add a cutoff timer after the first Fulu column for an unseen block that sends search_unknown_block for that root.

refute_note: Found the Gloas and partial-column BlockRootUnknown path, which starts a lookup from a sidecar of an unknown block. The earlier review searched only UnknownParentSidecarHeader. Fulu remains uncovered, so the verdict is partial.

title: Fetch missing blobs immediately for past slots
idea: When tracked data belongs to a past slot, fetch missing blobs at once instead of waiting the gossip delay.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:359 new_current_lookup creates the lookup and requests at once, no gossip-delay wait
impact: Lookups for past-slot roots have no availability wait, so nothing to remove.

title: Fetch missing columns within the slot
idea: Run the missing-column fetcher every second and request missing custody columns by root after a grace of half the time to the attestation deadline, instead of waiting a minute.
measured_best: block stayed unavailable for over a minute before (pr:caplin#24830)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:2874-2886 an attestation for a block that is pending in the DA checker (not in fork choice) starts a lookup within the slot
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:956-992 custody_lookup_request fetches only the custody columns that are not yet cached
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1023,1505-1518 reconstruction is queued (QUEUED_RECONSTRUCTION_DELAY 150ms) when columns are missing
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:805-842 there is no periodic missing-column tick
gap: There is no periodic fetcher that scans the DA checker for blocks with missing custody columns. Recovery inside the slot depends on attestations that reference the block, from at least 3 peers. Add a 1s tick that scans pending components past a grace period and issues custody by-root requests, so recovery does not depend on attestation traffic.
impact: Low to medium. The minute-long wait that Caplin fixed does not occur in Lighthouse when attestations flow. A tick would help only when few attestations reference the block, for example a late block or a small or isolated set of peers.
refute_note: The earlier review missed the following: when a block is stuck in the DA checker, gossip attestations for it fail with UnknownHeadBlock, and that already starts an in-slot lookup that fetches only the missing custody columns. This is event-driven, not periodic.

title: Disable blob tracking after retention passes
idea: After the blob retention window has passed beyond the fork that removed blob sidecars, swap in no-op blob sidecar managers and pools to stop their upkeep.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:285 PendingComponents allocates blob vec per block
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3255 prune_blobs by DA boundary
impact: Blob sidecars are not removed by any fork in Lighthouse's design; blob tracking is a few empty vectors per pending block, so a no-op swap saves almost nothing.

title: Disk-backed blob quarantine
idea: Persist quarantined blob sidecars in a database table keyed by block root and index, deleted at finalization, so the quarantine does not hold them all in memory.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:349 critical is an in-memory LruCache, no disk table
impact: Lighthouse deliberately removed disk overflow (sigp#5891) and bounds the in-memory LRU; a disk quarantine would go against that design.

title: Memory-only bounded LRU for pending components
idea: Remove the disk overflow of the pending availability cache and keep only a bounded in-memory LRU, removing the disk I/O.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:349-376 DataAvailabilityCheckerInner holds only RwLock<LruCache>, no store
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/mod.rs:103-118 Gloas pending cache also memory-only LruCache
impact: There is no disk I/O for pending components.

title: Remove duplicate column sidecar stores

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:68 single DA cache is the store for pending columns
impact: No second long-lived column store found in sync; fork choice does not hold columns. Not exhaustively traced.

title: Evict DA entries exactly when import completes
idea: Keep a block's pending components and sampling tracker in the availability cache until fork choice import completes, then remove them at once (otherwise LRU/finality), holding the write lock only for the insert. This prevents re-downloads and keeps the cache from growing.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:540 comment: components are never removed manually, only LRU

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:557 write lock held only for the insert, then downgraded
gap: Lighthouse keeps entries (deliberately, to avoid a re-insert race) until LRU/finality, so re-downloads are prevented and the write lock is short, but entries are not freed at import completion. Could remove in the import-complete path via a remove on overflow_lru_cache after fork choice import, if the race is handled.
impact: Only memory: a few tens of MB of columns held until finality; no CPU saving.

title: Wait on store events instead of polling

title: Request sampled columns concurrently
idea: Request and verify the sampled data columns from peers concurrently, not one after another, so sampling finishes inside the slot.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:240 continue_requests groups all pending columns by selected peer
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:295 one data_column_lookup_request per peer issued in the same pass, all in flight together
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:540 range sync issues column by-range requests alongside block requests
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:420 custody_lookup_request started as soon as the block is downloaded
impact: Lighthouse does not do separate peer sampling; custody column fetches go to many peers at once.

title: Fetch payload envelope and columns in parallel
idea: For Gloas blocks, request the execution payload envelope and the block's data columns at the same time instead of one after the other.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:398 data request starts once block is downloaded (peek_downloaded_data), not imported
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:455 payload envelope request starts on the same condition in the same continue_requests call
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:481 only envelope processing waits for block import
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:540 range sync BlocksAndEnvelopesAndColumns issues envelope and column by-range requests together
impact: Envelope and columns download concurrently on both lookup and range sync paths.

title: Reconstruct only requested blobs for blob API
idea: When serving blobs through the API, recover only the requested blob rows (cell recovery only for those rows) instead of reconstructing all blobs of the block.
measured_best: Half columns, 72 blobs: all 2.84 s vs single blob 73 ms; half of blobs 1.48 s (pr:lodestar#8567)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/kzg_utils.rs:767-822 reconstruct_blobs_with_indices recovers cells only for the requested row indices
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/kzg_utils.rs:829-842 reconstruct_blobs uses blob_indices_opt
beacon_node/http_api/src/block_id.rs:415-441 blobs endpoint maps versioned_hashes to indices and passes them
beacon_node/http_api/src/block_id.rs:371 blob_sidecars endpoint calls reconstruct_blob_sidecars with requested indices
impact: Single-blob API requests recover one row instead of all blobs.

title: Request only custody cells from EL getBlobs
idea: Use engine_getBlobsV4 with a per-blob cell bitmap so the EL returns only the cells for the node's custody columns instead of full blobs.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:158-169 uses fetch_and_process_blobs_v4 when the EL supports engine_getBlobsV4
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:420-436 CustodyColumnsBitArray built from custody_columns_indices and passed to get_blobs_v4
impact: EL returns only custody cells, which cuts EL-to-CL transfer and skips local cell derivation.

title: Partial data column dissemination at cell granularity
idea: Exchange data columns as gossipsub partial messages so peers send and request only the cells the other side lacks (tracked with per-peer bitmaps, served from held columns, verified with partial KZG checks) instead of whole column sidecars.
measured_best: Tested on Hoodi and Sepolia; 'advantageous', no reports of reduced performance (pr:lighthouse#9896)
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/partial.rs:3 gossipsub partial_messages Partial/Metadata implementation
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:374-375 enable_partials_for_topic for column topics; :907 publish_partial
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:939-985 full columns republished as partials; :1050-1134 partial verification and getBlobs trigger
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/partial_data_column_assembler.rs assembler
beacon_node/src/cli.rs:693-701 --enable-partial-columns default true
impact: Peers send only missing cells, which cuts column bandwidth.

title: Pass KZG commitments into DA check, skip DB read
idea: Pass the block's KZG commitments directly into the data availability check on import instead of reloading and decoding the block from the database.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:34 commitments read from the in-memory pending block
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:643 verify_columns_against_block takes commitments from the block/bid passed in
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1572 load_gloas_payload_bid checks pending_payload_cache then early_attester_cache before falling back to store, and caches the result
impact: No DB reload of the block on the import path; Gloas gossip columns hit an in-memory bid cache first.

title: Cooldown peers that return empty column responses
idea: After a by-root column request returns zero sidecars, exclude that peer for a short cooldown in peer selection so download loops do not re-ask it many times per second.
measured_best: one peer got 2,351 empty by-root requests in a minute (pr:caplin#24992)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:243 empty response counted as success; comment admits many retries
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:238 select_column_peer has no empty-response cooldown
gap: Record a per-peer last-empty time in ActiveCustodyRequest and skip such peers in select_column_peer for a few seconds.
impact: Fewer redundant DataColumnsByRoot requests during lookups; small CPU and bandwidth gain.

title: Filter column request peers by earliest available slot
idea: Select peers for sidecar requests using the earliest available slot they advertise in status, so requests do not go to peers that pruned the data.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/peerdb/sync_status.rs:34-40 has_slot uses earliest_available_slot
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/peerdb/peer_info.rs:343 is_synced_or_advanced_with_available_slot
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/peerdb.rs:255 synced_peers_for_epoch; :297 good_custody_subnet_peer(subnet, slot)
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:364 select_column_peer uses get_custodial_peers(column, block_slot)
beacon_node/network/src/sync/backfill_sync/mod.rs:225,883 and custody_backfill_sync/mod.rs:1042 synced_peers_for_epoch
impact: Column requests avoid peers that pruned the data.

title: Rank column peers by historical response rate
idea: Choose peers for column requests by past success rate (columns received versus requested), using free request capacity only as tiebreaker.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:353 select_column_peer ranks by concurrency limit, lookup_peers, per-lookup peer_attempts, random hash
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:578 select_columns_by_range_peers_to_request ranks by per-batch peers_to_deprioritize (batch.failed_peers), concurrency limit, random
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/peerdb.rs:297 good_custody_subnet_peer filters only by connected/good gossipsub score/custody/synced
gap: Failure memory is per-lookup (peer_attempts) or per-batch (failed_peers) only; global peer score is a coarse filter. Keep per-peer columns-received/requested counters (PeerDB or SyncNetworkContext) and sort on them in select_column_peer and select_columns_by_range_peers_to_request before the random tiebreak.
impact: Fewer failed custody column requests and retries in lookups and range sync; small sync latency gain, not CPU.

title: Persist columns before pruning
idea: Write new data columns to storage before running pruning, so a pruning pass never deletes data that is not stored yet.
evidence: store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3277 try_prune_blobs only prunes epochs older than min(DA boundary - margin, split)
beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:213 run on finalization in migrator thread
impact: Pruning only touches data older than the split, never data about to be written, so the ordering race does not exist.

title: Prune stale DA and quarantine entries by finality or expiry
idea: Prune the column quarantine, pending availability cache and related per-root caches on every finalization or pruning pass by slot or epoch, not only at a size threshold, so entries for blocks that never arrive cannot accumulate.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:693-751 availability_cache_maintenance_service runs every epoch with cutoff max(finalized+1, DA boundary)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:720-737 do_maintenance removes entries by epoch
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/partial_data_column_assembler.rs:256 assembler do_maintenance
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1615 observed_column_sidecars.prune; :1656 pending_payload_cache.do_maintenance
impact: Pending DA and assembler entries for blocks that never arrive are dropped each epoch, in addition to the LRU cap.

title: Store only original columns and rebuild extension on demand
idea: On supernodes, store only the first-half (original) data columns plus the extension columns' KZG proofs, and rebuild the extension columns on demand with deduplicated work, about halving column storage.
measured_best: ~508 GB to ~260 GB stated in #10137 for 14 blobs (pr:teku#10132)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:959-1011 put_data_column(s) writes every custody column sidecar in full to DBColumn::BeaconDataColumn
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1348-1371 get_data_columns/get_data_column read the store directly; no rebuild step
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:786,846 DeleteDataColumns only for pruned or abandoned-payload blocks, not for extension columns
beacon_node/http_api/src/block_id.rs:370,436 reconstruction from stored columns only to serve blobs over HTTP, not to save storage
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/kzg_utils.rs:889 reconstruct_data_columns used only by the in-memory DA checker / pending payload cache
gap: Supernodes store all 128 columns. To halve storage: persist only columns 0..63 plus the extension cell KZG proofs, and rebuild columns 64..127 in the hot_cold_store get_data_column(s) read path (RPC DataColumnsByRoot/ByRange and HTTP), with a dedup of concurrent rebuilds per block root and an LRU of rebuilt columns; needs a DB schema change and a migration.
impact: Supernode column storage roughly halves (Teku: ~508 GB to ~260 GB at 14 blobs); no effect on non-supernodes; adds CPU on serving extension columns.

title: Clean legacy unpruned column buckets at startup
idea: At startup, delete in batches columns in old storage buckets that the regular pruner never covers.
measured_best: 55,680 expired columns across 435 roots found on Hoodi (pr:lodestar#10223)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:261 single DBColumn::BeaconDataColumn
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1349 DeleteDataColumns in regular pruning
gap: Lighthouse uses one column DB bucket with no legacy unpruned buckets.
impact: None.

title: Blob pruning at startup policy
idea: Decide whether to run a blob pruning pass at startup: run one to remove blobs past retention when no new saves trigger pruning, or skip it to avoid a full directory scan at boot.
evidence: store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3277 prune driven by oldest_data_slot in DB info, no directory scan
hot_cold_store.rs:3300 should_prune uses epochs_per_blob_prune
impact: Blobs and columns live in a KV DB tracked by oldest_data_slot; there is no filesystem scan at boot.

title: Skip rebroadcast of columns already seen on gossip
idea: Before publishing columns built from EL blobs or reconstruction, skip those already received on gossip (mark them in the gossip seen cache) and those not from the current slot.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:1264-1322 publish_data_columns_gradually filters each batch by observe_gossip_data_column (PriorKnown skipped)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:632-650,710-732 EL-built columns deduped against gossip-observed and DA-cached indices
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:216 RPC/sync path calls fetch with publish_blobs=false
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1510 reconstruction (which publishes) is triggered only from gossip
impact: Avoids redundant column publishing bandwidth.

title: Retain sidecars for backfill window
idea: When backfill is required, keep sidecars in the quarantine back to the minimum request epochs instead of pruning at finalization, so backfill does not refetch them.
evidence: beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs no quarantine of sidecars; imported columns persisted to DB via put_data_columns (store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:985)
impact: Lighthouse has no sidecar quarantine; columns for imported blocks are stored in the DB and are not refetched by backfill.

title: Query columns by slot range during sync
idea: Request data columns by slot range during sync instead of one by-root request per block.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_sidecar_coupling.rs:236-262 range batch collects all data-bearing block roots and issues one custody_lookup_request
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:294-304 one DataColumnsByRoot request per peer carrying all block_roots of the batch
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:1606-1640 custody backfill uses DataColumnsByRange
impact: Forward range sync and backfill do not send one request per block; they send one batched request per peer per epoch.

title: Reconstruct without holding the DA cache lock
idea: Run erasure-coding reconstruction outside the availability cache write lock and recheck the cache before publishing, so other columns keep being processed and duplicates are not published.
measured_best: Logs show reconstruction blocked incoming column processing (~500ms between verify at 15.781 and reconstructed at 16.280) (pr:lighthouse#5986)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:592 check_and_set_reconstruction_started clones columns under the write lock, then releases it
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:565 reconstruct_columns runs outside the lock
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:583 Fulu path rechecks cached_data_column_indexes after reconstruction
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/mod.rs:482 Gloas path takes existing_column_indices from the pre-reconstruction snapshot
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/mod.rs:512 Gloas filter uses the stale snapshot; no recheck before import and publish
gap: Gloas PendingPayloadCache::reconstruct_data_columns does not re-read the cache after reconstruction, so columns that arrived during the ~500ms recovery are imported and published again (gossipsub dedups the publish, so the cost is small).
impact: Avoids re-import and duplicate publish attempts of columns received during Gloas reconstruction.

title: Reconstruction queue capacity one
idea: Limit the beacon processor reconstruction queue to one item so bursts do not queue many expensive reconstruction tasks.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_queue.rs:381 column_reconstruction_queue: 1
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_queue.rs:522 LifoQueue::new(column_reconstruction_queue)
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1352 Work::ColumnReconstruction pushed into that queue
impact: At most one reconstruction task is queued, and the newest one replaces older ones.

title: Wall-clock timeout on column reconstruction
idea: Bound column reconstruction with a wall-clock timeout checked before each per-blob task and while waiting for results, so slow recovery cannot stall the node.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3785 reconstruct_data_columns awaits spawn_blocking_with_rayon_async on HighPriority pool with no timeout
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:537 reconstruct_data_columns: timer metric only, failure resets via handle_reconstruction_failure, no deadline
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:107 RECONSTRUCTION_DEADLINE is a start trigger (1/4 slot), not an abort
gap: No wall-clock bound on the reconstruction itself. Check a deadline per blob row in kzg_utils::reconstruct_data_columns / around the awaited rayon task, and on expiry abort and reset reconstruction state.
impact: Only matters for supernodes/semi-supernodes under slow recovery; protects the HighPriority rayon pool from stalls.

title: Minimum custody with full-subnet sampling mode
idea: Offer a mode that custodies the minimum column count but subscribes to 64 column subnets to reconstruct all columns, serving fewer RPC requests than a supernode.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/custody_context.rs:231 NodeCustodyType::SemiSupernode custodies and advertises number_of_custody_groups/2
beacon_node/src/cli.rs:63 --semi-supernode flag
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/globals.rs:68 sampling_subnets derived from spec sampling_size_custody_groups(cgc), no separate override
gap: Semi-supernode reaches reconstruction by advertising and serving 64 columns. No mode keeps the advertised cgc at the minimum while subscribing to 64 subnets; would need a sampling-subscription count decoupled from the advertised cgc in CustodyContext/NetworkGlobals.
impact: Reconstruct-capable node with fewer RPC serving duties; saves upload bandwidth versus semi-supernode.

title: Batch several epochs per missing-column refill
idea: When requesting missing columns, request several epochs (for example 3) per batch instead of one.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/custody_backfill_sync/mod.rs:40 CUSTODY_BACKFILL_EPOCHS_PER_BATCH=1
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:30 EPOCHS_PER_BATCH=1
gap: Raise CUSTODY_BACKFILL_EPOCHS_PER_BATCH (and its uses at lines 306-582) to 3; check batch size limits of columns-by-range.
impact: Fewer round trips during custody backfill only; a rare path, small gain.

title: Remove blob archival semaphore
idea: Remove the semaphore that throttles blob archival when it is no longer needed, and add sanity checks on blob segment files.
evidence: beacon_node/store (no blob segment archive; blobs live in the hot/cold DB)
impact: LH stores blobs in its DB, with no Caplin-style blob segment files or archival semaphore.

title: Gloas: check DA on the envelope, not the block
idea: For Gloas, check data availability on the execution payload envelope so the beacon block enters fork choice without waiting for columns, and do not refetch an envelope already held.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:871 Gloas blocks skip MissingCustodyColumns; DA is on the envelope
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/mod.rs:79 envelope DA via data_columns_required_for_bid
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:829 payload_lookup_request skips download only if envelope_is_known_to_fork_choice
gap: payload_lookup_request only avoids refetch when the envelope is already in fork choice; an envelope already held in PendingPayloadCache (executed, waiting on columns) is fetched again by RPC.
impact: Saves a redundant PayloadEnvelopesByRoot request in lookups racing gossip; the main block-without-columns effect is already present.

title: Remove redundant custody request layer
idea: Drop a custody-specific request layer when the sampler already covers the custody columns as a superset.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:987 sampling_columns_for_epoch used directly
impact: LH has no separate custody request layer; sync requests the sampling/custody columns directly.

title: Remove coarse locks from column retriever
idea: Replace the single coarse lock in the column sidecar retriever with finer synchronization so request scheduling and peer search do not serialize.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs (single-owner sync manager, no coarse lock)
impact: Teku Java retriever lock; LH sync runs in one task owning the network context, no shared coarse lock.

title: DA cache state storage: state root plus LRU vs direct
idea: Decide how the pending-availability cache keeps states: a state root with a small LRU and replay on miss, or full states held directly when tree-states share memory, avoiding a redundant layer.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification_types.rs:372 BlockImportData holds state: BeaconState<E> directly
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/ (only overflow_lru_cache.rs and error.rs; no state_lru_cache)
impact: The redundant state LRU/replay layer was removed in favour of storing tree-states directly (lighthouse#8724).

title: Shorter per-request lifecycle for column recovery
idea: Model column recovery as per-request objects with separate download and rebuild phases and one shorter timeout, so stale requests free resources sooner.
measured_best: timeout 2 minutes rather than 5 (pr:teku#9910)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:537 reconstruct_data_columns uses columns already in cache, no download phase
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:22 ActiveCustodyRequest already per-request
gap: Lighthouse reconstructs from columns already in the DA cache, with no separate recovery request or long recovery timeout.
impact: None.

title: Pool and retry data-unavailable blocks
idea: Keep blocks that failed import for missing data in a pool and retry them after more waiting instead of dropping and refetching them.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:351 pending components held in LRU awaiting missing data
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:200 make_available completes the block once columns arrive
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:398 lookups request only the missing data, not the block again
impact: Blocks missing data wait in the DA cache and complete when columns arrive.

title: Re-issue failed column fetches on availability recheck
idea: Let the availability sampler re-issue column requests on incomplete trackers when availability is rechecked, instead of a fetched flag that blocks retries after a failure.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:241 every column still awaiting download is re-requested on each continue_requests call
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:245 per-column retry bounded by MAX_CUSTODY_COLUMN_DOWNLOAD_ATTEMPTS
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:262 columns with no peer stay pending up to MAX_STALE_NO_PEERS_DURATION and are retried when peers appear
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:917 lookup-level retries after failed download
impact: Failed column fetches are retried per column; no sticky fetched flag blocks retries.

title: Read-only head state for sidecar verification
idea: Verify data column and blob sidecars against the read-only head state when it has the same validator set and shuffling, instead of copying or regenerating the parent state.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1746 with_proposer_cache keyed by proposer shuffling root; state loaded only in miss closure
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1759 miss path uses get_advanced_hot_state (state cache, not a regen on the hit path)
impact: Hit path needs no state at all, which is stronger than using the head state.

title: Data column sampling off by default
idea: Keep peer data column sampling behind an opt-in flag while it is not needed on the critical path.
evidence: beacon_node/src/cli.rs (no peer-sampling flag; grep sampling finds only custody sampling_columns_for_epoch)
impact: LH implements custody columns only, with no separate peer sampling stage to gate behind a flag.

title: Scale blob fetch concurrency with max blobs
idea: Size blob or column fetch concurrency from the max blobs per block config instead of a fixed constant.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:98-117 per-peer MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS limit
network_context.rs:1127 max_blobs_per_block already read from spec per epoch
impact: LH concurrency is capped per peer by RPC limits, not by a fixed fetcher constant; request sizes already use spec max blobs.

title: Serialize column persistence tasks
idea: Allow only one data column persistence task at a time, so bursts of writes do not saturate the thread pool.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:985 put_data_columns writes inline
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1003 data_columns_as_kv_store_ops batched into block-import ops
impact: LH has no separate async column persistence task pool; columns are written within the block import batch, so there is no burst of tasks to serialize.

title: Serve column reads from in-flight writes
idea: Keep recently written column sidecars in an in-memory map and serve by-root reads from it before the DB write completes.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1229 get_data_columns_checking_all_caches checks DA checker, pending payload cache, early attester cache before DB
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4756 do_atomically_with_block_and_blobs_cache writes columns synchronously inside import_block
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:998 block cache populated on column put
impact: By-root reads hit in-memory caches first; DB write is synchronous within import and the DA cache entry is not removed on import (only LRU eviction / remove_block_on_execution_error), so there is no in-flight write window to cover.

title: Single shared buffer for all column sources
idea: Write full gossip columns, partial cells and EL-built columns into one per-slot column cell cache, instead of separate caches, so one buffer serves all sources.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/pending_components.rs:31-32 Gloas PendingComponents.verified_data_columns is a per-block HashMap<ColumnIndex, PendingColumn> of per-cell Option<(Cell, KzgProof)>, partial or full
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/pending_components.rs:96-116 merge_data_columns writes full gossip/RPC columns cell-by-cell into the same PendingColumn store
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/pending_components.rs:122-150 merge_partial_data_columns writes partial cells into that same store
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:368-386 Gloas EL getBlobs columns merge into pending_payload_cache, the same store
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:326-363 Fulu EL columns go into PartialDataColumnAssembler, then full columns go to the DA checker separately
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/partial_data_column_assembler.rs:13-34 Fulu PartialDataColumnAssembler is separate from overflow_lru_cache PendingComponents
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:230-270 Fulu missing_cells_* consults both caches
gap: Gloas already has one per-block cell buffer (PendingColumn) fed by gossip full columns, partial cells, RPC and EL getBlobs. Fulu, the live mainnet fork, still keeps partial and EL cells in PartialDataColumnAssembler and full columns in the overflow_lru_cache PendingComponents, which means double lookups and conversions. Porting the Gloas design back to Fulu is the remaining work. It may not be worth doing as Gloas will replace this path.
impact: Fulu only: saves duplicate cache lookups and the partial-to-full copies per column. Small CPU and memory gain, not a bottleneck. Gloas already has it.
refute_note: The earlier review looked only at the Fulu path. I found that the Gloas pending_payload_cache already uses one cell-level store for all sources, including EL getBlobs. This leaves only the Fulu split, so the verdict stays partial.

title: Singleflight proposer signature verification
idea: Deduplicate concurrent proposer signature verification for sidecars of the same block (singleflight keyed by signing data), so one parent-state load and BLS verify serves all its columns.
measured_best: cache misses reduced (graph); up to 128 concurrent duplicates avoided (pr:prysm#15954)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:197 OnceCell makes the proposer shuffling/state load single-flight
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2490-2501 partial-column headers: a cached verified header for the block root skips re-verification (dedup after the first verify)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:654-668 GossipVerifiedPartialDataColumnHeader::new verifies the signature once, then caches the header in the assembler
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1185 the full gossip column path calls verify_proposer_and_signature for every column and does not check the assembler header cache
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1774-1787 the header BLS verify runs every time it is called
gap: The parent-state load is single-flight. Partial-column headers are verified once per block and then reused from the assembler cache, but this is not single-flight for concurrent first arrivals. Gloas columns carry no signed header, so this applies to Fulu only.

title: Slot-keyed finalized block archive with root and parent indexes
idea: Since finalized history is linear, store finalized blocks/block roots in a slot-keyed table with secondary indexes (block root to slot, parent root to slot). A slot prefix or a slot->root index needs a schema migration (store/src/metadata.rs) and changes to the BeaconBlob/BeaconDataColumn get/put paths.

The mechanism (big-endian slot keys, seek to the cutoff, stream in order) exists for the freezer and LC-update tables, and blob pruning uses it to find its start point. Only the root-keyed prunable tables lack it, so I upgraded the verdict to partial.

title: Run DB compaction rarely

evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:19-23 MAX 7d, MIN 2h, COMPACTION_FINALITY_DISTANCE 1024

title: Compress outside the cache lock
idea: In the state diff cache, do compression and decompression outside the mutex-protected section to cut lock contention.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2424-2468 cold diff read/decode/apply run outside historic_state_cache lock

beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:295-310 get_hdiff_buffer_by_state_root clones buffer or runs HDiffBuffer::from_state (full-state SSZ encode + validators to_vec) while holding the hot state_cache mutex
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:284-292 put_hdiff_buffer deep-clones the buffer under the state_cache lock
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1861-1866,1920-1923 load_hot_hdiff_buffer takes state_cache.lock() for get/put
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1777-1794 store_hot_state_as_diff calls load_hot_hdiff_buffer on the state-store path
beacon_node/store/src/historic_state_cache.rs:33-66 get_hdiff_buffer from_state/clone and get_state as_state (SSZ decode) under the historic cache lock
gap: Diff decode, apply and zstd do run outside the lock. The expensive buffer conversions do not. In the hot StateCache, get_hdiff_buffer_by_state_root runs HDiffBuffer::from_state (it SSZ-encodes the whole state and copies validators, balances and inactivity scores into Vecs) inside the state_cache mutex, and put_hdiff_buffer and the cache-hit path deep-clone multi-hundred-MB buffers inside it too. Block import and get_advanced_hot_state use that same mutex. The cold HistoricStateCache does the same in get_hdiff_buffer and get_state (as_state). Fix: under the lock, clone only the Arc-backed BeaconState (or hold buffers in an Arc), and do the from_state/as_state conversion after the guard is dropped.
impact: Removes lock hold times of tens of ms (full-state SSZ encode and Vec clones) on the hot state cache mutex when hot states are stored or loaded as diffs, typically at epoch boundaries and during non-finality. It also cuts contention for historic-state API serving.

title: Concurrent archive write and hot delete
idea: During finalization pruning, issue the cold archive write and the hot batch delete concurrently instead of sequentially.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3532 migrate_database writes cold ops (3615, 3626) and syncs, then updates split
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:348-372 migrate_database then prune_hot_db run sequentially on the migrator thread
gap: Run prune_hot_db's batch delete concurrently with the cold write in Migrator::run_migration; must stay ordered after the cold sync and split update for crash safety.
impact: Migration runs once per finalization on a background thread; for pruned nodes the cold write is tiny, so overlap saves little, and crash-safety ordering limits it.

title: Configurable in-memory diff buffer cache

title: Store validator immutable fields once, not per state
idea: Do not store the full validator registry (or its immutable fields such as pubkeys and withdrawal credentials) in every stored historical state; store them once in a separate table and persist states with only mutable fields (or with pubkeys zeroed so compression removes them), restoring them on load. This shrinks each stored state greatly.
measured_best: ~20% faster overall ncli_db bench; DB block+state store ~60% faster; DB size 17GiB to 3.9GiB (75% smaller) (pr:nimbus#2297)

beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:440-470 ValidatorsDiff emits only changed validators and zeroes unchanged pubkey/withdrawal_credentials

title: Prune blocks and states older than the retention window
idea: By default (unless archive mode), continuously delete finalized blocks, states and similar large tables older than a retention window (MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS, weak subjectivity period or a fixed count), at finalization or in a background job. The database stays roughly constant size instead of growing without bound.
measured_best: caps database usage at around 60-70gb (pr:nimbus#4445)

The only freezer-state pruning is the manual prune-states command, which deletes all of them. Add an automatic retention pass that deletes old BeaconBlock and cold state entries and moves the anchor forward.
impact: Database growth of non-archive nodes would be bounded; little runtime effect.

title: Defer post-finalization archival within slot
idea: Schedule block/state archival triggered by finalization later in the slot instead of at slot start, so it does not contend with time-critical duties.

refute_note: Read the whole migrator thread loop and the after_finalization path, and grepped migrate.rs for slot_clock, sleep and delay. The only batching is notification coalescing, and there is no time-of-slot deferral.

title: State delta against snapshot, not parent
idea: Store each non-snapshot state as a delta against the nearest snapshot on its branch rather than against its parent, so a cold read applies one delta instead of folding a chain of deltas.

title: Drop in-memory index for archived block range

title: No delta encoding before general compression
idea: Do not delta-encode balances in stored state snapshots when a general compressor (Snappy) is applied anyway; the delta pass costs much more CPU on load than it saves.

title: Store data column sidecars as flat files
idea: Store data column sidecars as flat files outside the KV DB (for example all columns of a block in one file with an offset table, in epoch directories), and prune by deleting whole files or directories. This avoids DB compaction and inode exhaustion and allows partial column reads.

beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:261 DBColumn::BeaconDataColumn

gap: No flat-file sidecar store. Add a per-epoch directory file store (one file per block with offset table) behind put_data_columns/get_data_column/prune paths in hot_cold_store, replacing the BeaconDataColumn KV column in blobs_db; prune by unlinking epoch dirs.
impact: Removes per-key deletes and leveldb/redb compaction on the blob DB; enables partial column reads. Lighthouse already isolates columns in a separate blobs_db, so compaction does not touch hot/cold state DBs; real gain is uncertain.
refute_note: Checked store/src/database (only leveldb_impl, redb_impl), all fs::create_dir_all/File writes in beacon_node (only debug SSZ dumps and network dirs), and the blob pruning path. Only related mechanism is the separate blobs_db KV instance, which is not a flat-file store.

title: File datastore for persisted states

store/src/hdiff.rs:316 diffs in BeaconStateDiff KV column

impact: Slightly less LevelDB compaction/write amplification for big snapshot values; small and unmeasured.

title: Periodic SQLite WAL checkpoints during bulk writes
idea: During pruning tools and backfill, checkpoint the WAL periodically so it stays small and no multi-minute checkpoint is needed at the end or at startup.
measured_best: stated: avoids a startup checkpoint of a few minutes (pr:nimbus#3516)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:329 - hot/cold DBs are leveldb/redb, no SQLite in beacon store
impact: Nothing to checkpoint: no SQLite WAL in the beacon DB (only the validator client slashing protection uses SQLite, not bulk-written).

title: Flat per-epoch span records in slasher DB
idea: Store slasher min/max spans as one flat record per epoch for all validators instead of an index entry per validator per epoch, reducing DB indices and attester-slashing detection I/O.
measured_best: SetValidatorSpan 235 ns/op; SaveEpochSpans 27 ms/op (pr:prysm#6061)
evidence: slasher/src/array.rs:15-47 spans stored as 2D chunks of K validators x C epochs (Vec<u16> distances)
slasher/src/array.rs:159-177 one compressed DB record per chunk
impact: None left: chunked span records already collapse per-validator-per-epoch entries into far fewer DB records.

title: Lazy-load finalized validator list
idea: Load the finalized validator list from the DB only when needed instead of eagerly at startup.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:55-81 - load_from_store reads all pubkeys at startup
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:87-100 - only new validators beyond cache len are imported
impact: No separate finalized validator list in the DB; the pubkey cache is needed for gossip signature checks of any validator, so lazy loading is not usable. (Startup load is sequential point reads plus decompression, a different optimisation.)

title: Do not preload all block summaries at startup
idea: Read block summaries from the database on demand instead of loading all of them into memory at startup.
measured_best: RSS 1.56 GiB -> 1.11 GiB; DAG load 6m45s -> 7m00s (pr:nimbus#3164)
