impact: No startup preload of block summaries; fork choice is restored from the persisted proto-array.

title: Lazy branch nodes for reloaded tree states
idea: When loading a finalized state stored as tree nodes, create lazy branch nodes that fetch children from the DB only on access instead of loading the full tree.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:173 HDiffBuffer::from_state/as_state work on SSZ bytes
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2235 load_cold_state_as_snapshot deserializes whole SSZ state

impact: None: Lighthouse does not store states as DB-resident tree nodes; milhouse trees are built from SSZ bytes.

title: Lazy demand-driven warming of known-branch cache
idea: Do not scan all stored branch keys at startup to prefill the stored-node cache; on a miss do a point read and add it, so restarts of archive nodes are fast.
measured_best: startup scan "can take over an hour" on archive nodes (pr:teku#11078)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:197 - states stored as SSZ snapshots/diffs, no Merkle branch node store
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2103-2280 - store_cold_state snapshot/diff paths
impact: Lighthouse does not persist tree nodes, so there is no known-branch cache to prewarm at startup.

title: Size stored-node cache to the full state tree
idea: Size the cache of already-stored Merkle branch nodes to cover a mainnet-scale state tree so unchanged subtrees are skipped on write rather than rewritten after eviction.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2143-2280 - cold states written as snapshot or hdiff bytes, not per node
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:439-524 - validator diffs computed by comparing vectors
impact: No stored-node cache exists in Lighthouse; hdiff replaces node-level dedup.

title: Store finalized states as shared Merkle tree nodes
idea: Persist finalized states as SSZ tree nodes keyed by hash, skipping nodes already stored and empty subtrees, so consecutive states share storage and only changed nodes are written. Historic state requests can then be served directly instead of replaying blocks.
measured_best: Improves access times for ARCHIVE nodes (pr:teku#4580)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:253-333 - HDiff::compute between states
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2258-2280 - store_cold_state_as_diff
impact: Lighthouse shares storage between consecutive states via hierarchical diffs (different design, same goal); node-hash storage would be a redesign with unclear gain.

title: Write finalized validators only when a state is stored
idea: Persist the finalized validator list/records to disk only when a state is actually stored, not on every finalization or update.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:86-99 import_new_pubkeys only processes validators beyond the cache length
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:126-133 new pubkeys staged as StoreOps in the block import batch
impact: None left: Lighthouse has no separate finalized-validators record rewritten on finalization; pubkeys are written once per new validator, and validator data otherwise lives only inside stored states/hdiffs.

title: Persist decompressed BLS pubkeys

title: Persist derived light-client data in the DB
idea: Store light-client bootstrap and update data (sync committees, epoch-boundary headers) in a small DB table at finalization so they are served without historic states or block replay after restart or pruning.
measured_best: "A full database with default settings (129 periods) uses <15 MB disk" (pr:nimbus#3823)

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_server_cache.rs:203
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_server_cache.rs:396
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:834
impact: Bootstrap and best updates are served from small DB columns (sync committee per period, branch per block root, LightClientUpdate per period), no state replay.

title: Pooled buffer for state serialization
idea: Serialize states for archiving and checkpoint persistence into a pooled, reused buffer instead of allocating a fresh large buffer each time.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2148-2151 - state.as_ssz_bytes() allocates a fresh Vec per snapshot
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2193-2196 - same for hot snapshot
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:197 - fresh Vec in HDiffBuffer

impact: Saves a few large allocations per snapshot; snapshots are rare, so marginal.

title: Presize state-diff serialization buffer
idea: Compute the serialized size of a state diff first and allocate the output buffer at that capacity, avoiding repeated growth and copies for large registries.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:198 compress_bytes presizes output via estimate_compressed_size (len/2)
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:390 CompressedU64Diff::compute builds uncompressed_bytes with flat_map().collect(), no exact capacity
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:173 HDiffBuffer::from_state uses as_ssz_bytes (presized by ssz)
gap: Presize uncompressed_bytes in CompressedU64Diff::compute (ys.len()*8) and the ValidatorsDiff buffer, and size the compressed output from a better estimate; currently only the compressed Vec is presized with a fixed factor 2.
impact: Small cut in allocation/copy churn when computing hdiffs at snapshot/diff boundaries during migration; background-thread work, not on the block-import path.

title: Preallocate validator key slice in DB migration
idea: Preallocate the collection with known capacity when gathering validator keys during a DB migration.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs: no validator-key gathering migration
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/schema_change/: migrations do not collect validator keys in a growing Vec
impact: Migration-specific one-off Prysm code; nothing comparable in Lighthouse.

title: Pool and cap ETL sort buffers of history collectors
idea: Share preallocated in-memory sort buffers between the many history-indexing/state-reconstruction collectors via a pool and divide their size, so combined worst-case buffer memory is bounded.
measured_best: 18 collectors * 256mb / 8 = 512mb worst case vs ~4.5 GB (pr:caplin#9217)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs: freezer indexing done by direct leveldb batches, no ETL collectors/sort buffers
beacon_node/store/src/reconstruct.rs: state reconstruction writes batches, no per-index collectors
impact: Lighthouse has no ETL-style collectors with large sort buffers, so there is no combined buffer memory to pool or cap.

title: Pool compression decoders, share one low-memory encoder
idea: Reuse zstd/compression decoders from a pool instead of creating one per call, and use a single shared, reset encoder with a small window instead of pooling large encoders. This bounds memory while keeping read throughput.
measured_best: Decoder pool gave 2x throughput; encoder pool caused high memory (pr:caplin#16023)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:198-213 compress_bytes/decompress_bytes create a fresh zstd Encoder/Decoder per call
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2152 Encoder::new per snapshot write
no pool anywhere in beacon_node (grep Decoder::/Encoder::)
gap: Keep a reusable zstd Decompressor (or bulk::Decompressor) per thread or in a pool and use it in StoreConfig::decompress_bytes; optionally share one reset encoder for compress_bytes.
impact: Cuts per-call zstd context allocation on historic state loads (HTTP state queries, reconstruction); modest, probably single-digit percent of diff apply time.

title: Finer-grained snapshot retirement schedule
idea: Retire DB data into snapshot files on a short ticker with a small, consistent merge limit so the work is spread out instead of large infrequent batches.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:247: DBColumn - cold data in leveldb columns, no snapshot files
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs: migrate_database moves finalized data to freezer per finalization
impact: Lighthouse has no snapshot file retirement; freezer migration already runs per finalization (every few epochs), so no scheduling to refine.

title: Retire snapshot segments one at a time
idea: Retire backlogged segments one at a time, reopening snapshots and pruning the DB after each, so DB space is reclaimed early and failures keep prior work.
measured_best: backlog of 72 segments took >8 hours with no progress (pr:caplin#24586)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs: no segment/snapshot retirement; freezer migration is incremental per finalized range
impact: No snapshot segments exist in Lighthouse, so there is no backlog to retire one at a time.

title: Parallel compression of backlogged segments
idea: When the retirement backlog spans multiple chunks, compress segments with several workers (single worker at tip) under a shared limiter.
measured_best: 54 min per ~1.45 GB chunk single-threaded, ~2.4 days for 72-chunk backlog (pr:caplin#24316)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs: no segment compression stage; leveldb handles compression internally
impact: No segment compression pipeline in Lighthouse.

title: Native async generator over DB iterator
idea: Wrap the DB range iterator directly in a native async generator, removing a stream wrapper layer per item on range reads.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/leveldb_store.rs and hot_cold_store.rs: iterators are synchronous Rust iterators, no stream wrapper layers
impact: Lodestar JS async generator overhead; Rust iterators are already direct.

title: Strict read-only DB open, drop legacy tables
idea: Open the database read-only without creating legacy tables, and drop unused pre-fork compatibility tables.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/database/leveldb_impl.rs:39: options.create_if_missing = true on every open
beacon_node/store: no read-only open mode found by grep for read_only/ReadOnly/OpenFlags
gap: Add a read-only open option to LevelDB/redb wrappers (open in leveldb_impl.rs / redb_impl.rs) for offline inspection tools in database_manager. Legacy-table part does not apply (no SQLite).
impact: Only helps offline DB inspection tools; no effect on running mainnet nodes.

title: Single bucket per type, fork from serialized slot
idea: Store blocks and states of all forks in one bucket and read the slot from a fixed offset in the SSZ bytes to choose the fork type, avoiding per-fork buckets and extra lookups.
evidence: consensus/types/src/block/beacon_block.rs:133-145 BeaconBlock::from_ssz_bytes reads slot from the first 8 bytes and decodes for fork_name_at_slot
consensus/types/src/block/signed_beacon_block.rs:153-155 SignedBeaconBlock::from_ssz_bytes uses the slot-based decoder
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:3830 BeaconState::from_ssz_bytes reads slot at fixed offset
beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:247 one DBColumn per type (blk, bst), not per fork
impact: None left: one column per object type, fork chosen from the slot at a fixed SSZ offset.

title: Store blocks in framed snappy as on the wire
idea: Store blocks in the DB in framed snappy, the same encoding as req/resp and era files, so serving and exporting need no recompression.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2149 blocks stored zstd-compressed SSZ via Encoder
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:663 get_blinded_block decodes SSZ; no raw-bytes path
gap: Store blocks as snappy-framed bytes and have BlocksByRange/Root serve the stored bytes directly; needs a schema change and a new column format, touching get_block paths in hot_cold_store.rs and the RPC response encoder.
impact: Would skip decode plus snappy re-encode when serving blocks to peers; small, since block serving is a minor CPU cost on a mainnet node and zstd gives better disk ratio today.

title: Answer has-state without loading the state
idea: Answer has-state queries from state summaries or block plus diff-tree position instead of loading and decoding the state.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1087 get_state loads full state
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2992 load_cold_state_slot reads only ColdStateSummary
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3000 load_hot_state_summary exists
beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:65 key_exists on KeyValueStore
gap: Add a has_state(state_root) on HotColdDB that checks the hot summary then cold summary (key_exists) instead of get_state; replace call sites that only test presence. Few such call sites exist.

title: Hoist prune-interval config conversion
idea: Convert the epochs-per-prune setting to its typed value once at config time instead of on every prune check.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:63 epochs_per_blob_prune is a plain u64
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3289 read once per prune call, compared to Epoch arithmetic

title: Read only the last key for latest-slot queries
idea: When only the latest key of a column is needed (e.g. latest finalized state slot), read it with a reverse iterator instead of loading and deserializing the full value.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:88 iter_column / iter_column_from only forward iteration
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2306 cold state lookup is by slot key, no latest-key scan
gap: Add a reverse/last-key iterator to KeyValueStore and use it wherever the newest key in a column is fetched; no hot path currently needs it.
impact: No identified hot path scans a column for its latest key; gain negligible.

title: Leaner state diffs: whole small fields, parallel shuffle
idea: In the historical state diff store, store tiny fields (inactivity scores, slashings) whole instead of as diffs, reconstruct the previous epoch without DB reads, and compute shuffled sets in parallel.
measured_best: removed 15GB; dumps 2048 to 1024 added 5GB; 2x faster participation reads (pr:caplin#8963)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:173 HDiffBuffer::from_state: whole state SSZ goes through xdelta BytesDiff; only balances, inactivity_scores, validators, historical lists are split out
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:385 inactivity_scores use CompressedU64Diff (diffed, not whole)
gap: Lighthouse does not keep a per-field store with participation/slashings diff tables; the idea is specific to Caplin's per-field layout. The only transferable bit (store inactivity scores whole) is a tuning of CompressedU64Diff with unclear gain.
impact: Not applicable to the single-blob hdiff design; no clear mainnet saving.

title: Load small diffs before decoding the base snapshot
idea: When reconstructing a state from diffs, verify and load all required diffs before decoding the large base snapshot, so a missing ancestor does not cause repeated wasted snapshot decodes.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2423 load_hdiff_buffer_for_slot recurses to base first, then loads each diff
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2325 historic_state_cache caches snapshot/hdiff buffers
gap: Pre-check that all hdiffs on the path exist (cheap key_exists) before decoding the snapshot in load_hdiff_buffer_for_slot. Only matters when a diff is missing, and decoded snapshot is cached anyway.
impact: Only saves repeated snapshot decodes on a corrupt/missing-diff error path; not a normal mainnet case.

title: Memoize deserialized diff anchor states
idea: Cache the deserialized anchor/snapshot state per diff level (invalidated on replacement) instead of deserializing it on every reconstruction, and snapshot resume states periodically.

evidence: beacon_node/store/src/historic_state_cache.rs:14
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2423

title: Step by archive-point stride in cold migration
idea: In hot-to-cold migration, iterate archive-point slots by stepping the archive interval from the first aligned slot instead of testing a modulo on every slot.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3574 loop over every slot in state_roots
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3590 cold_storage_strategy(slot) evaluated per slot
gap: Loop must visit each slot anyway to write BeaconBlockRoots; only the per-slot cold_storage_strategy call could be replaced by stepping to diff boundaries. Gain is a few hundred cheap modulo ops per finalization.

title: Manual pseudo-finalization to migrate and prune
idea: Provide an operator-triggered pseudo finalization that migrates hot DB data to the freezer and prunes side chains during long non-finality, bounding hot DB growth.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/lib.rs:2860 POST lighthouse/finalize
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1866 forwards to store_migrator.process_manual_finalization

title: Upgrade the embedded database library
idea: Upgrade the embedded KV database library (mdbx) to a newer release for upstream fixes.

refute_note: Confirmed that across a diff chain only the final step converts (intermediate buffers stay as Vec, cached in hot/cold hdiff buffer LRUs), so the in-place part of the idea exists; the registry rebuild at as_state remains.

title: Snappy-compress stored states and blocks
idea: Compress states (including full snapshots) and blocks with snappy before writing them to the DB and decompress on read, cutting disk size and read I/O.
measured_best: 3gb vs 12gb for 4000 epochs; 3-4x sync blocks/sec (commit:nimbus@360ebd705fd7)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2143 store_cold_state_as_snapshot zstd-compresses freezer snapshots
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2187 store_hot_state_as_snapshot zstd-compresses hot snapshots

beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:42 compression_level comment mentions blocks, but no block path calls compress_bytes
gap: All state storage (hot and cold snapshots, diffs) is zstd-compressed, which covers the state part of the idea and more. Blocks (blinded, with payloads already pruned to the EL), blobs and data columns are written as raw SSZ and LevelDB's own compression is off. Compressing the BeaconBlock column would need a schema migration and changes in the block put/get paths.
impact: Low to medium: blinded blocks compress poorly (signatures, roots), maybe 1.2-1.5x on the block column. That saves disk and some read I/O, little CPU. The headline Nimbus/Prysm wins came from state compression, and Lighthouse already has that.
refute_note: Searched every Encoder/compress_bytes call site in store and beacon_chain: states, hdiffs and fork choice are compressed, block/blob/column paths are not. Also noted that Lighthouse already stores only blinded blocks, which removes most of the block size.

title: Compress slasher span chunks on disk
idea: Snappy-compress slasher min/max span chunks before writing them to the DB.

slasher/src/array.rs:164 ZlibDecoder on load

title: Prefix slasher records with signing root
idea: Store the signing root as a prefix of each slasher attestation/header record so equality checks need no decode of the full object.

slasher/src/database.rs:591 in-memory attestation data root cache for dedup

gap: Attester path already avoids full decode via compact ids and an in-memory data-root cache. Proposer records (proposers_db) still store the bare header and compare after SSZ decode; prefixing a signing root would need a schema bump in check_or_insert_block_proposal.
impact: Saves decoding a 208-byte header per proposal check; negligible, slasher only.

title: Stream block roots from cursor during state load
idea: When reconstructing a state by iterating blocks, stream block roots from the DB cursor and stop at the needed block, instead of collecting all roots first.

title: Walk parent-child index between finalized checkpoints
idea: Compute newly finalized block roots by walking the parent-to-child index between previous and new finalized checkpoints instead of a broader scan.
measured_best: shaves off 10ms from epoch processing time (pr:prysm#13486)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:618 state_summaries_dag.ancestors_of(new_finalized_state_root)

title: Skip legacy read-only tables when pruning
idea: Do not attempt to prune legacy read-only tables, where deletion is impossible or very slow.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:247 DBColumn set has no read-only legacy tables
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3471 prune_historic_states

title: Cap state reconstruction batch to yield to migration
idea: Limit the number of blocks per historic state reconstruction batch so finalization migration runs regularly and the hot state cache does not thrash.
measured_best: Reduced by 32x to 1024 blocks; ~110 epochs to ~3.5 epochs between migrations (pr:lighthouse#6668)

impact: Migration runs between reconstruction batches.

title: Cache regenerated finalized states for sequential reads
idea: Keep recently regenerated finalized (cold) states in a soft/LRU cache so walking forward through historical slots replays from the previous regenerated state instead of from the stored snapshot each time.
measured_best: state by slot API: ~12 s per request uncached vs 0.3-0.6 s sequential (pr:teku#2216)

beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:26 DEFAULT_HISTORIC_STATE_CACHE_SIZE = 1
impact: Sequential forward historic reads replay only one slot from the last result.

title: Reopen DB iterator per migration batch
idea: During block migration, reopen the DB block stream for each batch instead of holding one iterator open for the whole migration.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:520 migration walks hot state summaries DAG, no long-lived block iterator
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3532 migrate_database uses RootsIterator per finalization
impact: Migration does not hold one DB block stream open over a large range; work is per-finalization batch.

title: Batch many small DB writes into one transaction
idea: Group many per-item writes or deletes (attestations, votes, validator index entries, states, slasher spans) into one key-value write batch or transaction instead of one commit per item. This removes per-commit fsync and lock overhead.
measured_best: validator test ~400s down to ~1s (pr:prysm#1732)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1459 do_atomically_with_block_and_blobs_cache takes a Vec<StoreOp>
beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:71 KeyValueStore::do_atomically
beacon_node/store/src/database/leveldb_impl.rs:143 one WriteBatch per do_atomically
slasher/src/slasher.rs:94 one rw txn per slasher batch
impact: Block import, pruning and slasher writes already go in one batch or transaction.

title: Split large prunes into many small transactions
idea: Delete large ranges of old data in bounded chunks, each in its own write transaction, instead of one huge transaction. The writer lock is not held for the whole prune, and the store does not rebalance or crash after a massive commit.
measured_best: naive prune had to delete over 37 million records at once; increments of 100 epochs (pr:prysm#8764)
evidence: store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3410 try_prune_blobs collects all deletes into one blobs_db_ops Vec, one do_atomically (~3452)
beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:~830 prune_hot_db builds one StoreOp batch, one do_atomically_with_block_and_blobs_cache
store/src/config.rs:30 DEFAULT_EPOCHS_PER_BLOB_PRUNE=1, so blob prune normally covers ~1 epoch
store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3501-3520 prune_historic_states stages every freezer key in one cold_ops batch
gap: Pruning is naturally incremental (runs each finalization), but nothing bounds a single batch. try_prune_blobs with force or after a gap, prune_hot_db after long non-finality, and prune_historic_states put the whole range in one write batch. Chunk the ops Vec in these functions (e.g. 1 epoch or N thousand ops per do_atomically).
impact: Only matters for catch-up cases (database_manager prune-blobs/prune-states, recovery after long non-finality); steady-state mainnet pruning is already small. Avoids a huge write batch and long write stall.

title: Spread pruning over slots instead of epoch bursts
idea: Prune a small slice (one slot or one epoch leaving the retention window) on each slot tick instead of a large prune at an epoch or period boundary. Cost is spread out and there are no event-loop or import stalls at boundaries.
measured_best: "taking 1.1s or more at the epoch boundary"; per-slot queries up to ~50ms (pr:nimbus#8852)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:32 DEFAULT_EPOCHS_PER_MIGRATION = 1 (prune each finalized epoch)
beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:30 DEFAULT_EPOCHS_PER_BLOB_PRUNE = 1
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:434 background migrator thread, off the import path
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:808 prune_hot_db deletes all abandoned/finalized items in one atomic batch
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1725 migration and blob prune triggered on finalization update
gap: Pruning runs in a background thread, one finalized epoch per run on a healthy chain (epochs_per_migration and epochs_per_blob_prune default 1). It is not split per slot. After a finality gap, one run deletes the whole range in one atomic batch. Only the reconstruction step is chunked (BLOCKS_PER_RECONSTRUCTION).
impact: Small on a healthy chain, because work is already per-epoch and off the import path. It helps mainly with the large burst when finality resumes after a stall.
refute_note: Checked the migration/blob-prune default frequencies (one epoch), the background thread and the single atomic delete batch in prune_hot_db. The only chunked work is reconstruction, so partial stays.

title: Apply store updates in memory before disk write
idea: Apply block-import and finalization updates to the in-memory store immediately and write them to disk asynchronously, keeping references to pending data to avoid read-before-write races. Block import does not wait on storage I/O.
evidence: beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:~4750 import_block calls store.do_atomically_with_block_and_blobs_cache(ops) synchronously, fork choice write lock held until it returns
store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:~1520 hot_db.do_atomically runs inline under the block_cache mutex
store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1665 store_hot_state puts the state into state_cache in memory first, but the diff/summary KV ops are still written inline
gap: Block import writes block, state diff and blobs to disk synchronously before releasing the fork choice write lock and declaring the block imported; only the state cache is updated in memory first. To copy Teku, import would hand the KV batch to a background writer, serve reads from a pending-writes overlay, and release fork choice before the write finishes. This conflicts with the explicit crash-consistency design (fork choice must not be ahead of disk, issue 2028).
impact: Removes the DB write (BLOCK_PROCESSING_DB_WRITE, tens of ms, more on diff slots) from the import critical path and fork choice write lock, at the cost of crash-consistency risk; modest gain.

title: Slot-indexed canonical block root lookup
idea: Maintain a slot-indexed index (DB table or in-memory array) from slot to canonical block root, updated on head change, reorg and finalization, so by-slot lookups (REST, BlocksByRange, ancestors) are direct reads instead of walking parent links back from the head.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1060 block_root_at_slot_skips_none reads head state's block_roots vector
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1124 block_root_at_slot_skips_prev same fast path
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3096 get_cold_block_root: slot-indexed DBColumn::BeaconBlockRoots in the freezer
beacon_node/store/src/forwards_iter.rs:29 forwards_iter_block_roots_using_state for the unfinalized range
impact: By-slot lookups are O(1) from the head state's 8192-slot vector or the freezer column; a walk happens only for unfinalized slots more than 8192 slots behind the head.

title: Big-endian fixed-width integer keys for range scans
idea: Encode integer DB keys (slots, indices) as fixed-width big-endian so lexicographic key order equals numeric order. Slot-range queries become one ordered cursor range scan instead of a full scan.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3577 BeaconBlockRoots keyed by slot.to_be_bytes()
beacon_node/store/src/forwards_iter.rs:138 iter_column_from BE start slot
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2161 BeaconStateSnapshot keyed by BE slot
impact: Slot-keyed freezer columns use BE u64 keys and ordered range scans.

title: In-memory caches of blocks and states over DB
idea: Keep bounded LRU caches of recently used blocks and states (and latest votes) inside or in front of the store layer, pruned on finalization, so fork choice, import and every read path do not read and decode them from disk on every access.
measured_best: intermediate state memory down 32x; removes read amplification (pr:lighthouse#837)
evidence: store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:74 block_cache: Option<Mutex<BlockCache>> LRU of blocks, blobs, columns
store/src/config.rs:22 DEFAULT_BLOCK_CACHE_SIZE=0 and beacon_node/src/cli.rs:794 --block-cache-size default 0: block cache off by default
store/src/config.rs:23 DEFAULT_STATE_CACHE_SIZE=128; store/src/state_cache.rs state LRU pruned in update_finalized_state (hot_cold_store.rs:434)
store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:87 historic_state_cache; fork choice keeps latest votes in memory (proto_array)
gap: States are cached by default (state cache 128, hdiff buffer cache, historic state cache), and the block LRU code exists, but the block cache is disabled by default, so blocks are read and SSZ-decoded from the DB on each get_blinded_block/get_full_block outside the early attester cache. Change DEFAULT_BLOCK_CACHE_SIZE and the CLI default after measuring memory.
impact: Cheaper repeated block reads (BlocksByRange/Root serving, REST, payload lookups) for a few MB per cached block; small on a validating node, larger on one serving peers.

title: Disable contended store block cache
idea: Make the store-level block cache optional and off by default, because the mutex around it contends when many threads read blocks concurrently.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:22 DEFAULT_BLOCK_CACHE_SIZE = 0
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:229 block_cache Option<Mutex<..>> only if size > 0
impact: The cache is off by default, so readers do not contend on its mutex.

title: Do not store EL-reconstructible execution payloads
idea: Store beacon blocks blinded (without payload transactions and withdrawals), or prune payloads of finalized blocks at migration, since the execution client already holds them, and rebuild the full block from the EL when serving it. This avoids storing each payload twice and cuts disk usage and write I/O.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:527 block_as_kv_store_ops stores blinded block and payload separately
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:868 finalization deletes ExecutionPayload/Payload when prune_payloads

beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1019 Gloas envelope bodies are stored in a separate PayloadBody column and pruned too
impact: Finalized payloads are not kept twice; full blocks are rebuilt from the EL when served.

title: Load blinded block when payload not needed
idea: When a caller only needs block metadata or commitments, read the blinded block from the DB instead of the full block with payload, avoiding a large read and decode.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:663 get_blinded_block

title: Compact block summary table for fast startup
idea: Persist a compact summary (root, parent, slot) for each block in its own table, loadable in one query, so startup can build the block DAG without loading and decoding full blocks.
measured_best: startup times from minutes to seconds (pr:nimbus#1950)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:692 load_fork_choice reads one persisted ForkChoice blob (proto-array with root/parent/slot per node)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1746 persist_fork_choice
impact: Startup rebuilds the block DAG from one persisted proto-array read, with no full block decode.

title: Store each data column/blob sidecar under its own key
idea: Key each data column or blob sidecar by (block root or slot, index) instead of storing the whole per-block list under one key. Serving one column reads and decodes one item, and shared fields are not duplicated.
measured_best: avoids up to x128 more I/O than necessary (pr:lighthouse#5890)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:144 get_data_column_key = block_root||column_index
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:956 data_column_as_kv_store_ops one key per column
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2679 get_data_column reads a single column key
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:943 blobs_as_kv_store_ops still stores the whole pre-Fulu BlobSidecarList under the block root
impact: Done for data columns, the live post-Fulu path. Pre-Fulu blob sidecars remain one list per block, but that path is legacy and expires with the retention window.

title: Key-only DB iteration without reading values
idea: When listing, counting or scanning keys (column indices, state roots, blob counts), iterate keys only and do not read or copy values into memory.

Upstream PR lighthouse#10503 is still OPEN

title: Existence check without loading value
idea: Check whether a state or record exists in the DB with a key-existence call that does not allocate or read the value bytes.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/database/leveldb_impl.rs:121 key_exists uses db.get then is_some (reads value)
beacon_node/store/src/database/redb_impl.rs:128 key_exists uses table.get, no value copy
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:909,915 block/blob existence via key_exists

title: Single cursor pass for bulk state deletion
idea: When deleting many states, collect the keys in a set and traverse the bucket once with a cursor instead of a separate seek or binary search per key.
measured_best: "much faster deletion of states" (pr:prysm#4909)

beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1446 delete_batch dedups keys in a HashSet
impact: LevelDB deletes are tombstone writes in a WriteBatch, with no per-key seek or binary search, so the BoltDB cursor problem does not exist.

title: On-demand DB compaction endpoint
idea: Expose an API endpoint that triggers a background compaction of the key-value store, so operators can reclaim disk after large prunes or migrations.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/lib.rs:2897 POST lighthouse/compaction
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1833 manually_compact_database -> store_migrator.process_manual_compaction
impact: Operators can trigger a background compaction on demand.

title: Manual finalization endpoint to migrate and prune
idea: Expose an endpoint to force a finalization migration to the freezer and prune side chains (with summaries-DAG pruning), freeing hot DB disk during long non-finality.

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1837 manually_finalize_state -> store_migrator.process_manual_finalization
impact: Forces migration and pruning during long non-finality.

title: Hierarchical state diffs in the hot DB
idea: Store hot states as periodic snapshots plus hierarchical diffs, as in the freezer, and skip storing a state whose summary already exists. Hot DB disk footprint and write I/O drop a lot, especially during non-finality.

impact: Done.

title: Share validators via Arc in hdiff buffer
idea: Hold the validator list in hierarchical-diff buffers as reference-counted shared records, so cloning a buffer shares validators instead of copying them.

idea: Keep an in-memory cache of the hot DB hierarchical-diff buffers on the path to the finalized state, so storing a new hot state does not reload and rebuild those buffers.

title: Bound prune iteration to not-yet-pruned range
idea: Start pruning at the first existing key or oldest stored slot and stop at the first entry already pruned or still retained, using an ordered cursor or backward iterator, instead of scanning the whole column on each prune.

title: Prune blobs outside retention window, verify deletion
idea: Delete blob sidecars from the DB once they are outside the data availability retention window, and check that pruning uses the same key encoding as writes and a correct existence check so expired data is really deleted and the blob store stays bounded.

title: Delete abandoned fork blocks and states at finalization

title: Serialize state once without extra copies
idea: When persisting a state, reference large lists (validators, balances, inactivity scores) instead of copying them and serialize once directly into a value buffer preallocated from the known SSZ size. This saves full state-sized copies and shortens state write transactions.

title: Store only hot blocks, regenerate hot states
idea: Do not persist each new unfinalized state on import; store only hot blocks and regenerate hot states by replaying from the finalized (or migrated) state, leaving state persistence to the finalization migration. This trades CPU for disk and write volume.

title: Get state root from next block in replay
idea: During block replay, load one extra block to read the state root it commits to instead of tree-hashing the replayed state.
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/block_replayer.rs:176 get_state_root uses prev_block.state_root() when the state is at the block's slot
consensus/state_processing/src/block_replayer.rs:221 extra leading block skipped and used only for its state root
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2530 load_blocks_to_replay includes the block at start_slot for its state root
impact: None: post-block state roots come from the block, so no tree hash at block slots during replay.

title: Write DB backups without freelist
idea: Write DB backups without copying the free-page list so backup files are much smaller, at the cost of a slightly slower backup.
measured_best: "a bit slower, but results in a much smaller backup file" (pr:prysm#4847)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/database/leveldb_impl.rs and redb_impl.rs: no backup function, only compact
gap: Lighthouse uses LevelDB/redb with no freelist-based backup feature.
impact: none

title: Keep freelist sync on bolt-style DBs and backups
idea: On a bolt-style DB with many deletions, and in its backups, keep freelist sync enabled: skipping it saves write cost but forces freelist reconstruction by traversing every bucket at open, which can take hours.
measured_best: startup freelist reconstruction exceeded 2 hours on Pyrmont (pr:prysm#8629)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/database/redb_impl.rs, leveldb_impl.rs: no freelist sync option
gap: Freelist sync is bolt-specific; neither backend in Lighthouse exposes it.
impact: none

title: Back up DB without large memory snapshots
idea: Do not copy the database through process memory or one long read transaction (for example in an HTTP backup handler); copy the DB file externally or in many small per-bucket write batches. This avoids a large memory spike and keeps the node live.
measured_best: Large memory spike when backing up big DB; no numbers (pr:prysm#11235)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/database/interface.rs: no backup API
gap: Lighthouse has no in-process DB backup handler, so no memory snapshot to avoid.
impact: none

title: Blob sidecars as files with atomic rename
idea: Store blob sidecars as individual files written to a temporary file and atomically renamed, instead of in the key-value DB, keeping writes crash-safe without DB overhead.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:275 blobs_db opened as BeaconNodeBackend (LevelDB/redb)
beacon_node/store/src/database/leveldb_impl.rs:36 and redb_impl.rs:28 are the only backends
gap: There is no file-per-sidecar storage. Blobs and data columns go to a separate KV instance. A filesystem backend with temp-file plus rename would have to sit behind put_blobs/get_blobs/delete and pruning.
impact: Low: blobs are already in their own DB, so this would mostly remove compaction write amplification on that DB.
refute_note: Searched beacon_node and common for fs::rename and tempfile persist use: the only hits are test mocks and account_utils, none in the store. The store has only the leveldb and redb backends.

title: Epoch-keyed blob directory layout with summary
idea: Lay out blob files as period/epoch/root/index and keep an in-memory summary per block root (epoch plus index mask), so startup warmup and pruning list epoch directories instead of reading every sidecar.
measured_best: order of magnitude faster cache warm up time and sub-ms pruning times (pr:prysm#14023)
evidence: store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3340-3430 prune_blobs walks back from end block until an already-pruned block, only touching newly expired blocks
store/src/lib.rs:259 BeaconBlob column in KV DB keyed by block root
impact: Blobs/columns live in a KV database (no file tree), there is no startup cache warm-up and pruning only visits the newly expired range, so a directory layout does not apply.

title: Check DB before regenerating justified state
idea: Before regenerating and saving the justified state, check whether the DB already holds it, so initial sync does not regenerate it at every justified checkpoint.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_fork_choice_store.rs:340-368 set_justified_checkpoint uses balances_cache, loads the state only on a miss and never stores it
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_fork_choice_store.rs:260-300 balances_cache filled from epoch-boundary states during import
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1696-1704 store_hot_state skips the write when the summary already exists
impact: None.

title: Write large states as fixed-size chunks
idea: Persist the finalized or anchor state as several fixed-size chunks (for example 8 MiB) instead of one large value, avoiding huge single byte-array allocations on write and read.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2187 - store_hot_state_as_snapshot SSZ-encodes whole state into one Vec then compresses into one value
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1661 - hot states normally stored as hdiffs, not full values
gap: Split snapshot writes in store_hot_state_as_snapshot/store_cold_state_as_snapshot into fixed-size chunk keys with a count key. Needs DB migration.
impact: Only lowers peak allocation for the rare full snapshots (a few hundred MB for mainnet); the tree-states hdiff layout already avoids per-block full-state writes.

title: Chunked field storage shared between states
idea: Store large BeaconState fields as separately keyed chunks so consecutive states share unchanged chunks, reducing duplication in the DB.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:341-362 the chunked columns (bsr, bbr, bhr, brm) are now DEPRECATED
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2160,2286 the freezer stores BeaconStateSnapshot plus BeaconStateDiff (hdiff hierarchy)
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1705-1706 the hot DB stores the state summary plus hdiffs
impact: None: hdiffs remove the duplication between states more fully than chunking did.

title: Close DB environments on shutdown of loops
idea: Close a persistent DB environment when its owning loop exits so it does not leak goroutines or threads.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/database/leveldb_impl.rs - LevelDB handle closes on Drop, no loop-owned environment
impact: none

title: Always close DB iterators
idea: Close every DB iterator (RAII) in full-scan reads so native memory is not leaked.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/database/leveldb_impl.rs:206-281 - iterators are Rust values dropped by RAII
impact: none

title: One KV instance for hot and finalized data
idea: Keep hot and finalized data as column families or tables in one key-value store instance instead of two, so each instance's native caches and buffers are not duplicated and a write that touches both is one atomic transaction.
measured_best: "should reduce native memory consumption by ~500Mb" (pr:teku#2934)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:270 hot_db = BeaconNodeBackend::open(hot_path)
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:284 cold_db opened separately at cold_path
beacon_node/store/src/database/redb_impl.rs:30 each redb backend is its own database file
gap: Hot, cold and blobs are three separate KV instances, and the redb backend does not share one either. Merging them would need one instance with column prefixes or tables, a datadir migration, and an atomic migrate_database.
impact: A few hundred MB of native cache, and an atomic finalization migration; no CPU gain.
refute_note: Checked HotColdDB::open and both backend constructors: every instance is opened on its own path. Neither backend shares a cache or an environment between instances.

title: Fetch justified block from DB by root
idea: Load the justified block from the DB by its root instead of deriving it from block roots in a state.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:6653 fork_choice.get_justified_block() reads the justified node from proto-array by root
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_fork_choice_store.rs:341-368 set_justified_checkpoint keys by checkpoint root and loads the state by stored justified_state_root (balances cache first)
impact: None; justified block/state are resolved by root, never derived from a state's block_roots.

title: Resolve block slot without loading block or state
idea: Answer root-to-slot queries (for example in state pruning) from fork choice, a slot index, a state summary or the block instead of decoding the full state, so callers that need only the slot do not load large objects.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3000 load_hot_state_summary gives the slot without loading the state
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2992 load_cold_state_slot from ColdStateSummary
beacon_node/http_api/src/state_id.rs:68 Root state id resolves the slot from the hot summary or cold summary
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:537 prune_hot_db builds the DAG from summaries only
impact: None: slot lookups for pruning and the API use summaries, not full states.

title: Defer pruning until block-processing cascade ends
idea: Run heavy state and block pruning only after a cascade of pending child blocks finishes processing, so states just computed for those children are not deleted and recomputed.
measured_best: Fixes devnet loop at 100% CPU (pr:ethlambda#240)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:310 run_migration on finalization in background thread, prune_hot_db at :509 only deletes states not descendant of finalized checkpoint
gap: Lighthouse prunes on finalization in a separate migrator thread and removes only non-viable forks and pre-finalization states, never states of pending child blocks; there is no block-processing cascade that would invalidate freshly computed states.

title: Clean up temporary hot states and their flags
idea: Clear the temporary flag on stored advanced pre-states correctly, delete a state's temporary flag whenever the state is deleted, and prune hot states older than the split slot by scanning hot state summaries. Advanced states and stale flags then do not accumulate on disk or need garbage collection at startup.
measured_best: "Garbage collecting 223069 temporary states" at startup (problem) (pr:lighthouse#6422)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:302 BeaconStateTemporary column deprecated
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:455 advanced state written with put_state, no temporary flag
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:664 every hot summary not descendant of finalized and not a required hdiff slot goes into states_to_prune
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:790 DeleteState for each pruned state
impact: None: temporary flags no longer exist, and advanced and stale states are pruned from the summary DAG at each finalization.

title: Direct lookup for block at exact slot
idea: For a block at an exact slot, do a direct key lookup (plus an in-memory store check for non-finalized blocks) instead of a seek for the latest block at or before the slot.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1050-1110 block_root_at_slot_skips_none: fast path reads head state block_roots (in-memory), else a two-element forwards iter over the slot-keyed BeaconBlockRoots column
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:944-956 block_at_slot then fetches the block by root
impact: None; exact-slot lookups are in-memory for recent slots and a keyed read for finalized slots.

title: Drop orphan block roots without states at startup
idea: At restart, delete stored block roots that have no matching state and do not load those blocks into memory.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_fork_choice_store.rs:212 - fork choice restored from persisted proto-array, not by loading all stored block roots into memory
impact: Lighthouse does not load hot block roots into memory at startup, so orphan roots only cost disk until pruned by finalization migration.

title: Do not store payload-derived state separately
idea: Do not persist a separate state for the post-payload step; regenerate it by replaying blocks, which reduces storage and regeneration work.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/import.rs:293-312 envelope import writes only data columns and StoreOp::PutPayloadEnvelope, no state
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/mod.rs:372 load_snapshot_from_state_root uses the block post-state as pre-state
impact: None; no separate post-payload state is persisted. Gloas-only.

title: Avoid a global or redundant store lock
idea: Do not serialize unrelated DB operations on one global store mutex or an outer lock around an already thread-safe DB handle: remove it where atomicity is guaranteed elsewhere, or give small disk I/O paths their own lock so they do not wait behind large state writes.
measured_best: state dump 420 ms p50 vs envelope 0.2-3.6 ms (contention avoided) (pr:caplin#25436)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:52 HotColdDB fields: hot_db/cold_db/blobs_db are plain handles, no global store mutex
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:74 only cache mutexes (block_cache, state_cache, historic_state_cache)
beacon_node/store/src/database/redb_impl.rs:14 RwLock taken for read on reads and writes; write lock only for compaction (line 197)
impact: None: no outer store lock serializes unrelated I/O; small writes are not queued behind a store-level lock.

title: Embed DB cursor wrapper by value
idea: Store the cursor wrapper inline in the cursor struct instead of behind a pointer, saving one heap object and one indirection per cursor operation.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/database/
impact: Go cursor-wrapper pointer indirection; Rust leveldb/redb wrappers have no equivalent heap object.

title: Retention pruning during finality stalls
idea: When finalization does not advance, still prune states, blocks and attestation tables older than max(finalized, head - window) on head updates, protecting head/justified/finalized and evicting orphans whose parents never arrive, so storage does not grow without bound.
measured_best: Estimated 10,800 states x 100+ MB after 12h without finalization; closed unmerged (pr:ethlambda#175)
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/lib.rs:2860 POST lighthouse/finalize manual finalization endpoint
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1837 manually_finalize_state sends ManualFinalizationNotification
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:292 run_manual_migration runs full run_migration/prune_hot_db at an unfinalized checkpoint
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3307 blob pruning also capped by split slot
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:310 automatic migration only on finalization
gap: Lighthouse has an operator-triggered equivalent (POST /lighthouse/finalize) that migrates and prunes the hot DB at a chosen unfinalized checkpoint during a stall, but nothing automatic: no head-driven retention window that prunes old hot states/blocks while finality is stuck. Blob pruning is also capped by the split, so it stalls too. Missing: an automatic head-window prune in migrate.rs that keeps head/justified/finalized and fork-choice nodes.
impact: Bounds hot DB growth in long non-finality without operator help; hdiff storage and the manual endpoint already reduce the need.
refute_note: Beyond the earlier review I found the manual finalization HTTP endpoint and its migrator path, which prune the hot DB during non-finality when an operator calls them. I also checked that blob pruning is bounded by the split slot.

title: Keep few recent headers in DB, rest in snapshots
idea: Keep only a few recent block headers in the hot DB and serve older ones from immutable snapshot files, limiting hot DB growth.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:558 headers are part of full blocks in DBColumn::BeaconBlock; no snapshot-file layer
impact: Caplin-specific snapshot (static file) architecture; Lighthouse prunes hot DB through finalization migration into the freezer instead.

title: Prune hot states older than finalization
idea: When a new checkpoint finalizes, delete hot-DB states older than the finalized slot (including boundary states), optionally keeping only sparse periodic states, and enable this by default so state storage stays bounded.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:509 prune_hot_db runs on every finalization migration
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:646 required_finalized_diff_state_slots keeps only sparse hdiff layer states
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:664 everything else not descendant of the finalized checkpoint is pruned
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:790 DeleteState batch
impact: None: hot state storage is bounded by finalization by default and keeps only sparse hierarchy states.

title: Optional pruning of historical states
idea: Make deletion of historical (cold) states not needed for the node's mode available, as a configurable option or an offline command, trading availability of old states for much less disk usage.
measured_best: takes a few seconds max on mainnet (pr:lighthouse#4835)
evidence: database_manager/src/lib.rs:440-463 prune-states (with --confirm) calls prune_historic_states
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3471-3525 prune_historic_states sets state_upper_limit NO_RETAIN, deletes freezer state columns, compacts
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3583-3611 migrate_database stores only cold state summaries below state_upper_limit afterwards
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2776 checkpoint-synced nodes default to STATE_UPPER_LIMIT_NO_RETAIN
impact: Nodes can drop all historic states offline and do not store new ones after; checkpoint-synced nodes never store them by default.

title: Index finalized block roots
idea: Maintain a DB index of finalized block roots so finality checks and lookups by root do not scan.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1219-1242 forwards_block_roots_iterator over slot-keyed DBColumn::BeaconBlockRoots
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3577 finalized block roots written to BeaconBlockRoots on migration
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:631-646 is_finalized_block checks finality via slot comparison plus a keyed slot->root lookup
impact: None; finality checks use the slot index, not a scan.

title: Hot state-root to state index
idea: Keep a hot DB index from state root to stored state, pruned periodically, so states can be found by root without regeneration.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3867 HotStateSummary keyed by state root
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1870-1876 get_hot_state resolves by summary then diff/snapshot
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:509-620 prune_hot_db deletes summaries not descending from finalized
impact: None; hot state-root index exists and is pruned at finalization.

title: Hoist DB bucket lookup out of loops
idea: Look up or create the DB bucket handle once per call instead of once per item inside a loop.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/database/leveldb_impl.rs: column is a key prefix, no bucket handles
impact: bolt bucket handle lookup; Lighthouse uses column-prefixed keys in leveldb/redb, no per-call bucket creation.

title: Run metric column scans off the pruning path
idea: Run full O(N) column count scans used only for metrics on a separate low-priority task, not at the end of the pruning cycle, so pruning is not delayed by minutes.
measured_best: scans "can take minutes on large databases" (pr:teku#11171)
evidence: store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:456-506 store metrics set only in-memory gauges (caches, anchor info)
beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs: no column count scans at end of pruning
impact: Lighthouse does not run O(N) column-count scans for metrics, so there is nothing to move off the pruning path.

title: More threads for storage query executor
idea: Give the storage query executor enough threads that concurrent DB reads are not queued behind each other.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/database/ no executor; DB calls run on spawn_blocking in beacon_chain
impact: JVM executor pool for storage queries; Lighthouse reads run on the tokio blocking pool or caller threads, which is sized by the runtime.

title: Dump chain in ascending order with rebase
idea: When dumping or iterating many states, go in ascending slot order and rebase each state on the previous one, which is cheaper for tree-structured states; back the in-memory store with an ordered map.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7840 chain dump calls beacon_state.rebase_on(&prev) while iterating ascending
beacon_node/store/src/memory_store.rs:9 MemoryStore DBMap is a BTreeMap
impact: None; test/debug path only.

title: Partial state getters and cached state hash
idea: Give callers getters for single state fields (validators, balances) and a cached state hash, so they do not clone or rehash the whole state.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:3070 update_tree_hash_cache incremental milhouse hashing
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1087 canonical_root
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs states cloned cheaply via structural sharing
impact: Field accessors return references and state clone is O(1) with cached subtree hashes, so no whole-state copy or rehash.

title: Read only needed vote cache entries from DB
idea: Keep the block vote cache outside the state and read or write only the entries for the block hashes involved, instead of the whole cache per block.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/persisted_fork_choice.rs:1 votes persisted in fork choice, no vote cache in state
impact: Lighthouse keeps no per-block vote cache in the state or DB; votes live in fork choice proto-array.

title: One persist task per arriving sidecar
idea: Spawn a persist task per data column sidecar as it arrives instead of one batched task for all, so sidecar writes do not wait on each other.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:8407 PutDataColumns store op at import
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:985 put_data_columns
impact: Columns are held in the DA cache and written in one op with the block import, there is no separate batched persist task to split.

title: Write-back buffer for state summaries
idea: Buffer state summaries in memory in the DB layer and flush them in one batch (on a count threshold, or with blocks during initial sync) instead of writing each summary on its own.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4751-4756 block, columns and PutState (summary+diff) go in one do_atomically_with_block_and_blobs_cache batch per block
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1307 PutState -> store_hot_state; :1722 store_hot_state_summary pushes one op immediately, no cross-block buffer
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1630-1633 each skipped-slot state written in its own hot_db.do_atomically
gap: No write-back buffer: each block import (and each skipped-slot state) is its own DB batch. A buffer would batch summaries across blocks during range sync and serve reads from it; LH already avoids Prysm's original problem (separate summary transaction) by writing the summary in the block's own batch.
impact: Small: summaries are ~100 bytes and already share the block's atomic write; saving is fewer write batches during initial sync only.
refute_note: Checked the block-import op list and StoreOp::PutState handling: the summary rides in the same batch as the block, which covers the 'with blocks' half of the Prysm idea, but there is no in-memory summary buffer or count-threshold flush anywhere in store/.

title: Persist states only when a block follows
idea: Do not write states produced by empty-slot advancement or attestation-driven processing to the hot DB; store a state only when a block is applied to it. Such states are cheap to recompute, rarely read and bloat the DB.
measured_best: storing states is (very) slow; avoids state database size explosion (pr:nimbus#1860)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:455 put_state of the empty-slot-advanced head state every slot
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1068-1076 put_state -> store_hot_state
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1750-1760 ReplayFrom slots store only a summary; Snapshot/DiffFrom slots store a full snapshot or hdiff
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1698-1706 skips diff computation if summary already on disk
gap: The state-advance timer still persists the advanced (empty-slot) state each slot; it is a summary on most slots but a diff/snapshot when the advanced slot is a hierarchy boundary. That state is not in chain history when a block does follow at that slot. Drop the put_state in advance_head (or defer it until the slot is known to be empty).
impact: Avoids one summary write per slot and an hdiff/snapshot computation+write at boundary slots on the state-advance thread; DB-size impact is small because of hierarchical storage.
refute_note: Confirmed no attestation-driven path persists states (attestation verification uses shuffling/state caches), and that the hierarchical diff scheme makes most empty-slot writes summary-only, which is the partial mitigation; the advance-timer write remains.

title: Persist all fork-choice heads in DB
idea: Store every fork-choice DAG head (not only the canonical head) in the DB so restart does not rediscover side branches and stray block data is not left behind during non-finality.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/builder.rs:245 load_fork_choice restores whole proto-array
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:537 prune uses summaries DAG
impact: Whole fork choice (all branches) is persisted and reloaded, and pruning uses the state summaries DAG, so there is no head set to rediscover.

title: Persist committee caches with stored states
idea: Store committee/shuffling caches together with the state in the hot DB so a state loaded from disk does not need a shuffling recompute.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3865-3871 HotStateSummary: slot, block roots, diff base, previous state root only
beacon_node/store/src/: no reference to committee_cache or ShufflingCache in the store crate
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs: in-memory only
gap: Committee caches are neither stored with hot snapshots/diffs nor is ShufflingCache persisted; a state loaded from disk rebuilds committees on demand. Would need an extra column keyed by shuffling id or decision root.
impact: Saves one shuffling compute (~100s of ms) after restart or on a state_cache miss; rare on a running node.
refute_note: Grepped the whole store crate for committee/shuffling persistence and checked the state cache put path; the only committee data persisted is sync committees for light client, not attester shufflings.

title: Persist deposit cache instead of refetching logs
idea: Store deposit containers in the DB and fill the deposit cache from them at startup instead of re-fetching deposit logs from the eth1 node.
evidence: beacon_node/ls beacon_node shows no eth1 crate
impact: Eth1 deposit log polling and deposit cache no longer exist in Lighthouse.

title: Store EL-fetched payloads when not pruning
idea: When payload pruning is disabled, store execution payloads fetched from the EL in the DB so later requests do not download them again.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:117 prune_payloads default true
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1295 get_payload_for_header from EL
impact: With prune_payloads=false the payload is already stored at import, so EL downloads only arise for blocks imported before disabling pruning; marginal.

title: Persist head, fork choice and eth1 data less often
idea: Write chain metadata (head pointer, fork choice, op pool, eth1 cache, wall-clock time) only when it changes or at coarse points (epoch crossing, every N blocks, shutdown) instead of on every block, attestation or tick. Split large persisted objects so only the changed part is written.
measured_best: "committing less frequently to the database, which should help with contention" (pr:teku#1232)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1564-1566 persist_fork_choice only on epoch transition or reorg
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1720 persist at finalization
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:8463-8466 op pool, custody context, fork choice persisted on Drop
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:687 head persisted as genesis root only
beacon_node/http_api/src/validator/mod.rs:1125 custody context persisted only when custody changes
impact: Metadata writes are already coarse (per epoch/reorg/finality, shutdown). Fork choice is still written as one blob, but only per epoch, so splitting it would save little.

title: Persist data columns on arrival, prune cache after
idea: Write each accepted data column sidecar to disk as soon as it is accepted, and remove it from the in-memory column cache only once persistence is confirmed (with a short retention window). No column is lost to cache pruning and the cache stays bounded.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:351 pending columns held only in an in-memory LruCache
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:8421 StoreOp::PutDataColumns built only at block import
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:985 put_data_columns only called from checkpoint-sync builder (builder.rs:583) and historical backfill (historical_data_columns.rs:121)
gap: Gossip/RPC columns are not written to disk on acceptance; they live in the DA LRU until the block imports, so eviction under load forces refetch. Persisting on arrival needs a hot-DB write in the DA put path plus orphan-column pruning.
impact: Avoids re-download of evicted pending columns; adds disk writes for columns of blocks that may never import; benefit unclear.
refute_note: Enumerated every caller of put_data_columns / data_column_as_kv_store_ops / PutDataColumns: none is on the gossip or RPC acceptance path (the old disk-overflow store of the DA cache is gone).

title: Preallocate slices for block root ranges
idea: Preallocate collection capacity when collecting block roots over a slot range from the DB to avoid repeated reallocation.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/forwards_iter.rs:41 collect::<Vec<_>>() without capacity
beacon_node/store/src/forwards_iter.rs:59 same for state roots
gap: Lighthouse collects the backward iterator into a Vec with no size hint, but ranges are short (post-finalization only). In SimpleForwardsIterator constructors (forwards_iter_block_roots_using_state / _state_roots_) use Vec::with_capacity(end_state.slot() - start_slot + 1).
impact: Saves a few reallocations on short ranges; negligible.

title: Store previous state root in hot summaries
idea: Store the previous state root in each hot state summary so loading a state from disk needs no tree hashing; reading a few summaries is cheaper than building a tree hash cache.
measured_best: tree hash cache costs 1s+ CPU and 300MB+ RAM; summaries read <250ms for 32 (pr:lighthouse#2954)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3867-3873 HotStateSummary.previous_state_root exists
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3743-3860 used only by get_ancestor_state_root
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2078-2084 load_hot_state_using_replay passes no_state_root_iter()
consensus/state_processing/src/block_replayer.rs:176-208 without an iterator, skipped-slot roots are computed with update_tree_hash_cache
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2381-2394 cold replay does supply a state-root iterator
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2016-2020 rebase_on_finalized limits the hashing cost
gap: Hot replay (load_hot_state_using_replay -> replay_blocks) gets no state-root iterator, so every skipped slot between replayed blocks and the advance to the target slot is tree-hashed. A reverse iterator over HotStateSummary.previous_state_root from the target state root could feed BlockReplayer::state_root_iter, as the cold path does. get_hot_state and get_advanced_hot_state also call update_tree_hash_cache after every disk load.
impact: Small: with milhouse plus rebase_on_finalized, only the changed subtrees are hashed. The saving is on skip-slot replays and reorg state loads that miss the cache.

title: Prune hot DB via state summaries DAG
idea: Prune the hot DB without a separately persisted head tracker: after migrating the finalized chain, load all state summaries and delete every summary not descending from finalized, so pruning cannot drift from fork choice.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:509 prune_hot_db
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:537-559 load_hot_state_summaries into StateSummariesDAG
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:590-600 keeps only descendants_of(new_finalized_state_root)
impact: None; head tracker removed, pruning driven by summaries DAG.

title: Prune orphaned execution payload envelopes
idea: On each finalization, delete hot-DB execution payload envelopes whose block is no longer in fork choice, since the finalized-chain walk never reaches them.
measured_best: Observed 17 stale hot envelopes on a devnet node (pr:lodestar#10206)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:707-738 blocks_to_prune = summaries-DAG blocks not descending from finalized checkpoint
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:777-781 DeletePayloadWithSummary for each pruned block
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:830-846 also deletes envelopes of canonical blocks finalized EMPTY
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1357-1366 deletes PayloadSummary and PayloadBody
impact: Envelopes of abandoned forks are removed at each finalization together with their blocks.

title: Prune unreachable data after head rewind
idea: When the stored head cannot be reconstructed at startup and the node rewinds, delete blocks and data between the old head pointer and the resolved head.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/builder.rs:245 load fork choice, head via get_head at :771
impact: Head is recomputed from persisted fork choice; Lighthouse has no startup rewind of the stored head.

title: Prune blocks older than retention window
idea: Delete blocks and associated data older than a retention tail (e.g. min_epochs_for_block_requests or a weak-subjectivity based tail) from DB and in-memory indexes, so storage does not grow without bound.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3119 try_prune_execution_payloads (finalized payloads deleted, the bulk of post-merge block bytes)
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3277 try_prune_blobs (blobs past DA boundary)
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3471 prune_historic_states (freezer states only, no blocks)
database_manager/src/cli.rs:75 subcommands: PrunePayloads/PruneBlobs/PruneStates, no PruneBlocks
beacon_node/store/src/metadata.rs:99 oldest_block_slot only ever moves down via backfill
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:919 delete_block used only for abandoned forks (migrate.rs pruning)
gap: No retention prune for finalized blocks: once stored, beacon blocks (blinded) below a retention slot are never deleted and oldest_block_slot never moves up. Add a retention prune in the migrator that deletes blinded blocks below e.g. current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS via the cold BeaconBlockRoots index and raises anchor oldest_block_slot (status/blocks_by_range already honour it).
impact: Disk only; since payloads are already pruned the remaining blinded blocks are tens of GB on a genesis-synced mainnet node. No CPU/hot-path gain.
refute_note: Searched store, beacon_chain and database_manager for any block retention/prune (prune_blocks, DeleteBlock callers, anchor oldest_block_slot updates, db subcommands); only payload, blob, freezer-state and abandoned-fork pruning exist.

title: Write intermediate states to DB as temporary
idea: Write intermediate states created during block processing directly to the hot DB marked temporary, clear the mark on success, and garbage-collect leftovers at startup, so they need not be held in memory.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1617-1634 skip-slot states stored with store_hot_state immediately
beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:300-305 BeaconStateTemporary deprecated
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:700-703 leftover hot states pruned on finalization
impact: Intermediate states go to disk right away and are not held in memory. Leftovers from failed imports are cleared by finalization pruning instead of a temporary flag.

title: Prune dangling states at startup
idea: At startup, delete states between genesis and the last finalized slot that are not on archive/restore-point boundaries, to shrink the state store.
measured_best: 4000 state keys down to 86 (pr:prysm#4697)

beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1661 store_hot_state: hot states stored as summaries+diffs, finalization migrates and deletes them
gap: Add a startup pass that scans hot state summaries below the split and deletes those not on a snapshot/diff boundary. Lighthouse already deletes non-boundary hot states at finalization migration, so only legacy leftovers would benefit.
impact: Smaller DB on nodes with leftover states; no runtime speed change. Lighthouse's finalization migration already prunes, so little to gain.

title: Prune invalid-block blacklist at finality

evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs: fork choice head handling; no persistent blacklist column in store/src/lib.rs DBColumn

impact: No per-block vote cache is stored in the DB, so nothing grows to prune.

impact: Lighthouse has no slot-to-block live-chain DB index; proto_array nodes are pruned at finality.

title: Store validator pubkey cache inside the DB

title: Raise DB and open-file resource limits
idea: Raise KV store limits (mmap/initial size) and the process open-file soft limit to the hard limit at startup, so the DB does not stall or crash on default resource limits.
measured_best: crash after days on 1024 limit (pr:ethlambda#422)
evidence: validator_client/src/lib.rs:128 fdlimit::raise_fd_limit used only in validator client
beacon_node/store/src/database/leveldb_impl.rs and redb_impl.rs: no open-files or mmap options set
grep fdlimit/rlimit finds nothing in beacon_node or lighthouse/src
gap: Call fdlimit::raise_fd_limit at beacon node startup (lighthouse/src/main.rs or the beacon_node client builder) and log the outcome, as the validator client does.
impact: Avoids too-many-open-files failures with leveldb and many peers/sockets on hosts with a 1024 soft limit; a stability fix, not speed.

title: Slot-ordered range scans instead of per-key lookups
idea: Iterate slot-ordered DB keys with range filters (gt/lt/reverse/limit, streaming) instead of issuing one lookup per slot or scanning a hash-keyed index, for custody scans, pruning and queries.
measured_best: Average ~400 block queries per call before (pr:teku#9797)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/forwards_iter.rs:117 freezer roots scanned by slot-ordered keys
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3366-3410 try_prune_blobs walks ParentRootBlockIterator (one block load per block) and calls key_exists for every column index
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2672-2676 get_all_data_column_keys builds all 128 keys
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2657-2665 get_data_column_keys prefix scan exists but is not used by pruning (and reads values too)
gap: try_prune_blobs does 128 key_exists point lookups per Fulu block via get_all_data_column_keys, where it could do one prefix range scan (get_data_column_keys). It also walks blocks backwards by parent root with get_blinded_block, where it could scan the slot-keyed BeaconBlockRoots range in the freezer. get_data_column_keys uses iter_column_from, which reads column values when it needs only keys; iter_column_keys_from would avoid that.
impact: Fewer DB reads in blob/column pruning (128 lookups per block become 1 seek). Pruning runs in the background, so this is a modest gain.

title: Move blocks hot-to-cold as raw bytes
idea: When migrating finalized blocks from the hot to the cold/finalized DB, copy the raw stored bytes keyed by the known root (use the DB key as root) instead of deserializing, re-hashing and re-serializing each block.
measured_best: Spike: doUpdate took 1522 ms (finalized 306 ms, hot 1216 ms) (pr:teku#7638)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3532 migrate_database only writes BeaconBlockRoots slot->root entries
beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs:257 single BeaconBlock column keyed by root

title: Take block root from DB key on load
idea: When decoding blocks loaded from the DB, set the block root from the storage key instead of recomputing hash_tree_root.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:676 get_block_with decodes bytes only; callers pass block_root explicitly (e.g. store/src/iter.rs:188)
SignedBeaconBlock has no cached root; no canonical_root() on loaded blocks in these paths
impact: Lighthouse APIs take the root as an argument and do not recompute hash_tree_root after load, so there is no rehash to avoid.

title: Reuse computed block root when saving blocks
idea: Carry the already computed block root (a wrapper caching hash_tree_root) into the block save path instead of re-hashing the block there.
measured_best: FullBlock SaveBlock ROBlock -99.99% time, allocs 2069 -> 1; SaveBlocks/64 -22.96% time, -38% B/op (pr:prysm#16300)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:507-521 put_block takes block_root from the caller
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:527-545 block_as_kv_store_ops keys by the given root, with no hashing
impact: None: the block root computed at verification is reused for storage.

title: Readdir-based pruning of bucketed sidecar files
idea: Prune bucketed on-disk sidecar stores by listing the bucket directories that exist instead of iterating every bucket index from slot 0 on each call, avoiding thousands of no-op remove syscalls per slot.
