evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3277 try_prune_blobs, KV-based
gap: Lighthouse has no bucketed sidecar files; blobs/columns live in the KV store keyed by root and pruned in try_prune_blobs.
impact: No equivalent cost exists.

title: Open redb with quick repair
idea: Open redb databases (store and slasher) with the quick-repair option so startup after an unclean shutdown does not re-read the whole DB to verify it.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/database/redb_impl.rs:30 redb::Database::create(db_file), no Builder or repair options
beacon_node/store/src/database/redb_impl.rs:73,146,157,277,297 begin_write() with no set_quick_repair call
slasher/src/database/redb_impl.rs:46 redb::Database::create(db_path)
slasher/src/database/redb_impl.rs:83,98 begin_write() with no set_quick_repair call
~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/redb-2.6.4/src/transactions.rs:1618-1630 set_quick_repair is per-transaction and defaults to disabled
~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/redb-2.6.4/src/db.rs:1050-1063 redb only sets quick_repair internally for its own allocator-state commit

title: Drop DB writes and indexes nobody reads
idea: Remove persisted variables and secondary indexes (e.g. sampling progress, blob versioned hash index) that no query path needs, saving a write per item and the pruning work for it.

gap: Lighthouse has no sampling-progress var or blob versioned-hash index; the only per-block write nobody reads outside finalized checkpoints is the light client sync-committee branch (see db_hot-132). A full audit of other unread columns was not done.
impact: Saves at most a small write per block; gain is marginal.

title: Avoid blinded-block storage layout
idea: Teku found storing blinded blocks (payload separated) slower than full blocks and dropped it, managing size by block pruning instead; check whether the blinded layout costs read performance.
measured_best: PR states it showed worse performance (pr:teku#6617)

impact: Lighthouse deliberately stores blinded blocks with payloads in a separate column; the Teku finding is a design-level tradeoff and changing it would be a storage redesign. Idea is only a check, no change implied.

title: Find highest block at or below slot quickly
idea: Answer 'highest block at or below slot' (e.g. replay base lookup) by seeking a slot index to the target and walking backwards, or with a per-slot bitfield, instead of scanning forward or keeping boundary-root bookkeeping.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3076-3091 store_frozen_block_root_at_skip_slots writes a root for every slot, skipped slots pointing at the prior block
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3096-3102 get_cold_block_root point lookup by slot

title: Avoid memory-hungry DB format

evidence: beacon_node/store/src/database/interface.rs:1 backend is leveldb or redb, selected by feature
beacon_node/store/src/database/leveldb_impl.rs no format-specific cache settings found

idea: Create SQLite key-value tables with an integer rowid (not WITHOUT ROWID) so deletes of large blobs during pruning and reorgs are fast.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/database/ has only leveldb_impl.rs and redb_impl.rs

idea: Write DB pruning as delete-everything-except-keep-set (rowid NOT IN, index-backed max per key) instead of correlated subqueries that scan.

evidence: beacon_node/store/src/database/ has only leveldb_impl.rs and redb_impl.rs

idea: Maintain secondary index buckets (e.g. by parent root, epoch) mapping to data roots and intersect them to answer filtered queries instead of scanning all keys and values.

title: Skip checkpoint state writes during sync
idea: Do not persist checkpoint states while syncing, avoiding large state writes not needed during sync.

What remains is the block-import path: hot summaries plus hdiff snapshots/diffs at hierarchy boundaries are written during range sync too; deferring the diff part while far behind is possible but migration needs those states.

refute_note: Checked the state advance timer, which the earlier review missed: it refuses to advance (and thus to persist the advanced epoch-boundary state) when head is >256 slots behind, matching the Grandine commit's is_forward_synced gate on its checkpoint-state append; import-path hot state writes remain unconditional.

title: Reuse fresh DB state instead of checkpoint download

beacon_node/client/src/builder.rs:423 CheckpointSyncUrl download happens only when there is no chain in the DB

title: Return cached states without deep clone
idea: Return states from the read cache without deep-cloning them on each read.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:275-281 get_by_state_root returns state.clone()

title: Skip writing empty blob sidecar lists

beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2254 iterators only in migration/pruning paths

title: Skip fork pruning with a single head
idea: Skip fork pruning at finalization when there is only one head, since it replays blocks and rebuilds tree hash caches for nothing.

gap: The 2020 pruning replayed blocks via head tracker; current pruning is a pure summary-DAG walk with no block replay or tree-hash cache rebuild, so the pathology no longer exists.

title: Trust local blocks, skip signature work on load
idea: Mark blocks read from the local DB as trusted and skip BLS signature deserialization and checks when loading them; load blocks lazily during state rewinds.
measured_best: 50x startup time improvement, 200x block load time improvement (Initialize DB 187709 ms -> 3815 ms; load block 0.558 -> 0.043 ms) (pr:nimbus#1227)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:663-686 get_blinded_block/get_block_with decode every read with SignedBeaconBlock::from_ssz_bytes

crypto/bls/src/generic_signature.rs:68-74 GenericSignature holds a decoded point, no lazy bytes mode
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:96,571-597 LRU block_cache only avoids re-decoding recently used full blocks
gap: No trusted/lazy decode for DB blocks: every uncached block load decompresses all G2 signatures. A decoder using SignatureBytes on the DB path would be needed. The LRU block cache mitigates repeated loads but is not the mechanism; startup does not replay blocks, so Nimbus's startup gain does not apply.
impact: Tens of microseconds per signature on uncached block loads (RPC serving, replay, migration); minor on a mainnet node.
refute_note: Checked the BLS GenericSignature wrapper for lazy decoding and the store block cache; neither skips signature decompression on a DB read.

title: Skip legacy DB lookups on state write

title: Snappy-compress blocks and states in DB
idea: Compress stored block and state values with snappy by default, shrinking disk size and I/O and speeding sync.

refute_note: Checked the dependency layer the earlier review skipped: the leveldb crate defaults to Compression::No and Lighthouse disables its snappy feature, so there is no hidden storage-engine compression. Enabling LevelDB snappy is an S-effort route needing no schema migration.

title: Compress cached anchor states in memory
idea: Snappy-compress full states held in an in-memory anchor/diff-base cache to halve its memory, at the cost of compression time.

title: Per-entry compression choice (zstd)

title: In-memory cache over slasher span store
idea: Front the slasher span DB with an in-memory cache, flushing writes on eviction, to cut DB reads and writes.

title: Run DB reads off the async executor
idea: Run blocking DB reads (block by root, payload bids) on a blocking thread pool instead of async executor threads so they do not stall the runtime.

But the HTTP block and envelope GET handlers call BlockId::root (store.block_exists, get_blinded_block, block_root_at_slot) and checkpoint_slot_and_execution_optimistic synchronously inside spawn_async_with_rejection futures. These run on tokio workers. Move the BlockId::root resolution into spawn_blocking (or a blocking_task) in BlockId::full_block and in the execution_payload_envelopes handler.

title: Separate block header and body tables

title: Dial discovered peers concurrently

title: In-process p2p calls instead of local RPC
idea: Call the p2p/networking component in-process rather than over a local network RPC, removing serialisation per call.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:141 libp2p Swarm runs inside the same process; network service talks to others over tokio channels, no RPC
impact: Nothing to gain: no inter-process RPC exists in Lighthouse.

title: Do not serialize ENR in peer filter
idea: In the discovered-peer filter hot path, do not serialize each candidate ENR (RLP plus base64); do it only when logging or reporting an error.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/subnet_predicate.rs:17-52 reads ENR fields only; trace! fields evaluated only when trace enabled
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:833-840 eth2_fork_predicate compares fork_digest and dialable addrs, no encoding
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:242 to_string only for bootnodes at startup
impact: No RLP/base64 encoding per candidate in the discovery filter.

title: Cap pending inbound connections and backlog
idea: Cap the TCP listen backlog and the number of pending (not yet upgraded) inbound connections to a small multiple of max peers, so floods do not consume handshake CPU and memory.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:441-459 ConnectionLimits: max_pending_incoming_per_source(2), max_pending_outgoing(16), established limits from target_peers
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/utils.rs:52 tcp::Config::default().nodelay(true) keeps libp2p default listen backlog
gap: No global cap on pending inbound connections and no explicit TCP backlog; only a per-source cap of 2 (a flood from many IPs is not bounded). In service/mod.rs ConnectionLimits add .with_max_pending_incoming(Some(k*max_peers)) and set libp2p::tcp::Config::listen_backlog in service/utils.rs.
impact: Bounds handshake CPU and memory under a many-source inbound flood; no change on normal nodes.

title: Scale per-subnet peer target to total peers
idea: Set the target peers per subnet in proportion to the total target peer count, so nodes with many validator subnets do not run discovery queries forever trying to reach unreachable per-subnet targets.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:63 TARGET_SUBNET_PEERS = 3 const
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:773-783 and service/mod.rs:1215 use the constant
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/config.rs:355 target_peers default DEFAULT_TARGET_PEERS
gap: PR 5177 landed as a fixed constant of 3 (tuned for the 100-peer default), not proportional. A user who lowers --target-peers with many subnets still chases 3 per subnet. Replace TARGET_SUBNET_PEERS by a value derived from config.target_peers in discovery/mod.rs and service/mod.rs subnet checks.
impact: Avoids endless subnet discovery queries only for nodes with small target-peers and many subnets; default config already fine.

title: Skip subnet filtering of peers during sync
idea: While range syncing, do not filter discovered peers by attestation subnets, since subnets do not matter for sync and more discovered peers become usable.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:385-394 discover_peers starts FindPeers with |_| true
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:827-842 start_query only adds the fork-digest and dialable-address predicate
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:1041-1071 maintain_peer_count requests generic peers
impact: General peer discovery never filters by attestation subnet, in sync or not, so all fork-matching peers are usable for range sync.

title: Do not block startup on bootstrap connectivity
idea: Run the bootstrap connectivity check as a background task instead of a fixed blocking wait, so the rest of startup continues at once.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:261-320 Discovery::new awaits ENR requests for multiaddr bootnodes (while loop on FuturesUnordered) before returning
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:400-410 discovery built and awaited during network start
gap: Only multiaddr bootnodes (rare; default networks use ENR bootnodes) block startup until every request_enr resolves or times out; there is no fixed connectivity wait. Move the multiaddr request_enr loop in Discovery::new into a spawned task or into the poll loop so startup continues.
impact: Saves seconds of startup only for users with multiaddr bootnodes; no steady-state gain.

title: Omit UDP port to avoid serving FINDNODE
idea: As a workaround for discovery memory growth, omit the UDP port from the local ENR so the node is not asked to serve FINDNODE requests.
measured_best: pr:lodestar#4591: external memory stable for 3 days on test nodes
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/enr.rs:204-210 UDP port is put in ENR from listen config
Cargo.lock discv5 is the Rust crate, not the discv5 JS implementation with the leak
impact: The workaround targets a Lodestar-specific JS discv5 memory leak; omitting UDP would hurt Lighthouse discoverability.

title: Drive discovery on demand from peer manager
idea: Run discv5 lookups when the peer manager needs peers, filtering ENRs by fork digest and subnet needs before dialing and caching good results, instead of continuous background lookups.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:1041-1071 maintain_peer_count emits DiscoverPeers only when below target/outbound minimum
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:385-394 single FindPeers at a time (find_peer_active)
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:760-806 subnet queries skipped when enough good peers on subnet
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:827-842 fork digest and dialable predicate inside find_node_predicate
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:353-360 cached_enrs
impact: Discovery is demand-driven from the peer manager, filtered by fork digest and subnet before dialing, with ENR cache.

title: Stop discovery when peer target is reached
idea: Start discovery queries only when there is a free peer slot and the connected (and outbound) peer count is below target, and ease lookup frequency as the target is approached, instead of querying at a fixed fast rate.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:1041-1070 maintain_peer_count: wanted_peers=0 once connected_or_dialing >= target and outbound >= min
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:365-374 discover_peers returns while find_peer_active
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:389-398 peers_discovered stops recursion on no useful ENRs
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:51 HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL=30
impact: Discovery is idle at the peer target; query size shrinks to wanted_peers as the target is approached.

title: Pass ENRs between threads without re-encoding
idea: Pass ENRs from the discovery worker to the main thread as decoded objects instead of re-encoding them, so the main thread does not verify the signature again per ENR.
impact: n/a: discv5 runs as a tokio task in the same process, ENRs are passed as decoded objects, no worker re-encoding.

title: Cooldown before reconnecting disconnected peers
idea: After a disconnect (longer for serious goodbye reasons), keep the peer in a time-limited ban/cooldown list checked at the swarm layer and by discovery before dialing, so peers are not redialed or accepted in loops while at the limit.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:301-308 TemporaryBan inserts into temporary_banned_peers and emits PeerManagerEvent::Banned
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:1960-1962 Banned only calls discovery().ban_peer (discv5 ban_node), no swarm-level block
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/network_behaviour.rs:156-212 handle_pending/established_inbound_connection check ban_status/is_ip_banned (score/IP) only, not temporary_banned_peers
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/peerdb.rs:153-160 should_dial ignores temporary bans
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/peerdb.rs:176-183 ban_status is score/IP based
gap: temporary_banned_peers is write-only apart from expiry: no swarm-level enforcement remains (rust-libp2p dropped Swarm::ban_peer_id, and no allow_block_list behaviour is used). handle_established_inbound_connection accepts a recently disconnected peer while connected_or_dialing < max_peers (target..target*1.1 slack), and it is then pruned again at the next heartbeat; should_dial/dial_cached_enrs_in_subnet also do not consult it. The cooldown only blocks discv5 rediscovery. Fix: check temporary_banned_peers in handle_established_inbound_connection/handle_established_outbound_connection and in dial_peer; optionally scale timeout by goodbye reason.
impact: Stops accept-then-prune reconnect churn near the peer limit on crowded networks (the original goal of lighthouse#3757).

title: Persist known peers across restarts
idea: Save known peer ENRs (or the peer store) on shutdown and load them into the routing table on startup, so discovery does not restart from the boot nodes.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/service.rs:326-335 load_dht into routing table at startup
beacon_node/network/src/service.rs:1683-1698 persist_dht in Drop
beacon_node/network/src/persisted_dht.rs:23 ENRs stored in the store
impact: Routing table is restored from the store after restart instead of only boot nodes.

title: Preallocate subnet bitfield decode buffers
idea: When decoding ENR subnet bitfields or set-bit indices, allocate the output once at the right size instead of growing or concatenating intermediate arrays.
measured_best: pr:lodestar#10382: ~1.1us/op to ~310ns/op; 5M calls 4914ms to 710ms
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/enr.rs:58 from_ssz_bytes
impact: Negligible.

title: Prefix-targeted subnet peer search
idea: Search for subnet peers by targeting node ids whose prefix maps to the subnet (deterministic subnet-to-node-id mapping) instead of random targets, so each query finds more subnet peers per request.
measured_best: pr:lighthouse#5090: ~3x discovery bytes/nodes found vs random search
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:849 NodeId::random() target
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/subnet_predicate.rs:10 predicate filters results only
gap: Add a subnet-to-target-node-id mapping and pass prefix-matching targets in start_query/start_subnet_query.
impact: Fewer discv5 bytes per subnet peer found; minor CPU/bandwidth, up to a few x on subnet queries.

title: Protect useful peers from random pruning
idea: Tag in-use or useful peers as protected in the connection manager so that over-limit pruning does not drop them at random and cause churn and redials.
measured_best: pr:lodestar#4997: peer connection length metric improved
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:1136-1200 should_protect_peer protects outbound, sampling-column, sync-committee and scarce-attestation-subnet peers
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/network_behaviour.rs:197-210 libp2p connection limits reject new inbound only, nothing prunes existing connections at random
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:1060 build_peer_subnet_info excludes trusted peers from pruning
impact: Pruning is deterministic (score and subnet-usefulness ordered); no random connection-manager pruning exists to protect against.

title: Prune non-sync peers while syncing
idea: While not synced, disconnect peers that do not support sync protocols and a share of the lowest-scored sync peers each heartbeat, so slots free up for useful sync peers.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:1307 prune_excess_peers has no sync-state input
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/network_behaviour.rs:83-99 the only sync-state use in the peer manager: status re-polls are paused while syncing (the opposite of pruning)
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/rpc_methods.rs:164-170 process_status sends Goodbye IrrelevantNetwork only for wrong fork / different finalized chain, independent of our sync state
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:1237 is_synced_or_advanced only a sort key in custody-subnet pruning
gap: No step disconnects Behind or low-score peers while the local node is syncing. Add a sync-state-aware branch in the PeerManager heartbeat (sync state is already in network_globals) that drops Behind/Unknown peers and a share of the lowest scored peers when SyncingFinalized/SyncingHead. The 'no sync protocol' part has no analogue in eth2.
impact: Could speed initial/catch-up sync when slots are full of unhelpful peers; no steady-state saving; target peer count is high so benefit is uncertain.
refute_note: Also checked network_behaviour.rs, sync/network_context goodbye_peer callers and status relevance checks: only fork/finality relevance disconnects exist, nothing tied to local sync state.

title: Linear capability exchange loop
idea: Replace the O(n^2) peer capability exchange loop with a two-pass linear one.
measured_best: pr:prysm#15384: O(n^2) to O(2n)
impact: n/a: Lighthouse has no O(n^2) capability exchange loop; it was Prysm specific.

title: Ping peers less often
idea: Ping connected peers at about the rate peers ping us (minutes, not seconds), to cut network work competing for the main thread.
measured_best: pr:lodestar#2974: ping interval 4.01 min derived from metrics
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/config.rs:5 DEFAULT_PING_INTERVAL_OUTBOUND=15
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/config.rs:8 DEFAULT_PING_INTERVAL_INBOUND=20
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:194 HashSetDelay ping timers
gap: Raise the two default intervals in peer_manager/config.rs (to minutes) while keeping metadata seq-number refresh via pings.
impact: Roughly 10x fewer ping req/resp over ~100 peers; small CPU saving (about 5-10 pings/s down to under 1).

title: Fine-grained locks in network globals
idea: Remove the global lock around the network service and give each shared variable its own fine-grained lock in a globals struct.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/globals.rs:16-36 NetworkGlobals with one parking_lot RwLock per field
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/globals.rs:89-100 per-field lock construction
impact: Shared network state uses per-field locks, no global service lock.

title: Shorter idle connection timeout
idea: Close unused peer connections after a shorter idle timeout to free sockets and memory sooner.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:501 with_idle_connection_timeout(10s)
gap: Lighthouse already uses a short 10s idle timeout; the code comment says other clients can time out, so going shorter is risky. Only a constant in service/mod.rs could change.
impact: Negligible socket/memory saving.

title: Faster light client bootstrap peer cycling
idea: When few peers serve light client data, shorten the minimum interval between light client bootstrap queries so the client cycles through peers faster.
impact: n/a: Lighthouse has no light client bootstrap peer cycling loop.

title: Skip custody group computation for supernodes
idea: When the node custodies all groups (supernode), skip the get_custody_groups computation and use all groups directly.
evidence: consensus/types/src/data/data_column_custody_group.rs:28-39 get_custody_groups returns 0..N when custody_group_count == number_of_custody_groups
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/globals.rs:72 and :111 callers go through get_custody_groups
impact: Supernodes skip the hash loop; the computation is rare anyway.

title: Count pending dials against the peer limit
idea: Count in-flight dials toward the max/target peer count and skip dialing peers the connection limits would reject, so no dials or discovery queries are wasted near the limit.
measured_best: pr:nimbus#2443: fewer failed dials/discovery requests near max peers (screenshots)
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:354-380 peers_discovered gates on connected_or_dialing + to_dial_peers < max_peers
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:1041-1050 maintain_peer_count subtracts dialing_peers from wanted
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:458-472 dial_peer uses should_dial (skips connected/dialing/banned)
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/network_behaviour.rs:235-245 outbound limit check
impact: In-flight dials count toward limits; no excess dials or queries near max peers.

title: Skip ENRs with no dialable address
idea: Before dialing, skip ENRs with zero TCP/QUIC ports or no usable multiaddr (for example discovery-only bootnodes), so no dial slot or retry is spent on undialable records.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:459-463 dial_peer returns false when dialable_multiaddrs is empty
common/network_utils/src/enr_ext.rs:243-260 dialable_multiaddrs_tcp omits zero ports (quic likewise)
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:832-840 eth2_fork_predicate requires a dialable TCP/QUIC address
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:600-620 bootnode dial skipped when no dialable multiaddrs
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:1339-1360 cached-ENR subnet dials go through dial_peer
impact: No dial slots spent on undialable ENRs.

title: Disable discovery loop for tiny peer targets
idea: When the target peer count is tiny, disable the outbound-peer discovery loop, since on small networks every node is already connected and queries find nothing.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:1043-1069 maintain_peer_count: no tiny-target guard, outbound-only branch always runs
grep for '<= 10' and target_peers guards in lighthouse_network/src found nothing; PR 6162 guard is gone
gap: Skip the outbound-only discovery branch in maintain_peer_count when target_peers is tiny (e.g. <= 10).
impact: Only helps devnets and tiny testnets that loop empty discovery queries; no effect on mainnet.

title: Skip genesis block request in peer validation
idea: When nothing is finalized past genesis, skip requesting the peer's genesis block during chain validation and rely on the fork digest check, saving a round trip per peer.
evidence: network/src/network_beacon_processor/rpc_methods.rs:120-165 check_peer_relevance uses Status finalized checkpoints only
impact: None; Lighthouse never requests the peer's genesis block, relevance is decided from the Status message and fork digest.

title: Fall back instead of dialing unreachable peers
idea: Do not stall on dialing peers that cannot be reached; fall back to requesting data from other peers or via broadcast.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:458 dial_peer queues dials asynchronously, does not block requests
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/network_behaviour.rs:336 on_dial_failure marks failed dials
impact: Sync and lookups send RPCs only to connected peers; dials are asynchronous and never block data requests.

title: Skip unused metadata fetch on peer refresh
idea: Do not fetch peer Metadata during periodic peer refresh when the result is never used, saving a network call per peer.
evidence: lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:718-745 MetaData requested only on first contact or when ping/pong seq number differs
impact: No periodic metadata refresh exists; metadata is fetched on seq-number change and is used (subnets, custody).

title: Throttle random discovery lookup rate
idea: Space discovery lookups out (sleep between random lookups, longer polling period) and connect to a bounded number of candidates per lookup, to cut queries per second and their CPU.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:365-374 at most one FindPeers active, target capped at FIND_NODE_QUERY_CLOSEST_PEERS=16
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:64 MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBNET_QUERIES=4
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:51 HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL=30 drives maintain_peer_count
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:389-398 back-to-back requery only when the last query gave useful ENRs and peers are still wanted
impact: Lookup rate is bounded (serial queries, 30s heartbeat, zero at target, bounded candidates).

title: Dial most useful discovered peers first
idea: Sort random discovery results by usefulness (subnets covered, score) before dialing, so the dial budget goes to the best peers first.
evidence: lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:351 peers_discovered iterates a HashMap<Enr, Option<Instant>> in arbitrary order
lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:866 results collected into HashMap
gap: Collect discovery results into a Vec, sort peers with a subnet min_ttl first (and by subnet coverage) before the dial-budget loop in PeerManager::peers_discovered.
impact: Dial budget when near max_peers would go to subnet-needed peers first; small, only matters when slots are scarce.

title: Separate poll loops for channel and swarm
idea: In the network service, poll the command channel and the swarm in separate loops that each stop when not ready, so a busy source cannot spin the poll loop.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/service.rs:465-500 spawn_service tokio::select! loop over network_recv, validator_subscription_recv, subnet_service and libp2p.next_event()
impact: Each source is a separate async branch; select! awaits readiness with random fairness, so no busy poll loop.

title: Churn peers when head is starved
idea: During long non-finality, detect a starved head and churn extra useless peers while keeping peers far ahead of us, so the node finds peers that can serve it.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:1307 prune_excess_peers runs only above target and has no head-progress check

beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:1219-1243 find_prune_candidate sorts by (custody_subnet_count, is_synced_or_advanced): a weak tie-break that prunes behind peers first, not a protection for peers far ahead
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:1442 heartbeat has no starvation detector
gap: No detection of a starved head (head unchanged and behind wall clock) and no extra churn in that state. Add a check in the PeerManager heartbeat that, when starved, prunes extra useless peers below target and exempts peers whose head is far ahead.
impact: Helps recovery during long non-finality or stalls only; no steady-state saving.
refute_note: Grepped peer_manager, sync and discovery for stall/starve/stuck/head_slot logic; only the is_synced_or_advanced sort key in custody pruning touches peer head state, which is not the starvation mechanism.

title: Do not let subnet queries starve peer search
idea: Queue and group only subnet discovery queries; always run general find-peers queries regardless of active subnet queries, so they cannot be starved.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:179-180 queued_queries is VecDeque<SubnetQuery> only
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:385-394 FindPeers started immediately, not queued
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:742-748 at_capacity subtracts find_peer_active
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:711-735 process_queue groups subnet queries
impact: FindPeers cannot be starved by subnet queries.

title: Lookup-table decode of ENR subnet bitfields
idea: Decode ENR attnets/syncnets bitfields with a precomputed byte-to-bits table and no exceptions, instead of the generic SSZ bitvector path.
measured_best: pr:lodestar#3550: x20 faster than ssz BitVector implementation
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/enr.rs:58 attestation_bitfield from_ssz_bytes
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/subnet_predicate.rs:17 per-ENR decode in predicate
gap: Replace the BitVector decode in subnet_predicate/enr.rs with a direct bit test on the raw ENR bytes.
impact: Negligible on a mainnet node; discovery is a tiny CPU share.

title: Update local ENR only when fields change
idea: Update the local ENR only when a field value actually changes (and set the ip4/ip6 field matching the listen address), so the sequence number does not churn and fewer ENR updates spread in the DHT.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:417-440 update_enr_tcp_port returns Ok(false) when tcp4/tcp6 already equals port
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:448-475 update_enr_quic_port same for quic/quic6
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:483-491 update_enr_udp_socket persists only when discv5 reports a change
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:518-524 and 553-559 update_enr_bitfield returns early when the bit is already set
~/.cargo/registry/src/*/enr-0.14.0/src/lib.rs:585-589 Enr::insert_raw_rlp always bumps seq, so the equality guards are what prevent churn
impact: Port, socket and subnet-bitfield updates do not bump the ENR seq when the value is unchanged; this is the frequent path (listen-address events, subnet churn).

title: Fetch blobs from EL to build sidecars locally
idea: When a block or first data column sidecar arrives, call engine_getBlobs (V1/V2) to pull its blobs and proofs from the local EL blob pool and build blob or data column sidecars locally. This skips waiting for gossip or downloading from peers, and lets the node publish the sidecars itself.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1934-1941 process_gossip_verified_block spawns spawn_fetch_block_columns right after gossip verification
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1118-1133 getBlobs triggered on first partial-column header
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:210-222 RPC block path
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:224 HTTP publish path
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:998-1040 fetch_engine_blobs_and_publish_full publishes columns gradually
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:190-300 get_blobs_v2/v3 builds custody columns
impact: Saves column downloads and gossip waiting on block import.

title: Use getBlobsV4 to build partial columns from sparse blobpools
idea: Call engine_getBlobsV4 to get cells for the blobs the EL has, even when it holds only part of them, and build partial data columns locally. This reduces column downloads from peers when the EL blob pool is sparse.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:161 uses V4 when supports_get_blobs_v4
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:405-440 fetch_and_process_blobs_v4 requests custody cells
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:531 build_partial_columns_from_v4_response
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:317 import_custody_partial_columns merges into partial assembler / pending payload cache
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:989 publish_partial_data_columns after fetch
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/engine_api.rs:673,746 get_blobs_v4 capability
impact: Cuts column downloads when the EL blobpool is sparse.

title: Fetch blobs from EL during range sync too
idea: Also during sync, on the first received column sidecar call getBlobsV2 to build the remaining columns locally, and retry block import once half of the sampled columns are present. The node does not wait for peers to serve every column.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:209-231 getBlobs only after single-block lookup returns MissingComponents
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:960-995 spawn_fetch_block_columns (gossip/RPC/HTTP sources only)
beacon_node/network/src/service.rs:697 and gossip_methods.rs:1123,1936 gossip triggers
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:497-641 chain segment import path has no EL blob fetch
beacon_node/network/src/sync/ contains no fetch_blobs/get_blobs call (only a test mock at range_data_column_batch_request.rs:327)
gap: Range/backfill sync batches download all custody columns from peers; there is no getBlobsV2 call on first column or batch, and no early import once enough columns are local. Would need range batch requests to consult the EL for recent blocks and mark columns as satisfied.
impact: Lower column download volume and faster range sync near head while blobs are still in the EL blobpool; little effect for deep syncs.
refute_note: Grepped all callers of fetch_engine_blobs_and_publish_full/spawn_fetch_block_columns and the whole sync/ directory for EL blob access; only gossip, HTTP and single-lookup paths use it.

title: SSZ over REST transport for the engine API

title: Separate EL queue for payload-body serving
idea: Run engine_getPayloadBodiesByHash for peer RPC serving on its own bounded queue separate from newPayload/forkchoiceUpdated, with batching and per-peer limits. RPC serving then cannot delay block import calls.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:905-929 block import queues (chain segment, rpc block, gossip block) are dequeued before
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1110-1112 BlocksByRange/Root serving queues (separate bounded FIFOs, 1024 each at scheduler/work_queue.rs:390)
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1721-1725 serving work runs via spawn_async, holding a worker slot until done (lib.rs:1776-1784, max_workers=num_cpus lib.rs:130, 890)
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/config.rs:131-138 per-peer inbound quotas for blocks and payload envelopes (128 per 10s)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_block_streamer.rs:231 and payload_envelope_streamer/mod.rs:208,276 bodies fetched in batches of 32
gap: No dedicated EL-side queue or small in-flight cap for getPayloadBodiesByHash: up to num_cpus serving tasks can each have a bodies call in flight on the shared engine HTTP client while newPayload/fcU run. Add a semaphore (e.g. 2) around get_payload_bodies_by_hash v1/v2 and a global/per-peer concurrent-serving limit.
impact: Small for Lighthouse: unlike Teku, LH has no global EL throttle, so newPayload never waits behind bodies calls in a CL queue; the remaining effect is only EL-side contention under heavy serving.
refute_note: Beyond execution_layer, checked the beacon processor scheduler, worker-slot accounting and the RPC inbound rate limiter: queue separation, batching and per-peer limits already exist at the CL scheduling layer; only the EL-level dedicated cap is missing.

title: Bound concurrent in-flight EL requests
idea: Throttle Engine API and eth1 calls with a bounded queue or in-flight cap, and avoid overlapping validations of the same optimistic head. This keeps the EL from being flooded and timing out during bulk work.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:130 max_workers=num_cpus; lib.rs:890 can_spawn gate bounds all block import / chain segment / RPC serving work that issues EL calls
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1776-1784 async work keeps its worker slot until the EL call completes

beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:179 DuplicateCache; network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1561, sync_methods.rs:121 avoid concurrent import (and duplicate newPayload) of the same block
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7225 execution_engine_forkchoice_lock serialises fcU
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:1726-1731 backfill segments on a low-priority rayon pool when rate limiting is enabled
gap: No explicit in-flight cap in Engine::request/HttpJsonRpc; HTTP API, timer and proposer-prep paths bypass the processor bound. Add a semaphore in Engine::request with priority for newPayload/fcU.
impact: Modest; the worker-pool bound and duplicate cache already prevent most flooding, a hard cap would only guard against slow-EL timeouts from non-processor paths.
refute_note: The earlier review looked only for a Semaphore in execution_layer; the beacon processor worker pool indirectly bounds concurrent EL calls and DuplicateCache prevents overlapping validation of one block. The eth1 service no longer exists, so that half of the idea is n/a.

title: Optimistic block import when EL syncing or offline
idea: Import blocks optimistically when the EL returns SYNCING or is unreachable, instead of stalling. The beacon chain stays synced and can give the EL the latest head right away when it recovers.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/execution_payload.rs:150-152 Syncing|Accepted -> PayloadVerificationStatus::Optimistic
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/execution_payload.rs:213 Err(e) => ExecutionPayloadError::RequestFailed, block not imported
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/engines.rs:114 EngineError::Offline surfaces as a request error
gap: Only the SYNCING/ACCEPTED path imports optimistically. When the EL is unreachable or offline, notify_new_payload returns RequestFailed and the block is rejected; Nimbus #4458 treats a missing EL like SYNCING after local block-hash checks. On the gossip/head path LH stalls while the EL is down, except for finalized range sync, which skips the EL.
impact: During EL outages or restarts LH falls behind on head and must catch up after the EL returns, instead of handing the EL the latest head right away.

title: Skip EL calls for already finalized blocks during sync
idea: During range sync, treat blocks that are finalized or far behind the wall slot as optimistic on CL verification alone and skip per-block newPayload/forkchoiceUpdated, updating the EL only occasionally. Per-block EL calls on a syncing EL are wasted work.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:497-506 NotifyExecutionLayer::No only when is_syncing_finalized
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/execution_payload.rs:78 newPayload skipped for pre-Gloas blocks in that case

beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:175,350 lookup/parent paths always Yes
gap: (1) Gloas: BeaconChain::process_range_sync_envelope ignores the segment's NotifyExecutionLayer and calls newPayload for every envelope, even during finalized sync. (2) Head (non-finalized) range sync of blocks far behind the wall slot still calls newPayload per block.
impact: Pre-Gloas finalized range sync already avoids per-block EL calls. After Gloas that saving is lost, because the payload moved into the envelope path.

title: Ordered trie root for payload hash
idea: Compute the transactions and withdrawals roots of the execution block header with an ordered-trie routine specialised for index-keyed tries instead of a generic Merkle Patricia trie. Block hash verification gets much faster.
measured_best: 100x speed boost (pr:nimbus#6610)
evidence: beacon_node/execution_layer/src/block_hash.rs:7,25,29 triehash::ordered_trie_root (generic MPT, crate triehash 0.8.4) for transactions and withdrawals roots
Cargo.lock:659 alloy-trie 0.9.8 is in the tree but not used by any Lighthouse crate
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/execution_payload.rs:78-82 block hash computed only when NotifyExecutionLayer::No (finalized sync, optimistic_finalized_sync)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/mod.rs:436-441 also for Gloas envelope backfill
gap: Replace triehash in calculate_execution_block_hash with an index-keyed ordered trie builder (alloy-trie HashBuilder over sorted rlp(index) keys) for transactions and withdrawals roots.
impact: Not on the live newPayload path: the hash is recomputed only during finalized range sync without the EL and envelope backfill, where it is a per-block CPU cost that limits sync throughput.
refute_note: Confirmed no specialised ordered-trie routine and alloy-trie unused; corrected the earlier impact: verify_payload_block_hash runs only on the NotifyExecutionLayer::No path, not on every newPayload.

title: Use latestValidHash to mark ancestor runs
idea: Use the latestValidHash in newPayload/fcU responses to mark a whole chain of optimistic ancestors valid or invalid in fork choice at once, instead of verifying each block with the EL.

title: Correct payload id cache key for prepared payloads
idea: Key the proposer payload-id cache only by head block hash (and attributes or slot), the same key used when filling it, including skipped slots and epoch boundaries. The payload prepared by an earlier fcU is then reused at proposal instead of another fcU and build wait.

title: Stable payload attributes target slot
idea: Compute FCU payload attributes for a stable target slot and do not re-send FCU on proposer-data refresh or late block import. The EL then does not rebuild or drop its payload, and no corrective FCU plus immediate getPayload is needed.

title: Short getPayload deadline to fail over fast

title: Retry getPayload with fresh preparation

impact: Lighthouse's blst wrapper does not parallelize internally; parallelism comes from the beacon processor's worker pool, so there is no nested parallelism to remove.

title: Keep genesis validators root inside the batch verifier

title: Do not hold locks while awaiting batch verification

title: Pass decoded gossip objects to processing, avoid re-decode

title: Ignore attestations on shuffling cache miss
idea: Ignore gossip attestations whose committee shuffling is not already cached instead of computing it, so attackers cannot force expensive shuffling computation.

gap: Lighthouse still computes a shuffling (state load and partial advance) on a miss, but at most 2 at a time and deduplicated per shuffling id; any further miss is ignored. A plain ignore-on-miss with no computation, as Nimbus proposed, is not there.
impact: Small: the DoS cost is already bounded to 2 concurrent computations, deduplicated per shuffling id and limited to known targets in the gossip slot range. refute_note: The earlier review missed the MAX_CONCURRENT_PROMISES cap and its Ignore mapping in gossip_methods.rs. Together these bound attacker-forced shuffling computation, which is the purpose of the idea. The Nimbus source PR was closed unmerged.

title: Order gossip validation checks cheapest first
idea: Order gossip validation rules so cheap structural REJECT checks run first, then cheap in-memory IGNOREs (slot window, bit lengths, committee bits, seen cache, invalid block, parent root, target epoch), then state loads, pool lookups, shuffling and signature checks, so invalid messages are dropped before costly work.

gap: On the SingleAttestation path, the in-memory REJECT checks run only after the BLS check: committee_index < committees_per_slot (NoCommitteeForSlotAndIndex), attester in committee (AttesterNotInCommittee) and the subnet match (InvalidSubnetId). They are in VerifiedUnaggregatedAttestation::verify_late_checks (with_committee_cache), which runs after verify_attestation_signature in verify_slashable, and in batch.rs after the batch signature check. A message with a random attester_index or the wrong subnet therefore costs a BLS verify, or a failed batch and then single verifies, before a cheap shuffling-cache check would drop it. Separately, the aggregate path computes the ObservedAttestationKey tree_hash_root before verify_committee_index.
impact: Saves BLS work only on invalid or misrouted single attestations, which is the DoS path. On honest traffic the effect is nil, because the shuffling check has to run anyway. Moving with_committee_cache earlier has a cost: on a shuffling miss, the state load would come before the signature filter.

title: Ignore further blocks from same proposer and slot

title: Cache validation work per distinct AttestationData
idea: Cache per-slot gossip attestation validation results (signing root, data root, head/target checks, committee) keyed by serialized AttestationData plus committee bits, so many attestations and aggregates with identical data hash and check once; keep lookup and insert keys consistent.
measured_best: validateGossipAttestation was ~12% of CPU (5.8% signing root, 3.9% head/target check); reduced to under 3%; cache <300kb per slot (pr:lodestar#5333)

refute_note: Searched attestation_verification, its batch module and signature_sets for any data-root or signing-root memoisation; only shuffling/pubkey caches exist, which every client has.

title: Verify proposer header signature once across sidecars

refute_note: The earlier review missed the partial-column header cache in PartialDataColumnAssembler, which already verifies a block's header once and reuses it; the full-column and block paths do not share it.

title: Verify early attestation signatures and cache result

title: Cache invalid block roots to reject descendants
idea: Keep a bounded cache of block roots that failed validation, and immediately reject gossip blocks, attestations and aggregates that are, reference or build on them, without repeating state work or full verification when they arrive from other peers.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3879 check_invalid_block_roots reads only static config.invalid_block_roots

Add an LRU filled on state-transition/signature failures and checked in GossipVerifiedBlock::new_without_slasher_checks, column/envelope gossip verification and attestation verification.

title: Memoize fork digest computation
idea: Memoize the fork digest keyed by fork version and genesis validators root instead of recomputing it for every gossip message.

title: Check snappy declared length before decompressing
idea: Read the uncompressed length from the snappy header and reject gossip messages outside the topic's valid size range (max gossip payload) before allocating, decompressing or SSZ decoding, including in the message-id function, so oversized messages cost no CPU or memory.

title: Reject future-slot messages before queueing or hashing
idea: Reject gossip blocks and sidecars whose slot is beyond wall clock plus disparity before computing hash tree roots or inserting them into pending queues, with one shared helper.

Move the now_with_future_tolerance check to before signed_block_header() in GossipVerifiedBlock::new; a check before queueing would need a slot peek in the router.

title: Cap in-flight gossip validations per large topic
idea: Limit concurrent in-flight validations per large-message topic and drop excess before SSZ decode; ignore envelopes whose state is not cached instead of regenerating.

gap: There is no per-topic cap on in-flight validations before decode; queues are bounded by count after decode. Envelope verification loads the state from the store instead of ignoring when the state is not cached; external builder envelopes always load it. Add a per-topic limit before PubsubMessage::decode and an ignore-on-miss path in envelope gossip verification.

refute_note: Searched the sigp rust-libp2p gossipsub checkout for validation backpressure or in-flight limits and found none; its only per-topic limit is transmit size. Confirmed that the external builder path always loads the state (TODO builder pubkey cache).

title: Keep compressed payload in gossip validation queue
idea: Hold only the compressed payload plus a small decoded prefix for queued gossip messages, decompress in the worker, apply a byte-weighted per-topic limit, and read slot from fixed SSZ offset to drop far-future blocks before decoding.
measured_best: held heap per queued block 6.20 MiB -> 0.20 MiB; far-future block flood no longer OOMs (pr:teku#11503)
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:106-125 snappy decompression in gossipsub inbound_transform on the network thread

refute_note: Checked the transform and decode path and the gossipsub dependency: decompression and decode are both eager. No lazy or byte-weighted queue exists under any name.

idea: Read the slot from the serialized gossip bytes and ignore messages older than a window (e.g. 32 slots) before deserializing or queueing them.

title: Reject pre-finalized gossip blocks and attestations

idea: Penalize peers that gossip pre-finalization blocks heavily enough that they are banned sooner, cutting repeated validation and bandwidth.

title: Harden aggregate validation with bounded verifier queue
idea: Bound the aggregate-and-proof batch verifier queue and reject cheap duplicates or invalid aggregates before signature work.

idea: On gossip reject/ignore paths return result codes or plain objects instead of throwing stack-capturing errors and converting error metadata to JSON, since this cost is paid for every invalid or duplicate message.

title: Avoid cloning conversions between sidecar wrapper types
idea: Use one sidecar validation path across forks so validation does not convert between Arc-wrapped and inner types, which clones.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:195 sidecars decoded per fork into owned types
impact: The Arc-wrapper conversion clone is specific to Grandine's types; Lighthouse has no double wrapper.

title: Batch KZG verification of gossip column sidecars
idea: Verify KZG proofs of multiple gossip data column sidecars together in a batch rather than one sidecar at a time.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/lib.rs:417 GossipDataColumnSidecar(AsyncFn) is one work item per sidecar
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1035 verify_kzg_for_data_column verifies one column via iter::once (also :1060 with_commitments variant)

title: Bounded wait for unknown block attestation validation

title: Attestation admission budget scaled to traffic
idea: Rate-limit gossip attestation processing with a node-wide budget per window sized from expected traffic (subscribed subnets times active validators per slot and subnet, with headroom), so CPU is bounded without dropping legitimate attestations.

Missing: peeking semantic keys from bytes, e.g. AttestationData bytes shared by thousands of distinct attestations, or a block root for an already-imported block re-sent with other bytes, to skip decode and per-data validation.

title: Minimum bid increment before forwarding
idea: Forward a gossip builder bid only if it beats the current best bid for its tuple by a minimum increment, so tiny-increment bid spam is neither validated nor propagated.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_bid_verification/gossip_verified_bid.rs:318-329 only rejects bid_value <= cached value (TODO(gloas): bid_value_over_threshold)

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_bid_verification/gossip_verified_bid.rs:304-316 seen_builder_bid_for_parent rejects a second bid from the same builder for (slot, parent)

impact: Fewer BLS signature checks and forwards of tiny-increment bids. The existing one-bid-per-builder-per-(slot, parent) dedup already stops a single builder from laddering, so the extra saving only applies when many builders bid against each other.

title: Once-cell per shuffling key for concurrent computes
idea: Guard the proposer shuffling cache with a per-(epoch, decision root) once-cell or promise so concurrent gossip verifications wait for a single computation instead of each recomputing it.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:85-87 LruCache<(Epoch, Hash256), Arc<OnceCell<EpochBlockProposers>>>
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:188-200 get_or_insert_key then get_or_try_init outside the mutex

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/gossip_verified_envelope.rs:227 envelope gossip uses it

title: Singleflight state replays for sidecar verification
idea: Deduplicate concurrent state replays/regenerations for the same target when many data column sidecars arrive at once and each needs the same verifying state.

title: Reduce duplicate work in aggregate validation
idea: Share checks and cached states across the steps of gossip aggregate-and-proof validation so the same state or computation is not produced twice per message.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:1617-1660 map_attestation_committees resolves committees once via with_committee_cache (shuffling cache, state load only on miss)

impact: Aggregate validation already does one committee lookup per message and shares it across the aggregator, membership and indexing checks; no duplicate state work.

title: Pass gossip attestations by reference
idea: Take gossip attestations by reference in the processing entry point and clone only the small attestation data where needed, not the whole signed object.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:280-301 process_gossip_attestation verifies &attestation, then calls verified_attestation.attestation().clone_as_attestation() and then into_indexed_attestation(), which drops the owned Attestation
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:357 same clone_as_attestation in process_gossip_attestation_batch

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:352-362 VerifiedUnaggregatedAttestation owns `attestation: Attestation<E>` but only exposes into_indexed_attestation, so callers cannot move it out

title: Penalize peers sending too-old messages
idea: Penalize peers strictly for attestations and sync messages older than the earliest permissible slot (after clock disparity) to discourage spam of stale messages.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:76 STRICT_LATE_MESSAGE_PENALTIES = false
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:2654-2675 attestation PastSlot only Ignore, penalty gated by the false const
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:3350-3395 sync PastSlot same
gap: Set STRICT_LATE_MESSAGE_PENALTIES true, or make the hindsight-invalid penalty unconditional (keeping tolerance high) in the AttnError::PastSlot and SyncCommitteeError::PastSlot arms. PR 4873 was closed unmerged.
impact: Only a peer-scoring hardening against stale-message spam; no direct CPU saving on a normal node.

title: Plain map for bounded seen key space
idea: Track already-seen slashed validator indices in a plain map instead of an LRU cache, since the key space is bounded and needs no eviction bookkeeping.
measured_best: None (pr:prysm#8332)

impact: None; Lighthouse already uses a plain set for the bounded validator-index key space.

title: Only BLS-verify queued envelopes for known proposers
idea: For a gossip payload envelope whose block is unknown and that will only be queued, ignore it unless it is non-self-built or its proposer is in the known lookahead, so unknown-parent envelopes cannot force signature checks.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/gossip_verified_envelope.rs:162-168 BlockRootUnknown is returned from the fork choice lookup before any store read or signature check
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:3894-3925 unknown-block envelope is IGNOREd and a closure that re-runs full verification is sent to the reprocess queue
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:115 UnknownBlockForEnvelope queued by block root
impact: Unknown-parent envelopes never trigger BLS work before the block is known, so the Prysm DoS vector does not exist.

title: Precompute per-shuffling committee aggregate pubkeys
idea: Precompute aggregate public keys per committee for the shuffling and derive aggregate keys by subtracting non-participants, and pass parsed views to avoid re-parsing and re-hashing in attestation validation.
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/signature_sets.rs:295 indexed_attestation_signature_set collects participant pubkeys per attestation
crypto/bls/src/generic_signature_set.rs:119 verify aggregates the pubkey list each time (fast_aggregate_verify)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:39 CachedShuffling holds committees only, no aggregate pubkeys
gap: No per-committee precomputed aggregate pubkey; each aggregate sums participant pubkeys from scratch. Cache per-shuffling committee aggregate pubkeys and derive by subtracting non-participants when participation is high.
impact: Cuts G1 additions per aggregate; small next to pairing cost; adds memory.
refute_note: Searched beacon_node/consensus/crypto for AggregatePublicKey use: only the sync committee spec field and op-pool, nothing cached for attestation committees.

title: Use proposer lookahead to skip epoch transitions
idea: Post-Fulu, read the expected proposer for gossip blocks and data column sidecars from the parent state's proposer lookahead instead of advancing a state across an epoch boundary or regenerating a block-slot state.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:321-355 ensure_state_can_determine_proposers_for_epoch advances only when state epoch < decision_slot+1 epoch (post-Fulu: E-1)

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1031-1050 gossip block proposer via with_proposer_cache, miss loads parent state un-advanced (load_parent -> get_advanced_hot_state at block_verification.rs:2065)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1746-1769 column proposer via with_proposer_cache with the parent state
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:219 get_beacon_proposer_indices reads the lookahead
impact: Post-Fulu, a parent state in epoch E-1 or E is used as is; the lookahead gives the proposer and no epoch transition runs unless the parent is more than one epoch behind (which the lookahead cannot cover anyway).

title: Read-only head or parent state, no copy
idea: Validate gossip objects (exits, BLS changes, blocks) against a read-only reference to the head or parent state instead of cloning the state per message.
measured_best: None (pr:caplin#24523)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2845 voluntary exit uses head snapshot reference
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2894 proposer slashing calls wall_clock_state()

title: Use cached checkpoint or advanced states for validation
idea: Validate gossip aggregates, blocks and sync messages against already cached states (checkpoint/target state, pre-advanced slot state, parent post-state, tip state) instead of copying the head state or regenerating.

title: Direct state lookup by block root

measured_best: None (pr:teku#11215)

title: Synchronous cached state read, conditional pool add
idea: For payload attestation gossip, read the state synchronously from cache instead of the regen queue, and add messages to the pool only when this node is the next proposer.
measured_best: None (pr:lodestar#9969)
evidence: beacon_chain/src/payload_attestation_verification/gossip_verified_payload_attestation.rs:102-110 PTC from shuffling cache, no regen queue

beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2389 add_payload_attestation_to_pool
gap: Cached read is done; missing the condition that pool add happens only when this node is the next proposer. Gate the call in process_gossip_payload_attestation_result on a proposer-duty check for next slot.

title: Small immutable validation view cache for bids
idea: Cache a small immutable view of the fields bid validation needs per (parent root, slot) instead of a full advanced parent state.

title: Ignore bids that force epoch-transition regen
idea: Ignore execution payload bids that build on the head's parent at epoch boundaries, since validating them forces regenerating an unusable parent state through an epoch transition.

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_bid_verification/gossip_verified_bid.rs:~440 prev_randao taken from cached_head.parent_random()
impact: Lighthouse validates parent-building bids against the cached head state and cached randao values, never regenerating the parent state through an epoch transition.

title: Signature check before state advance
idea: Run the BLS signature check against the un-advanced dependent state before advancing a state copy across an epoch boundary, so forged messages never trigger an epoch transition.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/proposer_preferences_verification/gossip_verified_proposer_preferences.rs:133-169 on a proposer-cache miss, get_advanced_hot_state + ensure_state_can_determine_proposers_for_epoch (partial_state_advance across the epoch) runs first

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/proposer_preferences_verification/gossip_verified_proposer_preferences.rs:178-194 signature checked only after, although it needs only pubkey_cache.get(validator_index) and the fork
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:188-197 OnceCell caches the result per (epoch, dependent_root), so repeats of the same key do not re-advance

The validator_index is in the message, so the signature can be checked first with validator_pubkey_cache and spec.fork_at_epoch(proposal_epoch), which is exactly prysm#17656. Lighthouse's proposer-cache memoisation limits the cost to once per (proposal_epoch, dependent_root), but a forged message on a new qualifying fork-choice tip still pays an epoch transition.
impact: Removes a DoS vector where forged proposer preferences referencing a new valid dependent root trigger an epoch transition before BLS rejection; bounded today by the per-key cache.

title: Builder pubkey in fork choice for envelope sig
idea: Store the builder pubkey on the fork choice node so gossip payload envelope signatures can be checked without loading or replaying a block state.

consensus/proto_array/src/proto_array.rs has no builder field on ProtoNode
gap: Store the builder pubkey (or the builder index plus a builder pubkey cache) on the proto-array node, and in the external-builder branch of GossipVerifiedEnvelope::new call verify_signature with that pubkey and the fork. Do not load the snapshot there.
impact: Gossip checks of external-builder envelopes would no longer need the block state, so spam with bad signatures could not force state loads. The gain is partial: the block's post-state is usually still in the hot state cache, and import reuses the snapshot.

title: Drop redundant finalized-descendant check

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1874 also needs split-block descent check, not implied by parent lookup

title: Drop redundant slot-window check
idea: Remove an attestation slot-window check implied by the later clock-disparity check, and compute the epoch once.

idea: Ensure aggregate/attestation signatures are verified once: remove duplicated verification calls and honor an already-verified flag.
measured_best: None (pr:prysm#5676)

title: Single fork choice lock per attestation
idea: Take the fork choice read lock once in attestation gossip verification and run all head-block checks under it.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:1251 verify_head_block_is_known takes fork_choice_read_lock for get_block

title: Skip validating locally produced or self-published objects
idea: Skip full gossip validation of objects the node produced or published itself (blocks, data columns, own messages echoed back, trusted local builder bids), keeping only required checks like equivocation.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:395 new_for_block_publishing skips gossip checks for locally built columns
accba72/protocols/gossipsub/src/behaviour.rs:701 published message ids enter duplicate_cache, so own messages echoed back are dropped at :1985 before any Lighthouse validation

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1285 import reuses the gossip-verified proposer signature (include_all_signatures_except_proposal), so gossip-verifying an own block is not repeated at import
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:246 own block still fully gossip-verified before broadcast
beacon_node/http_api/src/beacon/execution_payload_bids.rs:117 API-submitted bids always gossip-verified (no trusted local builder bypass)

gap: Locally built blocks (ProvenancedBlock::Local) still wait for full GossipVerifiedBlock::new before broadcast; Teku publishes them after only an equivocation check. Gloas bids/envelopes from a trusted local builder are always validated; Lodestar adds an operator flag to skip bid validation.
impact: Lower publish latency for own proposals (proposer sig verify + parent lookup moved off the critical path) and for Gloas bids from a trusted local builder; no CPU saving since import needs the checks anyway.
refute_note: Beyond the earlier review: confirmed gossipsub drops self-echoed messages via duplicate_cache (the Prysm#3403 idea), that block import reuses the gossip proposer-signature check, and that Gloas bid/envelope API paths have no trusted-local bypass.

idea: Before processing a gossip block or data column sidecar, check whether it is already in the store or block input and skip it.

idea: Do not create pending-pool trackers for blocks already imported, since trackers linger for slots and can leak.

impact: Lighthouse's availability cache is size-bounded LRU with no per-block tracker that lingers; an already-imported block does not leak a tracker in the same way.

gap: After the async state load in verify_envelope_for_gossip, pass a closure to check whether the sender is now banned and return Ignore before computing the signing root.

idea: After queued processing, re-check that attestations and sync messages are still timely before accepting them for propagation.

title: Regossip envelopes after reprocessing

title: Reject null-slot gossip before queueing
idea: Reject and penalize gossip messages on slot-bearing topics when no slot can be extracted, rather than queueing them.

title: Queue gossip awaiting unknown dependency
idea: Hold gossip messages whose block or payload is unknown in a root-keyed queue and reprocess them on arrival, extracting slot and root from bytes before decoding.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:111-151 root-keyed queues for unknown block (unaggregate, aggregate, payload attestation, data column, envelope) and unknown payload envelope (UnknownPayloadUnaggregate/Aggregate)

beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:2960-2975 UnknownPayloadEnvelope triggers an envelope lookup and queueing
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:195 full SSZ decode before routing
impact: Hold-and-release by block root and by envelope root already exists for the Gloas types the Lodestar PR targets.

title: Add attestations directly to pool after verify
idea: After signature check, add attestations directly to the pool without an intermediate queue, pass a single validator index for single votes, and free decompressed buffers before async validation.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:390-470 verified unaggregate goes straight to fork choice and add_to_naive_aggregation_pool in the same worker
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:592-660 verified aggregate goes straight to fork choice and add_to_block_inclusion_pool
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2596-2633 add_to_naive_aggregation_pool takes the attestation by reference
impact: There is no intermediate queue between signature verification and the pools, and SingleAttestation already carries one attester index.

title: Avoid copying signature batches
idea: Do not copy the signature batch in the batch verifier when nothing mutates it, cutting allocations.
measured_best: None (pr:prysm#16398)
evidence: crypto/bls/src/generic_signature_set.rs:19 Cow aggregate signature, borrowed
crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:36-39 verify_signature_sets takes an iterator of &SignatureSet and collects refs
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification/batch.rs:109 signature sets built from borrowed data
impact: No defensive copy of the batch exists to remove; the remaining per-batch Vecs in blst.rs are needed by the blst API.

title: Backoff retries of queued blocks
idea: Back off retries of queued gossip blocks failing on execution status instead of retrying every tick.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1756-1760 EL-status block errors are just Ignored, not queued

beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:67 QUEUED_RPC_BLOCK_DELAY
impact: Lighthouse has no per-tick retry of queued gossip blocks; failures on execution status are ignored and recovered via lookups, so there is nothing to back off.

title: Serialize decoding of large gossip messages
idea: Take the block-validation lock before decoding gossiped blocks/envelopes so only one large SSZ decode runs at a time.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:1390 PubsubMessage::decode called inline in the single network service poll loop
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:266 block decode

title: Shallow validation before propagation

beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:432-460 apply_attestation_to_fork_choice and add_to_naive_aggregation_pool after propagation

title: Shorter batch signature verification deadline

title: Do not feed aggregate contents to fork choice
idea: Store gossip aggregates only in the pool and do not push their attestations through the per-attestation chain/fork choice path.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:631 aggregates applied to fork choice
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2573 apply_attestation_to_fork_choice

title: Skip aggregate and contribution work without validators
idea: Skip signature-set construction and processing of aggregates and sync contributions when no local validator needs them.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/topics.rs:56 BeaconAggregateAndProof and SignedContributionAndProof are core topics regardless of attached validators
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:631 verified aggregates are applied to fork choice, so their signatures are needed even without validators

beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:2421 sync contributions added to op pool unconditionally
gap: No validator-count gating anywhere in aggregate/contribution handling. Signature checks on aggregates cannot be skipped safely because Lighthouse feeds them into fork choice and forwards them. The part that could be gated is op-pool insertion (add_to_block_inclusion_pool, add_contribution_to_block_inclusion_pool), and for contributions the whole non-forwarding post-processing, on nodes with no local validators.

refute_note: Searched gossip_methods, subnet_service and topics for any validator-presence condition (import_all_attestations, subscribe_all_subnets only affect subnets); none. Added that aggregates feed fork choice, so only op-pool work is safely skippable.

title: Send IDONTWANT after publishing own messages
idea: After publishing a message the node already has (own block, columns or blobs from the EL), send IDONTWANT to mesh peers so they do not send it back. Saves inbound duplicate bytes.
evidence: accba72/protocols/gossipsub/src/behaviour.rs:711-724 publish sends IDONTWANT only when config.idontwant_on_publish() is true
accba72/protocols/gossipsub/src/config.rs:560 idontwant_on_publish default false

gap: PR #6513 put IDONTWANT-on-publish into the old vendored gossipsub. After the move to the sigp/rust-libp2p fork it is behind a config flag that Lighthouse does not set. Add .idontwant_on_publish(true) to gossipsub_config in lighthouse_network/src/config.rs (this is open PR #8364).
impact: Stops mesh peers from sending back large messages the node published itself (blobs or columns from getBlobs, own blocks). The gain is modest inbound bandwidth.
refute_note: The prescreen said this was in LH because of the merged PR #6513, but that code was in the vendored crate that has been removed. I grepped beacon_node for every IDONTWANT config use and checked both IDONTWANT send sites in the pinned fork (accba72). Nothing turns the flag on.

title: Size threshold for sending IDONTWANT
idea: Send IDONTWANT only for messages above a size threshold, since for small messages such as single attestations the control message costs about as much as the payload it saves.

title: Time-based O(1) gossip duplicate cache
idea: Keep the gossipsub seen-message cache as a time-based structure with O(1) insert and expiry inside the gossipsub layer, not an LRU with O(N) updates per message, so duplicate checks do not block network threads.
measured_best: pr:lighthouse#1490: fixed high CPU, nodes not following head, HTTP delays; no numbers
