impact: Already done.

title: QUIC transport alongside TCP
idea: Offer a QUIC transport next to TCP and dial QUIC when the peer advertises it. QUIC has built-in encryption and multiplexing and fewer handshake round trips than TCP+Noise+mux.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/utils.rs:70-76 QUIC transport or'd with TCP
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/config.rs:365 disable_quic_support defaults false
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:479-486 dial list puts ENR QUIC multiaddrs before TCP
impact: QUIC is on by default and is dialed first when the peer advertises it.

title: Coded-chunk block broadcast (RLNC or erasure coding)
idea: Broadcast blocks as network-coded or erasure-coded chunks (RLNC, Reed-Solomon) so peers forward distinct pieces before holding the whole block and receivers reconstruct from any k chunks. Cuts propagation time versus whole-message gossip.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:843 Network::publish sends the whole encoded block per topic
~/.cargo/git/checkouts/rust-libp2p-b7fa834aec8fc27c/accba72/protocols/gossipsub/src/behaviour.rs:3024 forward_msg sends RpcOut::Publish with the full RawMessage
grep -i rlnc|reed_solomon|erasure|fountain|raptor over beacon_node and the gossipsub fork: no matches
gap: No coded-chunk block gossip. The only chunked path is the partial-messages extension for data columns (cell level, from PeerDAS erasure coding of blobs), not for blocks. Would need a new gossip protocol in the libp2p fork and network-wide spec agreement.
impact: Could cut block propagation latency per hop, but needs all clients to support it; gain unproven.
refute_note: Searched beacon_node, network and the gossipsub fork (incl. extensions/partial_messages) for any coding scheme; only PeerDAS column cells exist, which do not apply to blocks.

title: Use the fastest snappy codec for gossip and RPC
idea: Use the fastest available snappy implementation (native or optimized, with preallocated or reused buffers) for gossip and req/resp compress and decompress, chosen per message size or topic where benchmarks show it wins. Compression runs on every gossip message, so a faster codec cuts CPU on the hot path.
measured_best: 10000 B compress 51.5us (snappyjs) vs 5.9us (native); 100 B uncompress 154ns snappyjs vs 235ns native (slower for tiny uncompress) (pr:lodestar#8557)
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:123-124 Decoder::new() and decompress_vec per gossip message
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/pubsub.rs:149-150 Encoder::new() and compress_vec per message
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/codec.rs:127,187 snap FrameEncoder/FrameDecoder per RPC message
Cargo.lock snap 1.1.2 (pure Rust, no native/SIMD codec)
gap: Uses the pure-Rust snap crate everywhere, which is already fast, but allocates a fresh Encoder/Decoder and output Vec for every message and does not reuse buffers or pick a codec by size. Could use thread-local reusable Encoder/Decoder and preallocated output buffers in inbound_transform/outbound_transform, or a faster crate (e.g. snap-simd/lz4-style snappy bindings).
impact: Small CPU saving on gossip receive path (decompress of attestations/aggregates/blocks); likely well under 1% of node CPU. Gains mostly avoiding allocations.

title: Close RPC streams asynchronously
idea: Close req/resp streams with close-write plus reset, without waiting for the remote EOF on each request, so per-request latency does not include the close handshake.
measured_best: pr:prysm#8015: maybe latency improvements; no numbers
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/handler.rs:686-735 the last response moves the stream to Closing and is returned to the behaviour at once
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/handler.rs:786-815 Closing is polled with Sink::poll_close, a half-close that does not wait for the remote EOF
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/handler.rs:1154-1164 inbound side closes after the response has been sent
impact: Request latency does not include a wait for the remote side to close.

title: Encode gossip message once and share bytes
idea: SSZ-encode and snappy-compress a published or forwarded gossip message once, then share the same byte buffer by reference across the async publish path, all peers, the message cache and the transport. Avoids re-encoding or copying the message per peer or per async frame.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:846 message.encode() inside the per-topic loop, then message_data.clone() at :849
~/.cargo/git/checkouts/rust-libp2p-b7fa834aec8fc27c/accba72/protocols/gossipsub/src/behaviour.rs:635 publish passes data.clone() to outbound_transform
~/.cargo/git/checkouts/rust-libp2p-b7fa834aec8fc27c/accba72/protocols/gossipsub/src/behaviour.rs:3026 forward_msg clones RawMessage per peer
~/.cargo/git/checkouts/rust-libp2p-b7fa834aec8fc27c/accba72/protocols/gossipsub/src/types.rs:136 RawMessage.data: Vec<u8>
~/.cargo/git/checkouts/rust-libp2p-b7fa834aec8fc27c/accba72/protocols/gossipsub/src/types.rs:341 RpcOut::Publish owns a RawMessage (no Arc/Bytes)
gap: Make RawMessage.data a bytes::Bytes or Arc<[u8]> in the fork so per-peer RpcOut::Publish and mcache share one buffer; remove data.clone() in Behaviour::publish (pass ownership, compute msg_id first); messages have a single topic so the per-topic encode is minor.
impact: Removes one memcpy of each block/column per mesh peer (about 8 to 12) plus one extra copy at publish; small CPU and allocator relief at block time.
refute_note: Checked types.rs, queue.rs and mcache.rs in the fork for Bytes/Arc sharing: none; the queue only Arcs a counter. Verdict upheld.

title: No broadcast to self; reply to single peer
idea: Do not broadcast messages back to the local node, and answer a single peer's request directly instead of broadcasting the response to all peers.

impact: rust-libp2p does not self-deliver and LH answers requests over req/resp.

title: Do not republish gossip the library already forwards
idea: For messages received from the network (for example attestations), do not re-serialize and republish them at the application level or again from the op pool path; let gossipsub forward and dedupe them, and publish only locally created messages once. Removes duplicate gossip and serialization work.

impact: Remaining saving is bandwidth and gossipsub decode/mesh overhead (not BLS verification) on a node that has fallen behind after first sync; small and rare.

title: Subscribe duty subnets one epoch early
idea: Subscribe to the attestation subnet one epoch before the duty slot so the mesh is formed in time.

gap: Span levels were lowered to debug/trace (PR #7620), but the unfiltered MetricsLayer pushed in main.rs returns Interest::always and no max_level_hint for every callsite. title: Expire pending blocks and lookups by age
idea: Give each pending unknown-parent block or lookup a maximum lifetime (TTL or max duration) and drop it, with its children, when it expires. This bounds the queue and frees state and peers held by stuck lookups.

title: Exponential backoff for failing by-root roots
idea: Track retry count and next-retry time per missing root in a bounded map, back off exponentially after failures and stop after a max count, servicing newest roots first. Stale unservable roots then stop consuming peer request slots every loop.
measured_best: Retry rate ~170 req/s from 82 stale roots; verified by unit tests only (pr:lodestar#9791)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:917 failed_downloading capped at SINGLE_BLOCK_LOOKUP_MAX_ATTEMPTS=4
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:721 peers that already failed the request are de-prioritized
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:922 notified_unknown_roots dedups (peer, root) for 30s (NOTIFIED_UNKNOWN_ROOT_EXPIRY_SECONDS, manager.rs:93)
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:1059 record_unknown_root requires unknown_root_min_peers distinct peers before a new lookup
gap: Retries are count-capped, peer-deprioritized and event-driven (no polling loop), and re-triggers from attestations are throttled to once per (peer, root) per 30s plus corroboration. But there is no per-root memory of failure after a lookup is dropped and no exponential backoff, so an unservable root can be re-looked-up every ~30s per corroborating peer set. Add a bounded LRU of failed roots with attempt count and next-retry time checked in new_current_lookup.
impact: Small: Lighthouse does not have the poll-every-loop pattern that produced ~170 req/s in Lodestar; saves occasional repeat by-root requests for dead roots.
refute_note: Beyond the earlier review, found the 30s per-(peer,root) notification cache, the multi-peer corroboration gate and failed-peer deprioritization, which together act as a fixed-interval throttle but not a per-root exponential backoff.

title: Attestations for unknown root trigger block lookup
idea: When a gossip attestation references an unknown block root, start a by-root block request at once instead of waiting for the gossip block, since attestations often arrive first.

title: Event-driven unknown-parent lookup, not timer tick
idea: When a gossip block has an unknown parent, or a parent's payload arrives, request or drain the pending queue immediately instead of waiting for the next periodic tick (up to a third of a slot).

title: Request unknown block from peers that announced it
idea: Record which peers sent attestations or blocks referencing each unknown root and request the block from those peers first, deduped per (root, peer). Those peers are the ones most likely to have it.

impact: Requests go to peers that attested/sent the root; no further gain.

title: Keep failed or peerless lookups instead of dropping
idea: Do not delete a lookup when its download fails or it has no peers; return it to pending until it is idle and a timeout passes. Downloaded components and accumulated peers survive, so the next retry does not start from zero.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:844-852 no peers -> LookupRequestResult::Pending, lookup kept

gap: Peerless lookups are retained (PR #5839), but a lookup whose download fails SINGLE_BLOCK_LOOKUP_MAX_ATTEMPTS times returns TooManyAttempts and on_lookup_result calls drop_lookup_and_children. LH could reset failed_downloading/failed_peers and leave the lookup in AwaitingDownload, and let drop_stuck_lookups/no-peer pruning remove it.
impact: Avoids re-downloading child components and re-collecting peers after transient download failures near the head; rare in practice.

title: Lookup peer set only peers able to serve
idea: Add a peer to a block lookup only if it must have the block's components (it sent the block or attested to it), not a peer that merely announced a descendant. Requests then do not go to peers that lack the data.

title: One in-flight lookup per block root
idea: Keep a set or state machine of in-flight lookups keyed by block root and skip creating another request for a root already being fetched or already queued (including delayed lookups and parent/child lookups). This removes duplicate concurrent downloads and processing of the same block.

impact: Duplicate concurrent lookups per root are already impossible.

title: Skip lookup if block already received or processing
idea: Before issuing a by-root request, check gossip-seen caches, the pre-import and data-availability caches, fork choice and recently completed lookups, and skip or suppress the lookup if the block is already there. Gossip-delivered blocks are then not downloaded again via RPC once per attestation.
measured_best: Testing showed many more rpc_block than usual (no number) (pr:lighthouse#5681)

gap: block_lookup_request deliberately re-downloads when get_block_process_status returns NotValidated (gossip block in execution), and handle_unknown_block_root / the gossip UnknownHeadBlock path never consult the gossip seen-block cache for blocks still in gossip verification; only ExecutionValidated (DA-pending) blocks are skipped. Lighthouse dedups processing, not the download.
impact: Saves one by-root block download per root when attestations or columns arrive while the gossip block is still executing; reduced already by the 3-peer corroboration in record_unknown_root.

title: Request deepest missing ancestor directly
idea: When a block's parent is unknown, walk the locally held pending/queued blocks to the oldest missing ancestor and request only that root (processing queued parents first). This ends a parent-chain search in far fewer round trips than re-walking one block at a time.
measured_best: "we found the previous block search never ended, so we sped it up" (pr:ethlambda#114)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:374 new_current_lookup reuses the existing lookup for an ancestor root instead of re-walking

beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:586 continue_child_lookups processes queued children after the parent imports
impact: Held ancestors are never re-requested; only the oldest missing root downloads.

title: Serve lookups from locally stored orphan blocks

title: Remember invalid and unviable blocks and forks
idea: Keep a cache of block roots and chains found invalid or unviable (failed lookups, bad parent) and refuse to look them up, request them or reprocess them again; remove them from missing tables and penalise peers that keep sending them.
measured_best: 86 low-score disconnects in ~30 min before, 0 after; 580 penalized empty responses -> 0 (pr:nimbus#9288)

gap: Only too-long lookup chains (60s), failed range chains (30s) and EL-invalid payloads (fork choice) are remembered. Blocks that fail consensus validation in a lookup (bad signature, state transition error, etc.) are retried up to 4 times, dropped with children, and not cached, so a later attestation/gossip can trigger the same download and verification. Insert penalty-bearing failed roots into a longer-lived lookup-side LRU and check it in new_current_lookup and search_parent_of_child.

refute_note: Checked range sync failed_chains, fork choice invalid-payload tracking, the operator invalid_block_roots set and drop-with-children; none caches consensus-invalid roots for lookup sync.

title: Bound lookup child-peer map size

title: Slot-window caps on by-root payload envelopes

title: Store pending unknown-parent blocks on disk
idea: Store blocks waiting for a missing parent in the database and keep only root/parent-root indexes in memory, so long syncs with many pending blocks do not grow RAM unboundedly.

title: Header-only backward chain tracking for unknown chains
idea: Track unknown chains as backward chains of headers or roots linked to fork choice without holding full blocks, then forward-sync the blocks by root, so long non-finality does not exhaust memory.

gap: The goal (deep unknown chains do not grow memory; discover backward, then sync forward) is met by a different mechanism: a bounded backward walk with full blocks, then a hand-off to forward range sync to the tip root. Missing: a header/root-only backward chain linked to fork choice and a forward sync by root, so the backward phase still holds up to PARENT_DEPTH_TOLERANCE full blocks per chain and the forward phase is by-range from the peers, not by-root along the known chain.

idea: When building a by-root columns request for a peer, drop roots whose intersection with the peer's custody is empty so no empty entries are sent.

beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/requests/data_columns_by_root.rs:25-35 identifiers built per root from one column list
gap: Lighthouse asks every block root for the same set of indices per peer, so no per-root intersection with the peer custody exists and no empty entries are built.
impact: No change needed.

title: Dedupe column indices in by-root request
idea: Deduplicate missing column indices when building a column by-root request so the same column is not requested twice.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:27 column_requests is an FnvHashMap keyed by ColumnIndex
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:241-262 each column index assigned to exactly one peer per round
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:976-992 indices from sampling_columns_for_epoch minus cached
impact: Already done; a column index can appear only once per by-root request.

title: Cap blocks per by-root columns request
idea: Limit the number of blocks in a by-root columns request to the peer's max-blocks-per-request, besides the sidecar cap, so requests are not rejected and retried.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_sidecar_coupling.rs:234-262 range custody request covers one epoch batch (at most 32 roots)
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/methods.rs:580 DataColumnsByRootRequest::new errors if above max_request_blocks
gap: Request size is bounded by batch size (one epoch, 32 blocks, 128 columns max = 4096 sidecars), well under both caps, so no splitting is needed.
impact: No change needed.

title: Exclude already-stored blobs from by-root request
idea: Before requesting blob sidecars by root, filter out indices already in the database so only missing blobs are requested.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:976-992 custody_lookup_request filters out cached_data_column_indexes unless ignore_cache
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:420-431 single lookups pass ignore_cache=false
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/requests/ (no blobs_by_root request type exists)

title: Time column fetching relative to gossip arrival
idea: Start by-root column fetching at a point timed against expected gossip arrival so columns gossip will deliver are not also fetched by RPC.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:396-431 data request starts as soon as the block is downloaded; only the DA cache is consulted
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:967-992 custody_lookup_request waits only for a non-empty lookup_peers set, then filters cached_data_column_indexes
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:120-155 gossip/RPC dedup (duplicate_cache + QUEUED_RPC_BLOCK_DELAY) is for blocks, not columns
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:20 MAX_STALE_NO_PEERS_DURATION is a give-up timer, not a start delay
gap: Add a gossip-timed start for the column by-root request (for recent blocks, wait until a point after the expected column gossip arrival, then re-read cached_data_column_indexes before sending).
impact: Avoids RPC download of columns that gossip delivers moments later on lookups of recent blocks; modest bandwidth saving.
refute_note: Also checked the beacon processor reprocess queue (RPC block delay, unknown-block column queue, delayed reconstruction) and the custody request timers; none delay column fetching relative to gossip arrival.

title: No column fetch at Gloas block import
idea: For Gloas blocks skip fetching custody columns at block import (DA is checked on the envelope) and drain queued gossip columns instead of re-requesting all columns from peers.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:403-433 columns still requested in the block lookup for Gloas blocks (num_expected_blobs reads the bid)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:866-873 Gloas blocks import without columns (NoData allowed)
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:976-992 gossip-cached columns are skipped
gap: Block import is not gated on columns for Gloas and gossip-cached columns are not refetched, but the lookup still tracks a DataRequest and fetches missing custody columns from peers at block time instead of at envelope time. Move column fetch to the envelope step.
impact: Avoids column requests for Gloas blocks whose payload is withheld; small and only after Gloas.

title: Request blobs only after block is downloaded
idea: Do not request blobs or columns for a lookup root until the block is known, so they are requested only if the block has data and with the exact count.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:398-415 DataRequest::WaitingForBlock until block downloaded, then data_columns_required_for_block chooses Request or NoData
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:237 lookups start in WaitingForBlock
impact: Already done; no data request is sent before the block is known.

title: Key parent blob lookups by parent root
idea: Deduplicate parent blob lookups by the parent block root rather than the child root, so the same parent's blobs are not requested twice.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:374-393 new_current_lookup reuses an existing lookup with is_for_block(block_root)
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:256 search_parent_of_child creates lookup for the parent root
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:420-431 data request is part of the lookup for that root
impact: Already done; parent data requests are owned by the parent-root lookup and deduped by root.

title: No EL getBlobs during by-root sync
idea: Do not call engine getBlobs while serving by-root lookup sync; use it only for validated gossip objects.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:206-222 lookup block with MissingComponents triggers fetch_engine_blobs_and_publish_full(EnvelopeSource::Rpc)
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1127 gossip path
gap: Lighthouse calls engine getBlobs after RPC lookup blocks (process_type lookup) when components are missing; remove or gate that call in the MissingComponents arm of the lookup block processing in sync_methods.rs.
impact: Avoids one EL getBlobs call per by-root lookup block; Lodestar removed it for complexity, gain is small and may even lose a fast path, so likely skip.

title: Avoid retrying failed peers in lookups
idea: Remember per root (or per column) which peers failed or returned empty, cap retries per peer and exclude or deprioritise them when picking the retry peer, resetting when all are exhausted. Retries then spread over peers that may have the data instead of looping on the same one.
measured_best: Retry storm: 131 WARN retries over 56 roots in ~35 s on one node, peers hit 45+ times (pr:ethlambda#186)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:777 failed_peers per request state
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:640 record_failed_peer on block download error
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:708 block_lookup_request sorts failed peers last
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:353 select_column_peer excludes peers over MAX_CUSTODY_PEER_ATTEMPTS and orders by attempt count
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:61 SINGLE_BLOCK_LOOKUP_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 4 bounds retries per lookup
impact: Retries spread over other peers and are bounded per lookup; no retry storm.

title: Request missing payload envelope at payload deadline
idea: Do not search for a missing execution payload envelope at block arrival; record the root and, at the payload-due deadline, issue one by-root request (polling) if gossip has not delivered it, deduping triggers per payload.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:1103 handle_unknown_payload_envelope triggered by attestations (index==1), debounced
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:458-480 lookups request envelope right after block download
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2242 get_payload_due only used for timing metrics
gap: Envelope fetch is not deadline-based: lookups request the envelope immediately after the block, and attestations trigger separate searches. Would need a timer at payload-due in sync manager that issues one by-root request for blocks with payload_received false, deduped per root.
impact: Gloas only: fewer premature by-root envelope requests when gossip delivers the envelope within the deadline; small bandwidth/peer-load saving.

title: Fetch payload envelopes on demand only
idea: Do not fetch execution payload envelopes by RPC for every imported block; fetch one only when a child block or attestation needs the full payload.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:456-480 every Gloas lookup gets a PayloadRequest::Request after its block downloads
gap: Every looked-up Gloas block also fetches its envelope. Make PayloadRequest lazy: only request when a child block or index==1 attestation needs it (use the existing search_payload_envelope path).
impact: Gloas only: skips envelope downloads for lookup blocks nobody builds on; saves bandwidth during lookups, not on steady-state head.

title: Request parent envelope in parallel with parent block
idea: When filling a block gap, request the parent's payload envelope by root concurrently with the parent block request instead of after it, saving one round trip.
measured_best: Saves one round trip syncing to head (pr:prysm#16908)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:458-480 payload_request stays WaitingForBlock until block_request has downloaded data
gap: Payload request waits for the block to download (needs block for bid hash and fork check), so parent block and parent envelope are sequential. Request the envelope in parallel using the child's bid parent_block_hash (AwaitingParent already carries parent_block_hash) in the PayloadRequest init instead of waiting for the parent block.
impact: Gloas only: saves one RPC round trip per parent in a gap fill, roughly 100-300 ms per hop; only matters when lookups chain.

title: Batched by-root requests to best-scored peers
idea: Request missing parent blocks by root in batches from the best-scored peers with short dial timeouts, so a slow peer does not stall lookups.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:716-731 peer chosen by (failed, at-concurrency-limit, random) among lookup peers; no peer score; one root per request
gap: Peers are picked randomly with failed-peer and concurrency deprioritisation, not by score, and roots are not batched. Add the peer score as a sort key in block_lookup_request and batch roots into one BlocksByRoot request.
impact: Marginally fewer stalled lookups with a slow peer; negligible on mainnet nodes.

title: Redundant parallel lookup requests to two peers
idea: Send a missing-ancestor by-root request to two peers in parallel and take the first good response, so a slow or failing peer does not stall the lookup.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:708 block_lookup_request sends to exactly one peer, retries on failure
gap: Single peer per lookup request with retry. Would send the request to two peers in block_lookup_request and keep the first response.
impact: Cuts tail latency on a slow peer but doubles bandwidth for lookups; marginal.

title: Run parent lookups off the sync event loop
idea: Run parent lookups on a separate task and report the result by message instead of inline in the sync manager, so slow lookups do not block the sync loop.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:386-394 send_block_for_processing hands the block to the beacon processor
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:236 result returned as SyncMessage::BlockComponentProcessed
impact: Already done; lookup processing runs on beacon processor workers and reports by message.

title: Pass fetched block into blob validation
idea: Pass the already-fetched block directly into blob sidecar validation rather than re-reading it from the database.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3589 process_rpc_blobs takes block_root+slot, no DB block read
impact: Nothing; blob import never re-reads the block from the DB.

title: Run cheap subset check first on by-root responses
idea: Check that a by-root response is a subset of what was requested before the more expensive sanity checks, rejecting bad responses earlier.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/requests/blocks_by_root.rs:38-45 root check is the only check, done first
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/requests/data_columns_by_root.rs:57-71 block_root check first, then verify_inclusion_proof, then the cheap requested-index check
gap: DataColumnsByRootRequestItems::add runs verify_inclusion_proof (merkle hashing) before the cheap self.request.indices.contains(index) subset check, so a column with an unrequested index costs a proof verification before rejection. Swap the two checks.
impact: Negligible CPU saved only on misbehaving peers; one merkle proof per bad column.

title: Compute hash tree root outside pending-blocks lock
idea: Compute block roots before taking the pending-blocks lock so the lock is held as briefly as possible.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:92 lookups are owned by the single sync task, no shared pending-blocks mutex
impact: No lock around a pending-blocks map exists; sync manager is single-threaded.

title: DAG of unknown blocks drives by-root lookups
idea: Maintain a dedicated DAG of unknown blocks and their parent links and drive by-root lookups from it.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:92 single_block_lookups map by lookup id
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/parent_chain.rs:40 compute_parent_chains builds chains on demand
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:98 TODO notes lookups not indexed by block_root
gap: Lighthouse tracks lookups and derives parent chains on demand each time (O(n) scans) rather than keeping a persistent DAG; a persistent root-indexed DAG would need single_block_lookups re-indexed by block_root and parent links maintained incrementally in BlockLookups.
impact: Marginal CPU saving in search_parent_of_child under many concurrent lookups; function is only hot during attack or deep-fork conditions.

title: Debounce unknown-root attestation events per peer
idea: Debounce unknown-block-root events from attestations per (root, peer) pair so a peer forwarding thousands of attestations for one root causes one lookup update.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:271 notified_unknown_roots LRUTimeCache<(PeerId, Hash256)>
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:921-926 UnknownBlockHashFromAttestation skipped when (peer, root) already notified
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:927-934 same debounce for unknown payload envelopes
impact: Already done; one lookup update per (peer, root) within the cache TTL.

title: Do not start RPC lookups from partial gossip
idea: When gossip has delivered only a block or one blob, do not start a delayed RPC lookup for the rest; let gossip deliver it, avoiding double downloads.
measured_best: RPC takes ~1s; delayed lookups often double download (pr:lighthouse#4992)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1016 Fulu column MissingComponents: no lookup
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1972 gossip block MissingComponents: no lookup
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:790 Gloas gossip column with BlockRootUnknown sends UnknownBlockHashFromAttestation
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1182 same for partial columns
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:1242 BlockRootUnknown when no bid is cached for the column's block
gap: On Gloas, a gossip data column (or partial column) for a block not yet known (load_gloas_payload_bid returns None) immediately triggers UnknownBlockHashFromAttestation, so after 3 corroborating peers (DEFAULT_UNKNOWN_ROOT_MIN_PEERS) an RPC block lookup starts while the block is probably still arriving on gossip; there is no delay to let gossip deliver it.
impact: Avoids a by-root block download per slot when columns race ahead of the block on Gloas; Fulu is unaffected.

title: Bound pool size with hard cap and oldest-first eviction
idea: Put a hard cap on the number of attestations or gossip signatures held in the pool and evict the oldest slot or data root first (FIFO) when it is exceeded, with an O(1) size counter. This keeps memory bounded when finalization stalls or gossip floods.
measured_best: Devnet memory climbed to ~11.5 GB and crashed every ~27 min before; caps 4096/512 entries (pr:ethlambda#182)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/naive_aggregation_pool.rs:143 SLOTS_RETAINED=3
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/naive_aggregation_pool.rs:287 hard cap MAX_ATTESTATIONS_PER_SLOT rejects new entries (no eviction)
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:632 op pool prune by target epoch only
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:457 insert has no size check
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:638 stats() walks every map (no O(1) counter)
gap: The gossip-signature analogue (naive aggregation pool) has a hard per-slot cap but rejects new items rather than evicting oldest. The op pool has no entry cap, only a 2-epoch target window that does not depend on finalization, so it cannot grow without bound under a finality stall. Add a cap with oldest-slot eviction and an O(1) counter to AttestationMap.
impact: Low on Lighthouse: the time-based prune (not finality-based) plus observed_aggregators/observed_attesters dedup already bound pool size; a cap only guards pathological floods.
refute_note: Checked observed_aggregates/observed_attesters capacities and the naive pool cap; the ethlambda crash case (pool tied to finalization) does not apply because LH prunes by epoch, but no hard op-pool cap or FIFO eviction exists.

title: Size pool retention to the inclusion window
idea: Size the attestation pool cap and retention period so it still holds every attestation that can be included (64 slots post-EIP-7045, worst-case validator set), and re-read the live size while trimming. Block building then still has old attestations instead of pruning them early.
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:632-635 prune keeps target_epoch+1 >= current_epoch (previous and current epoch)
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:455-457 prune_attestations is the only removal
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1566 pruned by epoch on head update
impact: Already done; retention covers the full EIP-7045 window and there is no count cap that can trim early.

title: Skip attestations whose attesters are already on chain
idea: Track, per attestation data, the union of validators already included on chain (bitlists or index sets updated incrementally from imported blocks, with epoch-scale expiry) plus those already covered in the block being built, and reject, prune or skip pool attestations whose bits are all covered. The pool stays smaller and block packing does less work and carries no redundant attestations.
measured_best: None (pr:prysm#6993)
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation.rs:96 has_attested_in_epoch drops on-chain-covered validators at packing
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/max_cover.rs:62 zero-score items excluded
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs:574 is_known_subset rejects gossip aggregates that are subsets of already-seen aggregates
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5067 observed_block_attesters filled from block attestations
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:8355 observed_block_attesters used only for liveness, not pool filtering
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2699 add_to_block_inclusion_pool inserts without on-chain check
gap: Packing skips on-chain-covered attesters and gossip rejects subset aggregates vs seen aggregates, but nothing rejects or prunes pool entries whose bits are all already included on chain. observed_block_attesters already tracks per-epoch on-chain attesters and could be used to filter at add_to_block_inclusion_pool and to prune after block import.
impact: Smaller op pool and fewer AttMaxCover constructions during block production; modest packing-time win.
refute_note: Beyond the earlier review, found observed_block_attesters (on-chain attester set) and the gossip subset check; neither is used to drop pool entries covered on chain.

title: Remove block-included attestations from the pool on import
idea: When a block is imported (or becomes canonical on head change), delete its attestations from the op pool right away instead of waiting for expiry, decomposing post-Electra multi-committee attestations into per-committee aggregates so they match pool entries. The pool stays small and block production does not rescan or re-pack them.
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:295 insert_attestation; no remove-by-block method in the op pool API
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:455 prune_attestations by epoch only
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1566 only op-pool attestation prune call site
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation.rs:96 reward-cache filter only skips them at packing
gap: Block-included attestations remain until epoch prune. Add op_pool removal on block import/head change (decomposing Electra multi-committee attestations per committee), or reuse observed_block_attesters to drop fully covered entries.
impact: Smaller pool, cheaper get_attestations and less memory; packing cost scales with pool size.
refute_note: Listed every op pool pub fn and every op_pool.prune/remove call in beacon_chain; the only attestation removal is the epoch prune.

title: Aggregate attestations into pool entries on arrival
idea: When an unaggregated gossip attestation arrives, OR its bits and add its signature into an existing pool aggregate with the same data (keyed by attestation data), so the pool holds few large aggregates. Fewer objects are stored, hashed and compared, and an aggregator request becomes a lookup of a precomputed aggregate.
measured_best: None (pr:prysm#4376)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/naive_aggregation_pool.rs:255-293 AggregatedAttestationMap::insert ORs the single bit and aggregates the signature into the one entry per attestation key root
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/naive_aggregation_pool.rs:543-547 get() serves aggregator requests by lookup
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:422-456 gossip unaggregated attestations go into the naive pool on arrival when should_import
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:457-484 AttestationMap::insert greedily merges disjoint aggregates with the same data
impact: Already in place; the aggregator endpoint is a hash map lookup of a precomputed aggregate.

title: Aggregate lazily at block production or aggregator duty
idea: Store single-vote attestations separately, with no periodic background aggregation routine, and aggregate them only when an aggregate is requested or a block is produced, using hash tables keyed by attestation data and a temporary cache. No aggregation or signature deserialization is paid for aggregates that are never used.
measured_best: Speeds up iterating all attestations for a slot; improves aggregate quality and block packing (commit:nimbus@4ed2e34a9eb7)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2596,2699 single votes are aggregated eagerly on arrival, in both the naive pool and the op pool
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:380 Electra cross-committee aggregation is lazy, done only in get_attestations
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5944 naive pool is copied into the op pool lazily at block production
gap: Only cross-committee aggregation and the naive-to-op-pool copy are lazy. Per-attestation aggregation into the op pool happens eagerly on each gossip arrival (BeaconChain::add_to_block_inclusion_pool); making it lazy would mean storing singles and aggregating in get_attestations.
impact: Small CPU saving at best (skips aggregation for votes never packed); Lighthouse already uses hash maps keyed by data and has no background aggregation routine.

title: Avoid duplicate aggregation passes per slot
idea: Do not aggregate the same unaggregated attestations twice in a slot (for example for fork choice and again for an aggregator request), do not re-aggregate an aggregate with itself, and do not reset aggregate expiry on update. Reuse the earlier result to cut CPU and keep the pool small.
measured_best: pool count below 500 versus 2000 before (pr:prysm#4932)
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:540-549 insert only aggregates when bits are disjoint; equal entry is detected, so an aggregate is not merged with itself
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5944-5960 every block production re-inserts the whole naive pool into the op pool, recomputing attesting indices and cloning each attestation
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/naive_aggregation_pool.rs:268 naive pool skips already-set bits
gap: No self-re-aggregation and no expiry reset, but the naive pool is re-imported in full at each block production (import loop in produce_partial_beacon_block), repeating work done in prior slots. Track a high-water mark or drain imported entries to avoid it.
impact: Saves a few hundred to a few thousand insert calls (index lookups plus clones) per produced block; only matters on proposer duty.

title: Aggregate only committees a local aggregator will request
idea: Pre-aggregate gossip attestations and sync messages only for (slot, committee/subnet) pairs with a subscribed local aggregator or an imminent local proposer, and skip messages from old slots or arriving after 2/3 of the slot. Aggregation work for other committees is skipped.
measured_best: None (pr:lodestar#5256)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/subnet_service/mod.rs:353 should_process_attestation: true only if a local aggregator is tracked for the exact (subnet, slot)
beacon_node/network/src/subnet_service/mod.rs:270 aggregator subscriptions recorded per ExactSubnet
beacon_node/network/src/subnet_service/mod.rs:152 tracking disabled only with import_all_attestations
beacon_node/network/src/service.rs:572 should_process computed per gossip attestation
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:422 if !should_import return before fork choice and naive pool
beacon_node/src/cli.rs:122 --import-all-attestations opt-out flag
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/naive_aggregation_pool.rs:143 old slots refused (SlotTooLow)
gap: Unaggregated attestations are already only pre-aggregated for exact (subnet, slot) pairs with a subscribed local aggregator, as in Lodestar #5284 and Grandine. Missing: no gating of sync committee messages, no skip of attestations arriving after 2/3 of the slot, and no imminent-proposer exception (not needed since LH packs from aggregates).
impact: Remaining gain is small: sync committee messages are few, and late-arrival skipping saves little.
refute_note: The earlier review missed the network-layer gate: NetworkService asks SubnetService::should_process_attestation and the processor returns before add_to_naive_aggregation_pool unless a local aggregator has that exact subnet/slot.

title: Index pool entries in hash maps by data root
idea: Index attestations (and other pool items) by attestation data root or id in a hash map, so existence checks and lookups are O(1) and do not rehash data or scan the list.
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:59-67 HashMap<CheckpointKey, HashMap<CompactAttestationData, Vec<..>>>
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/naive_aggregation_pool.rs:236-239 HashMap keyed by AttestationKeyRoot
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:52-70 slashings/exits/payload attestations in HashMap/HashSet
impact: Already O(1) lookups by data key in every pool.

title: Prune pool by slot inclusion window each slot
idea: Store pool entries in per-slot maps and, every slot, drop whole slots that fall outside the inclusion window by the current wall-clock slot (for every attestation variant), instead of per-entry TTL caches or finality-based pruning. The pool stays bounded even during non-finality.
measured_best: None (pr:teku#5197)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7477 naive_aggregation_pool pruned every slot by wall clock
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/naive_aggregation_pool.rs:555-580 per-slot maps, SLOTS_RETAINED=3
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1564-1567 op pool attestations pruned by wall-clock epoch on epoch transition or reorg
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:191-200 prune_sync_contributions is slot-based but
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:739-753 its only caller is prune_all
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1710 prune_all runs only on finalization
gap: OperationPool::prune_sync_contributions and prune_payload_attestations are called only from prune_all, which runs only when finality advances (canonical_head.rs:1710). During non-finality the sync contributions and payload attestations of the op pool are never pruned, so they grow with every slot and are all serialized by persist_op_pool. Call both from per_slot_task with the current slot.

title: Reuse stored roots instead of rehashing pool keys

title: Fine-grained or concurrent locking in the op pool
idea: Put the locks inside the operation pool, per pool field or per attestation-data key, or use concurrent maps and lock-free groups, instead of one big lock around the whole pool on the chain. Gossip inserts and block production reads then do not contend on a single lock.
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:52-70 one RwLock per pool field, but all attestations share one RwLock<AttestationMap>

Lock per CheckpointKey (or per data), or aggregate on a snapshot outside the lock.

title: Greedy max-cover attestation selection by marginal reward
idea: When producing a block, select attestations from the op pool with a greedy maximum-coverage algorithm whose score is the marginal proposer reward (validators newly covered given those already chosen), instead of naive ordering. title: In-place bitfield operations in max-cover
idea: In the max-cover aggregation loop, mutate bitfields and candidate slices in place instead of allocating new bitlists and slices each step, and drop per-call length checks. This cuts allocations during aggregation and packing.

title: Compare and merge aggregates with bitfields, not indices
idea: Merge, compare and score aggregate participation (OR, subset, superset, intersection, unseen count) directly on committee-ordered aggregation bitfields, instead of expanding them to validator index arrays or Sets through committee lookups. title: Fast Electra committee-bits aggregation
idea: In post-Electra aggregation, skip committee-bit remapping when committee bits are equal, avoid recomputing committee start offsets and SSZ-hashing committee bits in superset checks, and OR aggregation bits directly on a bitset. Aggregation of many attestations gets faster with less memory.
measured_best: or rewrite ~4x faster, far less memory (pr:teku#8346)
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:254-277 same-committee checks and unions are byte-wise, no hashing (upheld)
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:279-300 aggregate_with_disjoint_committees rebuilds the whole bitlist and merges attesting_indices for every committee added
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:415-431 bitlist_extend copies bit by bit with get/set
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:578-586 compute_on_chain_aggregate folds 64 committees one by one, so the copy is quadratic
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:381-387 runs for both epochs on every block production under the write lock
gap: compute_on_chain_aggregate calls aggregate_with_disjoint_committees once per committee. Each call runs bitlist_extend, which allocates a new BitList and copies every bit of the growing aggregate one at a time, and re-merges the growing attesting_indices Vec. That is O(committees^2 * committee_size) per attestation data. Build the on-chain aggregate once: compute total length, then copy each committee's bytes (shift-OR at the offset) and concatenate the sorted indices once. Inferior single-committee aggregates are also re-aggregated on every call.
impact: Scratch bench (64 committees x 488 bits, mainnet size, ssz 974f78f, release): 1.59 ms per attestation data for the bit copy alone. With ~64+ data across prev/curr epoch that is ~100 ms per block production under the attestations write lock. Mainnet beacon_block_production_attestation_seconds is 170-270 ms on sigp ma-* nodes, against ~5 ms max cover and ~38 ms reward cache.
refute_note: Read the ethereum_ssz git dependency: union/intersection/is_subset are byte-wise on flat bytes, so the Teku costs (SSZ hashing, slow or, offset remapping) do not exist in Lighthouse; only the per-bit extend remains.

title: Time-boxed lock-free block attestation packing
idea: Build block attestation aggregates without a global pool lock and under a time budget, sort by reward and take the top entries, then fill up with single attestations under a total budget, so block production latency is bounded.
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:381-387 attestations.write() held for aggregate_across_committees, then downgraded to a read lock that is held through packing (blocks insert_attestation writers at lib.rs:301)
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/max_cover.rs:53-80 greedy maximum_cover, O(limit x items), no deadline or early exit
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5964-5989 block production calls get_attestations synchronously with only a timer metric, no timeout
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:424 only prev/curr epoch packed in parallel (rayon::join)
gap: There is no time budget for packing and no lock-free snapshot. Add a deadline to maximum_cover (return the best result so far) and/or take a snapshot of the per-checkpoint map so that packing does not hold the pool RwLock. Move the Electra aggregate_across_committees work out of the write-locked section. Lighthouse already has the parts that are not time-boxing: greedy packing ordered by reward score, and insert-time aggregation of single votes (a fill-up equivalent).
impact: This affects tail latency only. It bounds block production time with very large pools (non-finality, many aggregates that do not merge). Typical mainnet packing takes tens of ms.
refute_note: I also checked the block production call site for a timeout or a spawn_blocking deadline (none), and the max_cover internals for an early exit (none). Reward-sorted selection and insert-time aggregation exist, but the idea's core (time-boxed and lock-free) is absent.

title: Optimize unaggregated storage and expiry paths
idea: Optimize the attestation pool's unaggregated-attestation storage and its expiry pruning code paths.

title: Share one attestation pool for fork choice and blocks
idea: Use a single attestation pool for fork-choice votes and block inclusion instead of two separate pools, avoiding duplicate storage and processing.

title: Validate max-cover inputs once
idea: Validate that all candidate bitlists have equal length once before max-cover aggregation, instead of on every greedy iteration.
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/max_cover.rs:53 maximum_cover loop has no per-iteration length validation

title: Slasher bloom filter of data root for double votes
idea: In the slasher, store a tiny (about 2-byte) bloom filter of the attestation data root per validator and target epoch, inside the span entry, so double votes are detected without storing or loading full attestations. False positives are rare and are confirmed with a full lookup.
measured_best: None (pr:prysm#4948)
evidence: slasher/src/database.rs:595 check_and_update_attester_record stores a compact per-validator/target-epoch record (indexed attestation id) in attesters_db
slasher/src/database.rs:559 LRU cache of attestation data roots avoids loading full attestations
gap: Lighthouse reaches the same goal differently: the compact record is an id and the data root comes from an LRU (attestation_root_cache); a cache miss costs one indexed-attestation load. A 2-byte bloom filter in the span entry would only avoid those misses.
impact: Negligible; misses are rare because the LRU is primed with each batch's roots. Only affects slasher users.

title: Keep slasher span data cached in memory
idea: Keep recently used slasher min/max span data in an in-memory cache (LRU or a compact array over a recent epoch window), lazily load it, and write it to the DB only on eviction or shutdown, so detection does not save and load spans from disk on every attestation.
measured_best: None (pr:prysm#4388)
evidence: slasher/src/array.rs:397 get_chunk_for_update loads each chunk once per batch from DB and stores at the end of the batch
slasher/src/database.rs:76 only an attestation-root LRU exists, no cross-batch span cache
gap: Spans are loaded and written per batch (amortised over all attestations in the batch, not per attestation as in old Prysm), but there is no cache persisting chunks across batches. Add an LRU of chunks in SlasherDB used by get_chunk_for_update and flushed on eviction/shutdown.
impact: Cuts chunk read/decompress and write per slasher batch; modest, and only for --slasher nodes. Write-back risks crash consistency.

title: Aggregate lazy min-max surround detection
idea: Detect possible surround votes with one aggregate min-max of source/target epochs across all attestations (constant size, about 65KB) instead of per-validator min/max span arrays, and scan historical blocks only when the aggregate flags a possible surround. This replaces gigabytes of slasher storage.
measured_best: None (pr:lodestar#8873)
evidence: slasher/src/array.rs:140 per-validator chunked min/max spans (MinTargetChunk/MaxTargetChunk) are the only surround detector
gap: Would need a new aggregate min/max surround prefilter in slasher plus a historical block scan fallback; a redesign of Slasher::process_batch.
impact: Slasher is opt-in and few nodes run it; would save slasher disk (GBs) not normal node cost.

title: Append-only compressed validator reward files
idea: Persist per-epoch validator reward data as append-only compressed CSV plus aggregated daily summaries, and clear the state cache each iteration, so reward/analysis tooling writes faster, stores less and reports quickly.

title: Automatic checkpoint state download on first start

impact: Go string-to-byte-slice conversion allocation; no equivalent in Rust.

evidence: beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs: no DB analysis tool in store crate
impact: Nimbus offline DB inspection tool; Lighthouse has no comparable hashing tool on a hot path.

idea: Construct tagged-union objects (for example light client fork variants) directly with their final variant, instead of default-initializing, zeroing and then assigning, to avoid the redundant memset.

title: Cold-start span init over history length only
idea: On a slasher cold start with no DB, initialise the min/max span arrays by looping only over the circular-buffer history length instead of every epoch since genesis, because older cells are overwritten anyway. Boot goes from O(epochs*validators) to O(validators).
measured_best: None (pr:prysm#13620)
evidence: slasher/src/array.rs:528-530 epoch_update_for_validator returns early when no current epoch is stored (cold start: no genesis loop)

slasher/src/database.rs:96-101 cells are indexed modulo history_length (circular buffer)

But after a restart following downtime longer than history_length, epoch_update_for_validator (called from update_array for both MinTargetChunk and MaxTargetChunk) loops over every elapsed epoch per validator, rewriting the same circular cells several times. Start the loop at max(previous_current_epoch, current_epoch + 1 - history_length).

impact: The JVM thread-per-event pattern does not exist in Lighthouse.

title: Shrink large error enums by boxing
