beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/sync_committee_verification.rs:472 subcommittee_positions_for_public_key scans the committee
consensus/types/src/sync_committee/sync_committee.rs:70 linear scan
gap: Lighthouse has no cache keyed by sync period root. The committee lives in the state (Arc) so lookups need no state copy or tree hash; the cost that remains is the per-lookup pubkey scan. A period-root keyed cache of (committee, validator->positions) in BeaconChain would fix it; see other_caches-060.
impact: Small: no copy/hash per lookup already, since the state holds the committee in an Arc. Gain is only avoiding repeated scans.

title: Populate sync committee cache on miss
idea: On a sync committee cache miss (e.g. after restart), compute and fill the cache asynchronously so later lookups hit.
evidence: consensus/types/src/sync_committee/sync_committee.rs:73 positions computed from the committee stored in the state
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:162 only error variant mentions a sync committee cache
impact: No cold cache after restart.

title: Cheap nil checks in hot validator accessors
idea: Make the read-only validator view constructor do its cheap null check first and avoid expensive checks on this hot path.
measured_best: pr:prysm#12677: 10-20ms in happy case flame graph
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs validators accessed through milhouse lists, no Go-style nil check wrapper
impact: None.

title: Committee cache invalidation only when needed
idea: Make sure the committee-per-slot cache is not cleared on every state transition, only when its key actually changes, and do not re-broadcast already-seen gossip messages.
measured_best: pr:teku#711: enabled 4 node test to finalize
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:2824 build_committee_cache skips if initialized
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:2887 caches only rotated at epoch transition
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5220 skip if shuffling id already cached
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/config.rs:507 gossipsub duplicate cache
impact: No per-slot committee cache invalidation; duplicates not re-forwarded.

title: Committee cache also covers previous epoch
idea: Populate the committee cache for the previous epoch too, so previous-epoch attestations near an epoch boundary hit the cache instead of recomputing the shuffling.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:59 CACHED_EPOCHS=3
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:2768-2773 build_all_committee_caches builds previous/current/next
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:2887-2893 advance_caches rotates current into previous at epoch transition
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1692 build_all_committee_caches on block import
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5211-5230 shuffling cache (16 entries keyed by shuffling id) populated on import
impact: Previous-epoch attestations hit the state or shuffling cache without recompute.

title: Dynamic committee cache size during non-finality
idea: Size the committee/shuffling cache small by default and grow it only when the chain is not finalizing, instead of permanently using a large capacity.
measured_best: pr:prysm#13640: significantly less memory
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:25 DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE = 16 fixed
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/chain_config.rs:169 shuffling_cache_size static; shuffling_cache.rs:247 prune to fixed cache_size
gap: ShufflingCache::new takes a fixed cache_size and prune uses it; make cache_size a function of finalization distance (update in the head-update path) and shrink back when finalizing.
impact: Memory only: each entry is a few MB at 1M validators; 16 entries is already small, so saving is tens of MB at best. Non-finality growth is a resilience gain, not speed.

title: No redundant mutex around thread-safe caches
idea: Remove extra mutexes wrapped around caches that are already internally thread-safe (e.g. committee LRU), and use atomic contains-or-add instead of check-then-insert under a lock. Each access then takes one lock instead of two, cutting contention.
evidence: slasher/src/database.rs:76 Mutex<LruCache> is the only cache lock, single lock per access
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/rate_limiter.rs no locks
impact: Rust caches use one explicit lock; there is no double-lock wrapper around an internally thread-safe cache.

title: Concurrent caches instead of synchronized LRU
idea: Replace globally synchronized LRU caches on hot paths (state transition caches, finalized state cache, db block/validator caches) with a concurrent cache (Caffeine/ristretto-style), so a slow miss on one key does not block readers of other keys.
measured_best: pr:teku#10225: Stated bottleneck only: synchronized get blocks all threads on a slow fallback; JMH benchmarks added, no numbers in text
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:571 block cache lock taken only for the map get; DB load and full-block rebuild happen outside the lock
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:82 state_cache is Mutex<StateCache> with short critical sections
impact: Not worth it: Rust Mutex sections are short and slow misses are not computed under the lock, so the Java synchronized-fallback blocking problem does not occur.

title: Lock-free concurrent map instead of sharded dashmap
idea: Replace sharded-lock concurrent maps (dashmap) with a lock-free, async-aware concurrent map (scc) for state maps and caches shared across threads, to reduce shard lock contention.
evidence: Cargo.toml: no dashmap or scc dependency found
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src: caches use parking_lot RwLock/Mutex around LRU or maps
gap: Lighthouse does not use dashmap, so there is no sharded map to swap; replacing its RwLock caches with scc would be speculative.
impact: Contention gain unproven; no mainnet hotspot known.

title: Fine-grained locks in rate limiter
idea: Use read-write locks on the rate limiter map, per-bucket locks and a separate heap lock instead of one global lock, to reduce contention.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/rate_limiter.rs:485 Limiter<Key> plain struct with FnvHashMap, mutated via &mut self, no locks
impact: The RPC rate limiter is owned by the network task and has no locks to split.

title: Configurable slasher span cache size
idea: Make the slasher span cache size configurable so operators can cache more spans during long non-finality, trading memory for faster span updates.
evidence: slasher/src/config.rs:46 attestation_root_cache_size configurable
slasher/src/database.rs:76 LRU of attestation roots
slasher/src/config.rs:35-56 chunk_size, validator_chunk_size, history_length
gap: Span arrays are stored in the DB in chunks with no in-memory span cache whose size is configurable; only the attestation-root LRU size is configurable. Adding a span chunk cache config would need changes in slasher/src/array.rs and config.rs.
impact: Only slasher operators during long non-finality would gain.

title: Preallocate committee vector with true count
idea: Preallocate the all-epoch committees vector with the actual committee count, not slots per epoch, to avoid reallocation while appending.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/committee_cache.rs:276-286 get_all_beacon_committees uses Vec::with_capacity(epoch_committee_count())
impact: Landed (Lighthouse's own PR); trivial saving.

title: In-memory cache for validator builder registrations
idea: Keep validator builder (MEV) registrations in an in-memory cache by default instead of reading and writing them to the beacon database on every registration and proposal, and fetch proposer settings mid-epoch rather than at the epoch boundary. This removes DB round trips from block production.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/preparation_service.rs:124 validator_registration_cache in-memory RwLock<HashMap>
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/lib.rs:482 proposer_preparation_data in-memory Mutex<HashMap>
gap: Registrations are cached in memory and only changed keys are re-published; Lighthouse has no DB write for them, so the main idea already holds. Mid-epoch proposer-settings fetch is not applicable.
impact: Nothing meaningful remaining.

title: Delete unviable blocks from orphan quarantine
idea: When orphan blocks are marked unviable, also remove them from the orphan quarantine so they do not stay in memory.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs: lookups are dropped on failure
no orphan quarantine found in beacon_node
impact: Lighthouse has no orphan quarantine; failed lookups are dropped, so nothing stays in memory.

title: Drop intermediate deposit data early
idea: Generate deposits in a structure that drops intermediate values promptly, lowering peak memory (test harness).
evidence: beacon_node/genesis/src/interop.rs:85 build_genesis_state builds state directly, no 2019 test_harness deposit generator
beacon_node/genesis/src/interop.rs:146 drop_all_caches after build
impact: Test-only deposit generation from 2019; the harness no longer exists. No mainnet effect.

title: Do not precompute next-epoch proposer cache
idea: Drop the separate one-epoch-ahead proposer-indices precomputation once current-epoch shufflings already provide them, avoiding redundant work and memory.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:369-394 next-epoch proposer cache priming only after the decision slot, served from the state
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1673-1694 get_beacon_proposer_indices reads proposer_lookahead for current/next epoch post-Fulu
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1655-1661 get_beacon_proposer_index reads proposer_lookahead post-Fulu
impact: No redundant next-epoch proposer computation: post-Fulu the next epoch's proposers are a copy out of proposer_lookahead, and pre-Fulu only the current epoch is primed.

title: Recompute Merkle zero hashes instead of storing
idea: Do not serialize or store Merkle tree zero hashes; recompute or use a static table on construction since they are constant.
evidence: Cargo.lock tree_hash/milhouse: zero hashes are static tables built on first use, not serialized with trees
beacon_node/store/src/lib.rs: states stored as SSZ/diffs, no tree internals
impact: Lighthouse does not serialize Merkle zero hashes.

title: Array-backed maps for fork-keyed tables
idea: Use array-backed enum maps/sets for tables keyed by fork or milestone enum instead of hash or tree maps, for faster lookup and less memory.
evidence: consensus/types: fork-keyed data uses ForkName enum matches and struct fields, not hash/tree maps
impact: Rust enums with match need no enum-map; no hot table keyed by fork.

title: Proposer cache keyed by epoch and decision root
idea: Cache the proposer indices of an epoch keyed by (epoch, seed/decision root), pruned by epoch on update instead of a single LRU, so proposer selection runs once per fork and epoch and eviction is deterministic.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:1-9 cache keyed by (epoch, decision block root)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:26 CACHE_SIZE=16 LRU
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:14 OnceCell per key, so each key is computed once
impact: Already keyed by epoch and decision root and computed once per fork and epoch; LRU eviction of 16 tiny entries rather than epoch pruning has no measurable cost.

title: Evict empty reprocess queue entries
idea: In the delayed-work reprocess queue, remove the per-block-root entry when its last queued attestation times out, so entries for never-imported blocks do not leak.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:1264-1284 removes empty per-root Vec on expiry for both block and payload maps
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:1305-1316 same for light client updates
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:1850 regression test
impact: Per-root reprocess maps do not leak entries for never-imported blocks.

title: Cheap checks before shuffling in committee cache
idea: In committee cache construction, run cheap validity checks (validator count limits) before computing active indices and shuffling so failures return early.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/committee_cache.rs:120-139 initialized_unchecked checks ZeroSlotsPerEpoch and TooManyValidators before get_active_validator_indices, returns InsufficientValidators before get_seed/shuffle_list
impact: Only affects invalid-input failure paths.

title: Finalize deposits only up to finalized state
idea: Move deposits into the finalized deposit cache only up to the deposit count in the finalized state, not all deposits seen, so non-finalized deposits stay handled correctly.
evidence: beacon_node has no eth1 or deposit cache module (ls beacon_node: no eth1 dir); deposits come from execution requests (Electra)
impact: The eth1 deposit cache is gone from Lighthouse, so there is nothing to finalize.

title: Fixed growth step for pubkey cache
idea: Grow the validator pubkey cache by a fixed step instead of doubling capacity, avoiding a huge copy and over-reservation at mainnet registry size.
measured_best: commit:lodestar@133ef248a5e6: Doubling would copy ~450MB at mainnet scale
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:111 reserve(validator_keys.len()) on Vec (amortized, can still double) and HashMap
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:57 load_from_store pushes with no reserve
gap: validator_pubkey_cache load_from_store pushes without capacity and import_new_pubkeys uses Vec::reserve (amortized doubling); use reserve_exact or preallocate from the state's validator count.
impact: Only matters at startup/rare growth: avoids one transient copy of a few hundred MB and some over-reserved memory.

title: Free pre-genesis state after genesis
idea: Release the pre-genesis state and chainstart deposits from memory once the genesis state is built.
evidence: beacon_node/genesis/src/lib.rs and interop.rs: no eth1 genesis service; genesis loaded from a checkpoint/genesis.ssz
impact: No pre-genesis state or chainstart deposit flow exists in current Lighthouse.

title: Prune proposer cache once per duties request
idea: Prune the proposer-id cache once per duties request instead of once per matched validator inside the loop.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:7 LRU cache, never explicitly pruned per request
impact: None; no per-validator prune exists.

title: Per-period cache of validators' sync committee positions
idea: Compute once per sync committee period each validator index's positions/subcommittee indices in the current and next sync committee and keep them in the state caches. Is-in-committee checks, subnet computation, selection-proof validation, gossip validation and aggregation then are lookups instead of scanning committee pubkeys.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/sync_committee_verification.rs:472 subcommittee_positions_for_public_key per message
consensus/types/src/sync_committee/sync_committee.rs:70 iterates all 512 pubkeys comparing 48 byte keys
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1753 get_sync_committee_indices does 512 pubkey_cache lookups per block (altair/sync_committee.rs:50)
http_api/src/sync_committees.rs:307 same scan per duty
gap: Add a per-period cache (validator_index -> subnet positions, plus the committee index vector) stored in BeaconState caches or BeaconChain; use it in verify gossip sync messages, process_sync_aggregate (get_sync_committee_indices) and the HTTP duties.
impact: Cuts a 512-key scan per gossiped sync message (thousands per slot on mainnet) and 512 hashtrie lookups per block; likely sub-ms per slot of CPU, small but cheap.

title: Feed light client server only from new head blocks
idea: Compute and import light client server data only for blocks that become the new head, not for every imported block. Blocks that never become canonical then cost no light client work.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4786-4796 cache_state_data runs for every imported block (no head check)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_server_cache.rs:59-75 cache_state_data computes finality/sync-committee proofs via LightClientCachedData::from_state
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_server_cache.rs:467-477 from_state computes three merkle proofs per block
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5176-5190 producer event sent for any block with delay < 32 slots, not only new heads
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_server_cache.rs:141-160 updates only kept if is_latest by (attested_slot, signature_slot), a slot heuristic rather than fork-choice head
gap: Neither cache_state_data nor the update producer is gated on the block becoming the new head; only a recency filter (<32 slots) and a slot-based is_latest check exist. Gate both (or move them) to run after recompute_head when the block is the canonical head, or compute proofs lazily on demand.
impact: Only on --light-client-server nodes; avoids per-block proof computation and update recompute (DB block reads, sync committee store writes) for non-canonical blocks, a few percent of blocks.

title: In-memory execution payload envelope store for hot chain
idea: Keep execution payload envelopes for the recent (hot) chain in an in-memory store so envelopes-by-range requests are served without database reads.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_streamer/beacon_chain_adapter.rs:30-41 reads summary and body from store
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:703-719 hot_db reads
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_envelopes.rs:87 only holds unpublished envelopes
gap: Add an in-memory map of recent envelopes (summary + body) filled on import and pruned at finalization; consult it in the envelope streamer before get_payload_envelope_summary/get_payload_body.
impact: Saves hot DB reads when serving envelopes-by-range to peers, only on Gloas and mostly for recent ranges; small gain.

title: Keep aggregated attestation payloads in memory, not DB
idea: Hold aggregated attestation payloads in an in-memory buffer instead of writing and reading them through the database, removing DB round trips on the aggregation path.
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:54 attestations are held in memory (AttestationMap), no DB path
impact: Lighthouse aggregates in memory already; the ethlambda DB path does not exist.

title: Cached pubkey-to-index map instead of registry scans
idea: Maintain a pubkey-to-validator-index map built in one pass and extended incrementally from the last known index (indices never change), instead of linearly scanning the validator registry for each pubkey lookup.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:26 indices HashMap<PublicKeyBytes,usize>
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:87-101 import_new_pubkeys iter_from(self.pubkeys.len())
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:189 get_index
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1105 get_validator_index via per-state PubkeyCache
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:2979-2991 update_pubkey_cache extends from start_index
beacon_node/http_api/src/validator/mod.rs:47-63 pubkey_to_validator_index uses global cache
impact: O(1) pubkey lookups with incremental extension on block import, deposits, epoch processing and the API.

title: Single pubkey index map, no unfinalized pubkey cache
idea: Do not keep a separate per-fork unfinalized pubkey-to-index cache; since validator indices assigned by deposit processing cannot change on reorg, add new pubkeys directly to one global index map.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:26 single global map in the chain
consensus/types/src/state/pubkey_cache.rs:1-14 per-state PubkeyCache (rpds HashTrieMap) carried by every BeaconState
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1105-1111 get_validator_index uses the per-state map
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:2979-2997 update_pubkey_cache / drop_pubkey_cache
consensus/state_processing/src/per_epoch_processing/single_pass.rs:165,406 epoch processing uses the per-state map
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:2759 build_caches rebuilds it
beacon_node/store/src/reconstruct.rs:129 build_caches on reconstructed state
gap: State transition (get_validator_index, update_pubkey_cache, single_pass process_pending_deposits, verify_deposit) keeps a second per-state persistent pubkey map instead of using the one global ValidatorPubkeyCache. That map is cloned with each state and rebuilt from scratch (about 2M HAMT inserts) when a state is loaded without caches (build_caches, reconstruct).
impact: Saves some memory per cached state and avoids full rebuilds on cold state loads. Clones are already cheap because the map is structurally shared, so the gain is small.

title: Cache sync committee subnet ids per validator
idea: Cache the sync committee subnet ids for each validator per period so duty and subscription handling read them from a cache instead of recomputing from the state.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/subnet_service/mod.rs:282 computes from indices supplied in the request
consensus/types/src/sync_committee/sync_subnet_id.rs:45 compute is one integer division per index
impact: Subnet id is index/subcommittee_size taken from request data, no state lookup, so nothing worth caching.

title: Iteration-safe bounded maps in the operation pool
idea: Use a bounded map/set that is safe and consistent to iterate (copy-on-write or lock-based) for operation pool caches, instead of a weakly consistent concurrent wrapper.
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:49-70 every pool map/set is a parking_lot RwLock over HashMap/HashSet; no weakly consistent concurrent maps (no DashMap in beacon_node)
impact: Iteration is consistent under the lock.

title: Size shuffling cache for forks; compute each once
idea: Size the committee shuffling cache to hold several epochs across many forks (and long non-finality), and make a miss compute-once so concurrent requesters wait instead of recomputing. Late attestations and forks then do not evict and recompute shufflings repeatedly.
measured_best: shuffling ~6% CPU, ~20 computes/epoch reduced to 1 (pr:teku#5892)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:25 DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE=16
beacon_node/src/cli.rs:675 --shuffling-cache-size configurable
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:256 prune_cache never evicts head shuffling ids
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:362-374 miss creates promise under write lock; waiters block on it
impact: Each shuffling computed once; concurrent requesters wait on the promise.

title: Dependent-root keyed shuffling cache with lookahead
idea: Key the shuffling cache by the dependent (decision) root, separate from larger per-epoch data, and compute it ahead when the determining block is processed. Attestations on non-canonical forks then need no state replay, and forks sharing a dependent root share one shuffling.
measured_best: lower memory by sharing shufflings between EpochRefs of same dependent root (no numbers) (pr:nimbus#3990)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:143 keyed by AttestationShufflingId (epoch, decision block)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5211 primed at block import for current and next epoch
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:397-411 next-epoch shuffling inserted ahead
impact: Forks sharing a decision root share one Arc<CommitteeCache>; attestations hit the cache without state replay.

title: Never evict head epoch shufflings from cache
idea: Evict shuffling cache entries by lowest epoch rather than LRU, and pin the head's previous, current and next epoch shufflings so they are never evicted and recomputed.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:252-285 prune_cache sorts by shuffling_epoch and skips head_shuffling_ids
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:309 update_head_shuffling_ids
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1546 head ids updated on every head change
impact: Head previous/current/next shufflings are never evicted.

title: Persist pubkeys uncompressed to skip startup decompression
idea: Store validator pubkeys in uncompressed (or checksummed flat snapshot) form on disk and load them directly at startup, avoiding decompressing every BLS key on restart.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:231-242 DatabasePubkey::from_pubkey stores serialize_uncompressed, as_pubkey uses deserialize_uncompressed
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:55-79 load_from_store reads stored uncompressed keys
crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:141-152 deserialize_uncompressed -> blst PublicKey::deserialize (on-curve only, no decompression sqrt)
~/.cargo/registry/src/*/blst-0.3.17/src/lib.rs:876-889
impact: Restart skips per-key decompression; what is left is one KV read per validator plus a cheap compress() for the index map.

title: Parallel pubkey decompression when building pubkey cache
idea: When building the validator pubkey cache from a fresh checkpoint state, decompress the pubkeys in parallel on a thread pool, since serial decompression of every key dominates startup.
measured_best: Sepolia validator_pubkey_cache_new 109.64ms -> 21ms; Hoodi import 12.77s vs >120s timeout (pr:lighthouse#8451)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:36-51 ValidatorPubkeyCache::new calls import_new_pubkeys on an empty cache
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:117 is_initial_import
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:143-159 into_par_iter decompression
impact: Checkpoint-start cache build is parallel (lighthouse#8451).

title: Lazy TTL expiry without per-cache sweeper threads
idea: Implement TTL caches that check expiry on read and insert instead of running a background sweeper thread per cache, so per-peer or per-request caches cost no thread and do not leak.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/gossip_cache.rs: uses delay-queue polled in the swarm task, no thread per cache
gap: No per-cache sweeper threads exist; expiry is driven by async DelayQueue/HashSetDelay.
impact: None; no thread cost to remove.

title: Lazy dirty-flag rehashing of deposit merkle tree
idea: Store the deposit merkle tree as full levels and mark nodes dirty on push, recomputing hashes only when a root or proof is requested, so batched pushes hash each node once.
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/metrics.rs only mention of deposit cache; no eth1 DepositCache in tree
gap: Lighthouse has no deposit merkle tree cache any more (eth1 deposit tree removed).
impact: Nothing.

title: Configurable light client data retention period
idea: Make the number of sync committee periods of light client data the beacon node keeps configurable, so operators can retain fewer and shorten LC data computation during import and sync.
measured_best: lowering below default speeds up import (no numbers) (pr:nimbus#3799)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/chain_config.rs:88 only enable_light_client_server bool
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:831-885 get_light_client_update(s) read per period, no retention setting
beacon_node/src/cli.rs: no LC retention flag
gap: Add a CLI flag and ChainConfig field for number of periods kept, and have the LC update storing/pruning (store_light_client_update, recompute_and_cache_light_client_updates) skip or delete older periods.
impact: Small: LC server work is skipped entirely when disabled (enable_light_client_server); a retention knob would only trim DB size and per-block LC work for operators who keep it on. Gain unmeasured upstream.

title: Single-flight active validator count, fetched only when needed
idea: Compute the active validator count under a lock so one cache miss blocks other readers instead of each loading the state from disk, and fetch it only for gossip topics that need it.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/service.rs:832 reads count from cached head
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:389 active_validator_count from cached committee cache
gap: Count comes from the already-cached head state committee cache; no DB state load on a miss.
impact: Nothing to save.

title: Pubkey cache reads that do not serialize on LRU recency
idea: For the pubkey cache, avoid an LRU whose Get mutates recency under an exclusive lock: use a plain map with a read-write lock when all keys fit, or update recency asynchronously, so concurrent readers do not contend.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1629 validator_pubkey_cache.read() RwLock, no LRU
gap: Pubkey cache is a plain Vec/map behind an RwLock; reads do not mutate recency.
impact: Nothing.

title: Don't block pubkey cache readers while adding new keys
idea: When block import adds new validators to the pubkey cache, hold only a read (upgradable) lock or a separate lock while decompressing and persisting new keys, upgrading to write only when needed, so attestation verification readers are not blocked.
measured_best: small improvement in attestation verification times (pr:lighthouse#6190)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4487 upgradable_read then upgrade only if state.validators().len() > cache.len()
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:91-101,128-131 import and decompress run inside &mut self; DB write deferred as StoreOp
gap: Upgradable read and DB write deferral exist, but upgrade happens before decompression, so readers are blocked during decompression of new keys. Decompress the new keys (from state.validators().iter_from(len)) while only holding the upgradable guard, then upgrade just to push into pubkeys/pubkey_bytes/indices in import_new_pubkeys.
impact: Slightly shorter write-lock hold on blocks that add validators (a few per block, decompression is tens of microseconds each); small attestation verification latency gain.

title: Remove timeout locks on shared caches
idea: Use plain blocking read-write locks (or allow disabling lock timeouts) on attestation, pubkey and eth1 caches instead of timeout locks, so slow operations do not error and retry, wasting work and livelocking slow hardware.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/historical_blocks.rs:359 only remaining try_read_for (backfill, 30s)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1631-1700 pubkey cache accessed with blocking read()
impact: Timeout locks are gone from the hot paths. The 30s timeout left in backfill only matters on very slow hardware.

title: Native first/last DB lookups instead of iterators
idea: Use the key-value store's native first()/last() lookups to find the lowest or highest key instead of creating an iterator and calling next()/next_back(), which is cheaper on B-tree stores.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/database/leveldb_impl.rs:204 iter_column_from seeks; no min/max key lookups via next()/next_back found
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3339 only .next() use
gap: No code path finds a lowest/highest key through an iterator; LevelDB has no native first/last anyway, redb range is used for iteration.
impact: Negligible.

title: Cache unfinalized light client updates, flush on finality
idea: Keep light client updates for the non-finalized period in an in-memory per-branch cache, serve canonical updates from it, and write to cold storage only on finalization, avoiding DB writes for fork data.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_server_cache.rs:243 keeps only latest update per period, reads DB on miss
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:831 get_light_client_update from DB
gap: Updates are recomputed per block and written to the DB; Lighthouse would need a per-branch in-memory cache in recompute_and_cache_updates flushed at finalization.
impact: Saves small DB writes per block for fork data; only matters for nodes serving light clients.

title: Oldest-first eviction of slasher span cache
idea: Evict the oldest epochs from the slasher's in-memory span cache when pruning, and flush all spans to disk on shutdown, bounding memory without losing spans.
evidence: slasher/src/array.rs: spans stored in a database per chunk, no prysm-style in-memory span map
gap: Lighthouse slasher design differs (chunked on-disk arrays, batch updates), so the prysm eviction does not map.
impact: Only affects slasher users.

title: Persist light client sync progress across restarts
idea: Persist the light client's latest finalized header and sync committee to disk so a restart resumes from it and skips the slow bootstrap step.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_server_cache.rs:195 server persists updates; no LC client in beacon_node
gap: n/a: Lighthouse has no light client sync client (only a server that already persists updates via store_light_client_update).
impact: None; no client-side LC sync to resume.

title: Persist eth1 deposit and block caches on shutdown
idea: Save the eth1 deposit and eth1 block caches to disk on shutdown and reload them at startup, so they need not be re-downloaded and rebuilt from the execution node.
evidence: beacon_node/ has no eth1 module; consensus/state_processing/src/builder_deposits_cache.rs:42 only builder deposit sig cache
gap: n/a: Lighthouse removed the eth1 deposit/block caches; deposits come from state and execution requests.
impact: None.

title: Preallocate maps; copy only fork data for chain info
idea: Preallocate map capacity when the final size is known, and when serving chain info copy only the fork field rather than cloning the whole beacon state.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/state_id.rs:165 fork() reads only the fork
gap: n/a: Go-specific map prealloc and state copy; Lighthouse's state_id::fork returns only the fork, and Rust collections are sized explicitly where hot.
impact: Negligible.

title: Precompute own committee duties per dependent root
idea: Cache the node's own validators' committee membership keyed by dependent root and do the precomputation and pruning on a dedicated executor, off the block/attestation processing path.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:323-325 AttesterMap keyed by epoch with DependentRoot
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1253-1273 refetch only on (epoch, dependent_root) conflict
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1369-1384 selection proofs computed in executor.spawn background task
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1206-1212 pruning by HISTORICAL_DUTIES_EPOCHS in the poll task
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:397-411 BN shuffling cache primed per AttestationShufflingId off the import path
impact: Lighthouse's separate VC already scopes own duties by dependent root and computes them in background tasks, so none of this runs on the BN block or attestation path.
refute_note: Earlier review searched only the beacon node; Grandine's integrated validator maps to Lighthouse's validator_client DutiesService, which caches own duties keyed by (epoch, dependent_root), precomputes selection proofs in spawned tasks and prunes old epochs.

title: Check cache before recompute or reinsert
idea: Before computing a value for a cache (proposer indices, committees, pubkeys), check whether the key already exists and return early, skipping the duplicate computation, validation and locked write.
measured_best: initial sync up to 20% faster (pr:prysm#8096)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:133-143 get_or_insert_key returns a OnceCell
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:185-195 with_proposer_cache get_or_try_init computes once, even across threads
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:158 insert skips existing key
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5220-5225 import_block_update_shuffling_cache_fallible checks contains() before build_committee_cache
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:230-244 insert_committee_cache keeps existing Committee
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4490 pubkey cache write lock only when new validators
impact: Duplicate proposer, shuffling and pubkey computations are skipped.

title: Proposer index from pre-advanced next-slot state
idea: When validating gossip blocks, read the expected proposer index from a pre-advanced next-slot state cache instead of processing slots on a state copy for each call.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1025-1050 gossip proposer from with_proposer_cache keyed by shuffling decision root; parent state loaded only in the miss closure
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:355-394 pre-advanced head state primes current and next epoch proposers
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:175-195 state_provider called only when the OnceCell is empty
impact: The gossip block proposer check is a cache lookup. The state is loaded only on a miss, and then from the state cache, which already holds the advanced state.

title: Derive payload timeliness committee from cached committees
idea: Compute the ePBS payload timeliness committee from the already-cached beacon committees of the slot instead of recomputing the shuffling.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:3591-3627 get_ptc reads stored ptc_window
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:3632-3661 compute_ptc_with_cache builds PTC from committee_cache.get_beacon_committees_at_slot
consensus/state_processing/src/per_epoch_processing/single_pass.rs:566 epoch processing fills ptc_window with the lookahead committee cache
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:50-70 CachedPTCs stored next to committee cache for gossip
impact: PTC is never recomputed from a fresh shuffling.

title: Primitive int collections for validator indices
idea: Use primitive-specialized int maps, sets and lists (no boxed integer objects) for validator indices, subnets and similar collections, including those passed across APIs, to cut per-entry allocation and GC pressure.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:170 plain Vec<usize>
gap: n/a: JVM boxed integers; Rust uses unboxed u64/usize collections.
impact: None.

title: Prune the execution payload bid pool in production
idea: Actually prune old entries from the ePBS execution payload bid pool during normal operation (not only in tests) so old bids do not accumulate.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7480 gossip_verified_payload_bid_cache.prune(slot) in per_slot_task, outside the sync-gated section
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_bid_verification/payload_bid_cache.rs:135-139 prune split_off on highest_bid and seen_builder_bids
beacon_node/builder_client/src/bid_streams.rs:462-466 bid stream prune retain by slot
impact: Old bids do not accumulate.

title: Prune payload envelope input cache after each import
idea: Prune the payload-envelope (data availability input) cache after every block import, not only at synced next-slot preparation, so it cannot grow without bound during sync on a non-finalizing network.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/mod.rs:55 AVAILABILITY_CACHE_CAPACITY = 32
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/mod.rs:118 LruCache::new(AVAILABILITY_CACHE_CAPACITY)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/mod.rs:662 do_maintenance by cutoff epoch
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1656 maintenance on finalization
impact: Cache is hard-capped at 32 entries, so it cannot grow without bound during sync on a non-finalizing network.

title: Prune invalid execution payload envelopes
idea: Remove execution payload envelopes that failed validation from the cache and storage so they do not accumulate.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/import.rs:153 invalid payload status handled before storing
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/mod.rs:118 bounded LRU
gap: n/a: envelopes failing verification are never inserted in cache or store, and the cache is a bounded LRU pruned on finalization.
impact: None.

title: Drop finalized deposits and proofs from deposit cache
idea: On finalization, drop merkle proofs (and, post-Electra, pending deposits) of finalized deposits from the in-memory eth1 deposit cache, keeping only leaves needed for the tree, since proofs are only needed for block inclusion.
measured_best: Medalla deposit memory 223.17MB -> 19.50MB (92%) (pr:prysm#7478)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:359 only a static eth1_data field remains; no deposit cache/proofs in src
impact: Nothing to save: no eth1 deposit cache or proofs exist in the current tree (grep for DepositCache finds nothing outside tests/genesis).

title: Finalization-pruned seen cache for data column sidecars
idea: Bound the observed/seen data column sidecar cache by slot and prune it on finalization (as for blobs), instead of a never-pruned map or a fixed-size LRU sized for 1000 blocks x 128 columns.
measured_best: 16.4 MB constant -> 0.94 MB average (94.3%) (pr:prysm#15477)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/observed_data_sidecars.rs:129-135 HashMap<ObservationKey(slot), HashSet<index>>
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/observed_data_sidecars.rs:191-201 rejects sidecars at or before finalized slot
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/observed_data_sidecars.rs:205-213 prune retains slot > finalized
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1615 observed_column_sidecars pruned on finalization
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/builder.rs:1034
impact: The column seen-cache is bounded by finalization, not by a fixed LRU.

title: Prune payload-ID/proposer preparation cache on duty requests
idea: Prune past-slot entries of the proposer preparation / payload-ID cache also when serving proposer-duties requests, so stale entries do not accumulate.
evidence: beacon_node/execution_layer/src/lib.rs:741 spawn_clean_proposer_caches_routine runs every epoch
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/lib.rs:851 clean_proposer_caches retains last 2 epochs of proposer_preparation_data and proposers
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/engines.rs:135 payload_id_cache is a fixed-size LRU
impact: Memory stays bounded already; negligible.

title: Prune beacon proposer cache on finalization
idea: Prune entries of the beacon proposer cache for epochs older than finalization so the cache does not grow.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:7 doc: LRU, not pruned after finality
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:26 CACHE_SIZE=16
beacon_node/execution_layer/src/lib.rs:851 clean_proposer_caches (the cache lighthouse#3109 actually pruned)
impact: Entries are tiny and capped at 16; nothing to gain.

title: Prune eth1 data cache by voting-window timestamp
idea: Prune the eth1 block/data cache by the latest block timestamp so it holds only blocks inside the eth1 voting window range.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/builder.rs: no eth1 block cache; grep eth1_cache/DepositCache finds none
impact: No eth1 data cache exists, so nothing to prune.

title: Reject future-slot blocks before block timing cache
idea: Validate that a block's slot is not far in the future before inserting it into the block timing/observation cache, and bound its pruning, so peers cannot grow it with far-future entries.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3942 FutureSlot rejection before block_times_cache.set_time_observed
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_times_cache.rs:288 prune keeps slots in (current-64, current+1]
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1610 gossip records only after verify_block_for_gossip succeeds
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7478 prune per slot
impact: Prevents peer-driven growth of the cache; already done.

title: Slot-first nested map for cheap seen-cache pruning
idea: Key seen caches by slot in an outer map and by root in an inner map, so pruning below a slot removes whole outer entries instead of iterating every root and checking its slot.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/observed_block_producers.rs:44 flat HashMap<ProposalKey{slot,proposer},..>, prune at :187 iterates all keys
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/observed_slashable.rs:30 same flat layout
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/observed_data_sidecars.rs:132 flat HashMap keyed by ObservationKey
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/observed_aggregates.rs:429 slot-first Vec<SlotHashSet>, prune drops whole sets
gap: observed_aggregates is already slot-first; observed_block_producers, observed_slashable and observed_data_sidecars use flat maps and retain() over every key. Would need BTreeMap<Slot, ..> outer maps in those three.
impact: Prune runs once per finalization over a few hundred small entries; microseconds, practically unmeasurable.

title: Pubkey-indexed map in the deposit cache
idea: Keep a pubkey-to-deposit map inside the eth1 deposit cache so looking up a pending validator's deposit is O(1) instead of scanning all deposits.
measured_best: O(n) -> O(1) per validator lookup (pr:prysm#9885)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:359 no deposit cache
impact: No eth1 deposit cache; pending deposits are in beacon state post-Electra.

title: Recent blob sidecar cache in fork-choice store
idea: Keep a small in-memory cache of recent blob sidecars keyed by block root next to the fork-choice store, so recent-chain blob lookups (e.g. by-root/by-range requests) skip DB reads.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1204 get_blobs_checking_early_attester_cache checks early attester cache then DB
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1229 get_data_columns_checking_all_caches checks DA checker, pending payload cache, early attester cache then DB
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:304 get_blob / :312 get_data_columns from pending overflow LRU
gap: Recent-block sidecars are served from caches only while pending or for the single early-attester block; once imported, by-root/by-range of recent blocks hit the DB. A small LRU of recently imported sidecars keyed by root, filled in the import path and read in get_blobs/get_data_columns, would add it.
impact: Saves DB reads for peers requesting the last few slots' sidecars; modest, mostly relevant when many peers request the same recent data.

title: Block cache holding only most recent blocks
idea: Restrict the in-memory block cache to the most recent blocks (about 3 epochs) so lookups for the recent chain hit more often with the same memory.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:95-125 BlockCache is an LRU keyed by root, not age bounded
beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:22 DEFAULT_BLOCK_CACHE_SIZE = 0 and cli.rs:794 default 0 so disabled by default
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:571 try_get_full_block checks cache
gap: Cache is an optional count-based LRU, off by default; recent blocks otherwise come from early_attester_cache / DB. To match, enable a default size of about 3 epochs of blocks (~96) or evict by slot relative to head.
impact: Fewer DB reads and block decodes for recent-block RPC/lookups; teku saw ~10% more hits, likely minor on a Lighthouse node.

title: In-memory block and state-root maps before DB
idea: Check in-memory maps for hot block and state-root lookups before going to the database, so frequent lookups skip SSZ decode/encode.
measured_best: SSZ encode/decode was 20% of profiled time (pr:nimbus#945)
evidence: consensus/proto_array/src/proto_array.rs:93 ProtoNode keeps state_root in memory for fork choice
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3010 load_block_root_from_summary reads DB summary
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:316 get_by_block_root in-memory state lookup
gap: Fork choice and state cache give in-memory block/state lookups for hot path, but generic block-root/state-root lookups through HotColdDB (load_hot_state_summary, get_blinded_block) go to the DB unless block_cache_size>0. Could add small in-memory root maps in HotColdDB for the unfinalized range.
impact: Avoids SSZ decode of summaries/blocks on repeated hot lookups; Lighthouse already decodes lazily and has state cache so gain is modest.

title: Cross-fork SSZ schema registry with shared instances
idea: Build all per-fork SSZ type schemas through a registry primed at startup, reusing the previous fork's instance when a schema is unchanged, so each schema object exists once and reads are lock-free.
evidence: consensus/types/src/fork/fork_context.rs:41 types are static Rust generics; no runtime schema objects
impact: SSZ schemas are compile-time types in Rust; nothing to share.

title: Share chain spec via reference counting, not clones
idea: Hold the chain spec behind a shared reference-counted pointer (Arc) instead of cloning it per validator or component, so memory does not grow with the number of instances.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:403 pub spec: Arc<ChainSpec>
validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:69 spec: Arc<ChainSpec>
impact: Already shared via Arc across the chain and the validator store.

title: One background worker for pubkey cache fetches
idea: Send pubkey cache fill work to a single long-lived background worker instead of spawning a task per fetch, so large pubkey batches in block or aggregate processing do not spawn huge numbers of tasks.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/builder.rs:286 ValidatorPubkeyCache loaded once; no per-fetch task spawn in validator_pubkey_cache.rs
impact: Lighthouse does not spawn a task per pubkey cache fetch; cache is an in-memory lookup.

title: Linear-scan single-item eviction protecting new entry
idea: When a bounded cache exceeds its size on insert, evict a single item by an O(N) scan instead of sorting all entries on every insertion, and never evict the just-inserted entry.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:247-263 prune_cache sorts keys by epoch on each insert, excludes head ids from pruning
gap: ShufflingCache::prune_cache could use a min scan instead of sorted_by_key; cache is tiny (default 16) so gain is negligible. Just-inserted entry is not in the map at prune time, so already protected.
impact: Saves a sort of ~16 keys per shuffling insert; unmeasurable.

title: Inline loop equality for 32/48-byte roots and pubkeys
idea: Compare small fixed-size byte values (32-byte roots, 48-byte pubkeys) with an inline loop and use the native memcmp only for large buffers, since native call overhead dominates for small inputs.
measured_best: 32 B compare 49.7 ns -> 14.7 ns (3.4x) (pr:lodestar#8846)
evidence: consensus/types roots are alloy B256 / fixed arrays; slice equality compiles to inline memcmp
impact: Rust fixed-size array equality has no FFI call overhead.

title: Is-all-zero check instead of comparing to default digest
idea: Test whether a digest/root is zero with an is-all-zero check instead of constructing a default zero hash and comparing, avoiding a temporary 32-byte value on hot paths.
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/state_advance.rs:90 uses Hash256::is_zero()
impact: Lighthouse already uses is_zero and Rust avoids temporaries.

title: Skip cache insertion when the cache is disabled
idea: When a cache is disabled (or the value is cheap to recompute), skip insertions entirely, because locking and hashing keys on insert can cost more than computing the value.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:230 caches are always on; no disable flag
impact: No cache in Lighthouse has a disabled mode, so no insertion to skip.

title: Build light client store only when serving enabled
idea: Do not construct or maintain the light client server store and its data unless light client serving is enabled.
evidence: beacon_node/client/src/builder.rs:272 producer channel created only if enable_light_client_server
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4787 cache_state_data gated by config
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5178 producer event gated
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/chain_config.rs:174 enable_light_client_server defaults to true
beacon_node/src/config.rs:1498 --disable-light-client-server
impact: Light client work is skipped when serving is disabled. It is on by default, so most nodes pay the cost unless they pass --disable-light-client-server.

title: Stream validator comparison in state diffs
idea: When diffing two states' validator registries, compare them by streaming through iterators instead of materializing both validator lists, lowering peak allocation.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:102 HDiffBuffer holds validators: Vec<Validator>
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:185 from_state does take_validators().to_vec()
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:439-450 ValidatorsDiff::compute single pass over slices emitting only changed entries
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:227 apply rebuilds list via set_validators_from_iter
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1791 and :2272 HDiffBuffer::from_state(state.clone()) materialises target per diff
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:235-239 hot/cold hdiff buffer caches keep source buffers materialised (amortises source, not target)
gap: Target state's validator list is still copied to a Vec for every diff; compute ValidatorsDiff from milhouse iterators over the target state (and the cached source buffer) instead of to_vec.
impact: Lowers peak allocation by ~one validator Vec (~120 MB at 1M validators) per stored diff; small CPU change.
refute_note: Also checked hot_cold_store buffer caches: source buffers are cached materialised by design (needed for apply), so only the target-side copy is avoidable; the diff loop itself is already streaming.

title: Cache head state for sync committee duty requests
idea: Keep a cached head state reference for sync committee duty requests so repeated duty calls do not fetch or copy the state each time.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3032 sync_committee_duties_from_head uses with_head, no state copy
beacon_node/http_api/src/sync_committees.rs:44 duties served from head first; state load only on SyncCommitteeNotKnown
impact: Already avoids a state fetch or copy on each duties call; nothing further to gain.

title: Send forkchoiceUpdated once per sync batch
idea: During range/initial sync, do not send engine forkchoiceUpdated after every imported block; send it once per batch (for its last block, in the background) or once at the end of sync. This cuts EL round trips during bulk import.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:632-662 process_blocks calls recompute_head_at_current_slot once after process_chain_segment
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3207-3260 process_chain_segment loop has no head recompute
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1890-1920 fcU sent from a spawn_handle task inside recompute_head
impact: One fcU per range-sync batch, sent from a spawned task.

title: Pipeline batch download concurrently with import
idea: Decouple range-sync block fetching from block processing with a queue or batch state machine, so the next batches download from peers while earlier batches are imported in order. Network wait and import overlap instead of alternating.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:33 BATCH_BUFFER_SIZE = 5
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1124-1215 request_batches/include_next_batch download ahead of processing_target
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:384 process_completed_batches sends batches to the beacon processor in order
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:632 processing runs on the beacon processor, separate from sync networking
impact: Downloads of up to 5 batches overlap in-order import.

title: Self rate-limit outgoing by-range requests per peer
idea: Throttle outgoing blocks/blobs-by-range requests to each peer to the quota that peer enforces, counting cost the way the responder does (slots times max blobs, adjusted for empty slots), and schedule a retry exactly when the quota replenishes. Requests are not rejected, penalised or disconnected, and the node does not wait longer than needed.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/self_limiter.rs:83-123 allows() queues per (peer,protocol) and inserts into DelayQueue at the limiter's wait_time
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/self_limiter.rs:155-178 TooSoon(wait_time) re-queues instead of sending; TooLarge is sent anyway
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/rate_limiter.rs:388-399 tokens = request.max_responses(), the same cost function the inbound limiter charges
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/protocol.rs:853-866 BlocksByRange=count, BlobsByRange=max_blobs_requested, DataColumnsByRange=max_requested
beacon_node/src/config.rs:1500-1508 self limiter on by default with default quotas
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/config.rs:122-155 shared default quota table
impact: Already throttles to the peer's (Lighthouse-default) quota and retries exactly when tokens refill. The only difference from teku#8984 is that tokens are not refunded for empty slots, but the Lighthouse responder does not refund them either.

title: Keep block processing off the sync and network loop
idea: Send range-sync batches to a separate processor thread or work queue and receive the result as an event, instead of awaiting heavy import inside the sync manager or the shared async runtime. Networking and the sync loop are not blocked by import.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:664 range batches sent as Work::ChainSegment, backfill as Work::ChainSegmentBackfill
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:480 process_chain_segment runs in the beacon processor
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:546 result returned to sync via SyncMessage::BatchProcessed

title: Filter sync peers by earliest available slot
idea: Before assigning by-range requests (blocks, blobs, columns, envelopes, backfill), compare the requested slots with each peer's advertised earliest_available_slot and skip peers that cannot serve them. Requests are not wasted on peers that answer ResourceUnavailable.

refute_note: Beyond the earlier review: range-sync data columns are fetched by custody-by-root whose peer set is already filtered by earliest_available_slot, and custody backfill also filters; only the forward-range block peer is unfiltered.

title: Skip range requests for already known or queued blocks
idea: When new block roots or gossip blocks arrive during sync, check whether the block or its parent is already known or queued (keyed by root) and only request the span that is new. This avoids duplicate downloads and lookups.

title: Clip sidecar requests to DA window and fork
idea: Clip blob and data-column by-range requests (and column sync work) to slots that are inside the data availability retention window and in the fork that uses that sidecar type (no blobs pre-Deneb or post-Fulu). No requests go out for data peers do not have to serve; also re-request payload envelopes evicted from cache.

title: Choose range or by-root sync by distance
idea: When a peer is only a few slots or epochs ahead, use head sync or by-root fetches instead of a full finalized range sync; when it is further behind, fetch the gap with blocks-by-range at max request size instead of many by-root requests. Each gap size uses the cheaper method.

idea: When no peer has a high enough finalized slot or a head ahead of the local head, wait a fixed interval before re-checking or exit range sync, instead of spinning on the same peer set.

title: Batch-verify signatures across a whole sync segment
idea: Pass a complete downloaded range-sync batch to the chain as one segment, collect the signature sets of all its blocks and verify them in one batched BLS job (in worker threads) alongside the state transition. One batched verification is much cheaper than per-block verification.

title: Couple block and sidecar downloads per batch
idea: For each range-sync batch, request blocks and blob/column sidecars concurrently, buffer them until all are complete, and submit the batch to the processor only when fully downloaded, storing sidecars before importing their blocks. Import does not refetch sidecars or fail on partial batches.

title: Request sidecars only for blocks with commitments

idea: In range sync, download blocks first and then request custody columns by root for only the blocks with commitments, in one request per peer for the batch, instead of per-column by-range requests to separate peers. title: Request blocks in ranged batches, not singly

title: Use larger blocks-per-request batch size
idea: Raise the number of blocks (or blobs) asked for per by-range request to the peer rate-limit maximum (for example 64 blocks) and use arbitrary-length batches instead of epoch-sized units, halving request count.

title: Bound download lookahead ahead of processing
idea: Limit how many range-sync batches or slots are downloaded ahead of the processed head (for example 4 batches, or a bounded slot window started when the previous target is processed), and enforce that limit in the send path. This bounds memory and wasted bandwidth when a batch fails.

title: Cap concurrent in-flight sync requests per peer
idea: Track in-flight sync requests per peer (and per protocol), mark a peer at its limit as busy, and assign new batches only to free peers. Downloads spread over peers and do not queue at one peer or trip its rate limit.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:97-118 ActiveRequestsPerPeer/at_concurrency_limit

Making it strict would mean returning NoPeer/leaving the batch AwaitingDownload in block_components_by_range_request and retrying on request completion.

title: Temporarily blacklist failed sync chains
idea: Remember finalized sync chains that failed for peer-attributable reasons for a short period and refuse to retry them, but do not blacklist when the failure is not the peer's fault. Sync does not loop on bad chains, and valid chains are not lost.

title: Cancel in-flight import on batch abort
idea: When a sync batch is aborted, cancel its in-flight import (block, payload, envelope fetch) and check for cancellation between blocks, so abandoned imports do not stack up and slow retries.

impact: Saves at most the rest of one batch (up to 32 slots of import) after a chain removal; imports do not stack because the processor runs chain segments serially, so gain is small.

title: Cancel leaked futures and tasks in sync loops
idea: In sync loops that race timers against peer events or send on result channels, cancel the losing future and make sends context-cancellable, so abandoned timers and blocked tasks do not accumulate.

impact: Rust futures are cancelled on drop; no leaked timers or goroutines in sync loops.

idea: Keep downloaded blocks and sidecars attached to the batch through every lifecycle state and drop the references explicitly when the batch or request handler finishes, so large batch buffers are not leaked, duplicated or kept resident until GC.

idea: Sync at most a small number (for example 2) of head chains in parallel, avoiding duplicate block downloads and RPC timeouts when many head chains exist.

idea: Maintain a cheap is-syncing flag set as soon as sync starts, and have per-slot tick handlers read it to skip fork choice, duties and other per-slot work during sync, instead of computing a full peer-based sync status each tick. Resources go to catching up.

idea: Obtain a trusted head via light client updates and sync backwards to the known state, verifying historical blocks by hash chain only (skipping signatures and full state transition) since they lead to a trusted head.

title: Sync columns from minimal covering peer set
idea: Choose the smallest set of peers whose custody covers the needed data columns and sync columns from them, rather than querying many peers.

title: Prefer narrow-custody peers for column requests
idea: When assigning missing data columns to custodial peers, prefer peers that custody fewer columns, then maximise coverage, and skip peers with no overlap. Requests spread evenly and do not pile onto supernodes.

title: Do not block startup on sync
idea: Start sync and gossip subscription concurrently in the background during node startup instead of awaiting sync, so API, validator and gossip are not delayed.

beacon_node/network/src/service.rs:513 network service future spawned, not awaited
impact: Startup of API, validator duties and gossip is not blocked on sync.

title: Do not advance sync on unverified empty responses
idea: Treat a dropped connection during a range request as a failure, and require empty responses from several distinct peers before advancing past a range, so the queue does not skip real blocks and refetch them later.
