beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:1151-1172
impact: During initial sync, gossip is not subscribed. When the node falls behind later, unknown-parent and unknown-root lookups more than SLOT_IMPORT_TOLERANCE from head are ignored.

title: Extend forward batches to local head
idea: When range sync starts from finalized, keep creating forward batches past the last range end up to the local head slot instead of restarting from the head, so batches are not skipped or redone.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:193 to_be_downloaded starts at start_epoch
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:774-778 to_be_downloaded = max(validating_epoch), skips existing batches
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1188-1241 include_next_batch advances to_be_downloaded until target_head_slot
impact: Range chains keep a forward cursor and never restart batch creation from the local head, so no batches are skipped or redone.

title: Correct finalized range sync target slot
idea: Compute the finalized range sync target with the right slot offset: far enough past the peer's finalized slot (2 epochs plus 1 slot) that local finality advances, but without an extra batch that cannot be processed.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:147-152 target_head_slot = remote_finalized_slot + 2*slots_per_epoch + 1
impact: The fix is in place.

title: Do not start sync before genesis
idea: Delay starting the sync service until genesis, since no block can be imported before then.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/service.rs:362 sync spawned at network start, without a genesis-time gate
beacon_node/client/src/notifier.rs:70 node runs pre-genesis and only logs 'Waiting for genesis'
gap: Lighthouse does not delay the sync manager until genesis time. It needs only the genesis state, then starts network and sync before genesis. Pre-genesis, every peer status is at slot 0, so range sync and lookups stay idle and cost nothing.
impact: None measurable: the sync manager is idle pre-genesis.

title: Locate boundary batch by reverse scan
idea: Keep range-sync batches sorted and find the boundary batch (for example the last awaiting validation) by scanning from the end, instead of filtering and mapping the whole list and taking a max.
evidence: network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:45 batches is a BTreeMap (sorted)
network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1209 include_next_batch filters whole map to count in-buffer batches
chain.rs:708 advance_chain uses split_off on the sorted map
gap: Lighthouse keeps batches in a BTreeMap and uses split_off, but include_next_batch still scans all batches (at most BATCH_BUFFER_SIZE plus validating ones) with filter+count. A reverse scan or counter would replace it.
impact: Saves a scan of a few dozen entries per request; unmeasurable on a mainnet node.

title: Shorten sync state machine hot path
idea: Reduce the work done per call in the sync batch state machine event trigger, since it runs very often.
evidence: network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1124 request_batches
chain.rs:1188 include_next_batch
gap: Prysm's state machine event trigger has no Lighthouse counterpart; Lighthouse range sync is event driven over a small BTreeMap with no hot loop worth trimming.
impact: Nothing measurable.

title: Cheap batch attempt hashing
idea: Compute the identity hash of a downloaded sync batch from block tree-hash roots (cached per block/envelope) concatenated into one preallocated buffer, instead of SSZ-serialising blocks or manual byte loops. This avoids large temporary allocations.
measured_best: byteArrayConcat 2.03 ns/op vs Buffer.concat 1.35 ns/op (pr:lodestar#4343)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:65-69
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification_types.rs:63-67
beacon_node/network/src/sync/batch.rs:503
impact: The batch attempt hash streams only the cached 32-byte block roots into a SipHash hasher. It does not serialize blocks or build a buffer.

title: Downscore peers with timed-out sync requests
idea: Lower the score of peers whose sync batch requests time out so later batches go to responsive peers.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:657-671 outgoing StreamTimeout on BlocksByRange/DataColumnsByRange/ByRoot -> MidToleranceError
beacon_node/network/src/sync/batch.rs:203 failed_peers
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1038-1049 retry deprioritises failed peers
impact: Timed-out peers are downscored and deprioritised for the batch retry.

title: Do not redial poorly performing sync peers
idea: Do not re-dial peers disconnected for poor sync performance, and include the epoch's first slot in batches so the finalized block is downloaded.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/peerdb.rs:153-159 should_dial excludes peers whose score state is banned or disconnected
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/peerdb.rs:196-205 ForcedDisconnect | Banned block dialing
beacon_node/network/src/sync/batch.rs:186-188 batches start on epoch start slots
impact: Peers disconnected for bad score are not redialed until the score recovers. Batches include the first slot of the epoch.

title: Stop requesting columns at peer request cap
idea: Stop sending column requests to a peer once it reaches the configured request count (>=), so a peer that fails to deliver advertised columns gets no extra requests.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:318 peer_attempts incremented per request sent
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:367-370 filter keeps peers with peer_attempts <= MAX_CUSTODY_PEER_ATTEMPTS
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:397-398 MAX_CUSTODY_PEER_ATTEMPTS = 3 ('Max number of attempts ... from a single peer')
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:150-158 a missing column is a download error with no downscore for non-lookup peers
gap: ActiveCustodyRequest::select_column_peer has the same off-by-one that the nimbus PR fixed. The filter is `peer_attempts <= MAX_CUSTODY_PEER_ATTEMPTS`, so a peer that already got 3 requests and failed to serve its advertised columns can get a 4th. It should be `<`. The per-column cap MAX_CUSTODY_COLUMN_DOWNLOAD_ATTEMPTS = 3 limits this in most cases. The earlier cited at_concurrency_limit (>=) is a different counter: it counts in-flight requests, not failed attempts.
impact: At most one extra columns-by-root request to a withholding peer per custody request. Small.

title: Check batch is parent-linked chain before import
idea: Sort a downloaded batch and verify that each block's parent root links to the previous block before any state transition; reject the batch and switch away from the peer on failure. Invalid or orphaned batches are rejected cheaply.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3068-3112
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:960
impact: Batches that are not linked are rejected before signature verification or the state transition, and the fault is put on the peer.

title: Race duplicate range requests across peers
idea: Send the same block range request to several peers and use the first answer, so one slow peer does not stall sync.
evidence: network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1034 send_batch sends each batch to one peer and retries on failure
network/src/sync/network_context.rs:578 picks one custody peer per column
gap: Send the same range request to 2 peers in block_components_by_range_request and take the first complete response, cancelling the other. Costs bandwidth and complicates coupling state.
impact: Could cut tail latency of stalled batches, but doubles download bandwidth; marginal for most nodes.

title: Cap concurrent downloads per block root
idea: Limit in-flight downloads per block root and entity (blocks, sidecars, envelopes) to a small number (for example 2) with a stale window, so lookups do not fetch the same data from many peers at once.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:374-378 new_current_lookup does not re-request a root that already has a lookup
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:375-386 continue_requests uses maybe_start_downloading, one in-flight block request per lookup
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:367-380 column requests go to one peer per column, with attempts tracked
impact: Lookups are deduplicated per root, with at most one in-flight request per component, so there is no multi-peer fan-out for the same data.

title: Reject wrong fork digest before decoding
idea: After reading a req/resp response chunk, check its fork digest against the expected fork and reject it before SSZ decoding.
evidence: lighthouse_network/src/rpc/codec.rs:251 context bytes read before length/SSZ decode
lighthouse_network/src/rpc/codec.rs:909 context_bytes_to_fork_name rejects unknown digest
gap: Unknown digests are rejected before SSZ decode, but a valid digest for a fork other than the one expected for the request is not rejected until after decoding. Pass the expected fork into the response decoder and compare after context_bytes_to_fork_name.
impact: Saves a wasted decode of a block from a misbehaving peer; rare.

title: Never span fork boundaries in a sync batch
idea: Make the sync queue split ranges so no request crosses a fork boundary, so each batch is decoded and verified as one fork type without splitting or re-requests.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:30 EPOCHS_PER_BATCH = 1
beacon_node/network/src/sync/batch.rs:172-197 BatchInfo::new uses exact epoch start_slot..start_slot+n*slots_per_epoch, shift-by-one removed so batches are single-type
beacon_node/network/src/sync/custody_backfill_sync/mod.rs:40 CUSTODY_BACKFILL_EPOCHS_PER_BATCH = 1
impact: None left: one-epoch, epoch-aligned batches cannot straddle an epoch-aligned fork boundary.

title: Align sync batches to epoch boundaries
idea: Choose range-sync batch boundaries so all blocks in a processing segment are in the same epoch, so they share one shuffling/committee cache for batch signature verification.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:30
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3231-3245
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:668
impact: Each range batch is one epoch, and process_chain_segment also splits segments into same-epoch runs, so one shuffling is used for each signature batch.

title: Evict cached inputs after peer-caused batch failure
idea: When a range-sync batch fails due to peer-served data, evict its block input or envelope from the seen cache so the retry downloads fresh data from another peer instead of reverifying the same bad bytes.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/batch.rs:377-399 processing_completed FaultyFailure/NonFaultyFailure move to AwaitingDownload, dropping the batch data
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:327-379 process_batch hands the batch's own blocks to send_chain_segment (no seen-input cache reuse)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3202 process_chain_segment consumes the passed RangeSyncBlocks
impact: None: the Lodestar bug comes from reusing seenBlockInputCache/seenPayloadEnvelopeInputCache on retry; Lighthouse range sync redownloads the batch and has no such cache in the path.

title: Keep latest state in memory during initial sync
idea: During initial sync, keep the latest state in an in-memory cache instead of writing the state to the database after every block.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1661-1671
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1706-1707
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1749-1768
impact: Post-block states stay in the in-memory state_cache. On most slots only a small summary goes to disk (ReplayFrom), and snapshots or diffs are written only at hierarchy boundaries.

title: Download ranges from several peers in parallel
idea: Track the heads of all suitable peers and send block-by-range requests to several of them concurrently (round-robin), instead of syncing serially from a single peer. Total download time is bounded by the slowest parallel request, not the sum.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:33
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1040-1049
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:478-494
impact: Up to 5 batches per chain download at the same time. Each one goes to a peer chosen from the chain's peer set, which skips failed peers and peers at the concurrency limit, with a random tie-break.

title: Disable periodic peer status updates while syncing
idea: Turn off periodic Status re-requests to peers while range sync is running.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/network_behaviour.rs:83-99 status_peers HashSetDelay only polled when sync_state is not SyncingFinalized/SyncingHead
impact: Already saves periodic Status traffic during range sync.

title: Find common ancestor instead of restarting at finalized
idea: When starting or switching sync target, probe the peer for the highest shared block behind head (with exponentially growing jumps, never falling back to finalized on an RPC error, capped to a reorg range) and sync from there. During non-finality this avoids redownloading long ranges of known blocks.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain_collection.rs:225,329,389 start_syncing is passed local_head_epoch as the optimistic start epoch
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:882-887 optimistic_start set to the aligned local-head batch
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1130-1148 the optimistic batch is downloaded first, before any batch from the finalized start

beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:575-581,707-775 if it imports blocks, advance_chain drops every earlier batch and moves start_epoch/processing_target past it, so the known range is not downloaded
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:582-590,661-680,816-821 if empty or invalid, the candidate is rejected and sync falls back to processing_target (the finalized-derived start)
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:187 head-chain start_epoch = min(local head slot, remote finalized slot)
gap: Lighthouse probes one point (the batch at local head) and on failure falls back to finalized. It has no exponential back-off search for the highest shared block between finalized and local head, so a node on a minority fork during long non-finality still redownloads from finalized.
impact: Common case (local head on the peer's chain) already avoids redownload. The remaining saving is for fork-switch cases during long non-finality, which can still be thousands of blocks.
refute_note: The earlier review missed the optimistic_start mechanism: the chain first fetches the local-head batch, and if it links, advance_chain skips everything from finalized to local head. That is a one-step common-ancestor guess, not an exponential probe.

title: Include non-canonical heads in common ancestor search
idea: When finding the common ancestor with a remote chain, also compare against all local non-canonical chain heads and pick the highest-slot ancestor, so blocks held on side forks are not downloaded again.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:187 head chain starts at min(local head, remote finalized) epoch; no common-ancestor search
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:150 finalized chain starts at local finalized epoch
gap: Would need a common-ancestor search over fork-choice heads in RangeSync::add_peer before choosing start_epoch; today side-fork blocks we already hold are re-downloaded and dropped as duplicates.
impact: Saves re-downloading a few epochs of side-fork blocks in rare reorg cases; negligible on normal nodes.

title: Rank finalized sync peers by finalized epoch
idea: Select sync peers whose finalized epoch and head reach the target (same fork, not behind us), rank them by finalized epoch then head slot, and pick the highest target, so requests go to peers that can serve the range.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:127-170 chains keyed by remote finalized root, target = finalized slot+2 epochs+1
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain_collection.rs:276-300 update_finalized_chains picks max_by_key(available_peers)
beacon_node/network/src/sync/peer_sync_info.rs:26-80 remote_sync_type filters peers behind us / not ahead
gap: Peers behind or on another fork are filtered and grouped by finalized root, but the winning chain is the one with most peers, not the highest finalized epoch/head; no per-peer ranking. Rank in chain_collection::update_finalized_chains by (finalized epoch, head slot) before peer count.
impact: Marginal: avoids syncing toward a lower finalized target first; few redundant requests on mainnet.

title: Start range requests after blocks already held
idea: Compute the range-sync start slot from what the node already has (max of last imported block, local head and local finalized slot) and clamp every by-range request start, including the first, to it. The node does not re-download and re-import blocks it already holds.
measured_best: 66 bursts / 748 redundant blocks in ~3 h on a follower, ~65 ms per redundant arrival, one 67-block burst delayed a gossip block 4.2 s (pr:ethlambda#645)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:147-160 finalized chain starts at local_info.finalized_epoch
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:187 head chain starts at min(local head, remote finalized) epoch
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:855-880 start_syncing advances only to local finalized epoch
gap: Start epoch is the local finalized epoch, not the max of imported block, head and finalized slot, so a new/restarted chain re-downloads the blocks between finalized and head (typically 2-3 epochs, up to ~100 blocks) and filters them afterwards. Clamp the start in range.rs add_peer / SyncingChain::new and start_syncing to local head epoch when the head is on the target chain.
impact: Saves a few epochs of redundant block downloads and filter work on chain restarts; small steady-state effect.

title: Silently skip pre-finalization blocks in range sync
idea: In range sync, drop blocks from before local finalization without treating them as unknown-parent errors.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3162-3166 filter_chain_segment silently drops WouldRevertFinalizedSlot blocks from the segment
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:854-857 WouldRevertFinalizedSlot mapped to Ok(()) with no peer action
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1843 finalized-slot check
impact: Already skipped without penalty or unknown-parent handling.

title: Skip already-imported blocks before batch processing
idea: Before processing a sync batch, drop duplicate blocks and blocks already in fork choice or the DB, and skip their post-processing, so overlapping, replayed or retried batches cost almost nothing.
measured_best: 4x faster forward sync (title) (pr:caplin#11663)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3068-3142 filter_chain_segment drops DuplicateFullyImported, GenesisBlock and finalized-slot blocks via check_block_relevancy
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3218-3226 process_chain_segment runs the filter before signature_verify_chain_segment, KZG and import
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:646 recompute_head only when imported_blocks is non-empty
impact: Replayed or overlapping batches skip signature, KZG and state work; only the download cost remains.

title: Handle switching target chain without stalling
idea: Support switching from a longer target chain to a shorter one (including non-finalized back to finalized sync) without stalling batch sync, and mark sync failed when common ancestor search fails.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain_collection.rs, range.rs:130 independent chains per target; failed_chains set
impact: Lighthouse runs separate finalized/head chains per target rather than one retargetable batch sync, so the Teku stall does not arise.

title: Progress sync on local chain without remote
idea: Allow sync to make progress on the local chain without requiring a remote chain target.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:115 chains created only from a peer status; no remote-less mode
impact: Teku-specific edge case of its single-sync-target design; Lighthouse local progress is driven by peer-created chains and gossip.

title: Ordered async delivery of sync status events
idea: Deliver sync status notifications through an ordered async runner so subscribers cannot block the sync event thread.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs sync state is a plain message loop; network_globals sync_state set directly
impact: Rust sync manager does not call blocking subscribers on its event loop.

title: Yield between synced block imports
idea: Process synced blocks one by one and yield to the scheduler between them, so a cooperative event loop stays responsive during bulk import.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:474 process_chain_segment runs as beacon_processor work
impact: Tokio with a blocking pool and the beacon processor already keep other work responsive during chain segment import; no cooperative-loop starvation.

title: Race peers for block access lists alongside bodies
idea: When downloading block bodies in range/backward sync, fetch the block access lists (BALs) in the same pass and race several peers for them, taking the first hash-valid response, so blocks can execute in parallel with BALs available instead of falling back to serial execution.
measured_best: Blocks executed with downloaded BAL ~30% -> 100% on bal-devnet-7 resync (pr:caplin#21679)
evidence: beacon_node (grep block_access_list: only store/test/block_hash hits)
impact: Block access lists are a Glamsterdam feature not present in Lighthouse; nothing to race for.

title: Save synced blocks to DB concurrently
idea: During range sync, write imported blocks to the database asynchronously (off the import path) so DB writes do not serialize block processing.
measured_best: ~15 blk/s to 26 blk/s in initial sync (pr:prysm#3673)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4749-4756 import_block pushes PutBlock/PutState and calls store.do_atomically_with_block_and_blobs_cache synchronously, under BLOCK_PROCESSING_DB_WRITE timer, before fork choice is committed
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1459 do_atomically_with_block_and_blobs_cache is a synchronous batch write
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3340-3380 chain segment blocks imported one after another
gap: Move the hot DB write out of import_block into a background writer (queue ops, flush before head or finalization needs them) and keep crash consistency with fork choice persistence (issue 2028 revert logic).
impact: Could overlap DB writes with state transition during initial sync. Prysm saw ~15 to 26 blk/s, but Lighthouse's write share is unknown (measure BLOCK_PROCESSING_DB_WRITE first).
refute_note: Searched beacon_chain and store for any write queue, deferred or background write path; none exists. Only the migrator (finalization) runs in the background, not per-block import writes.

title: Verify execution payload in parallel with block
idea: In range sync, run the EL newPayload call and the payload envelope state transition concurrently with consensus block verification, and batch the envelope signatures together with the block signature set, instead of doing them serially per block.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3298 signature_verify_chain_segment gets blocks only; envelopes extracted at 3291
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3372 process_range_sync_envelope awaited after each process_block, serially
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/import.rs:432 verify_execution_payload_envelope (signature + state transition) runs first with its own signature check
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/import.rs:452 notify_new_payload awaited only after state processing, not concurrently
gap: In process_chain_segment, overlap envelope newPayload (EL) with the envelope state transition and with consensus verification of the next block, and add envelope signatures to the segment signature set in signature_verify_chain_segment.
impact: Gloas-only; range sync envelope import is fully serial (state transition, then EL, then import, per block), so overlapping could hide EL latency per block.
refute_note: Read process_range_sync_envelope itself: it verifies the envelope signature individually with VerifySignatures::True, then does the state transition, then awaits newPayload; no join/spawn overlap anywhere in this path.

title: Pause range sync while execution layer offline
idea: Stop processing range sync batches and lookups while the execution engine is offline and resume when it comes back, so batches are not processed, failed and penalised for nothing.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:1279-1282 beacon_processor_if_enabled returns None when EL offline
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:338-340 process_batch returns early without processing when EL offline
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:1177-1179 lookups refuse to start when EL offline
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:1183-1221 handle_new_execution_engine_state drops lookups on Offline, range_sync.resume on Online
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:898-912 EL-caused ExecutionPayloadError gives peer_action None (NonFaultyFailure)
impact: Already avoids processing, failing and penalising batches while the EL is offline.

title: Do not count non-fault failures against batch retries
idea: When a batch fails because the peer rate-limited us or for another reason that is not the peer's fault, do not consume the batch retry budget or penalise the peer; back that peer off and send the batch to a different peer, so the chain is not dropped and re-downloaded.
measured_best: Observed 1,396 rate-limited responses causing peer loss (pr:lodestar#8924)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/batch.rs:308 download_failed counts every failure incl. None against max attempts
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:652 NonFaultyFailure handled only for processing results
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:605 RateLimited from BlocksByRange -> MidToleranceError penalty
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:916 inject_error has no rate-limit branch
gap: Processing-side non-faulty failures are already exempt, but download-side RateLimited responses still burn a download attempt and penalise the peer. Add a RateLimited case in RpcResponseError handling in Chain::inject_error that skips Batch::download_failed's counter (or backs off the peer) and retries on another peer.
impact: Avoids dropping a range-sync chain after repeated rate-limit responses from peers; only matters on busy/overloaded peer sets, small gain.

title: Score sync peers by observed throughput
idea: Track per-peer download throughput (blocks returned and processed, bandwidth) and pick range sync peers by that score, weighted-random so others still get some requests, so fast peers receive more batches and slow peers fewer.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:476-495 block peer = min(deprioritized, at_concurrency_limit, rand::random); no speed term
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:116-118 at_concurrency_limit is a fixed MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS cap, not a throughput score
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:353-392 column peer pick uses attempts/lookup_peers/hash, no speed
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1028-1050 send_batch passes chain peers + failed_peers only
gap: No per-peer throughput or latency stats anywhere in sync or peer_manager. Add an EWMA of blocks (or bytes) per second per peer, updated on by-range responses, and use it as a weighted-random key in block_components_by_range_request, select_columns_by_range_peers_to_request and custody select_column_peer.
impact: Faster peers get more batches during initial sync, which cuts download stalls; gain depends on peer spread, maybe tens of percent of sync time when some peers are slow.
refute_note: Grepped network and lighthouse_network for throughput/latency/ewma/speed/response_time and every peer-selection .min()/sort; the only load-sensitive term is the 2-request concurrency cap, which lets a fast peer free its slots sooner but does not rank peers by speed.

title: Weighted round robin on peer rate-limit capacity
idea: Fetch each large contiguous batch from one peer and choose peers by weighted round robin on their remaining rate-limit capacity, so each peer's full burst rate is used without tripping its limit.
measured_best: up to 90% of burst rate (640 blk/s) (pr:prysm#5887)
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/self_limiter.rs:83 SelfRateLimiter::allows mirrors the peer's rate limiter per (peer, protocol) and queues outbound requests until quota is available
beacon_node/src/config.rs:1500 self limiter enabled by default with default params
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/mod.rs:465 outbound requests go through outbound_request_limiter
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:476 peer choice uses deprioritize set, concurrency limit and random tie-break, not remaining quota
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:30 EPOCHS_PER_BATCH = 1, whole batch from one peer
gap: Lighthouse already mirrors each peer's limit (self limiter) so it does not trip it, and fetches each batch from one peer; missing is using the self limiter's remaining tokens to weight peer selection in block_components_by_range_request (requests to a drained peer are delayed in the queue instead of routed to a peer with capacity).
impact: Avoids batches waiting in the self-limiter queue of a drained peer while other peers are idle; gain depends on peer count and limits, unclear.
refute_note: The earlier review missed the lighthouse_network outbound SelfRateLimiter, which is the 'mirror the peer's limiter' half of the idea and is on by default; only quota-weighted peer choice is absent.

title: Drop sync peers that return too few blocks
idea: When a peer returns only a few blocks per range request (throttling), fail the sync against it and do not choose it as sync target for a while unless it progresses a minimum number of slots.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:575-590 empty batch handling and optimistic rejection
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1034 failed_peers deprioritised in peer choice

gap: Throttled short responses are only caught after the following batch is processed (then faulty peers are deprioritised/penalised); no immediate per-response check for suspiciously few blocks or temporary exclusion from sync target selection. Add a min-blocks check in the by-range response handler and mark the peer failed for that batch.
impact: Avoids slow peers throttling range sync; gain only when a peer rate-limits by returning short ranges.

title: Keep partial column responses, retry only missing columns
idea: In range sync, accept column responses that miss some columns, keep the good data, attribute the missing columns to the responsible peer, and re-request only those columns from other peers of the syncing chain instead of failing and re-downloading the whole batch.
measured_best: Improve sync performance by retrying only the failed columns from other peers (pr:lighthouse#7733)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:133-160 on_data_column_downloaded keeps Downloaded columns and resets only the missing ones
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/custody.rs:229-262 continue_requests re-requests only columns awaiting download, from other peers (peer_attempts)
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_sidecar_coupling.rs:256-263 range batch columns via custody_lookup_request with lookup_peers = {block_peer} only

beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:976-984 in range sync, CustodyPeerForColumn -> peer_action None: 'Range sync tracks one peer per batch and drops the column PeerGroup while coupling'
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:651-656 NonFaultyFailure re-downloads the whole batch
gap: Columns that are missing at download time are kept and retried per column. But when a column fails processing (AvailabilityCheckError::InvalidColumn from the KZG check in process_chain_segment), range sync does not retry only that column from another peer. block_error_penalty's CustodyPeerForColumn is mapped to None in the range-sync arm of handle_failed_chain_segment, so the result is a NonFaultyFailure. The whole batch (blocks and all columns) is then downloaded again, and the peer that served the bad column is not penalized because the PeerGroup is dropped during coupling (RangeBlockComponentsRequest::responses). NonFaultyFailure never exhausts the batch, so a bad column peer can cause repeated full re-downloads. Also, only the block peer is in lookup_peers, so other column peers that withhold data are not downscored. A column is also accepted only when all of its block roots are present, so one missing sidecar makes the whole column be requested again.
impact: An invalid column from one peer costs a full batch re-download (blocks plus every custody column) with no attribution. This repeats until a different peer happens to serve that column.

title: Per-peer locks around fetch rate limiter
idea: Guard the sync fetcher's rate-limiter state with one lock per peer (pruning stale ones) instead of one global lock, so requests to different peers do not contend.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/rate_limiter.rs
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/self_limiter.rs
impact: Lighthouse's rate limiters are owned by the single-task RPC behaviour, not shared behind a global mutex, so there is no lock contention.

title: Re-trigger sync on a periodic timer
idea: Re-evaluate and restart the sync engine on a fixed timer in addition to peer status changes, so a node that is still behind with a stable peer set does not idle for minutes after a batch completes.
measured_best: restart takes ~5 minutes after 'Syncing completed' otherwise (pr:teku#9849)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:361 on_chain_removed (including ChainCompleted) calls network.status_peers(chain.peers()) at once

title: Peer-unbound worker pool keeps requests pipelined
idea: Use a pool of sync workers that each take a fresh available peer for every request and issue the next request as soon as any in-flight one completes, so slow peers do not stall the pipeline and peer bandwidth stays used.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1188-1242 include_next_batch keeps up to BATCH_BUFFER_SIZE=5 batches downloading or awaiting processing

title: Buffer gossip blocks to disk while syncing
idea: While syncing, buffer incoming gossip blocks in a disk-backed sorted collector and insert them in batches once the gap closes, so the tip does not need to be fetched again by forward sync.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs (unknown-parent leads to parent lookup)
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs (forward sync refetches head)
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs (no sync buffering)

impact: Lighthouse refetches the tip blocks via range/lookup after sync; saves a few blocks of download only, with large complexity.

title: Materialize cached blocks before processing

title: Probe peers for range sync support

impact: Saves a few wasted batch requests and retries per bad peer during range sync; small and only on peers that cannot serve.

title: Prune sync block buffer below finalized

beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_sidecar_coupling.rs:200-260

title: Skip importing orphaned payload envelopes

title: Serve stored SSZ bytes directly for by-range
idea: When serving blocks-by-range/root, send the stored SSZ bytes straight to the wire with only framing, instead of deserializing and reserializing each block, and take rate-limit quota per block.

title: Stream by-range/by-root responses chunk by chunk from DB
idea: Serve blocks by range/root by streaming items from the DB iterator to the network encoder and writing each as a separate chunk as it is produced, instead of collecting the whole response in memory first. This bounds memory and lets the first chunk go out early.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_block_streamer.rs:257-271 stream() loads every requested block into a Vec in one spawn_blocking task (collect) before yielding anything

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_block_streamer.rs:297-318 sends start only after all loads and EL fetches finish

Fix: load and send in chunks of 32 roots (load chunk, fetch its bodies, send, repeat), or pipeline loads with sends.

evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/task_spawner.rs:61-66 (blocking closure runs func() unconditionally; result send ignored if receiver dropped)

title: Decode snappy frames directly into one destination buffer
idea: Decompress framed snappy req/resp payloads straight into one final output buffer sized from the advertised length, without intermediate slices or composite buffers that are re-summed or re-copied, and abort as soon as the payload exceeds the expected size.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/codec.rs:182-190 vec![0; length] + FrameDecoder over Take(max_compress_len) + read_exact (single destination, size-bounded: matches)
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/codec.rs:279-292 same for responses
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/codec.rs:451-462 UnexpectedEof on incomplete input returns Ok(None) and discards the work
tokio-util-0.7.19/src/codec/framed_impl.rs:202-221 Framed calls decode() again after every socket read
gap: SSZSnappyInboundCodec::decode and SSZSnappyOutboundCodec::decode restart from the start of the chunk on every call. While a multi-MB block or column chunk is still arriving, each socket read allocates a new zeroed `length` buffer and decompresses all frames received so far, then throws the result away on UnexpectedEof. That is O(n^2) decompress and memset work per chunk, which is what teku#11587/#11589 remove. Fix: keep a persistent FrameDecoder state and output buffer in the codec across decode calls (decode each complete snappy frame once and append), or wait until max_compress_len bytes or a complete frame sequence is buffered before decoding.
impact: Less CPU and allocation when receiving large by-range responses (blocks up to 10 MiB, data columns) that arrive over many reads.

title: Deduplicate by-root request roots and stream in batches

title: Stagger large by-range responses over time

title: Non-blocking snappy frame decoding

title: Await each response write before loading next
idea: For multi-chunk responses, wait for the previous chunk write to complete (with a write timeout that closes the stream) before loading the next item from the DB, instead of firing all writes in parallel, so outbound buffers and memory stay bounded.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/handler.rs:471-486 (Idle substream pops one pending item and starts one send future; never more than one write in flight per substream)
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/handler.rs:526-559 (next chunk is written only after the previous send future completes)

beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/mod.rs:51 + inbound_limiter.rs (MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS=2 per peer/protocol bounds concurrent responses)
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/rpc_methods.rs:1840-1870 (loader still reads all items from DB and pushes them without waiting on writes)
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/handler.rs:169,337 (unbounded pending_items VecDeque)
gap: The write side already matches Teku's fix: chunks are written one at a time per substream, and a 10s per-chunk timeout closes a stalled stream. What is missing is backpressure on loading: the beacon processor reads every block/column from the DB and queues it into the unbounded pending_items before the peer reads, so memory is not bounded by the write rate. To close it, a bounded per-request channel or a write ack from the handler must gate the DB loader.
impact: Bounds memory held for slow peers on big by-range responses (at most 2 concurrent per peer/protocol, timeout-bounded); a robustness gain with little CPU change.
refute_note: The earlier review called RESP_TIMEOUT only an overall stream timeout. The handler resets it per chunk and serialises writes per substream, so the 'await previous write plus write timeout' half exists. Only the load-gating half is missing.

gap: The 128-byte inline buffer was sized for per-committee bitfields (pre-Electra). Since Electra, AttestationElectra.aggregation_bits spans all committees of a slot (~1M validators / 32 slots = ~31k bits = ~3.9KB), so every aggregate, block attestation and op-pool/naive-aggregation-pool attestation bitfield spills to a heap SmallVec. A 4KB inline buffer is not sensible, so the fix would be a different representation (e.g. pooled/arena buffers or a sparse form) rather than a bigger SMALLVEC_LEN.

The network service gets no head state on head change; it only receives small messages and the state is Arc/tree-shared anyway.
impact: None for a mainnet node: The network service gets no head state on head change; it only receives small messages and the state is Arc/tree-shared anyway.

title: Hand-written state copy instead of reflection clone
idea: Replace generic reflection-based clones of states and checkpoints with specialized copy methods, which are cheaper per copy.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/exit_cache.rs:12 plain derived Clone
Rust Clone is derived and monomorphic; milhouse clones are structural-sharing Arc bumps, no reflection.

title: Copy validator trie rather than move on recompute
idea: When a validator field trie is recomputed, copy it instead of transferring it, so a late block at a registry change does not recompute all validator roots from scratch.
measured_best: avoids expensive full root recompute; slight memory increase (pr:prysm#13661)
evidence: milhouse d67aabd src/tree.rs persistent tree
No field-trie ownership transfer exists; milhouse persistent trees share nodes via Arc and clones never lose cached hashes.
impact: None for a mainnet node: No field-trie ownership transfer exists; milhouse persistent trees share nodes via Arc and clones never lose cached hashes.

title: Dedupe dirty indices before full field-trie rebuild
idea: When the dirty-index count of a field trie reaches its rebuild limit, deduplicate the indices first and rebuild the whole trie only if still over the limit.
evidence: milhouse d67aabd src/update_map.rs, src/interface.rs
Milhouse uses an update map applied to the tree and rehashes only dirty subtrees; no dirty-index limit/rebuild threshold.
impact: None for a mainnet node: Milhouse uses an update map applied to the tree and rehashes only dirty subtrees; no dirty-index limit/rebuild threshold.

title: Defragment copy-on-write state lists periodically
idea: Rebuild copy-on-write multi-value state lists into a fresh base once they accumulate many per-index modification layers, so reads on long-running nodes stay fast.
measured_best: non-trivial effect on block processing for nodes running weeks (no numbers) (pr:prysm#13444)
evidence: milhouse d67aabd src/interface.rs, src/update_map.rs
Milhouse persistent trees have no per-index modification layers; updates are applied into the tree by apply_updates, so no layers accumulate.
impact: None for a mainnet node: Milhouse persistent trees have no per-index modification layers; updates are applied into the tree by apply_updates, so no layers accumulate.

title: Pointer-free fixed-size validator records
idea: Store validators in memory as fixed-size structs with inline pubkey and withdrawal credential arrays, without slice headers, pointers or per-validator allocations, cutting memory per validator.

Validator is already a fixed-size Rust struct with inline pubkey bytes and Hash256, stored packed in tree leaves without pointers.
impact: None for a mainnet node: Validator is already a fixed-size Rust struct with inline pubkey bytes and Hash256, stored packed in tree leaves without pointers.

title: LRU eviction for checkpoint state cache
idea: Evict checkpoint state cache entries by least-recent use rather than insertion order, so checkpoint states that attestations keep targeting stay cached instead of being recomputed via epoch processing.

impact: Nothing left to gain. I checked the Lighthouse Gloas code: envelope verification does not mutate state (execution requests are applied via process_parent_execution_payload in the next block). Gossip envelope import calls recompute_head_at_current_slot, which rebuilds the head snapshot on a payload-status change from get_advanced_hot_state and runs the FCU. The idea is therefore covered by an equivalent mechanism, and the Prysm next-slot-cache refresh has no counterpart to do.

title: Cache block post-states for block production
idea: Cache post-states (and block rewards) from block processing in a fine-grained-locked cache so block production reuses them rather than re-running state transitions.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_production/mod.rs:87-89 parent post-state served from the state cache via get_advanced_hot_state

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:6537-6553 complete_partial_beacon_block runs compute_beacon_block_reward as a separate pass, then per_block_processing + update_tree_hash_cache on the produced block
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:6589-6595 post-state returned in BeaconBlockResponse
beacon_node/http_api/src/produce_block.rs:101 _block_state discarded by the HTTP API
beacon_node/http_api/src/build_block_contents.rs:17 BeaconBlockResponse state not kept
gap: The grandine block processor caches the post-state and block rewards keyed by block root when it processes the produced block, so the import of the node's own block (and a second production of the same block) reuses them. In Lighthouse, complete_partial_beacon_block computes the post-state and then drops it (produce_block.rs `_block_state`). The own block is then processed again from the parent state in the publish -> process_block import path. Block rewards come from a separate compute_beacon_block_reward pass, not from the processing pass.
impact: Saves one per_block_processing pass and one tree-hash pass on the import of each locally proposed block (tens of ms on the proposal critical path). Only proposing nodes gain.

title: Reuse prebuilt pubkey cache from anchor state
idea: At startup, if the anchor state already carries a built pubkey cache, reuse it instead of rebuilding by deserializing all pubkeys.
measured_best: ~30 seconds for 350k keys (pr:lodestar#4319)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:53-78 load_from_store reads persisted uncompressed keys
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:237-242 as_pubkey uses deserialize_uncompressed
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/builder.rs:286 persisted cache loaded at restart
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/builder.rs:875 ValidatorPubkeyCache::new from state only when no cache is persisted
impact: Restart already skips pubkey decompression. load_from_store is sequential, so parallel loading could save a few seconds at most.

title: Reuse pubkey map allocation when reinitializing caches
idea: When re-initializing state caches, clear and reuse the existing pubkey-to-index map allocation rather than allocating a new map.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/pubkey_cache.rs:2-12 rpds HashTrieMap, cloned structurally
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:2996 drop_pubkey_cache just resets to default
impact: Persistent trie map has no big allocation to reuse; reinit is rare (drop_all_caches only).

title: Load startup state once and share across services
idea: Register the startup (genesis/finalized) state once and hand it to all services instead of each service reloading it from the database.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/builder.rs:302-330 set_genesis_state builds caches and stores the state once
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/builder.rs:406 weak_subjectivity_state
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/builder.rs:229 resume_from_db
impact: Startup state is loaded once by the builder and shared via the BeaconChain (canonical head / state cache).

title: Keep future-epoch info and per-block state cache
idea: Do not discard cached epoch info for future epochs, and do not build a fresh state cache per block application.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:825 committee_caches live on the state (prev/current/next) and are cloned with it
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1684 build_all_committee_caches on the state, no per-block fresh cache object
impact: Nimbus separate EpochRef/StateCache design does not exist; caches are part of BeaconState and Next-epoch caches are kept.

title: Persist skipped-slot states using state_roots
idea: When persisting intermediate skipped-slot states during block processing, derive their roots from the next state's state_roots field instead of tree hashing each one.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1609-1645 update_tree_hash_cache once per skipped-slot state, stored, then passed as Some(state_root) to per_slot_processing
impact: Each skipped-slot state is hashed once (needed anyway by slot processing) and reused for persistence; no extra hashing.

title: Store shuffling once, derive committees and duties
idea: Store only the shuffling plus a reverse map (validator index to position) in the committee cache and derive committees and duties on demand, instead of several redundant maps keyed by validator or slot.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/committee_cache.rs:26-34
impact: Already compact; committees and duties derived from shuffling + shuffling_positions.

title: Do not preallocate state cache tables
idea: Create state cache hash tables small so they do not preallocate many unused full BeaconState slots.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:89 LruCache::new(capacity) no preallocated state slots
impact: Nim hash table preallocation; Lighthouse uses an LRU sized by capacity that allocates on insert.

title: Store next-slot cache hit into checkpoint cache
idea: When the next-slot cache answers an attestation target-state request, save that state into the checkpoint cache so later attestations for the same target hit directly.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2161 get_advanced_hot_state used for attestation data; if state.current_epoch() < request_epoch it runs partial_state_advance (:2164) and drops the result
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1172 get_advanced_hot_state caches only the loaded state, not the advanced one
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:316 get_by_block_root returns the latest cached state <= slot
gap: In the miss path of the attestation data production, after partial_state_advance, put the advanced state into store.state_cache so later requests for the same target hit. The state advance timer already fills the cache in the common case, so this only matters on timer misses.
impact: Avoids repeating an epoch-boundary state advance (tens of ms) on rare cache misses at the first slot of an epoch; marginal.

title: Drop pubkey map and scan the registry
idea: Remove the per-state pubkey-to-index hash map and find validators by linear registry scan, trading slower deposit processing for no memory spikes.
measured_best: "completely removes memory spikes" (no numbers) (pr:prysm#8854)
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/pubkey_cache.rs:9 per-state PubkeyCache is a persistent rpds HashTrieMap shared structurally between states
consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/process_operations.rs:76 update_pubkey_cache adds only new validators
impact: Prysm per-state full map copies caused spikes; Lighthouse's persistent map shares structure, so there is no spike to remove and a scan would be slower.

title: Segmented page pool for lock-free state readers
idea: Grow the state page pool in fixed pre-zeroed segments with a pre-reserved segment list so growth never moves existing pages and lock-free readers stay valid.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:89 states are milhouse tree values in an LRU, no page pool
impact: Silver-specific page pool for lock-free readers; Lighthouse state cache is a mutex-guarded LRU of persistent trees.

title: Dedicated clearance state for block sync
idea: Use a separate state for block clearance so block sync does not alternate one temporary state between attestation and block use, which forces replays.
measured_best: helps block sync speed a lot (pr:nimbus#1352)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:2063 load_parent fetches parent post-state by block root from StateCache
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:316 get_by_block_root
impact: Lighthouse has no single shared temporary clearance state: each block gets a cloned (structurally shared) parent post-state from the keyed StateCache, so sync and attestation use do not alternate one state and force replays.

title: Process block attestations in target order
idea: Process a block's attestations sequentially ordered by target checkpoint so the first populates the checkpoint state cache and the rest hit it, instead of each recomputing the epoch-boundary state in parallel.
measured_best: logs show ~1.8s processSlots repeated per attestation (pr:lodestar#1557)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:315 with_cached_shuffling
consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/process_operations.rs (attestations processed in order on the one pre-state)
impact: Lighthouse verifies block attestations on the single block pre-state with its committee caches and uses a promise-based ShufflingCache for gossip, so no per-attestation target checkpoint state is regenerated.

title: Serve finalized-state lookups from the in-memory copy
idea: Serve finalized-state requests (by root, or for deposit pruning) from the finalized checkpoint state already held in memory instead of loading, regenerating or copying it from the database.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:275-281
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1812-1819
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1087-1110
beacon_node/http_api/src/state_id.rs:41-47
impact: API 'finalized' state resolves to slot >= split slot, goes through get_hot_state which returns the held finalized_state clone (cheap milhouse clone); no deposit-pruning path exists.

title: Cheap presence check on shuffling cache
idea: Give the shuffling cache a has/contains check so callers can test presence without computing or memoizing an expensive shuffling.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:209-211
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:196-207
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5216-5222
impact: Block import skips building committee caches when the shuffling is already cached.

title: Predict next-epoch duties without state advance
idea: Compute next-epoch attester shuffling and first proposer from the head state before the epoch boundary, skipping the full state advance when no effective balance can change.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:410-423 the next-epoch attester shuffling comes from a state advanced only to the start of the previous epoch

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:321-354 ensure_state_can_determine_proposers_for_epoch advances only when the decision slot needs it (post-Fulu, the lookahead makes the advance unnecessary)
beacon_node/http_api/src/proposer_duties.rs:91-109 next-epoch proposer duties are computed from the head
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:342-420 the next-epoch caches are primed off the critical path
impact: Post-Fulu, the proposer_lookahead gives next-epoch proposers without an epoch transition. The attester shuffling already uses the one-epoch lookahead. Before Fulu, a partial_state_advance was still needed for next-epoch proposers, but that path is historical on mainnet.

title: Single shared head state buffer for services
idea: Keep one head state shared with API/services under a read lock with release callback rather than keeping extra full copies for readers.
measured_best: "Reduces memory usage by 600MB too" (pr:caplin#12519)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:279 states are cloned with tree sharing (milhouse), no separate buffer per reader
impact: Rust BeaconState uses persistent tree structure sharing, so readers do not hold full copies.

title: Replay only blocks after base state on regen
idea: When regenerating from a stored base state, replay only blocks after it and do not require or fetch the base state's own block.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2514-2549 load_blocks_to_replay still loads block at start_slot (and may read one older block) for its state root
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2031-2042 load_hot_state_using_replay
gap: load_blocks_to_replay fetches the base-state block (kept deliberately for its state root) and can load one extra older block before take_while stops. Could pass the base state's latest_block_root and stop at it.
impact: Saves one block read per hot-state regen; negligible vs replay cost.

title: State cache eviction policy and insertion rules
idea: Tune state cache insertion and eviction: true LRU order, never evict the head, evict old epoch-boundary states first, cache ancestors only on epoch boundaries, and do not insert states read by migration/pruning so they do not evict useful states.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:357-412 cull is LRU with extra order: advanced, old boundary, mid-epoch, could-finalize boundary; the head is never culled; the most recent 10% are exempt
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:275-282 get_by_state_root uses LruCache::get (promotes)
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2031-2060 ancestor states are cached only on epoch boundaries and only when update_cache is set
impact: The policy is the merged form of the Lighthouse PRs themselves. No more gain is expected.

title: Store few checkpoint states while syncing
idea: During sync, skip storing checkpoint states or store them only once per archival interval rather than every epoch.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1661-1720 store_hot_state always caches and writes summary per state
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:660-700 storage_strategy: full diffs only at grid slots, replay otherwise
beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:254 exponents 5,8,11,...
gap: Hierarchical diffs already make full storage sparse (diff every 32 slots), but there is no sync-specific skip: every imported block puts its state in state_cache and writes a summary. Could skip caching/diffing while syncing far behind head.
impact: Some CPU/IO saved during range sync from diff computation at grid slots; small since diffs are sparse.

title: Delay next-epoch duty lookahead into the epoch
idea: Schedule next-epoch duties a few slots into the epoch so the lookahead state need not be advanced across empty slots to compute shuffling and proposers.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/attester_duties.rs:187-194 next-epoch attester duties use partial_state_advance only on cache miss
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5213-5225 shuffling cache primed for Current and Next epoch on import
impact: Beacon node answers next-epoch duties from the primed shuffling cache without advancing the state across empty slots; timing of VC lookahead is not a BN state cost.

title: Skip parent regen at genesis on startup
idea: On startup, skip regenerating the parent state when the finalized or head state is genesis.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/builder.rs:245-270 resume_from_db loads persisted fork choice and states, no regen of parent at genesis
impact: Lighthouse resumes from persisted fork choice/head and does not regenerate a parent state at startup, so there is nothing to skip.

title: Cache decompressed pubkeys only for active validators
idea: Do not insert decompressed pubkeys into the pubkey cache for validators that are not active, since they produce no consensus messages.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:103-177 import decompresses every key, parallel on first import
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:24 index-addressed Vec of PublicKey
gap: Cache is a dense Vec indexed by validator index covering all registry entries including pending/inactive; deposits-only validators are decompressed at import. Would need lazy/sparse decompression keyed by activation status in import().
impact: Saves decompression time at first startup and memory for not-yet-active validators (small fraction of ~1M validators; some tens of MB).

title: Exact state cache hit skips epoch transition
idea: When writing a state, skip slow legacy database reads and skip the epoch transition when an exact state match is already cached.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1124-1132
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:308-326
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1660-1690
impact: Cached (advanced) states returned without disk load or slot processing; no legacy DB in Lighthouse.

title: Skip state-root check when replaying stored blocks
idea: When regenerating a state by replaying stored blocks, skip the per-block post-state hash tree root comparison against block.state_root.
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/block_replayer.rs:241-283 apply_blocks runs per_block_processing and has no post-state root comparison
consensus/state_processing/src/block_replayer.rs:180-213 get_state_root takes the state root from state_root_iter or from the previous block's state_root, and hashes only on a miss
impact: Replay does not check state roots, and it gets per-slot roots without hashing whenever it can.

title: Skip block validation when replaying local blocks
idea: When regenerating states from blocks already validated on import, skip signature and other block validation.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2565-2567 replay_blocks uses no_signature_verification + minimal_block_root_verification
beacon_node/http_api/src/sync_committee_rewards.rs:69-70 the other production replayer also skips signatures
consensus/state_processing/src/block_replayer.rs:262-268 the proposer index is taken from the block and not recomputed
impact: All non-test BlockReplayer sites skip signature verification and most block-root checks.

title: In-memory cache of diff base/snapshot states
idea: Cache decoded hierarchical-diff base snapshots and buffers in memory (keyed by slot, holding either state or buffer form and converting lazily) so historic state loads skip DB reads and decoding and sequential queries reuse prior work.
measured_best: Most sequential queries after the first served in 400-700ms on mainnet (hierarchy exponents 5,7,11) (pr:lighthouse#6475)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/historic_state_cache.rs:14-56 LRUs of HDiffBuffer and BeaconState keyed by slot, converted lazily
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2310-2319 cold state loads check the historic cache
beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:26-27 defaults: 1 state, 16 hdiff buffers
impact: Already present (from Lighthouse's own PR #6475). The default sizes are small, so this is only a tuning question.

title: Reclaimable soft/weak references for cached states
idea: Hold non-head cached states or cached tree views through soft/weak references so the runtime reclaims them under memory pressure, bounding the cache by memory instead of count.
measured_best: avoids OOM at the expense of possible ~2x state access slowdown (pr:teku#2235)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:43 states is a count-bounded LruCache; Rust has no GC soft refs
impact: Rust has no soft/weak-reference reclamation by memory pressure; cache is bounded by count and finality.

title: Sparse checkpoint replay at attestation pool init
idea: At startup, replay checkpoint states only for the first block of each long interval rather than for many blocks, keeping only recent blocks exact.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs: fork choice is persisted, no attestation-pool EpochRef replay at startup
impact: Lighthouse persists fork choice and does not replay checkpoint states to init an attestation pool.

title: Replay from last block at or before slot
idea: To get a state at a slot, load the state of the last block at or before that slot and advance empty slots, rather than replaying from the latest saved state.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1087-1110
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1124-1186
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1531-1560
impact: State-by-slot resolves the exact state root (summaries exist for skipped slots) and loads from the nearest snapshot/diff, replaying only blocks after it.

title: Shared state cache keyed by state root
idea: Keep an in-memory state cache keyed by state root used by block processing, attestation handling and block production to avoid DB reloads.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:82 StateCache keyed by state root behind a Mutex
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:275 get_by_state_root
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_production/mod.rs:89 production uses get_advanced_hot_state
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:400-430 the attestation shuffling path uses the head or cached states
impact: Block import, attestation shuffling and block production all use the shared state-root-keyed cache.

title: Central state regenerator serving all pre-states
idea: Centralise pre-state lookup in one regenerator that serves block pre-states, attestation target states and duty states from caches and advances slots only when needed.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1124 get_advanced_hot_state serves block pre-states
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs and beacon_proposer_cache.rs serve attestation/duty lookups
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs pre-advances head state
gap: Lookups are spread across the store state cache, shuffling cache, proposer cache and state_advance_timer, not one regenerator; unifying them is a refactor with no direct speedup.
impact: Little speed gain; mostly code structure.

title: Store states as deltas over a base
idea: Define delta types for validator identity and beacon state so stored states are deltas over a base state.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:127 HDiff (state_diff, balances_diff, inactivity_scores_diff, validators diff) over a base buffer
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:622 default exponents [5,9,11,13,16,18,21]
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:407 hot_storage_strategy uses the same hierarchy for hot states
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1949 load_hot_state applies diffs from snapshot
impact: Already done: hot and cold states are stored as hierarchical diffs over snapshots, including a dedicated validators diff.

title: Compact backing-tree layout for balances and validators
idea: Change the state backing tree layout for balances and validator branch nodes to use fewer nodes, cutting per-state memory.
evidence: Cargo.lock milhouse 0.9.0 (sigp/milhouse): Lighthouse uses its own persistent tree layout, not Teku's
impact: Teku-specific backing tree layout; milhouse has its own packed leaves for balances and validators.

title: Committee caches embedded in the state
idea: Keep committee/shuffling caches as fields on the state, built explicitly and invalidated per epoch, instead of a separate duplicate cached state.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:825
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1039
impact: Committee caches are Arc-shared state fields built explicitly per relative epoch.

title: Struct-of-arrays validators with shared pubkey list
idea: Split the validator registry into an append-only pubkey list, effective balances and remaining fields, and share the pubkey list structurally between states so a state loaded from disk attaches it instead of copying every key.
measured_best: saves memory loading historical states (commit:grandine@70e0aad900ad)
evidence: consensus/types/src/validator/validator.rs:22 Validator keeps pubkey: PublicKeyBytes inline in each milhouse leaf
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:3416 rebase_on shares tree nodes (incl. validators) with a base state
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:197 rebase_on_finalized used for hot loads
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1988 hot load rebases on finalized state
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2340 cold load: buffer.as_state with no rebase
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:226 as_state rebuilds validators via set_validators_from_iter(cloned)
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:2198 set_validators_from_iter builds a fresh List::try_from_iter
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_pubkey_cache.rs:24 chain-wide append-only pubkey list exists but is not structurally shared into states
gap: No struct-of-arrays split: pubkeys stay inline in each Validator leaf. Hot loads share nodes only via rebase_on_finalized (extra tree walk); cold/historic loads (load_cold_state_by_slot -> HDiffBuffer::as_state) build a fresh validators List and are never rebased, so every historical state copies all keys. The chain-level ValidatorPubkeyCache is an append-only pubkey list but is not attached to states. Fix: rebase cold-loaded states on a shared base (e.g. finalized or the historic cache entry) or split pubkeys into a shared Arc list.
impact: Lower memory and load time for historical states (API, reconstruction, historic_state_cache); hot path mostly covered by rebase_on_finalized.
refute_note: Checked load_cold_state_by_slot and the historic state cache path for any rebase (none in store crate besides hot loads), set_validators_from_iter, and the beacon_chain ValidatorPubkeyCache as a possible equivalent shared pubkey list; it is not shared into state structure.

title: Copy head state outside lock, swap pointer
idea: When publishing a new head state, copy it outside the reader lock and take the lock only to swap pointers, so duty readers are not blocked for the copy.
measured_best: sync-committee efficiency dropped to 94.60% (199/3686 missed) due to blocking (pr:caplin#24165)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1150 build_all_caches on new snapshot before taking the write lock
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:1163-1171 cached_head_write_lock only swaps CachedHead (Arc snapshot)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs:748-751 head_beacon_state_cloned takes Arc clone, clones state outside the read lock
impact: Duty readers are never blocked for a state copy.

title: Faster persistent collection library
idea: Replace the persistent collection implementation behind structurally shared states with a faster one to cut clone and sharing overhead.
evidence: Cargo.lock:6570 milhouse 0.9.0 is already a custom persistent tree
impact: Lighthouse already uses milhouse; swapping libraries is speculative with no identified faster alternative.

title: Synchronous in-memory state cache access
idea: Make state cache lookups synchronous instead of async so hot paths avoid promise and scheduling overhead.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:81 - StateCache is a plain sync LruCache
impact: Rust cache lookups are already synchronous; no promise overhead exists.

title: Fill only proposer indices on proposer cache miss
idea: On a proposer-indices cache miss compute only the proposer indices for that seed instead of rebuilding the full committee cache entry.
measured_best: flame graph, no numbers (pr:prysm#4548)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:175-227 with_proposer_cache fills EpochBlockProposers from state.get_beacon_proposer_indices
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1674-1710 get_beacon_proposer_indices uses proposer_lookahead or get_active_validator_indices + compute_proposer_indices, no committee cache
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:197 OnceCell dedups concurrent fills
impact: Proposer cache miss computes only proposer indices; post-Fulu it reads proposer_lookahead directly.

title: Tiered retention for persisted checkpoint states
idea: Prune persisted checkpoint states with tiered retention (every epoch recently, then exponentially sparser) so disk stays bounded while keeping sparse history.
measured_best: 64 epochs retained even over ~1 year (pr:lodestar#9898)
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:407 hot_storage_strategy: every unfinalized epoch state stored as hdiff/snapshot per hierarchy
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:509 prune_hot_db runs only on finalization
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:127 update_finalized_state retains in-memory layer points only (memory cache, not disk)
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3471 prune_historic_states deletes all cold history, not tiered
gap: No tiered retention of unfinalized hot states: during long non-finality the hot DB keeps every epoch's diff and summary until finalization (prune_hot_db in migrate.rs), so disk grows linearly with non-finality length rather than staying bounded. The hdiff hierarchy makes each kept state cheap but does not drop old unfinalized ones.
impact: Mostly mitigated by hdiffs (per-epoch cost is a diff, not a full state as in Lodestar); only matters for months-long non-finality devnets.

title: One-entry state cache during range sync
idea: Shrink the hot state cache to one entry during initial range sync, since states are not reused out of order, and restore it afterwards.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/config.rs:39 - fixed state_cache_size
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:81 - capacity set at construction, no runtime resize (grep for resize in beacon_chain/network found none)
gap: Add a resize on StateCache and shrink it while range sync is active, restoring on sync completion; callers are StateCache::new and the sync state machine in network/src/sync.
impact: Saves some memory during initial sync only; Lighthouse sync rarely reuses states, so gain is modest and rare.

title: Justified balances from epoch-boundary cache
idea: When fork choice needs justified checkpoint balances, take them from the epoch-boundary state cache instead of regenerating the state.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_fork_choice_store.rs:96-102

evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/verify_exit.rs:31-34 single bounds-checked validator lookup
consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/verify_exit.rs:81-89 Electra pending-withdrawal check without a second index range check
impact: None: the duplicated validator-index range check removed in nimbus#7082 never existed in Lighthouse's verify_exit.

title: Compute committees once for assignment
idea: When computing a validator's committee assignment, compute committees once and reuse them instead of computing them twice.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1735-1764 validator_attestation_duties reads one cached CommitteeCache for all validators
consensus/types/src/state/committee_cache.rs:295-327 get_attestation_duties via shuffled_position, no committee recompute
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:1766-1812 compute_ptc_duties calls get_ptc_assignment per validator (TODO notes O(N*slots*PTCSize))
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:3685-3698 get_ptc_assignment calls get_ptc for each of 32 slots per validator
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:3621-3626 get_ptc allocates a fresh Vec<usize> of PTCSize on each call
gap: Attester duties are done once from the committee cache, but Gloas PTC duties (BeaconChain::compute_ptc_duties -> BeaconState::get_ptc_assignment -> get_ptc) rebuild each slot's PTC vector (512-entry Vec allocation + linear contains) for every requested validator: 32*N PTC materialisations per request instead of 32 once plus an index map.
impact: PTC duties request for e.g. 10k validators: ~320k Vec allocations of 512 usize and ~160M comparisons per call; building the 32 PTCs once and a validator->slot map makes it O(32*512+N). Gloas-only, API path.

evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs balances is a milhouse List accessed directly
impact: No proxy wrapper in Rust; balances accessed directly (and via the single-pass epoch cache).

title: Linear deposit processing for many deposits
idea: Process many deposits in linear time by avoiding repeated work per deposit (e.g. recomputing proofs or trees), instead of quadratic work.
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/genesis.rs:37-46 incremental DepositDataTree push_leaf per deposit at genesis, no tree rebuild
consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/process_operations.rs:652-690 block deposit proofs verified independently

impact: None: genesis deposit tree is built incrementally (linear), block and pending-deposit processing use O(1) pubkey lookup.

title: Avoid double copy of randao mix
