evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs randao mixes are a milhouse Vector read by reference
impact: Go owned-copy getter detail; Rust returns references, no double copy.

title: Skip slot processing when state already at target
idea: Return early from slot advance when the state is already at the target slot, and call only block processing when the pre-state is already advanced. This avoids a redundant state hash tree root and redundant state transitions.
measured_best: 3x reduction when profiling attestation-request RPC (pr:prysm#4314)
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/state_advance.rs:40 and 98 while state.slot() < target_slot: no-op when already at target
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1607-1615 distance-based per_slot loop; reuses parent state_root instead of hashing when not advanced
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:2064-2069 pre-state loaded already advanced to block slot
impact: No redundant state-root hashing or slot transitions when the pre-state is already at the block slot.

title: Avoid per-committee temporary allocations in transition
idea: Remove per-validator/per-attestation temporary allocations in state transition, e.g. reuse the participation flag sequence instead of allocating it per committee computation.
measured_best: hundreds of thousands of temp seq allocations removed (pr:nimbus#5235)
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/common/get_attestation_participation.rs:77 SmallVec for flag indices (no heap)
consensus/state_processing/src/per_epoch_processing/single_pass.rs single pass epoch processing avoids per-validator allocs
consensus/state_processing/src/common/get_attesting_indices.rs:102 vec![] per call in some paths
gap: Minor: a handful of per-attestation Vec allocs remain (get_attesting_indices variants, get_payload_attesting_indices.rs:33); could reuse buffers or return iterators.
impact: Already mostly alloc-free; the participation-flag case is covered. Remaining savings are tiny versus signature and tree-hash cost.

title: Reuse hasher and scratch buffers in sync selection
idea: Reuse one SHA-256 hasher and stack scratch buffers in sync committee index selection and Merkle branch verification, instead of allocating a digest or result per hash.
measured_best: IsValidMerkleBranch depth 33: 67 -> 34 allocs/op, 3201 -> 1088 B/op (pr:caplin#22406)
evidence: consensus/merkle_proof/src/lib.rs:382-397 merkle_root_from_branch uses hash32_concat on stack, no per-level alloc
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1487-1513 shuffling_random_byte/u16 does seed.to_vec(), int_to_bytes8 and hash()->Vec per candidate
consensus/swap_or_not_shuffle/src/compute_shuffled_index.rs:80-90 new Context per hash
gap: Merkle verification is fine, but sync committee/proposer selection allocates a preimage Vec and digest Vec per candidate and rehashes the same 32-byte block for up to 16/32 consecutive i. Cache the digest per i/16 and use a stack buffer in compute_proposer_index / get_next_sync_committee_indices.
impact: Sync committee selection runs once per 256 epochs and proposer selection once per epoch (pre-Fulu or at lookahead), so the saving is a few hundred microseconds to low ms at most.

title: Reuse computed next-epoch proposer indices
idea: After importing the last slot of an epoch, reuse the already computed next-epoch proposer indices during forkchoice update instead of recomputing the proposer shuffling.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5307-5345 get_pre_payload_attributes looks up proposer via with_proposer_cache keyed by proposer shuffling decision root
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_proposer_cache.rs:227 proposer cache populated once per decision root
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1681-1696 post-Fulu next-epoch proposers read from proposer_lookahead
impact: None: the FCU/proposer-prep path reuses cached proposers by decision root; on a miss, post-Fulu it reads the state lookahead instead of reshuffling.

title: Reuse pre-advanced state across validation, import, replay
idea: Reuse the slot/epoch-advanced state computed earlier (for gossip proposer checks or the next-slot cache) when importing a block or replaying it for rewards, so the epoch transition runs only once.
measured_best: 500ms+ to ~20ms for slot-0 blocks (pr:prysm#13678)
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1030-1050 gossip proposer-cache miss loads parent once and keeps it in opt_parent for import
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:2064-2069 import uses get_advanced_hot_state
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_production/mod.rs:95-101 block production (and its consensus_block_value) uses the advanced state
beacon_node/http_api/src/sync_committee_rewards.rs:48-77 get_state_before_applying_block loads the parent state at the parent slot and replays to block.slot with BlockReplayer
beacon_node/http_api/src/standard_block_rewards.rs:18 block rewards API uses that replay
gap: The rewards API path does not reuse the pre-advanced state: get_state_before_applying_block (used by compute_beacon_block_rewards and compute_sync_committee_rewards) calls chain.get_state at the parent slot and runs BlockReplayer to block.slot. That reruns the epoch transition for slot-0 blocks, even when the advanced state is in the state cache. Fix: use store.get_advanced_hot_state(parent_root, block.slot, parent_state_root) and replay only the remaining slots.
impact: Gossip, import and production run the epoch transition once. The beacon rewards APIs pay a full epoch transition per slot-0 block query (the prysm#13678 500ms-to-20ms case).

title: Reuse checkpoint state for attestation production
idea: For attestation production on an old head, use a cached epoch-boundary checkpoint state instead of replaying slots, so committees are not recomputed.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2124-2136 same-epoch head: justified checkpoint and committee length from the head state
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2152-2168 other epoch: get_advanced_hot_state, partial_state_advance only if still behind
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/state_advance_timer.rs:283-288 timer advances the cached head state one slot every slot, so an old head's epoch-boundary state is already cached
impact: An old head across an epoch boundary is served from the timer-advanced cached state; committees come from the state's caches instead of a replay.

title: Reuse attesting indices cache in block import
idea: Pass the shared attesting-indices cache into block attestation processing so attesting indices are not recomputed per attestation.
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/consensus_context.rs:161-195 indexed_attestations memoised by attestation root
consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/block_signature_verifier.rs:297 signature verification fills the cache
consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/verify_attestation.rs:92 block processing reuses it
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:1283-1285 same context carried from signature verification into execution-pending block
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:4987-5106 fork choice, observers and slasher on import reuse ctxt.get_indexed_attestation
impact: None: attesting indices are computed once per block attestation and shared across signature verification, state transition, fork choice and slasher.

title: Cache the full epoch shuffling per seed
idea: Compute the full shuffled validator list once per epoch, cache it keyed by seed/epoch, and slice committees from it at every call site, instead of shuffling per slot or per call.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/committee_cache.rs:135-150 active list and shuffle_list computed once per epoch; committees are slices
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:128 ShufflingCache keyed by AttestationShufflingId (decision root + epoch)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:7593 with_committee_cache serves gossip attestation verification from the shuffling cache
impact: The full shuffle runs once per epoch per decision root and is shared by all call sites.

title: Per-index shuffle with per-index cache
idea: Compute committee membership by shuffling individual indices with swap-or-not and caching by (seed, index), instead of shuffling and caching the whole list.
measured_best: 4M validators worst case 282 ms; 128000 validators 10 s -> 7.7 ms uncached (pr:prysm#2728)
evidence: consensus/swap_or_not_shuffle/src/compute_shuffled_index.rs:21 per-index shuffle exists, used only for proposer/sync selection
consensus/types/src/state/committee_cache.rs:147 committees use whole-list shuffle_list
impact: Lighthouse needs every validator shuffled each epoch, where the whole-list algorithm is ~250x faster than per-index; the per-index idea only suits tiny lookups, which it already does for proposer/sync.

title: Pass committee cache into voluntary exit processing
idea: Pass the existing committee/state cache into voluntary exit processing instead of building it from scratch per exit.
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/verify_exit.rs:21 verify_exit only reads validators, no committee cache
consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/process_operations.rs:573 process_exits
impact: Exit processing in Lighthouse needs no committee cache; nothing is rebuilt per exit.

title: Reuse destination tree buffers on state copy
idea: When copying a state's Merkle tree into a reusable destination, reuse its layer buffers (grow with headroom only when too small) and memcpy, instead of allocating new layers per copy.
measured_best: Reduced allocs by 58% overall (pr:caplin#12696)
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/upgrade/capella.rs:70 mem::take moves caches
beacon_node/store state handling uses milhouse persistent trees with structural sharing
impact: Milhouse persistent trees share structure on clone; there is no flat destination buffer copy to reuse.

title: Reuse tree nodes and hashes at fork upgrade
idea: In the fork upgrade, reuse the previous state's tree nodes for unchanged fields instead of rebuilding them, so cached hashes survive and the post-fork hash tree root is cheap.
measured_best: 'upgradeStateToGloas 3205ms to 1178ms; hashTreeRoot 32196ms to 4899ms' (mainnet state) (pr:lodestar#9601)
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/upgrade/gloas.rs:89-94,107-109 block_roots/state_roots/randao_mixes/slashings/sync committees cloned (Arc tree, cached hashes kept); historical_roots, eth1_data_votes, proposer_lookahead mem::take'd
consensus/state_processing/src/upgrade/gloas.rs:98-99,104-109,117,146-152 validators, balances, participation, inactivity, pending_* rebuilt with ProgressiveList::try_from_iter(pre.x.iter().cloned())
d67aabd/src/progressive_list.rs:36-45 try_from_iter builds a fresh tree from values
d67aabd/src/progressive_tree.rs:101-128,394-410 ProgressiveTreeBuilder pushes values into new Builder subtrees with zero hashes; no constructor takes existing Arc leaves/subtrees from a List
gap: Registry and participation lists change from List to ProgressiveList at Gloas and are rebuilt element by element from cloned values, so every leaf hash and packed-leaf hash is lost and the first post-fork hash_tree_root re-hashes the whole registry. milhouse has no List->ProgressiveList conversion that reuses Arc leaves (for Validator) or carries over cached leaf hashes; adding one (or pre-seeding leaf hashes) would keep the leaf work and only rebuild the interior spine.
impact: One-off at the Gloas fork boundary: shorter state upgrade and much cheaper first post-fork tree hash (Lodestar: 3.2s->1.2s upgrade, 32s->4.9s hash on mainnet); no steady-state gain.
refute_note: Checked the git-pinned milhouse (rev d67aabd) that Lighthouse actually uses, not the registry 0.9.0: ProgressiveList/ProgressiveTree only offer value-based construction (try_from_iter/Builder), rebase only works between two ProgressiveLists, so no leaf-hash reuse path exists for the List->ProgressiveList conversion.

title: Mutate state in place in fork upgrade

consensus/state_processing/src/upgrade/electra.rs:103-169 same pattern
consensus/state_processing/src/upgrade/fulu.rs:45-66 same pattern
impact: None: upgrades take &mut pre-state and move fields; the leftover .clone() calls are on persistent milhouse vectors (cheap Arc clones); runs once per fork.

title: Roll back on failure instead of cloning state
idea: When producing a block or applying speculative changes, apply on the live state and roll back on failure instead of cloning the whole BeaconState.

beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:5344 states are taken by cheap .clone() of the head state
impact: Cloning a BeaconState in Lighthouse is a structural-sharing clone (milhouse Arc trees, rpds persistent caches), so the speculative-apply-on-a-clone design already avoids the full copy that rollback was meant to avoid.

idea: Avoid full-state clones on hot paths (or keep the state small) because whole-state clone cost scales with state size; use structural sharing.

consensus/types/src/state/pubkey_cache.rs:1-14
~/.cargo/registry/src/*/milhouse-0.9.0/src/leaf.rs:8-27
impact: None: state clones share structure through milhouse trees (Arc leaves) and persistent rpds caches.

title: Sample PTC per committee without concatenation

gap: Change compute_ptc_with_cache/compute_balance_weighted_selection to index into committee slices lazily (compute the committee-offset mapping) instead of collecting a Vec of all slot committee members.

title: Share pubkey caches across epoch-context copies
idea: Share pubkey-to-index and index-to-pubkey caches between epoch-context/state copies instead of deep-copying them per block, and check indexed-attestation sortedness with one linear pass instead of a set and sort.

consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/is_valid_indexed_attestation.rs:36-50

consensus/state_processing/src/upgrade/fulu.rs:109

title: Sync signature checks independent of exact state

title: Single shared shuffled-index computation for sampling
idea: Do proposer and sync committee sampling through one shared swap-or-not shuffled-index computation instead of a second private fixed-capacity cache.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1353 compute_proposer_index and :1770 get_next_sync_committee_indices both call compute_shuffled_index per candidate (consensus/swap_or_not_shuffle/src/compute_shuffled_index.rs:21)
gap: Both samplers compute per-index swap-or-not (90 rounds of hashing each) independently; could share a full shuffle_list result or memoise pivot/source hashes across candidates. Functions: compute_proposer_indices, get_next_sync_committee_indices, compute_balance_weighted_selection.
impact: Sampling needs a few hundred shuffled-index calls per epoch for sync committee (period boundary) and 32 proposers; saving is a few ms per epoch at most.

title: Single-pass participation flag update

title: SSZ encoding for VC-BN block traffic

title: Payload timeliness votes on payload-available event
idea: Have the beacon node push payload-available events to validator clients and cast PTC payload attestations as soon as the payload envelope and data columns are seen (deadline as fallback), signing one payload attestation per validator rather than per committee position.

title: Decrypt validator keystores in parallel at startup
idea: At validator client startup, read and run the keystore KDF decryption for each key in parallel across CPU cores (thread pool) instead of serially on the main thread. Each decryption is independent and CPU-heavy, so wall-clock load time drops roughly by core count.

gap: The dependent root already gates the full refetch. But two probe POSTs (current and next epoch) still go out every slot, and the proposer duties are polled every slot. To close the gap: add the dependent roots to HeadEvent, and probe only when they change, with a once-per-epoch fallback.

refute_note: I found the beacon_head_monitor head-event subscription, which the earlier review did not mention. It only drives attestation and sync committee timing, and its event drops the dependent roots, so the verdict stays partial.

title: Short lookahead, per-slot batches for selection proofs

gap: Attestation selection proofs follow the idea (8-slot lookahead, per-slot batches at mid-slot). Sync committee selection proofs in non-DVT mode precompute 64 slots ahead: on startup and when a new period's duties appear, fill_in_aggregation_proofs signs 64 slots x subnets x sync validators in one burst, not timed to a quiet point in the slot, which is the 32-slot-ahead pattern nimbus#6609 cut to 2. impact: Removes a burst of ~64*subnets signatures per sync-committee validator at VC start / period start (matters for remote signers); steady state already 1 slot per tick.

impact: Builder skips the voting-keystore KDF unless a withdrawal keystore/deposit is needed.

title: Skip key cache decrypt with no local keystores
idea: Do not decrypt or save the keystore key cache (scrypt) when no local keystore validators exist, e.g. only remote-signer keys.
measured_best: Excessive CPU / slow PATCH validators with hundreds of keys; no numbers (pr:lighthouse#4126)

title: One KDF per key on load
idea: Detect a wrong password from the decryption failure itself instead of running a separate password-check KDF, and load public keys without decrypting, so startup does one KDF per key.
evidence: crypto/eth2_keystore/src/keystore.rs:381-389 single derive_key, checksum mismatch -> InvalidPassword
crypto/eth2_keystore/src/keystore.rs:263 public_key from JSON without decrypt
validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:252-293 startup: one decrypt_keypair per key, cached in key_cache
validator_client/http_api/src/keystores.rs:197-204 import: separate decrypt_keypair password check, comment admits double decryption
validator_client/http_api/src/lib.rs:581 add-keystore endpoint also decrypts before adding
gap: Startup is one KDF per key, but keymanager API import (keystores::import_single_keystore) runs decrypt_keypair as a password check and then add_validator_keystore -> InitializedValidators::from_definition decrypts again (key_cache does not get the first result), so imports pay two KDFs per key. Fix: pass the decrypted keypair into the key cache / add_validator_keystore.
impact: Halves KDF time of bulk keystore imports over the keymanager API (seconds per key with default scrypt); startup already optimal.

title: Load validator keys only once at startup
idea: Ensure validator keys are loaded exactly once at startup, not once async and again sync.
evidence: validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:535-548 from_definitions single update_validators
impact: Teku-specific bug; not present.

title: Derive mnemonic keypairs in parallel

evidence: validator_manager/src/create_validators.rs:413 sequential for-loop over derivation indices
account_manager/src/validator/recover.rs:109 sequential loop
lcli/src/mnemonic_validators.rs:38 only rayon user (par_iter), lcli tool only

title: Flat directory listing for keystore import

evidence: common/account_utils/src/validator_definitions.rs:477 recursively_find_voting_keystores walks recursively

title: Poll unknown validator indices once per epoch

evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:477 unknown_validator_next_poll_slots

title: Use validator index from duties response
idea: Take validator indices from the duties response (or include them there) instead of separate per-validator index lookups and a VC-side pubkey-to-index map.
measured_best: "thousands of requests" avoided (pr:prysm#4567)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:911-1010 poll_validator_indices does one GET states/head/validators/{pubkey} per unknown pubkey, sequentially

gap: Duties are requested by index, so the index must be known first; Lighthouse resolves it with one HTTP call per validator. Batch via POST /eth/v1/beacon/states/head/validators with ids=[pubkeys] in poll_validator_indices (chunked), then set_validator_index for each result.
impact: Startup and key-import with thousands of keys drops from thousands of BN requests to a handful; steady state unaffected (known indices are cached).

title: Prune slashing protection database
idea: Periodically (and at startup) prune slashing-protection block/attestation records older than a horizon, relying on low-watermark guards, so tables stay small and signing checks stay fast.
measured_best: about 0.5s for 1000 validators and 54,000 epochs (pr:prysm#8221)

validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:1372-1415 prune_slashing_protection_db prunes attestations and blocks

impact: DB pruned every epoch to a 1-epoch horizon, at startup and periodically.

title: Per-entry sorted slashing protection storage
idea: Store slashing-protection history as individual ordered key/row entries per validator (by source/target epoch) and scan ordered keys with early stop, instead of reading and rewriting a whole encoded history blob per attestation.
measured_best: surround check 1.9ms, 7us, 2.2ms, 1.2ms in worst cases on BoltDB (pr:prysm#8211)
evidence: validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:96-105 signed_attestations one row per (validator_id,target_epoch), UNIQUE index
validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:405-475 indexed double-vote lookup, surround queries ORDER BY target DESC LIMIT 1
validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:1069-1090 prune_signed_attestations
validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:60 SLASHING_PROTECTION_HISTORY_EPOCHS = 1, :1372 prune each epoch
impact: Per-row SQLite storage with index prefix on validator_id; no blob rewrite; per-validator rows kept tiny by per-epoch pruning.

title: Min-max span arrays for surround checks
idea: Keep per-validator min/max surround span arrays indexed by epoch plus target-indexed attestations so surround/double-vote checks are O(1) lookups instead of history scans.
measured_best: O(1) surround detection (no timings) (pr:lodestar#1674)

validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:60 SLASHING_PROTECTION_HISTORY_EPOCHS = 1
impact: Lighthouse's DB is pruned to about one epoch of rows so surround scans touch a handful of rows; span arrays would add nothing.

title: Minimal slashing protection database
idea: Keep only the highest signed block slot and highest source/target attestation epochs per validator, shrinking the DB and making checks constant time.
evidence: validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:479-510 MIN(source)/MIN(target) lower-bound checks act as watermark
validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:1069-1090 prune keeps rows >= new_min_target and always the max row
validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:60,1372-1422 prune to 1 epoch of history every epoch
impact: DB stays at ~1-2 rows per validator, so checks are effectively constant time; a strict single-row design would save only a few indexed SQLite queries.

title: Snappy-compress stored attestation history
idea: Compress encoded per-validator attestation history with snappy before writing to the validator DB to cut storage and disk I/O.
measured_best: about 25% reduction in storage and disk I/O (pr:prysm#8129)
evidence: validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:96 plain SQLite rows, no encoded history blob
impact: There is no encoded history blob to compress; rows are pruned to about one epoch.

title: Read-only transactions for slashing lookups
idea: Use read-only DB transactions for read-only slashing-protection lookups so they do not take the single writer lock.
evidence: validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:158 SQLite pool with locking_mode EXCLUSIVE (apply_pragmas)
validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:200 with_transaction uses Exclusive behavior
impact: SQLite in deliberate exclusive mode serialises all access for safety; it is not bbolt, and read-only concurrency would defeat the cross-process lock.

title: SQLite exclusive locking for slashing DB
idea: Open the slashing-protection SQLite DB in EXCLUSIVE locking mode since only one process uses it, avoiding per-transaction file lock acquire/release.
evidence: validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:179-183 apply_pragmas locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE
validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:24 POOL_SIZE = 1
validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:162-170 pragmas applied via with_init on every connection
impact: Already done; no further gain.

title: Skip slashing DB writes for remote-signer keys
idea: Offer an option to skip local slashing-protection DB checks and writes for keys whose remote signer enforces slashing protection.
evidence: validator_client/src/config.rs:404 sets enable_web3signer_slashing_protection from --disable-slashing-protection-web3signer
validator_client/signing_method/src/lib.rs:131-141 requires_local_slashing_protection false for Web3Signer when disabled
validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:499 block path gate
validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:649-655 batched attestation path marks CheckSlashability::No
impact: Skips local slashing DB I/O for remote-signer keys when opted in; web3signer setups only.

title: Lazy default slashing protection records
idea: Return defaults when a key has no slashing-protection entry instead of pre-writing a default record per key at startup, avoiding N transactions on launch.
measured_best: removes a bottleneck for starting a validator client by no longer creating N validator DB transactions (pr:prysm#5323)
evidence: validator_client/src/lib.rs:265-268 register_validators for all voting pubkeys in one call
validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:214-244 single exclusive transaction, prepared INSERT, only inserts missing keys (existing enabled keys are a SELECT only)
impact: No N-transaction startup bottleneck; registration is kept on purpose to detect a missing DB.

title: Per-validator slashing protection locks
idea: Replace the global lock around slashing-protection check-and-record with per-validator locks so distinct validators sign concurrently; only shared storage writes stay serialized.
measured_best: about 2Gb memory for 1000 validating keys (pr:prysm#8086)
evidence: validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:20 POOL_SIZE=1 single sqlite connection
validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:646 check_and_insert_attestations: one Exclusive txn per batch
validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:589 block check also Exclusive txn
gap: Slashing DB is one SQLite file with pool size 1 and EXCLUSIVE transactions, so all signers serialize on it; no per-validator locks. Would need per-key in-memory state with async flush in SlashingDatabase::check_and_insert_*.
impact: Little on a normal node: attestations are batched into one txn per slot, so the lock is held briefly. Matters only for thousands of keys on slow disks.

title: Narrow attesting-history lock scope
idea: Hold the attesting-history lock only around the in-memory map access (with consistent lock order), not across DB reads or saves, to cut contention with many validators.
evidence: validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:191 with_transaction (exclusive txn, pool size 1)
validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:20 POOL_SIZE=1
gap: Lighthouse keeps no in-memory attesting-history map or lock; all state is in SQLite, serialised by design for safety.
impact: None.

title: Lock-free reads of signer state
idea: Make the signing path read validator signer/key state without a contended lock, e.g. via an atomically swapped immutable snapshot or optimistic read lock, so key-management updates do not block signing.
evidence: validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:9 parking_lot::RwLock (blocking, not async)

validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:186-213 add_validator: #[allow(clippy::await_holding_lock)] with FIXME; self.validators.write().add_definition_replace_disabled(..).await holds the write guard across the await
validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:581-612 add_definition_replace_disabled -> add_definition -> update_validators().await then definitions.save()
validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:1253-1258 update_validators decrypts the whole key cache ('a very expensive operation') whenever a local definition exists
validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:256-260 new keystore decryption 'can take several seconds', awaited while the caller holds the write lock
validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:1391-1400 key cache save awaited under the same lock
validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:243-256 doppelganger_checked_signing_method takes validators.read(), so it blocks for the whole import
validator_client/http_api/src/keystores.rs:272 and http_api/src/remotekeys.rs:160 delete paths hold write() over the per-key loop
gap: Signing reads are short, but key management holds the parking_lot write lock over long async work: LighthouseValidatorStore::add_validator holds InitializedValidators.write() across update_validators(), which runs decrypt_key_cache, InitializedValidator::from_definition (keystore scrypt/pbkdf2 decryption) and KeyCache::save. While that runs, every signing_method/voting_pubkeys/get_index read blocks, and because the lock is synchronous it also blocks the tokio worker threads. The fix is an ArcSwap snapshot of the signing map (as grandine does), or doing the decryption and I/O outside the lock and taking the write lock only to swap the result in.
impact: A runtime key import (keymanager API) can stall all signing on the VC for one key-cache decrypt plus keystore decrypt (seconds), which risks missed or late attestations for every validator. No effect when keys are not changed at runtime.

title: Read-lock check before write lock
idea: In the committee subscription API, check under a read lock whether a validator is already tracked and take the write lock only to insert new ones.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/validator/mod.rs:1165-1168 takes validator_monitor.write() per subscription
beacon_node/http_api/src/validator/mod.rs:668-670 same for sync subscriptions
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/validator_monitor.rs:1104 auto_register_local_validator(&mut self) returns early if !auto_register, otherwise checks maps
gap: Add a read-lock pre-check (a &self fn that returns false at once when auto_register is off) and take write() only when a validator needs registering, in the beacon and sync committee subscription handlers.
impact: Removes a write-lock acquire per subscription (hundreds per slot for large VCs) that contends with validator monitor readers; likely sub-millisecond total.

title: Separate duty locks per role
idea: Key the VC duty lock per role (attester, proposer) so a late attestation cannot delay a block proposal in the same slot.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:464-477 only per-map RwLocks for duties data
gap: Lighthouse VC has no global per-role duty lock; attestation and block services run as independent tasks.
impact: None.

title: Take duty lock after waiting
idea: Wait until the attestation deadline (1/3 slot) before taking the attester lock so it is not held while idle and does not block proposals.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:464-477 no duty lock
gap: No attester lock exists in the Lighthouse VC, so nothing is held while waiting for the 1/3-slot deadline.
impact: None.

title: Do not hold locks across beacon node I/O
idea: In the fallback status refresh loop, never hold a write lock on shared beacon-node status while awaiting network I/O; lock only to store results.
evidence: validator_client/beacon_node_fallback/src/lib.rs:620-623 update_all_candidates clones candidates and drops the read lock before I/O
validator_client/beacon_node_fallback/src/lib.rs:625-635 refresh_health futures run concurrently via join_all
validator_client/beacon_node_fallback/src/lib.rs:343-354 per-candidate health write lock taken only to store the result after I/O
impact: Already done; nothing more to gain.

title: Sign a slot's attestations in parallel
idea: Issue all per-validator signatures for a slot concurrently (CPU thread pool for local BLS, concurrent requests for a remote signer) instead of one after another, so the last attestation is published sooner.
measured_best: Sequential 32 votes published from 1.61 s to ~2.3 s into the slot; 2/3-wide aggregate p50 6.49 s vs block build at 6.40 s (pr:ethlambda#655)
evidence: validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:1022-1043 sign_attestations join_all over all per-validator signing futures
validator_client/signing_method/src/lib.rs:184-198 local keystore signing via spawn_blocking_with_rayon_async(HighPriority)
validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:1079-1088 slashing protection batch on a blocking thread
impact: All attestation signatures for a slot are issued concurrently (rayon for local BLS, concurrent HTTP for web3signer).

title: Flatten attestation service task spawning
idea: Replace nested spawn-await-spawn in the attestation service with one top-level spawn and join_all so per-validator work runs concurrently.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:346 spawn_handle for publication
validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:395 outer spawn awaits handle, then spawns per committee at :416
gap: PR 8568 was closed unmerged; the nested spawn remains but it is a code-quality refactor with no measurable latency effect.
impact: Nothing measurable gets cheaper; task spawn costs microseconds.

title: Parallel per-slot duty broadcast with sent cache
idea: Sign and broadcast per-slot duty messages in spawned tasks rather than serially in the slot loop, and keep an epoch-pruned cache of already-sent slots to skip rebroadcast.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:232 per-slot tasks
validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:1043 join_all attestation signing
gap: Nimbus-specific serial slot loop; Lighthouse already spawns per-duty tasks and signs concurrently.
impact: None.

title: Parallel attestation aggregation across subnets
idea: Run aggregation duties for different subnets/committees concurrently instead of sequentially.
measured_best: reduces aggregation time ~80% if you run more than 10 validators (pr:prysm#12699)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:380-427 groups duties by committee_index and spawn_ignoring_error(handle_aggregates) per committee
impact: Aggregation per committee runs as concurrent tasks.

title: Skip aggregate fetch without aggregators
idea: Fetch the aggregated attestation from the BN only if at least one local validator is an aggregator (reusing precomputed selection proofs), and sign/publish aggregates concurrently.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:645-652 early return when no duty has a selection_proof, before any BN fetch
validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:410-425 handle_aggregates spawned per committee index, so committees run concurrently
validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:695-715 one aggregate fetch per committee, cloned for each aggregator, using the precomputed selection proofs
impact: None left.

title: Fetch duty types and epochs concurrently
idea: Fetch current and next epoch duties, and attester, proposer and sync duties within each, concurrently instead of sequentially.
measured_best: reduces the time to fetch duties from ~8-9s to ~2.5s (pr:prysm#13789)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:683-857 separate spawned tasks for proposers, attesters, sync, PTC, IL
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1066 and :1090 current then next epoch attester fetch awaited sequentially
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1863 proposer epochs fetched in sequential for loop
gap: Duty types run as independent tasks, but within attesters current and next epoch are fetched one after the other (poll_beacon_attesters), and likewise in poll_beacon_proposers. Wrap the two epoch calls in futures::join!.
impact: Halves duty polling latency at epoch boundaries for large key sets; mostly background, not critical path.

title: Check validator roles in parallel
idea: Determine each key's roles for a slot in parallel across keys so duties start sooner with many keys.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:591 attesters(slot) is a lookup of precomputed duties
gap: Lighthouse has no per-key role check at slot time; duties come from BN polling.
impact: None.

title: Parallel is-aggregator checks
idea: Compute per-duty selection proof and is_aggregator checks concurrently across duties when subscribing to subnets.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1589-1660 fill_in_selection_proofs; parallel_sign branch at :1639, FuturesUnordered at :1652
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:147 make_selection_proof computes is_aggregator
gap: Selection proofs are signed sequentially unless parallel_sign (DVT) is set. Use the FuturesUnordered branch of fill_in_selection_proofs for all setups.
impact: Only many-key remote-signer nodes; proofs are computed ahead of the slot so no critical-path gain.

title: Share one HTTP client per remote signer
idea: Create one HTTP client per remote signer URL and reuse it for all validators and requests, so connections are pooled and memory/sockets do not scale per key.
measured_best: VC with 200 keys on Web3Signer: ~200MB to ~50MB (pr:lighthouse#3335)
evidence: validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:325-357
validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:440-451
impact: One pooled reqwest Client per Web3SignerDefinition shared by all validators using that signer.

title: Remote signer keep-alive below server timeout
idea: Set the remote signer HTTP keep-alive timeout below the signer's own idle timeout (e.g. 20s vs 30s) so pooled connections are reused, not dropped.
evidence: validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:50 DEFAULT_WEB3SIGNER_KEEP_ALIVE = 20s
validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:447-450 Client::builder().pool_idle_timeout(keep_alive_timeout)
validator_client/src/cli.rs:540-547 --web3-signer-keep-alive-timeout default 20000ms
validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:327-356 one reqwest Client per Web3SignerDefinition, shared across validators
impact: None left.

title: Sign block header root, not full block
idea: Send only the block header/roots to the signer rather than the full block body, shrinking signing requests.
evidence: validator_client/signing_method/src/web3signer.rs:75-80 BeaconBlock has optional block and block_header
validator_client/signing_method/src/web3signer.rs:113-150 Bellatrix and later send block_header only
impact: None left for blocks. Phase0/Altair send the full block, which does not matter on mainnet.

title: Throttle concurrent remote signer requests
idea: Queue signing requests to the remote signer and cap in-flight requests, since epoch-boundary selection proofs for all keys arrive in bulk.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1596-1625 attestation selection proofs are signed in per-slot batches at mid-slot with a lookahead, not all at the epoch boundary
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1666-1679 in the default (non-DVT) mode, selection proofs are signed serially (stream::iter().then(), one request in flight)
validator_client/src/lib.rs:68-74,488-511 defaults: lookahead 8 slots, offset slot/2, parallel_sign=false for non-distributed mode
validator_client/validator_services/src/sync.rs:636-680 the FuturesUnordered unbounded path runs only when parallel_sign is set (DVT)
validator_client/initialized_validators/src/lib.rs:448-451 the web3signer reqwest client sets only pool_max_idle_per_host, with no in-flight cap
validator_client/lighthouse_validator_store/src/lib.rs:1228-1341 attestation signing uses join_all with no cap
gap: The burst this idea targets (selection proofs for all keys at the epoch boundary) is already removed: default mode signs them serially and spreads them across slots. What is still missing is a general cap on in-flight remote-signer requests. Per-slot attestation and aggregate signing uses join_all with no bound, and the DVT/parallel_sign mode signs selection proofs with no bound. To close the gap, add a Semaphore around the Web3Signer requests in SigningMethod.
impact: Small. The epoch-boundary burst is already gone in default mode. A general cap would only smooth the per-slot signing of about 1/32 of the keys, or help DVT setups.
refute_note: The earlier review searched only for Semaphore/buffer_unordered. It missed that fill_in_selection_proofs signs serially and in per-slot batches (lookahead 8, mid-slot), which is a scheduling equivalent of throttling the selection-proof burst.

title: Prioritize duty signing over registrations
idea: Put registration signing behind a bounded queue and give aggregation/duty signing priority so slot-critical signing is not starved.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/preparation_service.rs:395-445 registrations signed sequentially, with a signed-data cache
validator_client/validator_services/src/preparation_service.rs:218-246 separate registration task
gap: Registration signing has no bounded queue or priority versus duty signing. Add bounded concurrency in the loop in preparation_service.rs ~395 and leave duty signing unthrottled.
impact: Helps only remote-signer nodes with thousands of keys when registrations are first signed; cached afterwards.

title: Parallel broadcast to fallback nodes with timeout
idea: Send VC requests to all fallback beacon nodes in parallel with a timeout on subscription requests, so one slow node does not delay the others.
evidence: validator_client/beacon_node_fallback/src/lib.rs:826-848 broadcast() runs func on all candidates with future::join_all
validator_client/src/config.rs:141 broadcast_topics defaults to [Subscriptions]
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1166 subscriptions use request(ApiTopic::Subscriptions)
validator_client/beacon_node_fallback/src/lib.rs:590-594 optimized timeouts when more than one BN
common/eth2/src/lib.rs:142-147 attestation_subscriptions timeout = slot/QUOTIENT
impact: Already shipped by #6223.

title: Return on first successful beacon node
idea: When submitting to multiple beacon nodes, return as soon as one accepts (or after a soft timeout, take the first success) and let the remaining calls finish detached.
evidence: validator_client/beacon_node_fallback/src/lib.rs:826-852 broadcast waits for join_all of every BN
validator_client/beacon_node_fallback/src/lib.rs:717-765 first_success awaits candidates sequentially
gap: broadcast() could race the futures and return on first Ok, leaving the rest detached; first_success could start the next candidate after a soft timeout instead of waiting for the full timeout.
impact: Only helps multi-BN setups with a slow node: cuts tail latency of broadcast topics from the per-call timeout to the fastest BN. Bounded already by per-call timeouts.

title: Per-call slot-fraction timeouts for failover
idea: Give each VC-to-BN HTTP call its own timeout as a fraction of slot time, short only when a fallback exists, so a hung BN is abandoned quickly.
evidence: validator_client/beacon_node_fallback/src/lib.rs:590-594 Timeouts::use_optimized_timeouts only when the list has more than one BN and long timeouts are off
common/eth2/src/lib.rs:142-164 every call type gets base_timeout / its own QUOTIENT
common/eth2/src/lib.rs:176-182 the timeouts are stored per BeaconNodeHttpClient
impact: Already shipped.

title: Primary beacon node first, fallback on error
idea: Send requests only to the primary beacon node while healthy and use fallbacks only after an error.
evidence: validator_client/beacon_node_fallback/src/lib.rs:717-750 first_success awaits lazy futures one at a time in health-sorted order and returns on the first Ok
validator_client/beacon_node_fallback/src/lib.rs:855-866 request() uses first_success unless the topic is in broadcast_topics
validator_client/src/config.rs:141 only Subscriptions are broadcast by default
impact: Default behaviour sends to the best node and falls back on error. Broadcast is opt-in except for subscriptions.

title: Reduce readiness polling of failed nodes
idea: Poll readiness of failed secondary beacon nodes rarely (e.g. every 60s), skip overlapping checks, and start assuming only the primary is ready.
evidence: validator_client/beacon_node_fallback/src/lib.rs:72-150 updater loop calls update_all_candidates every slot
validator_client/beacon_node_fallback/src/lib.rs:620-640 polls all candidates including failed ones concurrently
gap: update_all_candidates would need per-candidate state to poll Err candidates less often and skip overlapping checks.
impact: Saves a few failed HTTP attempts per slot for users with a dead fallback; negligible CPU or bandwidth.

title: Targeted beacon node status checks
idea: Check only the BN status properties relevant to each API call instead of full checks on every node, allowing optimistic/unsynced nodes where safe.
evidence: validator_client/beacon_node_fallback/src/lib.rs:291-340 refresh_health always runs is_compatible plus check_node_health with all fields
validator_client/beacon_node_fallback/src/beacon_node_health.rs health tiers by sync distance, optimistic, EL
gap: Would need per-API-call health requirements (e.g. allow optimistic for duties) in candidate selection instead of one global sort.
impact: Mostly resilience, not speed; minor reduction in status requests.

title: Poll next-epoch duties before boundary
idea: Fetch next-epoch proposer duties shortly before the epoch boundary, after the BN precomputes the next-epoch state, so the first-slot proposer is known without delay.
measured_best: polling at epoch start wasted up to 2 s causing missed proposals (pr:lodestar#5794)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:706-718
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1881-1884
beacon_node/http_api/src/proposer_duties.rs:91-108
impact: Next-epoch proposer duties are already cached in the VC before the boundary; the BN serves current_epoch+1 from head.

title: Recompute duties only after reorg ancestor
idea: On reorg, find the common ancestor and recompute duties only for epochs after it; late-block reorgs need no recompute.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1220-1273 poll_beacon_attesters_for_epoch queries a small sample, compares (epoch, dependent_root) per validator and refetches only mismatches
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1370-1382 selection proofs recomputed only for new_duties
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1875-1884 proposer duties also keyed by dependent_root
impact: Equivalent: only epochs whose dependent_root changed (reorg deeper than the shuffling boundary) get duties and proofs recomputed; late-block reorgs leave the current-epoch dependent root unchanged.

title: Target roots in head event
idea: Include current and previous target/dependent roots in the head event so VCs recalc duties only when those change.
evidence: validator_client/beacon_node_fallback/src/beacon_head_monitor.rs:15-20 HeadEvent has only index, slot, block root
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1254 duties are re-polled each slot and compared by dependent_root
common/eth2/src/types.rs:1212 SseHead has current/previous_duty_dependent_root but VC ignores them
gap: Pass SseHead dependent roots through HeadEvent and have the duties service skip the per-slot duties POST when they match the cached roots.
impact: Saves roughly one attester duties request per slot per VC; small on BN load.

title: Skip redundant next-epoch duties request
idea: Do not request next-epoch duties separately when the previous response already contained them.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1085 separate next-epoch poll with its own dependent_root check
impact: Standard HTTP API duties are per-epoch, so the next-epoch request is a distinct call; the Prysm saving came from its older RPC that returned both epochs. The PR was closed unmerged.

title: Skip attestation data without duties
idea: Do not request attestation data (or wait for the deadline) in slots with no local attestation duties.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:250-263 spawn_attestation_tasks returns before any attestation_data request when attesters(slot) is empty
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:591-610 attesters(slot)
impact: Saves one attestation_data request and the deadline wait per slot without local duties.

title: Skip duty requests with no active keys
idea: Skip all duty requests to the BN when the VC has no active keys.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1226-1233 attester poll returns when local_indices empty
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1875-1884 proposer duties fetched only if local_pubkeys non-empty
validator_client/validator_services/src/sync.rs:428-441 sync duty poll returns when local_indices empty
impact: No duty requests to the BN when the VC has no active keys.

title: Skip empty validators query
idea: Do not send a POST validators request with an empty id list, since the BN treats it as all validators.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:962 index resolution uses GET validators/{id} per single pubkey
common/eth2/src/lib.rs:902 post_beacon_states_validators exists but VC does not call it

title: DVT selections once per epoch
idea: In distributed validator mode, submit beacon committee selections to the selections endpoint once per epoch (current and next) instead of per slot.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1371-1378 selections_endpoint branch spawns fill_in_selection_proofs_selections_endpoint per epoch of new duties
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1713-1760 one make_beacon_committee_selection call per epoch, retried per slot only on failure
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:171-200 make_beacon_committee_selection batches all duties of the epoch
impact: DVT only: selections endpoint called once per epoch (current and next) instead of per slot.

title: Reuse duty data instead of extra requests
idea: Use data already in the duty (committees per slot, committee length, aggregator index) for subnet subscription and aggregation rather than re-querying the BN.
measured_best: reduces the time needed to subscribe from 1-2 seconds to 1 millisecond (pr:prysm#13702)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:152-158
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1135-1157
impact: Subscriptions and aggregator selection use AttesterData fields; no extra BN queries.

title: Reuse duty statuses for exit check
idea: Derive the all-validators-exited check from statuses already in the duties response instead of a separate status query each epoch.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/notifier_service.rs:137 active/inactive counts computed from local store, no BN query
duties_service.rs:911 poll_validator_indices only queries unknown pubkeys
impact: VC has no separate all-validators-exited status query each epoch, so nothing to elide.

title: Remove redundant head API call
idea: Drop an extra canonical-head API call before duties fetch; use the wall-clock current slot.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1031 poll_beacon_attesters uses slot_clock.now()
grep of validator_client finds no get_beacon_headers / head call before duties
impact: Lighthouse already takes current slot from the wall clock and makes no canonical-head call before fetching duties.

title: Memoize genesis from beacon node
idea: Fetch genesis info once and memoize it rather than requesting it on every call.
measured_best: for 1024 keys as many as 7 requests per second, becoming 1 total (pr:prysm#13796)
evidence: validator_client/src/lib.rs:388-397
validator_client/src/lib.rs:834

title: Fee recipient calls only for configured keys
idea: Avoid per-validator fee recipient lookups against the BN and send prepare-proposer/registration only for keys with a configured fee recipient.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/preparation_service.rs:262-290 prepare_proposers_and_publish/collect_preparation_data include only keys with Some(fee_recipient) and an index, skip publish if empty
validator_client/validator_services/src/preparation_service.rs:292-300 collect_validator_registration_keys skips keys without index/fee recipient
impact: Fee recipients come from the local validator store; no per-validator BN lookups; only configured keys are sent.

title: No duplicate registration calls at startup
idea: Send validator registrations once at startup, not both explicitly and via an epoch scheduler that fires immediately.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/preparation_service.rs:215-243 start_validator_registration_service is the only registration sender
validator_client/validator_services/src/preparation_service.rs:359-386 register_validators sends only changed keys or all keys every EPOCHS_PER_VALIDATOR_REGISTRATION_SUBMISSION
validator_client/src/lib.rs:640-655 pre-genesis loop sends proposer preparations, not registrations
impact: Registrations are sent once at startup (as changed keys) and periodically; no duplicate startup call.

title: Prune registration cache for inactive keys
idea: Key the builder registration cache by pubkey and prune entries for validators no longer active.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/preparation_service.rs:124 cache keyed by ValidatorRegistrationKey (fee_recipient,gas_limit,pubkey)
validator_client/preparation_service.rs:462 only inserts, never removes
gap: Cache is never pruned: old entries for changed fee recipient/gas limit or removed/inactive validators stay. Retain only keys returned by collect_validator_registration_keys in register_validators.

title: Skip current-slot sync selection proofs
idea: Do not compute sync committee selection proofs for the current slot, since aggregation already happened in the previous slot.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/sync.rs:624-636 fill_in_aggregation_proofs starts at current_slot + 1
impact: Sync selection proofs for the current slot are not computed.

title: Precompute own committee membership ahead
idea: Compute local validators' committee membership and aggregator selection proofs a few slots ahead once, and reuse it for attesting, aggregating and subscriptions; skip empty subnet updates.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1581-1700 fill_in_selection_proofs computes aggregator selection proofs lookahead_slot ahead and stores them in DutyAndProof
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:591-610 attesters(slot) reuses stored duties for attesting and aggregating
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1135-1162 subscriptions built from stored duties, POST skipped when empty
validator_client/validator_services/src/sync.rs:105-130 prepare_for_aggregator_pre_compute for sync
impact: Committee membership and aggregator proofs computed once ahead and reused by attestation, aggregation and subscription paths.

title: Staggered subnet subscriptions with retry
idea: Send each attestation subnet subscription only a few times ahead of the slot and retry only on failure, instead of every slot to every node.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:51 ATTESTATION_SUBSCRIPTION_OFFSETS [3,4,5,6,7,8,16,32]
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:246-282 SubscriptionSlots::new/should_send_subscription_at/record_successful_subscription_at
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1140-1200 only due subscriptions sent; marked sent on success or partial success; retried next slot when all BNs fail
impact: Per-duty staggered subscriptions with retry on failure are in place (this is LH's own PR #4806).

title: Cache sync duties, skip doppelganger for inactive
idea: Cache sync committee duties so subscriptions are not resent every slot, and skip doppelganger checks for not-yet-active validators.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/sync_committee_service.rs:539-560 publish_subscriptions: current-period subscriptions only on first run and at epoch start; next-period every slot only in the 4-epoch lookahead
validator_client/validator_services/src/sync.rs:88 all_duties_known caches duties per period
validator_client/doppelganger_service/src/lib.rs:400-430 compute_detection_indices_map omits validators with no index
impact: Sync duties are cached per period, and subscriptions go out per epoch, not per slot (except in the 4-epoch lookahead, which is on purpose). Validators that have no index are not queried for doppelganger.

title: Doppelganger liveness only for due validators
idea: Only query liveness for validators whose next doppelganger check epoch is now.
evidence: validator_client/doppelganger_service/src/lib.rs:243 check every slot at 75%
validator_client/lib.rs:400 filter only by requires_further_checks, not next_check_epoch
validator_client/lib.rs:99 two liveness requests (prev+current epoch) per run
gap: In compute_detection_indices_map also filter validators whose next_check_epoch is not yet due (previous_epoch >= next_check_epoch, as in lib.rs:566). Lighthouse intentionally polls every slot for fast detection, so this trades detection latency.
impact: Fewer indices in liveness POSTs for the first few epochs after adding keys; negligible on steady-state nodes.

title: No-op sync duties without assignments
idea: Treat a sync committee duty as a no-op with no subscriptions when there are no assignments or no head state.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/sync_committee_service.rs:217-225 no duties known or empty duties -> return before any work
validator_client/validator_services/src/sync_committee_service.rs:566-597 no duty slots / empty subscriptions -> no request
impact: No-op paths exist already.

title: Hash map index of local pubkeys
idea: Index local validators by pubkey in a hash map for duty and known-validator checks instead of linear scans.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:325 AttesterMap HashMap<PublicKeyBytes,..>
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1050,1875,2119 local_pubkeys HashSet used for proposer/sync/ptc filtering

validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1246-1290 poll_beacon_attesters_for_epoch: validators_to_update is a Vec, initial_indices_to_request is a slice; `.contains` inside per-duty filters
gap: poll_beacon_attesters_for_epoch builds validators_to_update as a Vec<&PublicKeyBytes> and filters the response with validators_to_update.contains(&&duty.pubkey). It also filters indices with initial_indices_to_request.contains (a slice). When uninitialized validators exist (startup, newly added keys), both have N entries, so the result is O(N^2): about 1e8 48-byte compares for 10k keys, for both the current and the next epoch. Fix: collect validators_to_update and the initial indices into a HashSet.
impact: Only at startup or when keys are added; on the steady-state path the initial query is a single index and lookups are hashed. Can cost a fraction of a second of CPU per epoch poll for VCs with very large key counts.

title: Map lookup for committee selections
idea: Index combined committee selections in a map keyed by duty rather than scanning a list per duty.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1759-1772 selection_hashmap keyed by (validator_index, slot), O(1) remove per duty
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:173-231 make_beacon_committee_selection one call per epoch
impact: Combined selections are looked up through a HashMap keyed by (validator_index, slot). This is the same as Lodestar #8710, and LH also checks the slot.

title: Fixed-size byte array as pubkey map key
idea: Key validator maps by a fixed 48-byte array instead of a string to avoid allocation and marshalling.
evidence: crypto/bls/src/generic_public_key_bytes.rs:20-23 GenericPublicKeyBytes { bytes: [u8; 48] }
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:325 maps keyed by PublicKeyBytes
impact: Keys are already fixed-size arrays; nothing to gain.

title: Shared buffer for pubkey hex encoding
idea: Reuse one buffer for hex-encoding pubkeys in hot duty paths instead of allocating per call.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1420 only to_string of validator_index in metrics
impact: Rust keys are fixed byte arrays, not hex strings, on hot duty paths; hex only at API/log edges.

title: Single-allocation lock key construction
idea: Build per-duty lock keys in one allocation instead of formatting and concatenation.
measured_best: 397 ns/op to 245 ns/op, 432 B/op to 408 B/op (pr:prysm#8349)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:325 maps keyed by (PublicKeyBytes, Epoch) structurally, no formatted string lock keys
impact: Lighthouse does not build string lock keys per duty.

title: Preallocate target-epochs slice
idea: Pre-size collections of target epochs in slashing code to avoid regrowth.
measured_best: 'minor improvement' (pr:prysm#8452)
evidence: validator_client/slashing_protection/src/slashing_database.rs:411-467 uses SQLite queries by target_epoch, no in-memory target epoch slice
impact: Slashing protection is SQL-backed with no target-epoch vector to preallocate.

title: Hoist registry scan out of per-key status
idea: When resolving status for many pubkeys, compute the last-active-validator index once per state instead of per pubkey.
measured_best: for large operators this is a strain (no numbers) (pr:prysm#12487)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:911-1000 resolves index per unknown pubkey via get_beacon_states_validator_id
beacon_node/http_api/src/attester_duties.rs:210 pubkey lookups via pubkey cache
impact: The VC resolves pubkey to index per key via the BN pubkey cache; there is no last-active-validator registry scan to hoist.

title: Single-pass multi-key committee assignments
idea: Compute committee assignments for all requested keys in one pass over the epoch's committees instead of per-key scans.
measured_best: 16k validators: 182708160 ns/op, 85 MB/op; previously over 4 minutes for 8k validators (pr:prysm#4294)
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/committee_cache.rs:295 get_attestation_duties: O(1) shuffled_position then linear scan over committees per validator
beacon_node/http_api/src/attester_duties.rs:15 per-index duties from cached CommitteeCache
gap: No O(validators) scan per key (shuffled_position is O(1)), but each index scans up to 2048 committees to find its range. A binary search over compute_committee_range in CommitteeCache::get_attestation_duties would remove it.
impact: Negligible: a few thousand integer comparisons per key per epoch on the BN.

title: Use epoch committee cache for attestations
idea: Use cached epoch shuffling/committees when producing attestations instead of recomputing committees from state.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:258 duties come from BN attester duties API
validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:268 attestation data fetched from BN
impact: The VC does not compute committees from state; the BN serves duties and attestation data, so the BN's committee cache applies.

title: Avoid state copies for selection proof serving
idea: Compute active indices and seed from the shared head state rather than copying the state several times per aggregate-selection request.
measured_best: reduces 3 state copies to 1 per call (pr:prysm#5813)
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/aggregate_attestation.rs:12 get_aggregate_attestation looks up the naive aggregation pool by data root, no state load or copy
Lighthouse selection proofs are signed in the validator client; the BN endpoint does not compute active indices or seed
impact: None: no per-request state copies exist on this path, and BeaconState clones are cheap (milhouse persistent tree).

title: Status from state for active validators
idea: Derive validator status from the beacon state when the validator is already active, skipping eth1 deposit RPC lookups.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:477 unknown_validator_next_poll_slots; index resolved via BN validators endpoint
impact: VC resolves validator indices through the BN state API; it makes no eth1 deposit RPC lookups.

title: No state regen for error logging
idea: Do not compute committee info (possibly regenerating state) just to log a failed attestation.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs: failure handlers do not compute committee info for logging
impact: Lighthouse does not compute committee info just to log a failed attestation, so the Teku-specific issue does not exist.

title: VC-side slot timer for attestations
idea: Trigger attestation production from the VC's own slot timer rather than BN head events, so the BN need not emit head events for empty slots.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:196-238 loop computes the deadline from the slot clock; head_event_or_deadline
validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:304-330 falls back to the deadline sleep then first_success
impact: The VC is driven by the slot clock. Head events are only an optional early trigger, so in empty slots it still attests at the deadline.

title: Skip stale duties when behind
idea: Drive duties from a slot tick and drop obsolete attestations/proposals when the node falls behind.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:218-237 re-reads the slot clock and skips if current_slot <= latest_attested_slot
validator_client/validator_services/src/block_service.rs:461-472 do_update skips block production when notification.slot != current slot
impact: Stale attestations and proposals are dropped; each iteration targets only the current slot.

title: Resolve non-positive sleeps immediately
idea: Resolve a sleep with zero or negative delay immediately instead of arming a timer.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:322 tokio sleep with zero duration
impact: Tokio sleep with a zero or elapsed deadline completes on the next poll; this is a JS timer quirk.

title: Fully async performance tracker
idea: Remove blocking joins on futures in VC performance tracking so slot handlers are not blocked.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/attestation_service.rs:spawn_attestation_tasks uses async/await, no blocking joins
impact: Rust async VC does not block on futures in a performance tracker; no such blocking join exists.

title: Multithreaded validator API serving
idea: Serve validator API requests on a thread pool to cut attestation generation latency (reverted: hurt nodes with many validators).
evidence: validator_client/http_api/src/lib.rs: VC API is warp on tokio multi-thread runtime already
impact: Idea was reverted upstream, and the VC runs on the tokio multi-threaded runtime with no dedicated pool to add.

title: Short-circuit no-op validator updates
idea: Return early from no-op validator setting updates before taking locks or O(n) key-cache work.
evidence: validator_client/http_api/src/lib.rs:731-771 equal_or_none no-op arms return Ok(()) for all settable fields (enabled, gas_limit, builder_boost_factor, builder_proposals, prefer_builder_proposals, graffiti)
validator_client/http_api/src/lib.rs:774-783 already-disabled no-op arm
validator_client/http_api/src/lib.rs:785-790 RwLockUpgradableReadGuard::upgrade only on a real change, before set_validator_definition_fields
impact: A no-op PATCH never takes the write lock, never rewrites definitions and never touches the key cache.

title: Prune past-epoch duty maps
idea: Drop per-epoch duty and tracking map entries for past epochs/slots so long-running VC services do not grow without bound.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:38-39 HISTORICAL_DUTIES_EPOCHS=2
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1206-1213 attesters per-pubkey epoch maps retained
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:1918-1921 proposers retained
validator_client/validator_services/src/duties_service.rs:2173-2176 lookahead duty maps (PTC/IL) retained
validator_client/validator_services/src/sync.rs:258 sync committee periods retained
validator_client/validator_services/src/builder_preferences_service.rs:83-84,158-159 slot-keyed caches split_off at current slot
validator_client/validator_services/src/request_auth_cache.rs:102-104 prune by slot
impact: Every epoch-keyed or slot-keyed duty map in the VC is pruned periodically, so growth is bounded.

title: Replace sync duties per period
idea: On a new sync committee duties response for a period, replace the stored duties instead of merging so removed validators drop out.
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/sync.rs:477-505 merges per-validator duties, replacing only when indices changed
gap: Lighthouse never removes validators that disappear from a re-fetched period response; replace the validators map (retain only returned indices) in poll_sync_committee_duties_for_period.
impact: Only matters after a deep reorg changes committee membership; stale duty would be a rare wasted/invalid sync message, no throughput gain.

title: Prepare hash-based signing keys off the signing path
idea: For stateful hash-based (one-time-signature) keys, advance key preparation windows/subtrees ahead of time, in parallel and on a background thread, only for keys about to sign, so signing never stalls on precomputation.
measured_best: 64 keys 1.54 s to 33 keys 142 ms (pr:ethlambda#621)
evidence: validator_client/validator_services/src/sync.rs: BLS signing only, no hash-based keys
impact: No hash-based one-time signature keys exist in Lighthouse (BLS only).

title: parent root index
idea: Add a secondary index parent_root -> list of block roots so headers-by-parent queries do a lookup instead of scanning.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/lib.rs:729-756 parent_root query uses block lookup plus forwards_iter_block_roots from the parent slot
impact: Lookup is a short iterator scan from parent slot to the first non-skipped root; no scan of all blocks, so an index gains almost nothing.

title: narrow lock scope, drop caches
idea: Release the shared state lock as early as possible during aggregate processing, and drop debug-only diff structures and compression of random 32-byte hash caches, which cost memory and allocations for no gain.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs (no Caplin-style debug diff structures); aggregate processing uses fine-grained locks
impact: Go/Caplin-specific lock scope and debug diff structures have no counterpart in Lighthouse.

title: pre-commit overlay notifications
idea: Publish head/state-change notifications to RPC subscribers from the in-memory overlay before the DB commit finishes, so latest-state queries do not wait on disk.
measured_best: responsiveness not throughput; no numbers
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/canonical_head.rs: head is in an in-memory cached_head, SSE events fire from memory
impact: Lighthouse has no DB overlay; latest-state queries read the in-memory cached head, not disk.

title: pre-sized direct JSON encoding
idea: For large JSON responses (blobs bundle), marshal directly into one pre-sized buffer with in-place hex encoding and write the already-encoded result verbatim through the RPC handler and codec, avoiding repeated reflection marshalling and compact re-scans of the payload.
