impact: Saves a thread-pool hop and 64-bit scalar muls per single-set verify; microseconds against a ~1ms pairing, so marginal.

title: Drop release loop over semi-aggregates in batch verify
idea: In batch BLS verification, skip the explicit per-item release/cleanup pass over semi-aggregates when the library holds no external memory. This saves one pass and one list allocation per batch.
measured_best: None (pr:teku#5456)
evidence: crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:36-117 blst Rust bindings own and free their memory; no per-item release pass exists
impact: Teku/JNI specific cleanup pass; nothing to remove in Rust.

title: Check signature subgroup once at deserialisation
idea: Validate signature points (subgroup and flags) once when deserialising and do not repeat the check in the verify or batch-verify path (or defer to the library, not both). Each signature then incurs the G2 subgroup check once rather than twice.
measured_best: None (pr:teku#4372)
evidence: crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:72-78 batch path subgroup-checks each signature once
crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:110-112 verify_multiple_aggregate_signatures with sigs_groupcheck=false
crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:194-196 deserialize via from_bytes (no group check)
crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:205 single verify checks the group inside blst
crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:257-281 fast_aggregate_verify/aggregate_verify check once inside blst; add_signature uses false
impact: Each signature gets exactly one G2 subgroup check on every verify path.

title: Skip Pippenger for tiny multi-scalar multiplications
idea: For multi-scalar multiplication over fewer than about 32 points, use per-point scalar multiplication plus summation instead of tiled Pippenger. This avoids Pippenger setup cost on small aggregate batches.
evidence: crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:36-117 batch verify uses blst mul_n_aggregate per set with 64-bit rands; no MSM/Pippenger call in Lighthouse BLS code
crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:99 pubkey aggregation is point addition, not MSM
impact: Lighthouse does not run a Pippenger MSM for BLS; KZG MSMs live inside c-kzg (not inspected).

title: Wake only as many BLS workers as queued items
idea: When enqueuing BLS jobs, signal only as many sleeping pool workers as there are new items (tracking the sleeper count under the queue lock) rather than broadcasting to all. This avoids thundering-herd wakeups and scheduler churn for small batches.
evidence: crypto/bls/src/impls/blst.rs:36 no Lighthouse-owned BLS worker queue
blst-0.3.17/src/lib.rs:41-50,1337-1350 blst uses the threadpool crate (mpsc, one wake per job), not a broadcast condvar
impact: No broadcast wakeup to fix; per-job wakeup already.

title: Bump dependency with cheaper generated-table compile
idea: Update dependencies that embed large generated lookup tables (e.g. an IP-to-ASN table in the libp2p stack) to versions that compile the table more cheaply. Check whether Lighthouse's discv5/libp2p dependencies pull in a similarly heavy generated-table crate.
evidence: Cargo.lock: no ASN/GeoIP table crate (only ipnet, phf); discv5 0.12.0 and libp2p 0.57.0 pull none
impact: Rust libp2p has no embedded IP-to-ASN table; this was a go-libp2p issue.

title: Fetch EL blobs when payload envelope awaits blobs
idea: When a payload envelope arrives before its blob data is available, call engine_getBlobs, build the missing column sidecars into the quarantine and re-enqueue the pending envelope. Availability is met locally without waiting for gossip columns.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1925-1941 Gloas gossip block inserted into pending_payload_cache then spawn_fetch_block_columns
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:960-995 spawn_fetch_block_columns -> fetch_engine_blobs_and_publish_full
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:369-392 Bid path merges EL columns into pending_payload_cache, publishes, calls process_payload_envelope_availability
beacon_node/network/src/service.rs:689-700 HTTP-published blocks also trigger the fetch
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/sync_methods.rs:209-224 RPC lookup block with MissingComponents also calls getBlobs
impact: getBlobs runs on Gloas block receipt (gossip, RPC, HTTP) from the bid's commitments, and the EL-built columns complete the pending envelope's availability without waiting for gossip columns. There is no second getBlobs attempt when the envelope arrives (process_gossip_verified_execution_payload_envelope), but nimbus#8498 also fires at block time, so this matches the source.

title: Refresh quarantine LRU position on sidecar request
idea: In the sidecar quarantine, move an entry to the front of the LRU on request (pop) as well as on insert. Blocks still being assembled are not evicted before completion.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/mod.rs:612-617 peek_pending_components uses LruCache::peek, no promotion
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/mod.rs:55 capacity 32
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker/overflow_lru_cache.rs:396-434 peek_blob/peek_data_columns/peek_pending_components use peek under a read lock
gap: Lighthouse could take a write lock and use get() in the by-root request paths (get_data_columns, peek_data_columns) to refresh LRU position; it chose read-lock peeks. Eviction needs >32 concurrent roots.
impact: Only matters under extreme churn (>32 roots in flight); negligible on mainnet.

title: Defer payload envelope signature checks in bounded queue
idea: Keep unvalidated gossip envelopes in a small bounded queue per (block root, builder) keyed by signature, and verify signatures only when the block arrives, preferring trusted-source envelopes. This avoids verifying envelopes that are never used.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/gossip_verified_envelope.rs:164-168 BlockRootUnknown returned before any signature work
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/gossip_verified_envelope.rs:173-186 observed-envelope dedupe before signature verify
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:3893-3965 unknown-block envelope queued unverified; verified only when the block is imported
beacon_node/beacon_processor/src/scheduler/work_reprocessing_queue.rs:763-799 bounded queue (MAXIMUM_QUEUED_ENVELOPES=16), one per block root, timeout
impact: Envelope BLS checks are deferred until the block is known, and the queue is bounded. The queue holds one envelope per block root with first-wins, not one per (root, builder, signature), and it does not prefer trusted sources. That is a robustness difference, not extra signature work.

title: Check in-memory column status before DB block read
idea: When answering whether blob data is available for a block, check the in-memory column availability status first and read the block from the database only if no columns are stored. The common case avoids a DB read.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2254-2259 payload attestation data takes blob_data_available from pending_payload_cache
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/mod.rs:149-162 is_blob_data_available peeks in-memory pending components only
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/pending_components.rs:216-220 compares cached column count to the custody requirement
impact: The PTC blob_data_available answer comes only from memory and never reads a block from the DB, so the cost prysm#17222 removed does not exist here.

title: Drop KZG commitments from data column sidecars
idea: Do not carry KZG commitments in every column sidecar when they are in the block or builder bid; take them from there. Sidecars are smaller to gossip, serve and store.
evidence: consensus/types/src/data/data_column_sidecar.rs:94-97 kzg_commitments is only(Fulu); Gloas commitments come from the bid
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_column_verification.rs:407-418 Gloas gossip verification takes the commitment count from load_gloas_payload_bid
impact: Gloas sidecars carry no commitments, header or inclusion proof. Fulu keeps them because the spec requires it.

title: Do not backfill columns when custody increases
idea: When validator custody count increases, custody only new columns going forward and advance the earliest-available slot instead of requesting historical columns by root. This removes periodic refill requests.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/custody_backfill_sync/mod.rs:130-330 full custody backfill sync state machine requests historical columns by range when custody grows
beacon_node/store/src/metadata.rs:215-221 earliest_data_column_slot tracks backfill progress
beacon_node/network/src/status.rs:36 advertises earliest_data_column_slot in Status
gap: Lighthouse would have to drop CustodyBackFillSync (start/include_next_batch/send_batch) and, when the custody group count rises, set earliest_data_column_slot to the current epoch start instead of downloading older columns. Needs a decision that serving fewer historical columns is acceptable.
impact: Only nodes whose validator custody grows (validators attached, balance increases) download the columns of up to ~18 days of history, one time. Dropping it saves that bandwidth and DB writes, but those nodes then serve less history.

title: Publish proposer column sidecars before payload envelope
idea: At proposal time compute and broadcast data column sidecars before the execution payload envelope is published. Receivers have the columns for their availability check when the envelope arrives.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes.rs:228-246 column build is spawned in parallel with envelope gossip
beacon_node/http_api/src/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes.rs:376-396 columns are published only after the envelope is published and imported
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:168-172 Gloas block publish does not publish columns
gap: In publish_execution_payload_envelope, await column_build_future and call publish_column_sidecars before publish_fn broadcasts the envelope (or at least at the same time). Trade-off with idea 172: publishing columns before validation.
impact: Peers would hold the columns when the envelope arrives, so payload availability could complete sooner. Only affects self-built or API-submitted payloads (proposers), a latency gain of the KZG column build time, not CPU.

title: Proposer publishes sidecars only when responsible
idea: Publish data column sidecars from the proposer only when it self-builds the payload, and on the envelope publish API only after the envelope passes validation. Invalid or builder-owned payloads do not cause sidecar gossip.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes.rs:262-271 envelope gossip-verified first; errors return before any publish
beacon_node/http_api/src/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes.rs:342-362 import errors return before columns are published
beacon_node/http_api/src/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes.rs:368-376 publish_and_import_columns only after successful envelope processing
beacon_node/http_api/src/publish_blocks.rs:168-172 self-built payload skips the EL fetch at block publish; columns come only from the envelope endpoint
impact: Invalid envelopes never cause column gossip. Self-built columns are published once, from the envelope endpoint. Builder payloads go through the normal getBlobs path that every node runs.

title: Per-type block data availability state machines
idea: Model block data-availability tracking as separate per-type structures (pre-DA, blobs, columns) so each does only the work its type needs and objects have a stable shape. This helps runtime optimization.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:764-775 AvailableBlockData enum with Blobs and DataColumns variants
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/pending_payload_cache/pending_components.rs separate Gloas pending-components type
impact: The Lodestar change is about stable object shapes for the V8 JIT (monomorphic classes); Rust enums and separate types are already static, so there is no runtime gain.

title: One getBlobs attempt per slot, not per column gossip
idea: Trigger the EL getBlobs call once at slot start for the latest sidecarless block instead of on every incoming column gossip message. This avoids repeated EL calls and work.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1936 getBlobs once per gossip block
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/gossip_methods.rs:1119-1133 partial-header path calls getBlobs only when !header.was_cached()
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/mod.rs:960-995 spawn_fetch_block_columns; full-column gossip handlers never call it
impact: There are at most about two getBlobs calls per block (block arrival plus the first new partial header), never one per column message.

title: Skip custody increase detection without validators
idea: Skip end-of-epoch validator custody detection and any column custody increase when no validators are attached. Non-validating nodes do not raise custody or download extra columns.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/custody_context.rs:401-445 register_validators raises custody only on VC registration
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/custody_context.rs:450-459 no validators -> spec.custody_requirement
beacon_node/http_api/src/validator/mod.rs:1104 only non-test caller is the validator HTTP endpoint
impact: There is no end-of-epoch custody scan. A node without validators stays at the minimum custody and never raises it.

title: Encode slot directly into range-scan bounds
idea: Build range-scan bounds for slot-indexed DB buckets by encoding the slot number into the key, not by allocating a buffer sized by the slot value. Check Lighthouse range queries for slot-sized allocations.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/forwards_iter.rs:138-140 slot range start is start_slot.to_be_bytes()
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:865 period-indexed scan uses start_period.to_be_bytes()
beacon_node/store/src/database/leveldb_impl.rs:254-260 full-column scans use vec![0; column.key_size()], a fixed per-column size
beacon_node/store/src/database/redb_impl.rs:235,272 same fixed-size start key
impact: Range bounds are fixed-size encoded keys. No allocation scales with the slot value.

title: Background service rebuilding historical states by block replay
idea: Offer an opt-in background task that replays stored blocks from genesis to regenerate historical finalized states, so a node can keep few states on disk yet regain archive state access later.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/reconstruct.rs:21 reconstruct_historic_states replays blocks from state_lower_limit with per_block_processing
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:221 run_reconstruction runs batches of BLOCKS_PER_RECONSTRUCTION and requeues itself
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:483 finalization and blob pruning run before each reconstruction batch so reconstruction does not starve them
impact: Opt-in background reconstruction already exists; it needs full block history (oldest_block_slot == 0), which backfill provides.

title: Partial-read length for archived era state fields
idea: When reading a single field or prefix of a state from an archived era file, pass the needed byte length so only that part is read and decoded, not the whole state.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2161 cold states stored as snapshot/diff columns, no era files
impact: Lighthouse has no era file archive; cold states are in the freezer DB.

title: Stream snapshot block reads into pooled buffer
idea: When reading historical blocks from snapshot or flat files, stream chunks into a pooled reusable buffer instead of allocating and appending a fresh slice per chunk.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs: blocks read from key-value DB, no snapshot/flat files
impact: Lighthouse stores blocks in the KV store, not flat snapshot files.

title: Precompute per-epoch summaries into the database
idea: At epoch end, compute derived data such as validator participation once and store it in the DB so API queries read it instead of recomputing from a historical state.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_rewards.rs:36 compute_attestation_rewards loads end-of-epoch state via get_state and recomputes
store/src/lib.rs DBColumn list has no per-epoch summary column
gap: Add an epoch-summary column written at epoch processing and have compute_attestation_rewards / http_api rewards read it.
impact: Rewards/participation API calls would skip a historical state load (tens to hundreds of ms each); only affects API users, not normal node operation.

title: Use read-only DB transactions for lookups
idea: Open read-only transactions for lookups that do not write, so they avoid the single-writer lock and commit/fsync cost.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/database/redb_impl.rs:98 get_bytes takes self.db.read() and begin_read
beacon_node/store/src/database/redb_impl.rs:128 key_exists uses begin_read
beacon_node/store/src/database/redb_impl.rs:212 iter_column_keys_from uses begin_read
beacon_node/store/src/database/redb_impl.rs:244 iter_column_from uses begin_read
impact: All redb lookups and iterators already use read transactions. Only puts, deletes and batches open write transactions.

title: Serialize finalization archival and cache pruning tasks
idea: On finalization, run block archival, state archival and cache pruning one after another, not concurrently, so heavy tasks do not contend for the runtime or DB.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:430 spawn_thread runs one background migrator thread that drains and coalesces notifications
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:483 run_migration, run_manual_migration, run_prune_blobs, run_reconstruction and run_manual_compaction run one after another
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/migrate.rs:310 run_migration does migrate_database and then prunes the hot DB on the same thread
impact: Heavy finalization DB work (block and state archival, pruning, blob pruning, reconstruction, compaction) runs in sequence on one dedicated thread. Pruning of in-memory caches is cheap.

title: Copy immutable validator fields only for new indices on load
idea: When loading a state from the DB into an existing state that already has validators, copy immutable validator fields (pubkey etc.) only for newly added indices, skipping the populated prefix.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:227 as_state rebuilds all validators via set_validators_from_iter(cloned)
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1990 rebase_on_finalized shares tree with finalized state afterwards
beacon_node/store/src/hdiff.rs:534 ValidatorsDiff::apply patches only changed fields on the buffer Vec
gap: Lighthouse never loads into an existing populated state: HDiffBuffer::as_state clones every Validator into a fresh list, then rebase_on dedups memory. To skip the populated prefix it would have to start from a cached state's validator list and only append new indices in HDiffBuffer::as_state / load_hot_state.
impact: Saves cloning/building the validator list (~1M entries) on a hot state cache miss; rare path and rebuild is already dominated by tree hashing, so small.

title: Skip state existence lookup when a summary proves it
idea: In the head-root save path, skip the extra state-existence read when the stored state summary already shows the state exists.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1697 store_hot_state returns early when load_hot_state_summary already finds the summary
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:687 persist_head does not read whether the head state exists
impact: One summary read is the only existence check. No second state lookup happens after it.

title: DB index from versioned hash to sidecar
idea: Maintain a DB index from blob versioned hash to stored sidecar identifier, updated on store, prune and move, so getBlobs-style lookups by versioned hash are a key read, not a scan.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/block_id.rs:395 get_blobs_by_versioned_hashes takes a block id and matches hashes against that block's commitments
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/fetch_blobs/mod.rs:139 getBlobs goes CL->EL, Lighthouse does not serve by versioned hash across the DB
gap: Lighthouse has no global versioned-hash lookup; its API resolves hashes within a known block via its kzg commitments, so no scan exists to index.
impact: none

title: Key stored aggregates by attestation root
idea: Key pooled attestation aggregates in the store by the attestation hash-tree-root so presence checks and removal of included attestations are direct key lookups or deletes instead of loading and scanning all stored aggregates.
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:66 pool is an in-memory HashMap keyed by CompactAttestationData, not a DB table
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:632 prune by epoch
gap: The Lighthouse aggregate pool is in memory keyed by attestation data (persisted only at shutdown), so there is no stored-aggregate scan to replace.
impact: none

title: Validate blocks before persisting as pending
idea: When a block's parent state is missing, check slot bounds, proposer and signature before writing it as a pending block, and delete discarded pending blocks from disk. Junk blocks are then neither written nor re-served in by-root requests.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs gossip verification returns ParentUnknown without any DB write
beacon_node/beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups holds unknown-parent blocks in memory only
gap: Lighthouse does not persist pending blocks with missing parent state to the DB nor serve them by root, so there is nothing to validate-before-write.
impact: none

title: Build peer id from ENR key without allocating
idea: Construct the libp2p peer id from the ENR's 33-byte secp256k1 key directly into a fixed stack buffer (protobuf header plus identity multihash) rather than via an intermediate Vec. Check how the ENR-to-peer-id conversion allocates.
evidence: common/network_utils/src/enr_ext.rs:269 as_peer_id: to_sec1_bytes (alloc), try_from_bytes, PeerId::from_public_key
~/.cargo/registry/src/*/libp2p-identity-0.3.0/src/peer_id.rs:67 from_public_key allocates via encode_protobuf (prost Vec)
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:395,878,913 enr.peer_id() on each discovered ENR
gap: Replace EnrExt::peer_id / CombinedPublicKeyExt::as_peer_id in enr_ext.rs with a fixed [u8;37] buffer (header 0x08 0x02 0x12 0x21 + 33-byte key, wrapped in identity multihash) and PeerId::from_bytes-style construction.
impact: Saves 2-3 small allocations per discovered ENR; negligible CPU at discovery rates (hundreds per minute).

title: Exclude NAT'd peers from discv5 routing table
idea: Do not insert peers behind NAT (unreachable) into the discv5 routing table, and tune the discv5 config, so lookups return reachable nodes and finish faster.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/config.rs:339 the default discv5 table_filter requires a global IPv4 address in the ENR
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/config.rs:176,197,233 table_filter variants for IPv4, IPv6 and dual stack
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/config.rs:324 tuned discv5 ConfigBuilder (ip_limit, incoming_bucket_limit, query_parallelism, timeouts)
~/.cargo/registry/src/*/discv5-0.12.0/src/discv5.rs:208 add_enr rejects ENRs that fail table_filter
~/.cargo/registry/src/*/discv5-0.12.0/src/service.rs:1263 the table_filter and contactable-address checks run before a node is inserted
impact: ENRs with no global, contactable address stay out of the routing table. This is the same as the PR #926 mechanism.

title: Run identify only after successful Status handshake
idea: Start the peer identify exchange only after a successful STATUS handshake and deduplicate concurrent identify attempts per peer, so no streams are spent on peers that close early or are irrelevant.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:414-427 identify::Behaviour added unconditionally, runs on every connection
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:1927 inject_identify_event only consumes result
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:501 identify used for client info only
gap: libp2p identify::Behaviour fires on connection establishment independent of STATUS. To gate it, wrap it in a custom NetworkBehaviour (or disable automatic exchange and use Behaviour::push) triggered from PeerManager after a successful Status in peer_manager/mod.rs.
impact: Avoids one identify stream per peer that is disconnected before/at Status; small per-connection saving, mostly under peer churn.

title: Enable libp2p smart_dial address ranking
idea: Enable the libp2p swarm smart_dial option so dialing a peer tries its addresses in ranked order instead of all or arbitrary ones. This reduces wasted dial attempts.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:502 swarm Config ... .with_smart_dial()
impact: Smart dial is already turned on in the swarm config.

title: Lock-free atomically swapped local ENR
idea: Hold the local ENR in a lock-free atomically swapped slot that discovery handlers read, with writers using compare-and-swap edits, so PING/PONG/handshake paths never take a lock or copy the record.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:437
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:211
gap: Replace NetworkGlobals.local_enr RwLock<Enr> with ArcSwap; discv5 keeps its own copy anyway.
impact: Negligible; ENR reads are rare and the lock is uncontended.

title: Mark disconnected peers in discv5 routing table
idea: When a peer disconnects or a dial to it fails, mark it disconnected in the discv5 routing table so its slot is freed for other nodes and lookups return more connectable peers.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:660 disconnect_peer calls discv5.disconnect_node and removes the cached ENR
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:1215 on_dial_failure marks the peer disconnected for Denied (when not connected), NoAddresses, Transport, WrongPeerId and LocalPeerId errors
impact: A failed dial frees the peer's DHT slot. This matches the source PR, which also marked peers only on dial failure.

title: Score peers by block-serving reliability
idea: Keep a per-peer score of how well the peer serves blocks, stored in peer metadata, so sync prefers reliable block providers.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/peerdb/peer_info.rs
gap: Add per-peer block serving success stat in PeerInfo and use it in sync peer selection (range_sync/ batch peer choice).
impact: Could cut sync retries from bad peers; gain unclear.

title: Retry subnet discovery when query returns nothing
idea: When a subnet peer discovery query returns no results, retry it, and track peers' gossipsub subnet subscriptions in the peer database, so the node reaches enough subnet peers quickly.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:893 an empty subnet query result requeues each subnet with add_subnet_query(retries + 1)
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/discovery/mod.rs:673 add_subnet_query stops at MAX_DISCOVERY_RETRY

beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/peerdb/peer_info.rs:442 PeerInfo::insert_subnet
impact: Empty subnet queries are retried up to a limit, and each peer's gossipsub subnet subscriptions are kept in the peer DB.

title: Shorter ping interval to detect dead peers
idea: Shorten the peer ping interval (e.g. outbound 30s to 15s, inbound 35s to 20s) so unresponsive peers are detected sooner and their slots are freed for useful peers.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/config.rs:5
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/config.rs:8
impact: Already done.

title: Sleep between retries of unavailable startup value
idea: When a startup loop retries reading a value that is not yet available (e.g. custody group count), sleep between attempts instead of spinning, to avoid burning CPU.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/service.rs:321
impact: No spin loop exists in Lighthouse.

title: Decode ENR attnets once into set for filtering
idea: When filtering discovered peers by attestation subnet, decode the ENR attnets bitvector once into a set or test the bit directly, instead of building a list and scanning it linearly per candidate.

title: Persist block access list for state read-ahead
idea: Persist the block access list when importing payloads in-process so the EL can warm state reads ahead of execution.

consensus/types/src/execution/signed_execution_payload_envelope.rs:166 block_access_list field

gap: The inclusion-proof sidecar format (spec #3531) is implemented. But validate_data_column_sidecar_for_gossip_fulu calls verify_proposer_and_signature for every column sidecar, and that function does a full BLS verify of signed_block_header each time. No cache keyed by header root records that a header's signature was already verified, so N custody columns of one block cost N identical proposer-signature verifications. The fix: keep a small header_root -> verified cache (or reuse the block's verified signature) and skip the BLS verify on a hit.

title: No retry for deterministic block processing errors
idea: In lookup sync, classify block processing errors determined by the block root (e.g. invalid state root) as non-retryable and discard the block at once, instead of re-downloading and re-processing it several times.

title: Cache block roots by slot while filtering attestations
idea: While filtering pooled aggregates for block inclusion, cache block roots by slot for the pass so source, target and head checks do not re-read each root from the state tree. Cheaper because repeated tree lookups become hash-map hits.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:2739-2754
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation.rs:74-95
consensus/state_processing/src/common/get_attestation_participation.rs:36-70
gap: AttMaxCover::new_for_altair_or_later calls get_attestation_participation_flag_indices once per pooled aggregate. Each call reads state.get_block_root_at_epoch(target.epoch) and state.get_block_root(data.slot) from the milhouse block_roots tree. No per-pass slot->root (or per-AttestationData) cache is shared across aggregates in OperationPool::get_attestations.
impact: Negligible. It saves two milhouse Vector lookups (about 13 levels) per aggregate, a few hundred per block proposal, which is microseconds.

title: Drop single-vote attestations once committee aggregate exists
idea: Once a full committee aggregate has been built, delete the single-vote attestations it covers from the pool, and key the production cache without the redundant slot. The pool stores fewer entries and does less work.
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:457 insert greedily aggregates into existing entries; no deletion of covered singles
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation_storage.rs:489 aggregate_across_committees only merges committees
gap: Insert already aggregates single votes into existing aggregates in place, so singles are not stored separately; the idea only matters if a full aggregate arrives after disjoint singles, and then should_aggregate/subset checks drop covered entries only partially.
impact: Marginally fewer entries in the op pool; negligible on a mainnet node.

title: Lazy max-heap greedy max-cover for block attestations
idea: Select block attestations by greedy max-cover using a max-heap and re-score only the top candidate, since marginal reward only shrinks. Avoids re-scoring all candidates after every pick.
evidence: beacon_node/operation_pool/src/max_cover.rs:51 documents O(limit * items)
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/max_cover.rs:73-96 each round does a full max_by_key scan and a full update_covering_set pass over every available item
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/attestation.rs:165-174 update_covering_set already returns early unless slot and committee index match, so most of the per-round update is cheap
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/lib.rs:413-441 curr and prev epoch covers already run in parallel with rayon::join; Electra limit is MaxAttestationsElectra (8)
gap: maximum_cover has no BinaryHeap or lazy re-scoring. To add it: keep a max-heap of (score, idx), pop the top, apply only the pending covering updates to that item, and push it back if its score dropped. score() sums a HashMap on every call, so cache it as well.
impact: Since Electra the limit is 8 rounds, so the current cost is about 8 full scans of the candidate list, and the per-item update skips other slots and committees. Expect sub-millisecond to low-millisecond savings, on block production only.
refute_note: Searched all of operation_pool for BinaryHeap, lazy or priority-queue selection and found none; max_cover.rs is the only selection path for attestations and attester slashings. Value lowered to low: the Electra limit is 8 and the per-item updates are filtered to the same slot and committee.

title: Abort rest of batch after first invalid block
idea: When processing a sync batch, stop at the first block that fails as invalid instead of processing the remaining blocks, which descend from the bad one. This saves state transitions on doomed blocks.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3366 process_block Err -> return ChainSegmentResult::Failed immediately
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3310 signature verification failure returns early
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3227 filter_chain_segment error returns early
impact: Blocks after the first invalid one in a segment are never state-transitioned.

title: Use only sync peers whose head is ahead of ours
idea: Exclude peers whose reported head is not ahead of the local head from range-sync peer sets and target selection. Requests are not wasted on peers that cannot serve needed blocks or on empty ranges.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/peer_sync_info.rs:26 remote_sync_type classifies Behind/FullySynced/Advanced by finalized epoch and head slot
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:435 only PeerSyncType::Advanced calls range_sync.add_peer; Behind does nothing
impact: Behind and synced peers never join range-sync chains.

title: Minimal block-processing path for synced blocks
idea: Give initial sync a lean import path that does only validity checks, state transition and cleanup, without per-block gossip re-broadcast or other regular-sync overhead.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3202 process_chain_segment: filter, per-epoch batched signature verification, direct process_block
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3334 BlockImportSource::RangeSync, no gossip verification or republish
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:680 signature_verify_chain_segment uses one cheap state advance for committees and one batch signature verify
impact: Range sync uses a dedicated segment import path without gossip checks or re-broadcast.

title: Verify batch data availability in parallel with execution
idea: During range sync, start data availability checks for the whole batch concurrently with state transition and signature verification instead of serially.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:699 verify_columns_against_block runs per block inside signature_verify_chain_segment, before the batched signature verify at :713-722 (serial, same blocking task)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3300 signature_verify_chain_segment awaited per epoch chunk, then blocks imported serially via process_block at :3322
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:639 verify_columns_against_block -> verify_kzg_for_data_column_list / validate_data_columns_with_commitments
crypto/kzg/src/lib.rs:222 verify_cell_proof_batch groups cells by column index and verifies groups with rayon into_par_iter (:263), so column KZG already uses all cores
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/data_availability_checker.rs:495 batch_verify_kzg_for_range_sync_blocks used only by backfill
gap: Column KZG verification for an epoch chunk runs before, not concurrently with, that chunk's signature verification and state transitions, and is not pipelined with import of the previous chunk. Data is coupled with blocks at download time, so there is no DA wait to overlap; only KZG compute could be overlapped (spawn KZG of chunk N+1 while chunk N imports, or run KZG alongside the signature batch).
impact: Small: KZG cell verification is already rayon-parallel across column indices and BLS batch verify is also parallel, so overlapping two CPU-saturating workloads mostly reorders work; gains limited to hiding KZG behind single-threaded state transition, maybe a few percent of batch time on blob-heavy ranges.

title: Await data availability once per payload segment
idea: In range sync, wait for data availability once for a whole segment of payload envelopes and then import each directly, instead of waiting per payload in a queue.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3376 envelope processed directly after its block in the segment loop
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/payload_envelope_verification/import.rs:420 process_range_sync_envelope imports directly, no DA checker wait
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:704 columns KZG-verified inline in signature_verify_chain_segment
impact: No per-payload availability waiting in range sync; columns come with the envelope and are checked inline.

title: Rank sync peers by request-outcome score
idea: Keep a per-peer score for block-serving reliability updated from request outcomes, and use it to pick a limited set of peers and assign sync batches, avoiding slow or faulty peers.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context.rs:578 select_columns_by_range_peers_to_request orders by failed-peer flag, concurrency limit, random
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:1038 send_batch passes failed_peers
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:608 penalties feed the global peer score used by the peer manager
gap: Peer choice uses only the batch's failed-peer set, concurrency and random tie-break; no per-peer success/latency/throughput score. Add a score field to chain peers updated in on_block_response/BatchProcessResult and sort by it in block_components_by_range_request and select_columns_by_range_peers_to_request.
impact: Avoids assigning batches to slow peers during initial sync; gain depends on peer quality, probably modest.

title: Persist snapshot download state to skip re-downloads
idea: Record completed snapshot downloads (flag, per-type lock file or download database) so restarts, upgrades and downgrades do not look up or re-request already downloaded files.
measured_best: For mumbai retrieving torrent info can take up to 15mins even after download is completed. (pr:caplin#9311)
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:77 range sync is RPC based, no torrent snapshot download
impact: Lighthouse does not download snapshot files via a torrent downloader, so there is no download state to persist. Checkpoint sync is a single HTTP fetch.

title: Remember roots of blocks that failed processing
idea: In tip sync, add the root of a block that failed processing to a seen-roots set so it is not fetched and processed again in a retry loop.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:282 ignored_chains is only inserted for parent chains that are too long (PARENT_DEPTH_TOLERANCE), not for processing failures
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/single_block_lookup.rs:980 on_processing_failure re-downloads the same root up to SINGLE_BLOCK_LOOKUP_MAX_ATTEMPTS
beacon_node/network/src/sync/block_lookups/mod.rs:616 drop_lookup_and_children forgets the root after TooManyAttempts
beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:922 notified_unknown_roots only debounces per (peer, root)
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:352 failed_chains keyed by chain target head root (range sync only)
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs:3879 check_invalid_block_roots is a static config set
gap: Block lookups do not record roots whose block failed processing as invalid: BlockLookups::on_processing_result -> on_block_processing_result -> on_processing_failure re-downloads and re-processes the same (content-addressed, so deterministically invalid) root from other peers up to SINGLE_BLOCK_LOOKUP_MAX_ATTEMPTS, and after the drop a new UnknownBlockHashFromAttestation/unknown-parent from another peer (or after debounce expiry) creates a fresh lookup. Insert the root into ignored_chains (or a beacon-chain invalid-root cache) on a BlockError that is a block-validity failure.
impact: Avoids repeated download and state transition of a known-invalid block in tip sync; only matters under attack or on bad forks.

title: Keep re-statusing peers in their sync head chains
idea: When a peer sends a new status, update it in place rather than removing it from syncing head chains, so chains are not torn down and rebuilt.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:177 Head arm calls self.remove_peer before add_peer_or_create_chain
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/chain.rs:248 remove_peer returns EmptyPeerPool when last peer leaves
beacon_node/network/src/sync/range_sync/range.rs:139 Finalized arm keeps the peer in chains (only that path avoids it)
gap: In RangeSync::add_peer Head arm, skip remove_peer when the peer is already in a head chain with the same target (head_root, head_slot), or add before removing from the others, so a sole-peer chain is not dropped and rebuilt and its batches are kept.
impact: Avoids dropping and recreating a head chain (and its in-flight batches) when a sole peer re-statuses to a new head, which reduces head-chain churn. Small gain, only while head-syncing.

title: Gate validator duties on sync status at startup
idea: Hold duty computation and validator-facing work behind a sync-status tracker that stays in a start-up state until enough peers, a timeout, or sync start, so early requests do not force processing of many blocks.
evidence: beacon_node/http_api/src/lib.rs:475 not_while_syncing_filter rejects duties only in SyncingFinalized/SyncingHead beyond sync_tolerance_epochs
beacon_node/http_api/src/lib.rs:509 SyncState::Stalled => Ok(())
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/types/globals.rs:95 sync_state starts as Stalled
gap: At startup sync_state is Stalled and the filter lets duty requests through, so a stale head can be asked for duties before peers arrive. Make not_while_syncing_filter also reject Stalled when head_slot lags the clock by more than the tolerance.
impact: Avoids a validator client forcing long state advances on a stale head during the first seconds after start. Small and rare.

title: Encode status and RPC messages in compact binary, not text
idea: Encode status/hello and other RPC and gossip messages as fixed-width binary (SSZ) fields rather than JSON or strings. Messages are smaller on the wire and need no text parsing.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/codec.rs:330 Status and all RPC messages are SSZ-snappy encoded
impact: Already binary SSZ on the wire as the spec requires.

title: Build status message only when sending
idea: Do not construct the Status message (reading shared chain state) each time peer sync info is evaluated; build it only when it is to be sent.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/sync/manager.rs:418 add_peer calls self.chain.status_message() for each peer status to read local head/finalized
beacon_node/network/src/status.rs:21 status_message builds from cached_head and takes only a cache read (store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:2592) and get_anchor_info
beacon_node/network/src/service.rs:976 send_status builds once for all peers
gap: SyncManager::add_peer could read the local SyncInfo straight from canonical_head.cached_head() instead of building a StatusMessage; the sending path already builds it once per batch.
impact: Saves a few locks and one small struct per received Status. Negligible; the real cost in the original PR was the Arc access, and cached_head is cheap now.

title: Combine status and ping/metadata exchange per peer
idea: Merge the peer status request and the ping/metadata request into a single exchange so fewer round trips are needed per peer.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:85 separate status and ping queues; both are independent libp2p streams
impact: Status and Ping are separate spec protocols on separate streams opened concurrently, so merging them is a code-level batching in Prysm and saves no round trips here.

title: Truncate peer-supplied error message before decoding
idea: Truncate peer-supplied req/resp error message bytes to a small bound (e.g. 256) before decoding and sanitising, so a peer cannot force large string allocations.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/codec.rs:307 decode_error rejects length > ERROR_TYPE_MAX before allocating decoded_buffer
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/protocol.rs:87 ERROR_TYPE_MAX derived from 256-byte ErrorType VariableList
impact: Peer error strings are bounded to 256 bytes before allocation.

title: Cap simultaneous inbound substreams per peer
idea: Limit the number of concurrent inbound RPC substreams per peer and disconnect the peer when exceeded, so stream state and timers stay bounded.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/handler.rs:41 MAX_INBOUND_SUBSTREAMS=32
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/handler.rs:994-1018 over cap emits HandlerRejected and calls self.shutdown
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/peer_manager/mod.rs:561 HandlerRejected => PeerAction::Fatal
impact: Inbound substreams are bounded per connection and the offending peer is disconnected; nothing to gain.

title: Run cleanup when async request supplier throws
idea: Catch exceptions thrown by async request task suppliers and propagate them to the returned future, so failed requests (e.g. closed streams) always run cleanup and do not leak pending request state.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/handler.rs:1017 errors surfaced as HandlerEvent::Err
impact: Teku future/supplier pattern; Rust handler state is dropped via RAII and delay-queue removal, no pending-request leak mechanism of that kind.

title: Trim by-root/by-range requests to servable range before expensive reads
idea: In by-root and by-range handlers, clip the request to the servable slot range and skip roots known to be too old before doing expensive DB or EL work, so out-of-range requests cost almost nothing.
evidence: beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/rpc_methods.rs:1651-1672 BlobsByRange rejects start below oldest_data_slot/boundary
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/rpc_methods.rs:217-250 BlocksByRoot has no age filter, goes to get_blocks_checking_caches
gap: By-range rejects out-of-range starts (cheap) instead of clipping, which is fine; by-root handlers could skip roots known pruned/older than boundary before DB/EL reads in handle_blocks_by_root_request_inner and blobs/columns by-root.
impact: Saves a few DB misses for peers asking for old roots; marginal on mainnet.

title: Send only each sidecar own bytes in by-range responses
idea: In BlobSidecarsByRange responses, serialize only each sidecar own bytes rather than all blobs of the block for every sidecar, avoiding inflated responses.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/methods.rs:666 each response chunk is one Arc<DataColumnSidecar>/BlobSidecar encoded separately
impact: Lighthouse encodes each sidecar as its own object; no whole-block blob bytes inflation exists.

title: Fork-dependent maximum RPC and gossip message sizes
idea: Set maximum RPC and gossip message sizes as a function of the active fork, so decoders never allocate or accept buffers larger than the fork allows.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/protocol.rs:138 rpc_block_limits_by_fork, :624-633 response limits per fork
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/service/mod.rs:246 gossipsub_max_transmit_size = spec.max_message_size()
consensus/types/src/core/chain_spec.rs:971 fixed max from max_payload_size
gap: RPC response limits are fork-dependent, but gossip max transmit size and RPC max_rpc_size (rpc/mod.rs:322) are single fixed values; per-topic/fork gossip limits would need gossipsub per-topic size checks.
impact: Tighter buffers bound DoS memory; small real-world gain.

title: Group column by-root requests per block root
idea: Encode data column by-root requests as one entry per block root with a list of column indices instead of one entry per (root, column), so roots are not repeated and requests are smaller.
evidence: consensus/types/src/data/data_column_sidecar.rs:40-45 DataColumnsByRootIdentifier { block_root, columns: VariableList<ColumnIndex> }
beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/methods.rs:574-576 DataColumnsByRootRequest holds a list of DataColumnsByRootIdentifier
beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/requests/data_columns_by_root.rs:16-32 try_into_request builds one identifier per block root with all requested indices
impact: Requests already carry one entry per block root (Fulu spec wire format).

title: Release pooled decoder buffers once response is decoded
idea: Close per-message context, payload and error decoders as soon as a req/resp response is fully decoded so pooled byte buffers are released rather than leaked.
evidence: beacon_node/lighthouse_network/src/rpc/codec.rs: codec uses owned BytesMut, no pooled decoder buffers
impact: Java pooled-buffer leak; Rust buffers are freed by drop.

title: Send builder validator registrations as SSZ
idea: Derive SSZ encode/decode for signed validator registrations and send them to the builder in SSZ instead of JSON. Payloads are smaller and serialization is cheaper.
evidence: beacon_node/builder_client/src/pre_gloas_builder_http_client.rs:244-259 post_builder_validators uses post_generic (JSON)
beacon_node/builder_client/src/pre_gloas_builder_http_client.rs:269 blinded blocks v2 does use SSZ
gap: Add an SSZ post path (as_ssz_bytes of the Vec, Content-Type octet-stream) in post_builder_validators with fallback to JSON when the relay rejects it.
impact: Registrations are sent once per epoch for all validators; SSZ shrinks payload and serialization, helpful only for nodes with many validators using builders.

title: Shared singleton instances for common integer constants
idea: Return shared cached instances for common uint64 values (zero, 32 ETH in gwei, max) from the value factory instead of allocating a new object each time.
evidence: milhouse-0.9.0/src/packed_leaf.rs: integers packed inline in leaves, no boxed values
impact: Rust u64 is a plain value; no allocation per integer, nothing to cache.

title: Direct byte-order primitives for SSZ integer conversion
idea: Convert integers to and from little-endian SSZ bytes with direct byte-order primitives instead of copying into an aligned temporary buffer and calling a generic swap. This removes a copy per integer in decode and hash paths.
evidence: Rust ssz uses to_le_bytes/from_le_bytes natively (ethereum_ssz); no aligned temp buffer + generic swap
impact: Already compiled to direct loads/stores.

title: Early return for already-parsed SSZ types
idea: In SSZ type resolution, return at once when the type is already in fully parsed form, before string and array checks, so repeated serialize and hash calls skip re-parsing.
evidence: Types are static Rust generics resolved at compile time; no runtime type parsing
impact: No runtime SSZ type resolution exists.

title: Ordered map for pending child changes in mutable SSZ
idea: Track pending child changes of a mutable SSZ container in an index-ordered map instead of a hash map, so committing the changes needs no sort. This speeds state mutation during epoch processing.
measured_best: pr:teku#5348: epoch transition 26.840 -> 28.711 ops/s (32768 validators)
evidence: ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/milhouse-0.9.0/src/update_map.rs:101 UpdateMap impl for VecMap (index-ordered)
~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/milhouse-0.9.0/src/list.rs:30 List default U = MaxMap<VecMap<T>>
~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/milhouse-0.9.0/src/list.rs:184 apply_updates
impact: Milhouse pending updates are held in an index-ordered VecMap, so commit needs no sort.

title: Value range loops in generated hash-tree-root code
idea: In generated hash-tree-root code, iterate list elements with a value range loop instead of an incrementing index, removing per-iteration bounds checks and indexing.
measured_best: pr:prysm#9867: "research indicates is more performant, so it should not cause any slowdown in HTR computations" (no numbers)
evidence: Rust iterators over slices/lists; no generated htr code with indexed loops
impact: Rust iterators already elide bounds checks; tree hashing is in tree_hash/milhouse.

title: Persist block-and-slot to state-root index for rewinds
idea: Persist a (block root, slot) -> state root index alongside saved states, so rewinding to an ancestor state, including at empty slots, is a direct lookup. Replay then starts from the nearest stored state instead of walking parent blocks.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:26 BlockMap block_root->slot->state_root (in memory only)
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:3743 get_ancestor_state_root via state_roots/summaries/cold roots
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1949 load_hot_state uses hdiff grid base, not parent walk
gap: The block+slot->state_root index exists only in the in-memory cache; on disk lookups go through HotStateSummary by state_root and the hdiff grid. Persisting it would only help rewinds to empty slots without a known state root.
impact: Marginal: rewinds already start from nearest hdiff/snapshot base, not by walking parents.

title: Bound state replay horizon for non-finalized-only queries
idea: For operations needing only non-finalized data (gossip validation, duties), limit the state lookup horizon to post-finalized data and fail gracefully. This avoids loading and replaying old states from disk.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1124-1150 get_advanced_hot_state: cache first, then rejects max_slot < split.slot with FinalizedStateNotInHotDatabase
beacon_node/store/src/hot_cold_store.rs:1157 load_hot_state only from the hot DB (bounded by split)
beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:316 get_by_block_root cache-first lookup
impact: Hot-state lookups used by gossip and duties are bounded by the split and fail gracefully instead of replaying finalized history.

title: Cache native state field reads in a wrapper
idea: Wrap the native-backed state view with a cache layer so repeated reads of the same field cross the native binding only once.
evidence: BeaconState is native Rust (milhouse); no FFI binding boundary
impact: No native-binding crossing to amortise.

title: Reuse cached weak-subjectivity state in light client proofs
idea: On finalization, reuse the already computed weak-subjectivity-period state in the light client init proof builder instead of recomputing the state.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/light_client_server_cache.rs:389 bootstrap branch persisted eagerly at finalization
beacon_node/network/src/network_beacon_processor/rpc_methods.rs:978 handler just reads stored bootstrap
impact: Lighthouse has no weak-subjectivity-state-based proof builder; it precomputes and persists the sync committee branch, so serving bootstrap needs no state recompute.

title: Ring buffer of in-place state deltas for unfinalized forks
idea: Keep unfinalized state forks as a fixed power-of-two ring buffer of delta structs reset or copied forward in place, with a lock-free read view. Readers get state without a full state clone per block.
evidence: beacon_node/store/src/state_cache.rs:39 StateCache (LRU of states)
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:825 Arc-shared committee caches, milhouse persistent trees
impact: Lighthouse state clone is O(1) structural sharing via milhouse, so a delta ring buffer with lock-free view has little to save and would be a redesign.

title: Pass large inputs by reference, not by value
idea: Pass shuffling inputs and hash lists to helper functions by reference or borrow instead of moving or cloning them on every call. This avoids per-call allocations and copies in shuffling and attestation helpers.
evidence: consensus/swap_or_not_shuffle/src/shuffle_list.rs:92 shuffle_list takes Vec by value, shuffles in place
consensus/types/src/state/committee_cache.rs:195 shuffling() returns &[usize]
consensus/state_processing/src/common/get_attesting_indices.rs:96 takes references to committees and aggregation bits
impact: Large inputs are borrowed or moved once; the 2018 commits are Lighthouse's own and long superseded.

title: Append into one shared output buffer
idea: When gathering results (such as expected withdrawals) from several helpers, pass one output buffer to each helper to append into rather than returning new vectors that are then concatenated. This removes intermediate allocations and copies.
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/withdrawals.rs:28 Vec::with_capacity(max_withdrawals_per_payload)

consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/withdrawals.rs:32-44 get_builder_withdrawals, get_pending_partial_withdrawals, get_builders_sweep_withdrawals, get_validators_sweep_withdrawals all append into &mut Vec<Withdrawal>
impact: Already a single shared output buffer.

title: Mutate one epoch context in place across transition
idea: Use a single epoch/shuffling context object through block and slot processing and mutate it in place, instead of wrapping and copying it into a transition-specific context and rebuilding it per block. This avoids per-block context copies.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:825 committee caches stored in the state as Arc, reused across blocks
consensus/state_processing/src/consensus_context.rs:18 ConsensusContext is a small per-block struct with no copied epoch data
impact: No per-block wrapping or copy of the epoch context exists in Lighthouse.

title: Cache sync participant reward per epoch
idea: Compute the sync committee participant reward once per epoch and store it in the epoch cache rather than recomputing it each block. Also read attestation aggregation bits through a faster direct accessor than generic bitlist indexing.
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/altair/sync_committee.rs:47 compute_sync_aggregate_rewards called on every block
consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/altair/sync_committee.rs:83-104 reward recomputed (BaseRewardPerIncrement::new does an integer sqrt) per block
consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/altair/sync_committee.rs:50 get_sync_committee_indices per block
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:1753-1767 get_sync_committee_indices: 512 pubkey-cache hash lookups + Vec alloc per call
consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/altair/sync_committee.rs:58 sync_committee_bits.iter() direct bit iteration
gap: The participant/proposer reward is not cached per epoch (compute_sync_aggregate_rewards runs per block), and the sync committee validator indices are re-derived via 512 pubkey lookups in BeaconState::get_sync_committee_indices on every block instead of being cached per sync-committee period. The bit-access half is implemented.
impact: Microseconds per block (one isqrt plus ~512 hash lookups); not measurable in block import time.

title: Store payload timeliness committee window in state
idea: Keep the payload timeliness committee for the lookahead window in the beacon state and refresh it once per epoch, so per-slot lookups read the cached value instead of redoing the balance-weighted selection.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:811
consensus/state_processing/src/per_epoch_processing/single_pass.rs:539-576
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:3591-3625
consensus/state_processing/src/common/get_payload_attesting_indices.rs:30
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/shuffling_cache.rs:41-90
impact: Per-slot PTC lookups (payload attestation verification, API, op pool) read state.ptc_window; balance-weighted selection (compute_ptc_with_cache) runs only in process_ptc_window and the Gloas upgrade.

title: Order operation validity checks cheapest first
idea: In request processing (for example consolidation requests), run the cheapest rejection checks before validator lookups and credential checks so invalid requests exit early.
evidence: consensus/state_processing/src/per_block_processing/process_operations.rs:1090-1160
impact: Negligible: requests are few per block and the checks already run in spec order.

title: Compact participation flag arrays with index accessors
idea: Expose epoch participation flags as compact byte arrays and read only the validator indices needed instead of materializing the whole participation list. This saves memory and copying.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:585
consensus/state_processing/src/per_epoch_processing/single_pass.rs:249
beacon_node/operation_pool/src/reward_cache.rs:22-24
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_rewards.rs:237-255
impact: Participation is a packed u8 milhouse List read by index. The op-pool reward cache uses BitVecs. No hot path materializes the whole list.

title: Make debug state and block dumps opt-in
idea: Do not serialize and write every post-state and block to disk in the state transition path unless a debug flag enables it. This removes a full SSZ serialization and file write per block.
evidence: beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:118
beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/block_verification.rs:2284-2310
beacon_node/beacon_chain/Cargo.toml:13
impact: The default build does no SSZ dumps.

title: Remove spec-dropped vectors from beacon state
idea: Drop state fields that the spec no longer uses (such as active index roots and compact committee roots), so the state is smaller and no per-epoch work computes or hashes them.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:516-563
impact: The state has no obsolete vectors to hash.

title: Hold state as persistent tree throughout the node
idea: Keep the beacon state as a persistent tree-backed structure everywhere instead of converting between flat objects and trees, so copies share structure and hashing is incremental.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:516
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:3070-3077
Cargo.toml:299
impact: State clones share structure, and hashing is incremental through milhouse.

title: Self-describing cache overlays avoid old-item copy
idea: Store the layout overlay (chunk offsets per field) inside the tree hash cache and walk it on update, comparing the current value only against cached dirty flags, so the previous item need not be cloned or kept. This removes a copy of the old value per cached update.
evidence: consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:3070-3077
consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:3082-3085
impact: Superseded: milhouse keeps the hash caches inside the tree, so no old-item copy is kept.

title: Native fixed-width integers in hashing paths
idea: Use native fixed-width integers (u64) rather than an arbitrary-precision bignum type for balances, slots and epochs in SSZ hash-tree-root and serialization. This avoids heap allocation and slow big-number arithmetic.

title: Hash fixed-size lists as packed primitive vectors
idea: Declare small fixed-size sequences of integers (such as a committee) as vectors of primitives instead of lists of per-element containers, so the hash tree root packs several values per 32-byte chunk. Fewer chunks mean fewer hashes.

consensus/types/src/state/beacon_state.rs:811

title: Promote cached hashes on state finalization
idea: When an unfinalized state delta is merged into the finalized base, promote its already-computed hash overlay into the base's hash tree so finalization costs no SHA-256, and keep read-only views separate from the hashing overlay.

title: Try SSZ on all beacon nodes before JSON fallback
